title: Kneser-Tits over fields of cohomological dimension $\le 2$ (with an appendix by Alexis Bouthier and Federico Scavia)
summary: We settle the Kneser-Tits problem over every field $k$ of (separable) cohomological dimension $\le 2$, thus resolving a conjecture of Gille. More precisely, for such a $k$ and a semisimple, simply connected $k$-group $G$ whose indecomposable factors over $k$ are isotropic, we show that $G(k)$ is generated by "elementary matrices" (the $k$-points of the unipotent radicals of the parabolic $k$-subgroups of $G$), in other words, that $K_1^G(k) \cong 1$. In fact, we show this vanishing already when $k$ has separable $p$-dimension $\le 2$ in the sense of Gille with respect to a subset of the torsion primes $p$ of $G$, and we reinterpret the separable $p$-dimension itself via syntomic cohomology. To approach those $G$ that escape the net of previously known cases, for an inclusion of reductive $k$-groups $M \subset L$, we develop a new method based on the Rost invariant for transferring $R$-eq

title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
summary: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of the Heisenberg result under rational Hodge isogenies. For arbitrary projective K3 surfaces with a faithful symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action, we obtain a motivic reduction to the minimal resolution of the fift

title: Splitting types of Richelot isogenies over finite fields and a newform of weight four
summary: A factorization $f=uvw$ of a square-free sextic over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic into three monic quadratics defines a genus-2 curve with a rational $(2,2)$-isogeny kernel, and the Richelot construction attaches to it three dual quadratics $U,V,W$. We determine, for every odd prime power $q$, the number of such factorizations with prescribed splitting behaviour over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of all six quadratics. Each of the $64$ counts is $q(q-1)(q+1-n_f)/64$ times $C(q)\pm t_q$, where $n_f$ is the number of roots of $f$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$, $C$ is an explicit monic cubic, and $t_q$ is the trace of Frobenius attached to the newform $η(2z)^{4}η(4z)^{4}$ of weight $4$ and level $8$. The proof reduces the counts by elementary means to a twisted second moment of the Legendre family of elliptic curves, which is a value of a hypergeometric function over $\mathbb{F}_q$ evaluated by

title: Calabi-Yau fibrations and orbifold Mordell
summary: We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false.

title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
summary: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

title: Stokes corners and the global structure of steady rotating waves in annular domains
summary: We study steady rotating water waves in a planar annulus, in the model of radial gravity and constant vorticity introduced by Li and the author. The stream function is harmonic, and the free surface carries the Bernoulli condition $p_0^2|\nablaΨ|^2=Q_α(S)$ with $Q_α(R)=(R-r_-)(R-r_+)$. We first settle the crest shape. For $α\neqα_\pm$, every stagnation point lies on the circle $R=r_-$, and the surface forms a symmetric $120^\circ$ corner there. At $α=α_\pm$ the corner is a right angle. The same holds for limits of smooth solutions and, in the lower region, for overhanging waves. We then study the global bifurcation continuum. Its waves are monotone from crest to trough, and they always cross the laminar circle. Hence there is no secondary bifurcation, and the parameter stays above an explicit floor. The continuum ends in an extreme wave, overturns, or degenerates; the last case is exclud

title: Wiener-type criteria for parabolic equations with two-sided Gaussian bounds
summary: We establish sufficient and necessary Wiener-type criteria for boundary regularity of parabolic equations whose fundamental solutions satisfy two-sided Gaussian bounds. In particular, our sufficient criterion holds at the critical exponent in the Gaussian lower bound. For the heat equation, the resulting double-series criterion is equivalent to the classical Wiener criterion of Evans and Gariepy. Our results apply to divergence form equations with bounded measurable, possibly nonsymmetric coefficients, and to non-divergence form equations with coefficients in $\mathrm{DMO}_x$ (Dini mean oscillation in space), without requiring continuity in time.

title: Modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear Schrödinger equation
summary: In this paper, we construct modified wave operators for the critical long-range nonlinear Schrödinger equation with final data $\langle x\rangle^s u_+\in L_x^2,\ d/2<s\le2$, for dimensions $d=1,2,3$, and for both defocusing and focusing cases. We impose no smallness, nonvanishing, or spatial derivative assumption. Most previous modified wave operator results require smallness on $\|\widehat u_+\|_{L^\infty}$, analytic final data or smooth amplitude-phase structure, and the large data modified wave operator problem with finite weighted condition is only solved for 1D defocusing equation. We introduce a new perturbation method which successfully applies to both defocusing and focusing signs when $d\le3$. The main ingredient is an improved growth estimate for the linearized flow, obtained by a low--high frequency decomposition. At low frequencies, spatial localization and freezing the coeff

title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
summary: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements

title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
summary: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a no

title: Variational Thresholds and Multiplicity for a Nonlocal r-Laplacian Logistic-Type Problem
summary: This paper investigates the existence, multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a class of nonlocal logistic-type problems with the \(r\)-Laplacian operator in the fast diffusion regime: %, with a real parameter $λ$: \[ \begin{cases} -Δ_r u - \displaystyle\int_Ω K(x,y)u(y)\,dy = a(x)u +λ|u|^{q-2}u \displaystyle\int_ΩQ(x,y)|u(y)|^q\,dy, & x\in Ω, \\[0.4em] u = 0, & x\in \partialΩ. \end{cases} \] The model has local diffusion, nonlocal dispersal, and nonlinear global interactions, and depends on a real parameter $λ$. For $λ\ge 0$, we establish the existence of nonnegative weak solutions via a variational principle. In the case \(λ<0\), we characterize two variational thresholds, \(-\infty<\widehatλ^*<λ^*<0\), which separate different solution intervals. For \(λ^*<λ<0\), the energy functional has a global minimizer with negative energy and a mountain-pass critical point with pos

title: Classification of fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system
summary: We study fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system with four reaction exponents, in which only one component diffuses. For nonnegative segregated initial data, we classify the limits for all exponents at least one under homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The limiting equations include the heat equation, a one-phase Stefan problem, a fixed-domain heat equation, and a nonlinear equation with a time-integral reaction term. We also describe the limiting behavior of the nondiffusing component and obtain a nontrivial rescaled limit. In the critical regime, we characterize the limit as the greatest weak solution and establish a transition between initial finite propagation and instantaneous positivity. Under Dirichlet conditions, permanent zero regions may occur for certain small initial data.

title: Inviscid limit of steady Navier--Stokes equations with Navier friction boundary conditions in a periodic channel
summary: The vanishing viscosity limit of the steady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations is studied in a periodic channel with Navier friction boundary conditions, where the slip length is assumed to be a nonnegative power of the viscosity. Depending on this power, the problem falls into subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes. In each regime, the Navier--Stokes solutions are constructed via the Prandtl expansion, and the validity of the expansion is rigorously justified. By the Prandtl--Batchelor theory, the leading Euler solution is a Couette flow, and the interaction between the interior and boundary-layer profiles is precisely characterized. Of particular interest is the critical regime, in which the leading order Prandtl profile solves a nonlinear steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition. The well-posedness of this problem is established using the von Mises t

title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
summary: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $δ^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the

title: Local Reynolds number criteria for the regularity of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations, and their consistency with forced finite-time blow-up
summary: We give four regularity criteria for the forced Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The first is an $\dot H^1$ estimate: a strong solution cannot blow up while the local Reynolds number $|v|^2/(ν|ω|)$ stays below $4/(3\sqrt3)$ wherever the vorticity exceeds a threshold $M(t)$ with $\int M^{6/5}\,dt<\infty$. It rests on an exact identity that gives the cubic vorticity term a favorable sign. Two further $\dot H^1$ estimates use the Newton potential of $|ω|^2$, either as a multiplier or as a gradient added to the Lamb vector, so that the integral of $|ω|^2|v|^2$ cancels. The second of these gives a critical condition on the vorticity alone, implied by $\int\|ω\|_{L^3}^2\,dt<\infty$. The fourth is a maximum principle for $\frac12|v|^2+λ|ω|$: vortex stretching is absorbed by viscous dissipation, and the pressure is controlled by a weighted local estimate. It requires a bound on $|v|^2/

title: Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
summary: We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for noninters

title: Exterior $p$-capacitary rigidity on groups of Heisenberg type
summary: We study the exterior Bernoulli overdetermined problem for sub-elliptic operators. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a group of Heisenberg type with Property (H), and let $Ω\subset \mathbb{G}$ be a domain enjoying a partial symmetry property and containing a Korányi-Kaplan ball $\overline{B_r}$ centered at the origin. We consider a function $u$ that is $p$-harmonic with respect to the $p$-sub-Laplacian $Δ_{\mathbb{G},p}$ in the annular region $Ω\setminus \overline{B}_r$, satisfying the boundary conditions $ u = 0 \;\text{ on }\; \partialΩ, \quad u = 1 \;\text{ on }\; \partial B_r.$ We show that if $p$ is even and $u$ satisfies a mild overdetermined condition on the sub-Riemannian norm of its gradient on the outer boundary $\partialΩ$, then $Ω$ must itself be a Korányi--Kaplan ball centered at the origin, and $u$ is the corresponding normalized capacitary potential; equivalently, away from the pole it

title: Localization and homogenization of anisotropic fractional energies
summary: We study the joint limit of localization ($s\uparrow1$) and periodic homogenization ($\varepsilon\downarrow0$) for anisotropic fractional energies with $p$-growth and oscillating kernels. We prove that the $Γ$-limit is governed by the single parameter $θ=\lim\varepsilon^{p(1-s)}$, and that its density is the convex combination $θ\mathcal{A}^* + (1-θ)\bar{\mathcal{A}}$ of the homogenized and the averaged densities. This shows that the picture recently obtained for quadratic energies also holds for every $p$ and for anisotropic kernels, with no regularity in the oscillating variable; the approach is different, and is based on convex duality. A nonlocal version of the duality argument gives the limit as $s\uparrow 1$ for a fixed kernel under weak assumptions, correcting a previous proof by the authors.

title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
summary: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly

title: On the linearization of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation in $\mathbb{R}^N$
summary: Let $u$ be a positive radial solution of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation $$-Δu=u^p \qquad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad p>\frac{N+2}{N-2}. $$ In this paper we classify the bounded solutions of the associated linearized operator $-Δw -pu^{p-1}w=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The resulting classification reveals the role of the threshold value $p=\frac{N + \sqrt{N^2 - 8N}}{4}$. In particular, above this threshold, the solutions are generated by the invariance of the problem under dilations and translations. Below this threshold, many new solutions appear, and their number tends to infinity as $p$ approaches the Joseph-Lundgren exponent and $N$ is large.

title: Self-similar solutions for capillary water waves
summary: In this paper we prove the existence of self-similar solutions to the capillary water wave problem. In particular, this implies finite-time formation of singularities in the form of a corner, and retraction from a corner due to the time-reversibility of the equations. Unlike most self-similar smooth solutions, the solutions with $2/3$ time-length scaling are seen in experiments like pinch-off retraction, bubble bursting or jet formation. The proof involves a new argument through the regularization of the Hamiltonian and does not require the existence of an approximate profile. We believe this strategy has further implications in the construction of self-similar solutions of dispersive PDE.

title: Rupture and far-field profiles for Hénon-type MEMS elliptic equation with pressure
summary: Motivated by membrane touchdown in electrostatic microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) under external pressure, we study the Hénon-type elliptic equation $Δu=λ|x|^αu^{-p}+F$, $u>0$, where $N\ge2$, $λ,p>0$, $α>-2$, $F\in\mathbb R$, and $α<2p$ if $F\ne0$. Near the origin, we construct positive radial rupture solutions with $u(0)=0$ for $F\ne0$ and infinitely many non-radial but asymptotically radial ones for every $F$, and derive expansions to arbitrary order. On exterior domains $Ω_{R_0}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:|x|>R_0\}$, with no condition at the origin, we establish existence and uniqueness of positive solutions on $[R_0,\infty)$ for radial initial value problems with $u(R_0)>0$ if $p\ge1$, or if $F\ge0$ and $u'(R_0)\ge0$. We determine the leading behavior of all positive radial exterior solutions as $|x|\to\infty$ for $F>0$ and $F=0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$ and $α\ge0$. For possibly non

title: A strict Neumann-Dirichlet eigenvalue inequality on planar domains
summary: On simply connected, bounded planar Lipschitz domains it is known from our earlier work that the ($k+2$)-nd eigenvalue of the Neumann Laplacian cannot exceed the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. In this note we sharpen this statement by showing that this inequality is always strict. This was previously only known under additional assumptions.

title: Uniqueness and comparison for a singular parabolic equation with a concave nonlinearity
summary: We consider the Cauchy problem for $\partial_t u-Δu=|x|^{-γ}u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, with $0<q<1$, $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$ and nonnegative initial data $u_0\in C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $s\mapsto s^q$ is not Lipschitz continuous at the origin, the uniqueness of nonnegative solutions is a delicate issue. {For $u_0\not\equiv0$, it was known for small values of $γ$ and, more recently, under the additional condition $γ<N(1-q)$.} We prove that, for $u_0\not\equiv0$, uniqueness holds on the whole range $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$, which settles a conjecture of the authors. In fact, we establish a comparison principle between bounded subsolutions and supersolutions which are bounded from below by a multiple of the profile $t^{1/(1-q)}(|x|+\sqrt t\,)^{-γ/(1-q)}$. We then describe completely the set of nonnegative solutions emanating from $u_0\equiv0$: it consists of the trivial solution, of a unique positive sol

title: Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem
summary: For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton. Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.

title: Boundedness and $L_p$-estimates for non-local operators with square-Dini continuous coefficients
summary: We prove the boundedness of the non-local operator $\mathcal{L}^a$ of order $σ\in(0,2)$ with kernel $a(x,y)|y|^{-d-σ}$ from $H^σ_{p,w}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L_{p,w}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for the whole range of $p\in(1,\infty)$, where $w$ is a Muckenhoupt weight. The coefficient $a(x,y)$ is bounded, merely measurable in $y$, and its modulus of continuity $ω$ in $x$ satisfies the square-Dini condition $\int_0^1ω(t)^2t^{-1}dt<\infty$. This condition allows, for instance, $ω(t)=(\log(1/t))^{-1}$, which is not a Dini modulus, and it improves the Hölder continuity assumption in previous work. Using the boundedness result, we obtain global estimates and the unique solvability in weighted $L_p$ spaces, as well as interior $L_p$-estimates, for the corresponding elliptic and parabolic equations. We also show that the square-Dini condition is sharp. By adapting a recent construction of C. Liu, we show that f

title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
summary: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines

title: (n-1)-Dimensional Hausdorff Measure Estimates for Free Boundaries of Infinity Laplace Equations
summary: We investigate the geometric properties of free boundaries associated with nonnegative viscosity solutions to the infinity Laplace equation with strong absorption $$ Δ_\infty u=λu_+^m, \qquad λ>0,\quad 0<m<3. $$ We first establish a sharp distance-to-free-boundary regularity estimate with an explicit optimal coefficient, which coincides with the constant in the non-degeneracy estimate. This exact matching yields a uniform interior tangent ball property at every sufficiently small scale for every free boundary point. As consequences, we obtain a sharp lower density bound of $1/2$ for the positive phase, a locally finite covering of the free boundary by Lipschitz graphs, and quantitative local estimates for its $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the question raised by Araújo, Leitão, and Teixeira (J. Funct. Anal. {\textbf 270} (2016), no. 6, 2249

title: Symmetries, conservation laws, series solutions and singularity formation for the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations in mass coordinates
summary: Written in Lagrangian mass coordinates, the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations for a polytropic gas become a single second-order equation for the radius $r(t,m)$ of the shell enclosing mass $m$, with adiabatic index $γ>1$ and entropy profile $S(m)$. We determine all point symmetries of this equation. Apart from time translation there is at most one scaling, except at the critical index $γ=4/3$, where a scaling exists for every entropy profile; these scalings are the entropy-fixed stabilisers of the two-parameter scaling group of the non-isentropic system, and we give the exact symmetry defect when $γ\neq4/3$. Noether's theorem singles out the profiles $S=Km^{14-10γ}$, for which a scaling is variational and gives a conservation law beyond energy; otherwise the scalings yield virial identities. We construct exact collapse solutions and reduce the self-similar problem to one ordi

title: Existence and nonexistence of global solutions to a semilinear parabolic equation with variable reaction on sub-Riemannian manifolds
summary: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t-Δ_{\mathcal{M}}u=h(t)[f(u)]^{p(x)}$ on $\mathcal{M}\times(0,T)$, with $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in L^q(\mathcal{M})$, where $\mathcal{M}$ is a complete sub-Riemannian manifold endowed with a smooth volume measure and $Δ_{\mathcal{M}}$ denotes the associated sub-Laplacian. The function $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty))$, $f$ is nonnegative and continuous, and $p$ is a bounded measurable function on $\mathcal{M}$. We establish sharp criteria for the existence and nonexistence of nonnegative global solutions. In particular, our framework applies to connected unimodular Lie groups, yielding global existence, nonexistence, and Fujita-type results. Our approach allows for nonlinearities $f$ beyond the convex setting, thereby broadening the scope of earlier nonexistence results in the Euclidean framework. Furthermore, our results generalize those of Ruzhansky and Yessi

title: $C^{m,α}$-rectifiability in Carnot groups
summary: In an arbitrary Carnot group $\mathbb{G}$ of homogeneous dimension $Q$, we characterize rectifiability of sets of finite Hausdorff measure by $\mathbf C_{\mathbb{G}}^{m,α}$-regular surfaces with complemented vertical tangent subgroups, for every $m\ge1$ and $α\in[0,1]$. The criterion combines positive lower density with approximation in measure by tubes around such surfaces. At almost every point, one tube radius $λr^{m+α}$ suffices for $α>0$, whereas the estimate must hold for every $λr^m$, $λ>0$, for $α=0$. Tubular approximation upgrades $\mathbf C^1_{\mathbb{G}}$-rectifiability to class $(m,α)$ without an additional density assumption. The proof combines ambient normal-form polynomial jets, a Remez-type norming inequality, and Whitney extension. In topological dimension at least two, quantitative volume approximation by noncharacteristic sublevel sets yields higher-order rectifiabilit

title: Global $C^{2,α}$ Estimates for Complex $k$-Hessian Equations on Kähler Manifolds
summary: We prove an a priori $C^{2,α}$ estimate for classical admissible solutions of the complex $k$-Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side.

title: Smooth Exterior Potentials for a Gradient-Weighted Hessian Equation
summary: We construct a positive solution of an exterior Dirichlet problem for a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian operator on each smooth strictly star-shaped domain whose boundary curvatures lie in $Γ_k$. For $p>1$ sufficiently close to one, the solution is smooth up to the boundary, has no critical points, and is unique among continuous potentials on the natural viscosity branch. Its levels remain strictly star-shaped and strictly $k$-convex. We determine its radial asymptotics through two derivatives and the uniform limit of $(p-1)|Du_p|$ on the boundary. The construction perturbs an inverse curvature-quotient flow. In logarithmic radial coordinates the exact equation is elliptic for $p>1$ and its limit is parabolic. A weighted inverse estimate on the half-cylinder controls the singular perturbation.

title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
summary: We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner. We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time

title: Probabilistic well-posedness of dispersive PDEs beyond variance blowup II: quadratic nonlinear wave equation
summary: We study the quadratic nonlinear wave equation (NLW), posed on the two-dimensional torus, with rough Gaussian random initial data beyond the variance blowup threshold observed by Okamoto and the fourth author (2021). By introducing a suitable vanishing multiplicative renormalization constant on the frequency-truncated Gaussian random initial data, we prove that the corresponding solutions converge in law to a solution to the stochastic NLW with zero initial data, driven by a Gaussian space-time noise whose temporal covariance at each spatial Fourier mode is given by the Bessel function of order $0$. We also show that the solution to the limiting equation almost surely blows up in a finite time, and that the convergence above holds on every compact time interval before the maximal existence time. %on the maximal time of existence. A main new ingredient is the analysis of the oscillatory c

title: Higher-Order Minkowski Inequalities via Gradient-Weighted Hessian Potentials
summary: We prove a sharp boundary inequality for exterior potentials of a gradient-weighted $k$-Hessian equation under regularity, level-curvature, flux conservation, and radial decay hypotheses. The inequality bounds a power of the Newton flux by the normalized integral of $H_k^p/H_{k-1}^{p-1}$, and equality characterizes balls. After a conformal change of metric, two Newton-tensor divergence identities give comparisons between regular levels even when the slab between them contains critical points. For smooth strictly star-shaped domains with strictly $k$-convex boundary, a companion existence theorem supplies exterior potentials for $p$ close to one. We identify the limiting flux with the integral of $H_{k-1}$ and recover the sharp consecutive Minkowski inequality, including its equality case.

title: The sharp Trudinger--Moser exponent in Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces
summary: We establish the sharp Trudinger--Moser inequality in the fractional Sobolev--Slobodeckij spaces $W^{s,p}$, $0 < s < 1$, at the critical index $sp=N$, including the endpoint. More precisely, there exists a constant $C_{N,s}$ such that for every measurable set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ of finite positive measure, $$ \sup\Bigl\{\frac{1}{|Ω|}\int_Ωe^{α_{s,N}|u|^{\frac{p}{p-1}}}dx: u\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^N), u=0\text{ a.e. on }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΩ, [u]_{s,p}\le 1\Bigr\}\le C_{N,s}, $$ where $[u]_{s,p}$ is the Gagliardo seminorm and $α_{s,N}$ is the upper threshold found by Parini and Ruf for $N\ge 2$ and by Iula for $N=1$. Moreover, the constant $α_{s,N}$ is sharp. This answers two of their questions. We use a nonlocal version of Moser's one-dimensional lemma. The $p$-th moment of a translation kernel on the logarithmic half-line determines the sharp coefficient, and finiteness of the next m

title: Uniform velocity support for the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system
summary: This paper proves that the velocity support of the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system remains uniformly bounded for all time for nonnegative initial data in \(C_c^1(\mathbb R^6)\). The proof establishes uniform bounds on a weighted fifth-order energy moment and an associated fourth-order force integral by exploiting the relative motion of particle pairs. On intervals where the target particle moves sufficiently fast relative to the expansion, these estimates give a summable bound for the current in its energy identity. This bound yields uniform control of the velocity support.

title: Unique continuation and its failure for the Monge--Ampère equation
summary: We study unique continuation for Alexandrov solutions with common Monge--Ampère density bounded above and below. In the plane, we prove that agreement on an open set forces global equality. For every bounded domain \(Ω\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(n\ge3\), we construct two distinct uniformly convex \(C^{1,1}(Ω)\) solutions that agree on a nonempty open subset of \(Ω\).

title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
summary: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integ

title: Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the quasilinear Lane-Emden equation
summary: We study isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to $-Δ_pu=u^q$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $Δ_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<n$, and $n(p-1)/(n-p)<q<np/(n-p)-1$. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u(x)\sim K_{n,p,q}|x|^{-p/(q+1-p)}$ as $x\to0$, where $K_{n,p,q}>0$ is an explicit constant depending only on $n,p,q$. The result holds without radial symmetry or an a priori growth assumption. The proof combines a removability criterion with a rigidity theorem for positive solutions in $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying two-sided power bounds. To handle the infinite $p$-Dirichlet energy at the singularity, we construct a continuous Steiner deformation that fixes all sufficiently high superlevel sets. The resulting energy comparison yields radial symmetry of the blow-up limits.

title: On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients
summary: We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete antiderivatives respectively for intricate hypergeometric sequences that arise in our analysis.

title: A Keller--Segel Chemotaxis Model on One-Dimensional Moving Domains
summary: We study a one-dimensional Keller--Segel system on an interval whose boundary moves according to a prescribed contracting law. The boundary motion makes the problem genuinely nonautonomous and destroys the mass conservation available on fixed domains. A time-dependent change of variables, combined with a time reparametrization, reduces the problem to a semilinear system on a fixed interval with time-independent principal part and nonautonomous transport terms. We prove global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions, and we show that the contraction of the domain yields a uniform bound on the total mass. For the long-time dynamics, our main tool is a singular Gronwall type inequality with an exponentially damped kernel, for which we provide a self-contained version with explicit decay rate and constants, tailored to our setting; under a small gain condition on the boundary velocit

title: Kinetic transfer or regularity in any dimension from uncertainty inequalities on the real line
summary: The purpose of this short note is to show that one dimensional uncertainty inequalities easily induce transfer of regularity inequalities in kinetic equations in any dimension.

title: Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity
summary: We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincaré inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and unifor

title: Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Operators: Strict Monotonicity and Asymptotic Behavior
summary: In this paper, we investigate the properties of the generalized principal eigenvalue for a coupled local/nonlocal operator. First, we establish sufficient conditions to guarantee strict monotonicity properties, obtaining weaker hypotheses than those currently available in the literature for nonlocal operators. Next, we establish several results concerning the asymptotic behavior of this generalized eigenvalue, along with the convergence of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are very useful for the study of nonlinear problems. Our findings reveal novel phenomena that are not present in purely local or purely nonlocal cases. The main mathematical difficulty lies in the fact that the generalized eigenvalue does not always admit an eigenfunction, in addition to the inherent technicalities of the considered coupling.

title: On the Unique Identification of Finitely Many Radial Heat Sources
summary: In this work, we investigate an inverse source problem for the heat equation in $\R^d$ ($d\geq1$), in which the source is a finite positive linear combination of translates of a known real-valued radial Schwartz profile with nonzero total mass. Both the locations and strengths of the sources are to be identified from the observations of time traces at finitely many spatial points over an arbitrary nonempty open positive-time interval. For $d\geq2$, we prove that the sharp universal measurement threshold is $dN+1$: every set of $dN+1$ measurement points in affine general position uniquely identifies every source configuration with at most $N$ locations. For $d=1$, we prove that two distinct measurement points uniquely identify every finite source configuration, independently of the number of sources, and that this count is sharp. The analysis relies on an equivalence between equality of h

title: Microlocal and global smoothing effect of variable coefficient ZK-type operators
summary: In this work, we study the smoothing effect of a class of Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equations, which generalize the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to higher dimensions. Specifically, we consider linear evolution equations generated by ZK-type operators with variable coefficients, and we study both their microlocal and global smoothing effects under suitable conditions on the coefficients of the operator. Our analysis requires a detailed study of the geometric properties of the Hamiltonian flow associated with the operator under consideration. These properties allow us to prove a dispersive and a strong smoothing effect associated with the Cauchy problem in question: under suitable moment conditions on the initial datum, the solution becomes smooth in space for positive times in a finite time interval.

title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
summary: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of [3] from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.

title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
summary: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).

title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
summary: We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.

title: Logarithmic stability from finite-time boundary measurements in an infinite slab
summary: We prove logarithmic stability for an inverse convection--diffusion problem in an infinite slab from finite-time partial boundary measurements. The data consist of boundary fluxes generated by a fixed temporal profile and varying spatial Dirichlet inputs. For coefficients with fixed interior support and uniform Sobolev bounds, the data determine the exterior derivative of the drift and a gauge-invariant reaction term with a logarithmic modulus. Prescribing the divergence gives separate stability for the drift and reaction coefficients. The input and observation patches may be arbitrary nonempty open subsets of the same or opposite faces. The proof combines a quantitative passage from finite-time responses to a stationary boundary map with a Runge approximation estimate in the measured $H^{3/2}$ input norm. The first step uses sectorial semigroups on the unbounded slab; the second transfe

title: Global Stability Analysis of an Excitable Infinite-Dimensional System
summary: Motivated by the study of excitable control of infinite-dimensional linear systems, we investigate the global stability properties of a closed-loop system consisting of a stable linear infinite-dimensional plant and a non-monotone controller. The controller has piecewise-linear dynamics that resemble the FitzHugh-Nagumo model of neural behaviour. As our main result, we derive a checkable condition for the global exponential stability of the closed-loop system using the circle criterion. Finally we illustrate the stability result for a one-dimensional heat equation.
comment: 7 pages, 8 figures, submitted to the European Control Conference 2027

title: Fundamental gaps of the restricted fractional Laplacian on thin planar convex domains
summary: We study the fundamental gap $Γ_s(Ω)=λ_{2,s}(Ω)-λ_{1,s}(Ω)$ of the restricted Dirichlet fractional Laplacian for $0 < s < 1$. Building on the thin-rectangle estimates of Dyda and Kulczycki, we establish compact Mosco convergence of shifted quadratic forms and convergence of their eigenvalues on collapsing convex strips. This yields the next-order expansion, with exact coefficients, of each fixed eigenvalue of a thin rectangle. Let $G_s(θ)$ be the infimum of $D^{2s}Γ_s(Ω)$ over bounded open convex planar domains with $|Ω|/D^2=θ$, where $D$ denotes the diameter of $Ω$. As $θ\downarrow0$, we obtain $G_s(θ)\simκ_s\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}θ$ for $0 < s < 1/2$, $G_{1/2}(θ)\sim3π^2γθ\log(1/θ)$, and $G_s(θ)\sim3π^2β_sθ^{2-2s}$ for $1/2 < s < 1$. The constants $κ_s$, $γ$, and $β_s$ are determined by the transverse interval ground state. On $I=(-1/2,1/2)$, let $\mathfrak{g}_t$ be the infimum of the fun

title: Scaling-invariant conditions for two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations
summary: We study the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with either far-field vacuum or non-vacuum. Under suitable smallness conditions on explicitly constructed scaling-invariant initial quantities, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions involving initial vacuum states and large oscillations. The two far-field regimes present distinct analytical difficulties and require different approaches to the {\it a priori} estimates. Although the two smallness criteria have different forms, they arise from the same intrinsic scaling of the equations. Our results provide a unified scaling-invariant framework for the global well-posedness of strong solutions in both far-field regimes.

title: Geometry of ground states in the long-range Ising model
summary: We study the ground states of the ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with long-range interactions and prescribed exterior data. We first show that the half-space configuration is a ground state, by means of a discrete calibration (which is the lattice counterpart of the calibrations of Cabré and Pagliari for nonlocal minimal surfaces). In dimension $d\ge2$ and for positive kernels, the half-space configuration is the unique minimizer in every finite domain, and it is "stable" with respect to perturbations of the exterior datum whose energy is below half of a positive excitation gap. This rigidity has no counterpart in the continuum. For general exterior data and positive kernels, we show that along a monotone family the minimizer is unique except for finitely many data. This can be considered a "generic uniqueness result" that provides the discrete counterpart of a recent work o

title: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
summary: In this paper, we study positive solutions to the problem \begin{equation*} -Δu = |x|^{-s_2}u^{2^*(s_2)-1} - \la |x|^{-s_1}u^{p-1} \quad \text{in }\Om, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Om, \end{equation*} where $\Om\subset\R^N$ ($N\ge 3$) is a bounded domain with $0\in\partial\Om$, $0\le s_1<s_2<2$, $2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$, $2^*(s_2)<p<2^*(s_1)$, and $\la>0$. This is the Li--Lin open problem \cite{LL} in the form studied by Cerami, Zhong, and Zou \cite{CZZ} and by Tang and Tang \cite{TT1}. Assume that $\partial\Om$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $0$ with a leading term of homogeneity $1+α$, and set $θ=\frac{(N-2)(2^*(s_1)-p)}{2}$. We prove that a solution exists for every $\la>0$ if $θ>α$ and the $α$-mean curvature of $\partial\Om$ at $0$ is negative, whereas $\la^*=\sup\{\la>0:\text{a solution exists}\}$ is finite if $θ\leα$, without any curvature assumption. For $α=1$, this removes the restr

title: Dirichlet does not imply Regularity for general elliptic operators in smooth domains
summary: In the upper half-space $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$, $n\geq2$, we show that there exists a real, diagonal, strongly elliptic matrix $A$ of bounded measurable coefficients, smooth in the interior of $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ and continuous on its closure, such that for the elliptic operator $L=-\operatorname{div}A\nabla$, the Dirichlet problem with data in $L^p$ is solvable, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$, but the Dirichlet-Regularity problem is not solvable for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. The counterexample has the following properties, in particular: 1. $A$ equals the identity matrix at the boundary and their $L^\infty$ distance in $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ can be made arbitrarily small. 2. $A$ satisfies that $t|\partial_t A|^2$ is a Carleson measure. 3. $A$ fails to satisfy the Dahlberg-Kenig-Pipher condition only slightly, in the sense that for every $q>2$, $t^q|\nabla A|^q\frac{dxdt}{t}$ is a vanishing Carleson m

title: Towards a unified treatment of structured deformations theories
summary: Relying on the theory of $\mathcal B$ gradients, with $\mathcal B$ a $\mathbb C$-elliptic homogeneous linear partial differential operator of order $k$, with constant coefficients, we propose a method which allows to treat in a unified way the theories of structured deformations. Introducing the space of structured $\mathcal B$-deformations, $SD_{\mathcal B}$, we establish an integral-representation result for the associated energies, involving both bulk and surface contributions. Our approach relies on a direct application of the global method for relaxation, suitably adapted to the space of functions of $\mathcal B$-bounded variation.

title: Quasilinear elliptic equations involving asymptotically linear operators
summary:

title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
summary: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=ψ(|D|/N)$ with $ψ\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_ψ\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>σ(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang

title: Normalized solutions of critical biharmonic equations on bounded domains
summary: We study the critical biharmonic equation with clamped boundary conditions and prescribed $L^2$ norm on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge5$. For every sufficiently small mass, the constrained energy admits a local minimizer. We also obtain a second solution for masses in the closure of a measurable set having positive measure in every interval adjacent to zero. This holds on arbitrary smooth bounded domains when $N\ge8$ and, when $N=5,6,7$, under a condition involving the first clamped eigenvalue and a cutoff quotient. Explicit sufficient conditions are given and verified on balls. The proof combines a quantitative monotonicity argument with a norm estimate excluding loss of compactness.

title: The sharp mass threshold for the three-dimensional Riesz liquid-drop model near the Coulomb exponent
summary: We determine the exact mass threshold of the three-dimensional liquid-drop model with repulsive kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ in a two-sided neighborhood of the Coulomb exponent $s=1$. The infimum is attained precisely for $0<m\le\mstar$, with balls as the unique minimizers up to translation and null sets. Here $\mstar$ is the mass at which one ball and two equal balls at infinite separation have the same energy. We compute the first-order variation of this threshold at $s=1$. For $s>1$, a diameter bound proportional to the mass supplies a lower bound on the averaged planar slicing integral and yields a uniform mass bound. The resulting compactness and a uniform quadratic energy gap for finite-perimeter sets close in measure to a ball allow us to transfer the Coulomb classification to nearby exponents. At $m=\mstar$, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence asymptotic in measure to single balls

title: Optimal quantitative stability near the Coulomb fission threshold
summary: We study the optimal quadratic stability constant for the three-dimensional Coulomb liquid-drop energy at fixed volume, measured by the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. Let $M$ be the critical mass at which the energy of one ball equals the limiting energy of two infinitely separated balls of equal volume. We prove that, as $m$ approaches $M$ from below, the optimal constant satisfies $Λ(m)=(36π)^{1/3}(2^{1/3}-1)(1-m/M)+o(1-m/M)$. We further show that every almost optimal sequence with masses $m_n\to M$ from below is asymptotic in measure to a union of two equal-volume balls whose centers diverge. We also identify the corresponding perimeter and Coulomb-energy limits and give a necessary and sufficient criterion for almost optimality after rescaling to mass $M$. The proof combines a strict binding inequality for mass partitions, a local spectral gap at the critical ball, and a BV truncation a

title: Sharp global well-posedness for the defocusing nonlinear wave equation outside a ball with radial data
summary: Let $Ω=\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $3<p<5$. We prove sharp global well-posedness of the defocusing Dirichlet boundary value problem of nonlinear wave equation with radial data in the critical space $\dot H^{s_c}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)\times \dot H^{s_c-1}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)$, where $s_c=\frac32-\frac{2}{p-1}$, thereby improve the result in \cite{XuYangYou2025}. The proof combines the distorted Fourier transform in \cite{LiSZ:NLS,XuYang2024} with the energy--Morawetz estimate by Dodson in \cite{DodsonCubic2018,Dodson2018}.

title: Principal spectral theory of time-periodic nonlocal advective cooperative systems and its applications
summary: We develop a new spectral theory for time-periodic nonlocal cooperative systems with advection on bounded intervals, allowing asymmetric dispersal kernels. By transforming the problem into a nonlocal moving-boundary problem, we show that the associated Poincaré map is strongly positive and power compact, which yields existence and uniqueness of the principal eigenvalue and several variational characterizations. For spatially homogeneous coefficients, we establish the limit of the principal eigenvalue as the interval expands to $\mathbb R$ and identify it as the minimum of the principal Floquet exponents of the associated exponentially weighted periodic systems. To the best of our knowledge, this spectral theory is new even in \textbf{the scalar case}. We then apply these results to nonlinear systems. On bounded intervals, the sign of the principal eigenvalue gives a sharp dichotomy: solu

title: Existence and multiplicity of radial solutions for higher order logarithmic and infinite mass Schrödinger equations
summary: We study radial solutions of the Schrödinger equation $-Δu+V(x)u=g(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$, where $V$ is radial and $g(t)/t\to-\infty$ as $t\to0$. In this infinite-mass case the energy functional is not finite on $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. First let $g(t)=t|\log|t||^{α-1}\log|t|$ with $α>1$. We only assume that $V$ is continuous and bounded from below. So $V$ may change sign, and it need not be coercive or have a limit at infinity. We obtain a nontrivial radial solution and a sequence of radial solutions whose energies tend to infinity. To do this, we add the term $λ|u|^{p-2}u$ with $1<p<2$, find critical points of the perturbed functional by minimax methods, and let $λ\to0$. The infinite-mass structure gives the compactness in this limit. Next let $g$ be odd, with a power bound near zero and at most critical growth at infinity. Let $V$ be bounded, with a smallness condition on $(x\cdot

title: Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow
summary: We study the fractional mean curvature flow near shrinking spheres. The first shape eigenvalue changes sign at \(s_*(n)=(\sqrt{n^2+6n+1}-n-1)/2\). Above this threshold, sufficiently small perturbations of a sphere become extinct at one point, and their extinction rescalings converge exponentially to the round shrinker. Below the threshold, the sphere is nonlinearly unstable modulo translations and dilations. We also construct smooth, strictly convex, nonspherical homothetic shrinkers bifurcating from the spherical family near the threshold. In the plane, the noncircular branch bifurcates on the side \(s>s_*(2)\).

title: Support monotonicity for quadratically regularized optimal transport
summary: We study the support of the optimizer $π_\varepsilon$ of the quadratically regularized optimal transport problem for quadratic cost and compactly supported marginals. As $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this support converges to the support of the Monge coupling. We investigate whether the regularized supports are nested as $\varepsilon $ decreases. Under regularity assumptions on the marginal densities, their domains, and the Brenier map, we establish interior support inclusions in every dimension. More precisely, for each compact $K\subset\operatorname{int}X$ and fixed $θ\in(0,1)$, we prove that $\mathrm{spt}π_δ\cap(K\times Y) \subseteq\mathrm{spt}π_\varepsilon\cap(K\times Y)$ whenever $0<δ\leθ\varepsilon $ and $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small. title: Spacelike Curve Shortening Flow of Entire Graphs in One Spacelike Codimension
summary: We study curve shortening flow of entire spacelike graphs in the pseudo-Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{2,k}$, $k\geq1$, where the graph directions have mixed spacelike and timelike signature. Consequently, the region of spacelike slopes is nonconvex, making the preservation of spacelikeness more delicate. We identify a natural geometric condition that overcomes this difficulty: the closed convex hull of the initial slopes is compactly contained in the spacelike region. We prove that the convex hull is preserved along the flow, yielding uniform spacelikeness and uniform acausality. For initially $C^{1,α}$ graphs, we establish global existence and uniqueness, without assuming convexity or initial curvature bounds. If the initial perturbation vanishes at spatial infinity, we further prove smooth and uniform convergence to the prescribed affine spacelike line, without rescaling. Finally, we sh

title: The first Fučík curve of the $p$-Laplacian on compact quantum graphs: slopes at the diagonal and nonresonance
summary: We study the Fučík spectrum of the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<\infty$, on a compact connected quantum graph, with Dirichlet conditions on a possibly empty set $V_D$ of vertices whose removal does not disconnect the graph and Kirchhoff conditions at the others. We construct the first nontrivial curve $\mathfrak C$ of the spectrum by a mountain pass argument and show that it is Lipschitz and strictly decreasing. As the parameter tends to infinity, $\mathfrak C$ tends to the first eigenvalue if $V_D\neq\emptyset$, and otherwise to the smallest first eigenvalue obtained by a Dirichlet condition at a single point. If the second eigenvalue is simple, we compute the two one-sided slopes of $\mathfrak C$ at the diagonal. The curve is differentiable there if and only if the positive and negative parts of the second eigenfunction have the same $L^p$ norm. On three-edge stars these norms differ for suitab

title: Difference estimates for Chern connections on homolomorphic vector bundles
summary: This paper investigates the uniqueness issue of Chern connections from the Cheng-Yau type estimate point of view. We establish local difference estimates for Chern connections on holomorphic vector bundles over complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded from below. These local estimates not only enable us to obtain uniqueness results for Hermitian-Einstein connections on complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, but also apply to study the Liouville theorem for complex Monge-Ampère equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ as well as the Chern flatness and Kählerness for Hermitian metrics on complete noncompact Ricci flat Kähler manifolds.

title: Growth versus boundedness for viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with a forcing term: a Fujita-type dichotomy
summary: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=Δu+|\nabla u|^q+a(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where $q>1$ and the integrable forcing has positive total mass. Unlike classical Fujita problems, regular solutions exist globally, so the relevant dichotomy concerns boundedness versus grow-up. We identify the critical exponent $q_c=N/(N-1)$ for $N\geq 2$, with $q_c=\infty$ for $N=1$. For stationary forcing, every solution grows at least linearly on a fixed ball when $1<q\leq q_c$. In two dimensions, solutions tend to infinity locally uniformly for every $q>1$, with an explicit logarithmic lower bound. For $q=2$, the Cole--Hopf transformation relates the exact growth rate to the spectrum of $-Δ-w$. Conversely, when $N\geq 3$ and $q>q_c$, bounded solutions exist for sufficiently small nonnegative data and forcing. We also establish growth criteria for time-dependent forcing, including decaying profiles.

title: Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices
summary: Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$. Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform li
