title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
summary: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^γ$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^γ$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$ on a prototypical tree

title: Analytic properties of distributions associated with multi-state Random Number Generators
summary: We analyze the analytic properties of probability distributions associated with possibly unfair, multi-state Random Number Generators (i.e., dice). Specifically, given a $q$-sided die, if $x_i\in \{0,\ldots, q-1\}$ denotes the outcome of the $i^{\text{th}}$ toss, then $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]$ is the associated cumulative distribution function---a probabilistic generalization of the famed Cantor function. We first establish easily computable bounds for the $L^1$-distance between the possibly unfair $F$ and the uniform distribution $y=x$. We then show that $F$ is both upper- and lower-Hölder continuous, where the associated Hölder exponents are shown to be sharp. Finally, we establish recursive formulae for the moments, $\mathbb{E}[X^n]$, associated with $F$ and use these moments to provide sequences of step-functions that converge uniformly to $F$ from above and below.

title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
summary: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton serie

title: Weighted Inequalities for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Trees with Flow Measures
summary: This paper develops a weighted theory for the fractional Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M_{μ,γ}$, $0<γ<1$, on infinite trees equipped with flow measures. Such measures are typically nondoubling and exhibit exponential volume growth, so the classical Muckenhoupt theory does not apply directly. By replacing Euclidean balls with admissible trapezoids, a class of fractional $A(p,q)(μ)$ weights is introduced, and a Muckenhoupt-type theorem is established: for $1\le p<1/γ$ and $1/p-1/q=γ$, the operator $M_{μ,γ}$ is bounded from $\ell^p_μ(ω^p)$ to $\ell^q_μ(ω^q)$ if and only if $ω\in A(p,q)(μ)$. The endpoint case $p=1$ is characterized via a weak-type estimate.

title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
summary: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.

title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
summary: Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carathéodory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraint

title: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees
summary: We study the Bergman projection $P_ω$ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_ω$, where $ω$ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_ω$ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $A^p_ω$ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $ω$ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_ω^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $L^p(ω) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $Ω\in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(Ω) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_Ω(\mathbb{D}) $.

title: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices
summary: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.

title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
summary: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces
summary: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answ

title: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
summary: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
summary: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $δ$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\logδ|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $δ$-neighborhood of an $ε$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim ε^{-1}|\logδ|^{-1}$, for $δ$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $ε$.

title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
summary: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

title: Solutions to Three Spline-Related Conjectures
summary: This AI-assisted article settles (partially) several conjectures coming from spline theory: Scherer--Shadrin conjecture on mirroring the sign patterns of polynomial derivatives is answered in the negative through a counterexample; the author's conjectures on the Lebesgue function of the orthoprojector onto spaces of polynomials multi-vanishing at an endpoint are answered in the affirmative; and Schumaker conjecture on interpolation with lacunary bivariate Bernstein polynomials is provided with solutions in a number of previously unknown situations.

title: Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases
summary: In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.

title: On the Bourgain-Rudnick eigenfunction restriction conjecture in four dimensions
summary: We prove a uniform upper $L^2$ bound for eigenfunctions of the four-dimensional flat torus on the compact paraboloid $\mathbb{P}^3$. The main novelty is the use of Fourier restriction estimates. We interpret spherical lattice point statistics as non-concentration inequalities of the strength needed to apply the Du--Zhang fractal restriction theorem. We apply their result on two-dimensional slices of $\mathbb{P}^3$. Further possible extensions are also discussed.

title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
summary: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every bounded set K\subset R^n, n\ge2, satisfying S^{n-1}\subset K-K has lower box counting dimension greater than or equal to n(n-1)/(2n-1), and the bound is also sharp.

title: A surprising bound for the $2\times2$ matrix weighted martingale multiplier
summary: For real $2\times2$ matrix weights, we prove that a scalar martingale multiplier on a dyadic root has $L^2(W)$ norm at most $CQ\sqrt{1+\log(Q)}$, where $Q$ is the dyadic matrix $A_2$ characteristic. A single multiplier, with signs alternating by generation, attains this order for every sufficiently large characteristic scale. We show that the restriction on the matrix size is essential: these estimates jump to the order $Q^{3/2}$ from the matrix size $3\times 3$ onward.

title: Qualitative WALA, Alberti representations and Lipschitz differentiability
summary: We show that the existing theory of Lipschitz differentiability spaces implies that a metric measure space satisfying a qualitative analogue of the WALA condition of David--Semmes has many independent Alberti representations, and provides conditions for when such a space is rectifiable.

title: Global topology and symmetry breaking in an indefinite superlinear Dirichlet problem
summary: Motivated by the work of Fencl and López-Gómez [13] on global bifurcation diagrams, we study the connected components of positive solutions of $-u''=λu+a(x)u^p$ on $(-1,1)$ with $u(-1)=u(1)=0$, where $a$ changes sign and $p\ge2$ is an integer. For generic $\mathcal C^r$ weights, $r\ge2$, with $n$ positive intervals, simple zeros and negative endpoint values, we obtain at least $2^{n-1}$ noncompact components. Apart from the principal component, each is a curve with both ends at $λ=-\infty$. The proof distinguishes at least $2^n-1$ ends and yields bounds for branching and compactly supported cohomology. For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.

title: Differential equations for Macdonald's hypergeometric series via Dunkl operators of type A
summary: We solve an eigenvalue problem for a family of trigonometric Dunkl operators depending on a parameter, extending the result of Ref.[16] to the case of a general parameter. We introduce families of nonsymmetric W-type operators closely related to Dunkl operators and analyze their algebraic structure, various representations and symmetrization. We then use these operators to characterize non-symmetric Macdonald's hypergeometric series introduced in Ref.[5] and recover several known results. These results suggest a direct connection between Macdonald's hypergeometric series and Dunkl operators.

title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
summary: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures. Mathematica notebooks and verification scripts included as ancillary files

title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
summary: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

title: Perturbed Nevo--Thangavelu maximal functions on two-step nilpotent groups
summary: Consider a step-two nilpotent Lie group $G$ identified with $\mathbb R^d\times \mathbb R^m$ in exponential coordinates. We study maximal operators associated with parabolic dilates of smooth convex hypersurfaces with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature in a tilted $d$-dimensional subspace of $G$. We focus on the low-rank regime, where the rank is determined by the group law and the tilt. When $m=1$, we determine the optimal range of $p$ for which the maximal operator is bounded on $L^p(G)$. For $m\ge2$, we characterize, in terms of a Łojasiewicz exponent, when the known necessary condition on $p$ is also sufficient.

title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels on a Ball and on a Simplex in the Full Range of Parameters
summary: We establish genuinely sharp heat-kernel estimates for orthogonal expansions on the Euclidean unit ball and on the unit simplex throughout their natural parameter ranges. For the ball weight $W_μ(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)^{μ-1/2}$, we extend the known estimate from the range $μ\geq0$ to every $μ>-1/2$. For the simplex, we prove the corresponding estimate for every $κ\in(-1/2,\infty)^{d+1}$. The estimates retain exactly the form known in the classical ranges. The proof is based on analytic continuation of the classical product and reduction formulas. Below the integrability threshold, the ball formula decomposes into an endpoint term and a derivative correction, while the simplex formula produces endpoint and mixed-derivative terms indexed by the negative coordinates. In the lowest simplex parameter range we use the auxiliary even ultraspherical kernel introduced by Nowak, Sjögren, and Szarek.

title: Finite Angular Derivative Sets and Almost Isometries of the Hyperbolic Disc
summary: We prove that a subset $E$ of the unit circle is the set of points at which an analytic self-map of the unit disc has a finite angular derivative if and only if $E$ is an $F_σ$ set. We also prove that, for every countable dense subset $E$ of the unit circle, there exists an almost isometry in the sense of Garnett--Papadimitrakis whose angular derivative is finite precisely on $E$.

title: A periodic Ambrosetti-Prodi problem with sign-changing nonlinearities
summary: We study the periodic solutions of the second-order equation \begin{equation*} u''+f(t,u)=s, \end{equation*} where $s\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter and $f$ is periodic in the time variable and satisfies the one-sided sublinear growth condition \begin{equation*} f(t,x)\geq a(t)|x|^p+b(t), \qquad 0<p<1, \end{equation*} for some $a,b\in L^1([0,T])$ with $\int_0^T a(t)\,\mathrm{d}t>0$. We establish an Ambrosetti--Prodi type theorem: there exists a threshold $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the equation has zero periodic solutions for $s<s_0$, at least one for $s=s_0$, and at least two for $s>s_0$. The main novelty of our result is the removal of the non-negativity assumption on the weight $a$, which is replaced by the weaker requirement of a positive mean value, thus allowing for sign-changing nonlinearities.

title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
summary: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(Ω,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(Ω), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(ξ) Z_Y(dξ), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For α>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(Ω, B_α^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(Ω, B_α^2(C^-)), where B_α^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(ω,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z

title: The Ritt problem is decidable
summary: We give an affirmative solution to the Ritt problem.

title: A rigorous Abel-summed Hardy-type identity for $p$-circle domains via regularized Poisson summation
summary: In our previous work, a generalized Hardy-type identity (GHI) for astroid-type $p$-circle domains was formally derived in terms of generalized $p$-Bessel functions. However, the direct application of the Poisson summation formula to the indicator functions of these domains leaves the convergence and rigorous justification of the resulting oscillatory series unresolved. In the present paper, we address this difficulty by introducing an anisotropic regularization based on convolution kernels with Fourier multipliers $e^{-t(|ξ_{1}|^p+|ξ_{2}|^{p})}$. We establish the corresponding regularized Poisson summation identity and rigorously justify the limiting process through uniform estimates for lattice-point sums. A key feature of our analysis is the determination of boundary contributions: smooth boundary points carry weight $1/2$, whereas the contributions from axial cusps vanish for $0<p<1$.

title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
summary: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

title: Nonlinear Fourier series
summary: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.
comment: 10 pages with 3 figures, and another page of references

title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
summary: We consider Hörmander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture.

title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
summary: We study positive solutions of the Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + a(t)g(u)=0,\qquad u'(0)=u'(T)=0, \] with a two-step sign-changing weight. Under an explicit condition on an increasing nonlinearity \(g\), we prove that for every prescribed integer \(N\ge 1\) and every prescribed ratio \(κ>0\) of the step lengths, there exist step weights of that ratio and strictly negative integral for which the problem has at least \(N\) distinct positive solutions. The multiplicity persists under small perturbations of the weight parameters. A structural condition on \(g'/g\) yields at least three positive Neumann solutions for \(g(u)=e^{u^p}-1\) for every \(p>1\). An explicit increasing nonlinearity also satisfies the \(N\)-solution criterion for every finite \(N\), with the weight chosen separately in each case.

title: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
summary: We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$.

title: Polynomial spaces are locally Paley-Wiener: local spectral geometry, sampling, and interpolation
summary: We identify the local Paley-Wiener structure of multivariate polynomial spaces on centrally symmetric convex bodies and apply it to sampling and interpolation. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density in the interior, the normalized reproducing kernel at scale $1/n$ converges to the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on the dual unit ball of the Baran metric. We call this set the local spectral body. It describes the frequencies available to polynomials near each point. By recovering local bandlimited functions together with their $L^2$ norms, we obtain bulk universality and Christoffel asymptotics uniformly on compact subsets of the interior. This connection allows us to use Fourier methods to study polynomial sampling. If weighted sampling is uniformly stable with asymptotically one node per polynomial coefficient, almost every local spectral

title: Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator
summary: We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average. The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

title: Low Moments, Small Balls and Star Discrepancy
summary: Let $D_P$ be the discrepancy function of a configuration $P$ of $N$ points in the $d$-dimensional unit cube, and let $\|D_P\|_q$ be its $L^q$ discrepancy. We prove that for all fixed $d\ge2$ and $0<q\le1$ the $L^q$ discrepancy of every configuration of $N\ge2$ points is at least $c_{d,q}(\log N)^{(d-1)/2}$ with a constant $c_{d,q}>0$. This bound is sharp; together with the classical results for $q>1$, it determines the minimal order of the $L^q$ discrepancy for every $0<q<\infty$ in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for $q=1$ it answers Chen's problem on the sharp lower bound for the $L^1$ discrepancy in dimension $d\ge3$. We prove the small ball inequality for Haar functions in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and for arbitrary real coefficients with the conjectured power of $n$, up to a polylogarithmic factor; here $2^{-n}$ is the smallest volume of the dyadic boxes involved. The method also e

title: On the $L^p$-Neumann problem for divergence form elliptic equations in the upper half-space
summary: A central question has been whether the $L^p$-Neumann problem is solvable for some $p\in(1,\infty)$ in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+:=\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty)$, $n\geq2$, for second-order uniformly elliptic equations in divergence form whose coefficients are either independent of the transverse variable or satisfy the Dahlberg--Kenig--Pipher (DKP) condition. We answer this question in the negative for both classes, even for matrices whose symmetric part is the identity. The two examples have the same nonzero Neumann datum $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ of mean zero. Although $g$ is bounded and belongs to the real Hardy space $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, neither equation admits a weak solution with this datum whose gradient has a non-tangential maximal function in $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ for any $1\leq p<\infty$. For the variational solution $u$ associated with either matrix $A$, the non

title: Variation bounds for averages over nondegenerate curves
summary: In this article, we prove sharp variational estimates for averaging operators over non-degenerate curves in $\R^3.$ The sufficiency follows from dyadic localisation, Sobolev embedding, and local smoothing estimates, and the primary novelty of this article lies in obtaining sharp necessary conditions for variational estimates.

title: Endpoint behaviour of vertical and horizontal Riesz transforms for the flow Laplacian on homogeneous trees
summary: We study endpoint estimates of Riesz transforms on a homogeneous tree equipped with its canonical flow measure $μ$. We prove that the known boundedness from $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ to $L^1(μ)$ of the vertical Riesz transform can not be strengthened to boundedness on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ itself. We also prove that the adjoint vertical Riesz transform is not of weak type $(1,1)$. For the scalar horizontal transforms defined by nonzero bounded coefficients with zero sum on each child set, we establish $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)\to L^1(μ)$ boundedness and show that failure to preserve cancellation on atoms prevents boundedness on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$. We then introduce a horizontal derivative based on deviations from sibling averages. Its associated Riesz transform retains the $L^p(μ)$ bounds for $1<p<\infty$ and the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate, and is bounded on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ itself.

title: Boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to diffusion operators in Lebesgue spaces
summary: We revisit boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to a diffusion operator both in fixed and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. We obtain optimal asymptotics in the former setting and we provide new tools to establish boundedness in the latter.

title: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
summary: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\neΛ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(Λ)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $Λ\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.

title: Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
summary: We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field. Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors us

title: Variational Estimates for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs
summary: We study edge variation estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on finite connected graphs. For $0<α<1$, we determine the optimal coefficient in the uniform estimate of the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge $p$-variation of the original function. We also obtain two-sided variation bounds involving the number of vertices and the diameter. On complete graphs, we prove that the sharp $(p,q)$ constant is $(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{1/q-1/p}$ for all $0<p\leq q\leq\infty$. On star graphs with $n\geq4$, we determine the sharp infinite-exponent constant and show that the sharp constant for $p=2$ equals $1-n^{α-1}$ if and only if $n^{α-1}\geq1/2$. Combining this with the known estimate for $p=1$, we also obtain sharp mixed estimates. Extremizers and counterexamples are given.

title: Variational Estimates for the Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operator on Finite Graphs
summary: We study edge variation for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on finite connected graphs. We determine the optimal uniform coefficient controlling the oscillation of the maximal function by the edge variation of the original function and derive two-sided estimates for the variational constant of an individual graph. These estimates involve point-mass tests, the diameter, and the number of edges. On star graphs, we determine the sharp constant for exponents greater than one and characterize all nonconstant real-valued extremizers for every exponent.

title: Sharp orthonormal Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger equation in all remaining cases
summary: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates for the free Schrödinger equation in homogeneous Sobolev spaces $\dot H^s$. We resolve the remaining open cases concerning the optimal summability of the coefficients. Together with earlier results and counterexamples, our theorems complete the classification for nonnegative Sobolev regularity $0\le s<d/2$.

title: On the multiplicity of crossing limit cycles of double diagonalizable piecewise linear vector fields
summary: We consider planar piecewise linear vector fields with two zones separated by a straight line and having two diagonalizable components, which we call the \emph{double diagonalizable configuration}. In this configuration, the Poincaré half-maps correspond to separatrices of saddle points in the foliations of symmetric differential forms $ω_r(x)-ω_r(y)$, where $ω_r$ is a rational $1$-form with exactly three simple poles. Limit cycles correspond to non-diagonal intersections of two such separatrices, and the multiplicity of a limit cycle is precisely the order of contact at the intersection point. We prove that two distinct separatrices which are not nested segments of the same straight line have a contact of order at most $4$ at a diagonal point and at most $2$ at a non-diagonal point. As a consequence, we obtain that the multiplicity of limit cycles in the double diagonalizable configurat

title: Circular Vector Tomography with Partial Radial Data
summary: In this article, we introduce and study several generalized circular Radon transforms acting on smooth vector fields compactly supported in a planar annulus, with centers restricted to the outer acquisition circle and truncated measurement radii. The operators of interest are the longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transforms and their weighted analogues. We characterize the kernels of the individual unweighted transforms. Then we establish the reconstruction of a vector field from the combined longitudinal and transverse circular Radon transform data. We further show that the pairs formed by each transform and its weighted analogue is not sufficient for the complete recovery of a vector field. However, we demonstrate that full reconstruction is possible with suitable additional data. Finally, we numerically implement and validate the derived inversion formulas.

title: $\ell^p$-Improving for Discrete Fractional Integrals and Averages on the Moment Curve
summary: We prove the $\ell^p$-improving estimates in the full range for discrete fractional integral operators on the moment curve (except at the endpoint) and discrete averages on the moment curve (with $N^ε$-losses). This follows via essentially sharp Diophantine solution counting estimates for inhomogeneous Vinogradov systems with an odd number of variables.

title: Round hyperspheres uniquely minimize most tangent-point energies
summary: We show that round hyperspheres uniquely minimize a broad class of generalized tangent-point energies among all boundaries of bounded Caccioppoli sets sharing the same perimeter or enclosed volume. This includes closed $C^1$-hypersurfaces. Equivalently, we establish sharp lower bounds for the associated scale-invariant ratios of energy to surface measure and energy to volume, respectively, with equality precisely for round spheres.

title: Characterization of parabolic rectifiability in terms of Jones' square function
summary: We show that a measure $μ$ in $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic metric is rectifiable (in the parabolic sense) if and only if the Jones' square function is finite $μ$-almost everywhere. This square function is constructed using the parabolic version of the Jones' beta numbers, which control how close $μ$ is to being supported in time-independent planes (these planes are the paradigmatic example of parabolic rectifiable set). Our only background assumption is that $μ$ has positive and finite densities (qualitatively) almost everywhere. A key feature of our proof is the use of a parabolic version of the Reifenberg parametrization theorem, which in the Euclidean setting is due to David and Toro (MAMS, 2012), and has recently been extended to the parabolic setting by Hoffman, Mourgoglou and the fourth author. In the latter work, the authors construct a bi-Hölder ma

title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
summary: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminusΩ$. For any $α\in(0,1]$ and $x\inΩ$, let \begin{align*} d_{α,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\geα\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $α\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(Ω)$, \begin{align*} \int_Ω\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le Cα^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $α^{-p'}$ as $α\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\i

title: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
summary: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
summary: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calderón--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

title: Subharmonic functions and convexity of the Radon transform, with applications to the Fourier transform
summary: Integrating a subharmonic function over parallel hyperplanes produces a convex function of the signed distance from the origin, provided that the function is absolutely integrable on bounded slabs. We prove this first for twice continuously differentiable functions and then without any smoothness assumption, and the same argument applies to a function defined only on a slab. Examples on the disk explain why subharmonicity on a bounded convex domain does not imply convexity of the integrals over its chords. We then apply a one-dimensional Fourier representation for convex functions to the Radon transform, which leads to a directional formula for integrable subharmonic functions on slabs. For functions on bounded convex domains whose Radon transforms are convex, we obtain a weighted estimate for the integral of the Fourier transform in terms of boundary layers and the gradient.

title: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
summary: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,β}$ hypersurfaces with $0<β\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

title: Global existence and emergent dynamics of singular Cucker-Smale model on general digraphs
summary: We investigate the global-in-time dynamics of the Cucker--Smale model under general network topologies with a singular communication weight function $ψ(r) = r^{-α}$, $α>0$. For $α\ge 1$, we establish the global-in-time existence of smooth solutions when network topologies belong to one of several classes of directed graphs. In particular, in one dimension, we present a necessary condition on the network topology for global existence by constructing finite-time blow-up solutions from non-collisional initial configurations. Moreover, we provide a sufficient framework for the emergence of mono-cluster flocking. For certain classes of network topologies, we further show that mono-cluster flocking occurs unconditionally for non-collisional initial configuration when $α=1$.

title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
summary: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hytönen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(σ)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calderón--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(σ)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{γ_p}$, where $γ_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calderón--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-suprem

title: Pinned simplex volumes from thin sets in Euclidean spaces
summary: Let $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a Borel set, with $d\geq2$. We prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H}(E)>d/2$, then there exist distinct points $a,b\in E$ such that the set of triangle areas with fixed base $a,b$ and third vertex varying in $E$ has positive Lebesgue measure. More generally, for $2\leq r\leq d$, if \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}(E)> \max\left\{r-1,\frac{d-r+2}{2}\right\}, \] then there are $r$ affinely independent points in $E$ for which the corresponding base-pinned $r$-simplex volume set has positive Lebesgue measure. The geometric input is a thin-plane estimate of Bright, Ortiz, and Zakharov \cite{BrightOrtizZakharov}. For a suitable $(r-2)$-dimensional anchor spanned by $E$, this estimate yields simultaneous Frostman bounds for a projected vertex measure in the normal space of the anchor and for the distribution of directions determining bases that share the anchor. The Peres--Schlag mach

title: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
summary: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that, in compact ambient manifolds, type-I singularities of the mean curvature flow in a gradient shrinking Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background have, after suitable parabolic rescaling, weighted minimal hypersurfaces as their limiting models, while in the noncompact setting, we establish the corresponding result for a gradient shrinking Schouten soliton background. This provides a geom

title: An improved weighted broad $L^2$ estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$
summary: For a compact smooth plane curve $S$ with nonzero curvature and a union $X\subseteq B_R$ of unit balls satisfying a one-dimensional Katz--Tao condition, we prove $\|\mathrm{Br}_A E_S f\|_{L^2(X)} \leq C_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'} R^{\varepsilon}|X|^{13/62}\|f\|_2$. The proof relies on a refined local broad estimate that uses density decomposition and the short frequency intervals associated with coarse tubes.

title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
summary: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exac

title: Convex polynomial approximation on the unit ball
summary: Let $\mathbb{B}^d$ be the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge1$. We prove that, for every convex $f\in C(\mathbb{B}^d)$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a polynomial $P_n$ of total degree at most $n$, convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\|f-P_n\|_{C(\mathbb{B}^d)}\le c\,ω_2(f,n^{-1};\mathbb{B}^d)$. Here $ω_2$ is the ordinary second modulus of smoothness and $c=c_d$ depends only on $d$. In particular, we obtain the rate $O(n^{-2})$ for convex functions with uniformly bounded second derivatives.

title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
summary: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.

title: Boundedness properties of bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases
summary: In this paper, we investigate mapping properties on Lebesgue spaces of bilinear Fourier integral operators (FIOs) with complex phases. Indeed, we provide for bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases boundedness theorems for the corresponding Seeger-Sogge-Stein orders, including the endpoint estimates. Our results extend the same boundedness property in the case of real-valued phases proved by Rodriguez-López, Rule, and Staubach, and provide the bilinear version for the linear one proved earlier by Ruzhansky for phases of positive type. Also, our Seeger-Sogge-Stein theorem for bilinear operators with complex phases cannot be directly deduced from its real counterpart. A new approach used in this article consists of providing directly the boundedness theorems on Lebesgue spaces without the use of the multilinear Fefferman-Stein interpolation theorem. For this, a maximal func

title: Discriminants and resultants of orthogonal polynomials
summary: The concept of a linked pair of two sequences of polynomials, one of which is orthogonal, is introduced. Such a pair always has a resultant that factors. Two methods for producing such linked pairs are given: one for general orthogonal polynomials and the other for any polynomial in the Askey scheme. Generalized discriminants are introduced and evaluated, including a general product formula for each operator in the Askey scheme. A new notion of companion orthogonal polynomials is also introduced and used to evaluate the discriminants of orthogonal polynomials. These methods recover all known formulas for the generalized discriminants of classical polynomials and provide new ones.

title: Variational Estimates for the Bilinear Hilbert Transform
summary: We prove that for every $q>2$, the $q$-variation operator associated with the bilinear Hilbert transform is bounded from $L^r(\mathbb R)\times L^s(\mathbb R)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R)$ whenever $1<r,s<\infty$, $p>2/3$, and $1/p=1/r+1/s$.

title: Sharp error estimates for Lagrange interpolation and Kantorovich-type operators in weighted $L_p$-spaces
summary: In this paper, we establish sharp direct and inverse approximation estimates for algebraic Lagrange interpolation polynomials and Kantorovich-type operators in weighted $L_p$ spaces on $[-1,1]$. A well-known limitation in the theory of approximation by interpolation polynomials states that for small rates of convergence $α\le 1/p$, classical moduli of smoothness fail to provide matching direct and inverse estimates due to the insufficiency of integral metrics to determine pointwise values at the interpolation nodes. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce new special semi-discrete measures of smoothness based on Steklov averaging operators, which combine global $L_p$-smoothness with discrete deviations from Steklov averages at the interpolation nodes. By using these measures, we establish fully matching direct and inverse approximation theorems for Lagrange interpolation polynomials, t

title: A study guide for Bourgain's 2003 sum-product theorem and 2010 discretized projection theorem
summary: These notes present Bourgain's proofs of the discretized sum-product theorem and its applications. The discussion emphasizes the construction of trees with multiscale porosity from small additive doubling, using either quantitative Freiman theorrem or the Plünnecke-Ruzsa inequality, and the amplification of these structures by multiplication. Additive combinatorial tools connect the resulting growth estimates to discretized sum-product problem. The notes also discuss the passage to the exceptional set estimates for orthogonal projections, the exclusion of Borel subrings of intermediate Hausdorff dimension, and Fourier decay for multiplicative convolutions of measures.

title: Scale profile, nesting, and the $A_2$ growth of dyadic paraproducts
summary: For the dyadic paraproduct $π_b$ and $Q\ge1$, let $Φ_b(Q)$ be the supremum of $\|π_b\|_{L^2(w)}$ over dyadic weights with $[w]_{A_2^d}\le Q$. Beznosova's linear bound $Φ_b(Q)\lesssim Q\,\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_d}$ is sharp over $\mathrm{BMO}_d$, while every nonzero symbol safisfies $Φ_b(Q)\gtrsim Q^{1/2}$. We ask which properties of a fixed symbol place its growth between these extremes, and identify two: the distribution of the Haar coefficients of $b$ over scales and the nesting of their supports. Symbols supported on $L$ consecutive scales obey a two-weight bound of order $\sqrt L$; as a consequence, polynomial decay of the scale tails determines the sharp trowth exponent, except at a critical rate where the growth is determined up to a factor $(\log Q)^{1/2}$. For symbols supported on a chain, $\sup_Q Q^{-1/2}Φ_b(Q)$ is comarable to $\|S_d b\|_{\infty}$, and for every symbol the boundedn

title: Equilateral-triangle-free sets in finite planes
summary: For a prime $p>3$, let $F(p)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of $\mathbb F_p^2$ containing no equilateral triangle with nonzero squared side length. Alex Iosevich asked for the exact value of $F(p)$. By constructing such subsets of $\mathbb F_p^2$ from cap sets in $\mathbb F_3^n$, we obtain the uniform lower bounds \[ F(p)\gg \begin{cases} p^{2γ}, & p\equiv 11\pmod{12},\\ p^{1+γ}, & p\equiv 1\pmod{12}. \end{cases} \] Here $γ=\log_3(2.2202)$, so the two exponents are $1.452008666\ldots$ and $1.726004333\ldots$, respectively. We also apply a quantitative corners theorem to show that $F(p)=o(p^2)$ as $p\to\infty$ through either congruence class.

title: Capacitary Hardy inequalities, Dirichlet boundary conditions, and the limit as $p\downarrow1$
summary: We use nonlinear Dirichlet resolvents to prove Hardy inequalities with capacity-based and resolvent-based weights for $1<p<\infty$ on arbitrary open sets. On bounded Sobolev extension domains, integrability against either weight characterizes Sobolev functions satisfying homogeneous Dirichlet conditions on arbitrary closed subsets of the boundary. On bounded Lipschitz domains, the resolvent-based weight $\bm{W}_{D,p}$ converges locally in $L^1$ to the negative of Barozzi's interior variational mean curvature as $p\downarrow1$.

title: Totally Positive Interpolation and Critical Sampling of Positive Operator Orbits
summary: How few observations are needed for the stable recovery of the initial state of a linear dynamical system? We study this question for systems governed by a positive operator, with fixed sensors and freely chosen sampling times and positive weights. Our main tool is an interpolation theorem for translates of a nonzero continuous integrable totally positive function. For every uniformly separated sequence of centers, we choose one node near each center so that the corresponding collocation operator is boundedly invertible. The displacement, node separation, and operator bounds depend only on the kernel and the lower separation of the centers; no upper bound is needed on their gaps. If a single integer orbit is a frame, we construct weighted Riesz bases whose sampling counts attain the spectral lower bound up to a bounded additive error. The same method yields bases from continuous function

title: Fractional integration with singularity on the light-cone
summary: In this paper, we solve a classical problem investigated by Gelfand and Shilov on a family of fractional integral operators whose kernels have singularity appeared on the light-cone in R^n+1. As an implication, we obtain a desired sharp estimate for the L^p to L^q-boundedness of cone multiplier operators having a negative order.

title: Exact multiplicity for a Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem with a step weight
summary: The DEG1 challenge asks whether positive solutions of a super-exponential Minkowski-curvature equation are unique for step weights with a single sign change and negative mean. In this paper, we give a Neumann counterexample by studying $\left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + λa_{μ,h}(t)(e^{u^2}-1)=0$ with $u'(0)=u'(2h)=0$, where $a_{μ,h}=1$ on $(0,h)$ and $a_{μ,h}=-μ$ on $(h,2h)$, with $μ>1$. Using the shooting method, we prove that the positive solution curve has exactly two nondegenerate folds for $(λ,h)$ in a nonempty open region. As $μ$ increases through the corresponding critical values, the number of positive solutions is successively $1$, $2$, $3$, $2$, and $1$.

title: The Erdős similarity problem for polynomials and analytic maps
summary: In this paper, we study the Erdős similarity problem by replacing affine copies with images of polynomial maps or analytic maps. This is inspired by a connection between a partial converse of Szemerédi's theorem and the Erdős similarity problem and its variants, as well as a version of polynomial Szemerédi's theorem by Bergelson and Leibman. In particular, we strengthen several known results in the literature. We show that a large class of sequence are not polynomially universal in this sense. First, for sequences satisfying suitable gap hypotheses, an explicit Cantor-type witness is constructed. Second, for sets satisfying certain growth conditions, a random Cantor-type witness is constructed, extending work of Kolountzakis. This also extends certain results in recent work of Cuéllar-Iosevich-Kulkarni-Aravena-Yavicoli to the polynomial setting. Finally, we show for arbitrary sequences $

title: The Fourier Ratio on Resistance Spaces and Applications to Electrical Networks
summary: We study the Fourier Ratio for spectral expansions of nonnegative self-adjoint operators. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz estimates turn eigenvalue counting bounds into Fourier Ratio bounds for spectrally regular functions. On a compact measured resistance space, Kasue's identity expresses the reciprocal eigenvalue sum as one half of the average resistance distance. We use this identity to obtain a sharp coefficient estimate for every finite-energy function, with no spectral cutoff. Bounded orthonormal system recovery theorems then yield reconstruction estimates whose sample counts depend on both the Fourier Ratio and the pointwise size of the chosen eigenfunctions. We distinguish these estimates from the weaker diameter-only bounds and give an interval example with a sample count logarithmic in the dimension of the spectral subspace for fixed accuracy and energy ratio. Resistance also controls

title: A logarithmic saving in the sum-free subset problem
summary: For every sufficiently large $n$ there is a set of $n$ positive integers, all at most $n^2$, whose largest sum-free subset has size at most $n/3+O(n/\log n)$. We bound the number of small divisible elements in a dense set with few Schur triples. A fixed-accuracy cyclic model gives a rotation, and the original integer triple count controls its density at the required scale.

title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
summary: Let $Γ$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(Γ)$ is edge-transitive, then $Γ$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(Γ)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.

title: Major progress on hamiltonian saturation in hypergraphs
summary: For $1\leq \ell< k$, an \emph{$\ell$-overlapping $k$-cycle} is a $k$-uniform hypergraph in which, for some cyclic vertex ordering, every edge consists of $k$ consecutive vertices and every two consecutive edges share exactly $\ell$ vertices. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is $\ell$-\emph{hamiltonian saturated} if $H$ does not contain an $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton $k$-cycle but every hypergraph obtained from $H$ by adding a new edge does contain such a cycle. For $n$ divisible by $k-\ell$, let sat$(n,k,\ell)$ be the smallest number of edges in an $\ell$-hamiltonian saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. In the case of graphs Clark and Entringer showed in 1983 that, for sufficiently large $n$, sat$(n,2,1)=\lceil \frac{3n}2\rceil$. By ad hoc methods, the present authors proved previously that sat$(n,k,\ell)=Θ(n^{\ell})$ for some rather narrow and scattered ranges of $\ell$. In thi

title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
summary: There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$ when $μ$ is obtained from $λ$ by adding one to a part of $λ$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $λ$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms. We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^λ$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^λ$ to $\mathcal{S}^{λ'}$.

title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
summary: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
summary: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(λ)$, where $L(λ)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(λ)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(λ)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we

title: Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$
summary: We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family. We give an elementary proof that this family has differential uniformity at most $3$ for primes $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and prove that the bound is attained for $p>1444$.

title: Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm
summary: We study Cop-Win Edge Completion: given a graph $G$, find the minimum number $\copfill(G)$ of edges whose addition lets one cop capture a visible robber. We first give an exact reduction from Dominating Set, constructing for every nonempty graph $H$ a graph $G_H$ on $2|V(H)|+2$ vertices with $\copfill(G_H)=γ(H)$. This resolves a complexity question of Mertzios et al. and implies NP-completeness even for connected graphs of diameter two with a dominating edge and domination number two. Interestingly, while Minimum Fill-in is fixed-parameter tractable in the number $k$ of added edges, Cop-Win Edge Completion, whose target class strictly contains the connected chordal graphs, is W[2]-hard parameterized by $k$, even by $k+γ(G)$. We then give two lower bounds. The first, $\copfill(G)\ge 2n-m-b-c-1$, where $n,m,b,c$ count vertices, edges, nontrivial blocks, and components, is tight for partial

title: Standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart rings have unimodal $h$-vectors
summary: We prove that the $h$-vector $(h_0,\ldots,h_s)$ of every standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart ring is unimodal, with a peak at position $\lceil s/2\rceil$. More generally, a standard graded Ehrhart ring has an alternatingly increasing $h$-vector if the radical of the ideal generated by the degree-one part of its canonical trace ideal contains the homogeneous maximal ideal. In characteristic zero or two, the generic Artinian reduction of each such ring has the strong Lefschetz property. We also prove unimodality for every standard graded nearly Gorenstein domain of dimension at least two with $h$-vector $(1,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, where $s\geq2$, provided that $h_1-h_s\leq1$. In the level case this $h$-vector is both concave and alternatingly increasing. If $h_1=h_s$, then $h_1=\cdots=h_s$.

title: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
summary: We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.

title: A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint
summary: We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.

title: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
summary: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.

title: Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game
summary: Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$. For $\{3,6,17\}$ we determine both least periods and preperiods for every positive $c$ and verify the complete table in Lean. Fixed bases with the same entire Grundy sequence realize infinitely many distinct positive quadratic coefficients for the augmented period. A second fixed triple gives a quadratic Grundy preperiod while the win/loss sequence repeats from heap zero. A third has a quadratic Grundy period but only a linear win/loss period. For an arbitrary fixed $S$, a linear bound on both Grundy invariants implies eventual a

title: Roman-Type Domination on Bisplit Graphs: Hardness and Inapproximability
summary: Inspired by the structure and name of split graphs, bisplit graphs have three independent sets $I,A,B$, where every vertex of $A$ is adjacent to every vertex of $B$, and vertices of $I$ may have arbitrary neighborhoods in the core $A\cup B$. Thus they have a complete bipartite core together with the remaining vertices, making them a structured setting in which to study how core size affects complexity. Mann and Fernau's construction already implies NP-completeness of perfect Roman domination on bisplit graphs with a singleton core side \citep[Theorem~20]{mann-fernau-pr}. Motivated by this result, we study all four Roman-type domination problems across further core-size regimes: we prove NP-completeness when one core side has size one or two, and when both sides have size at least three. For perfect Italian domination, even deciding whether prescribed core labels of total weight two can b

title: Gaudin's determinantal norm formula and Hall--Littlewood polynomials
summary: The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

title: The number of non-isomorphic spanning trees in regular graphs
summary: By a classical theorem of Otter, the number of non-isomorphic trees on $n$ vertices is $α^n\exp(-o(n))$, where $α\approx 2.956$ is Otter's constant. We prove that every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains $α^n\exp(-o_d(n))$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, where $o_d(n)/n\to0$ as $d\to\infty$.

title: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
summary: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits.
