title: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
summary: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independent

title: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
summary: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to

title: On the Geometry of Quadratic Maps
summary: To analyse a homogeneous quadratic map $Q:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ of its restriction to the unit sphere is very useful but difficult to handle. We prove its dual hypersurface $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is of degree $k$ (providing its equation) and is $\mathit{hyperbolic}$: every line though the origin in $\mathbb{R}^\ell$ cuts it at $k$ real points, counting multiplicities. These facts imply: $\boldsymbol{1}$. $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is the union of $k/2$ nested topological hyperspheres if $k$ is even, or the union of $(k-1)/2$ nested topological hyperspheres and one topological projective hyperplane if $k$ is odd. $\boldsymbol{2}$. The Toeplitz-Haussdorf Theorem on the range of of the restriction of $Q$ to the unit sphere if $k>\ell$. $\boldsymbol{3}$. The dual version of the hyperbolicity of $\mathcal{F}_{Q}$ is: the critical value variety $Σ_{Q}$ is of cla

title: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
summary: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $λ> 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $λ> 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

title: Joint statistics on vexillary involutions via Fulton's essential set
summary: We jointly enumerate various statistics over vexillary involutions among which there are the number of descents and the number of peaks. As a by-product, we get an equidistribution result between vexillary involutions and 3412-avoiding involutions, which, notably, implies that, for every $n$ and $k$, the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $3412$ and having $k$ descents equals the number of involutions of length $n$ avoiding $2143$ and having $k$ ascents. The proof describes $2143$-avoiding involutions through Fulton's ranked essential set, translates the count into a weighted enumeration of walks in the quarter plane, and solves the latter explicitly. Finally, we show that arbitrary vexillary permutations are encoded by excursions of the same walk model.

title: Via a New LP Relaxation: Stronger Performance Guarantees for WSEPT, and an LP-Based Proof of Kawaguchi & Kyan
summary: We present a new linear programming relaxation for minimizing the total weighted completion time on identical parallel machines. Its right-hand side is supermodular, so the relaxation can be solved by a greedy algorithm. We show that the WSPT rule is within a factor $\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{2})$ of the optimal LP value. This bounds the integrality gap of the relaxation and gives a short, LP-based proof of the tight bound of Kawaguchi and Kyan on the performance of WSPT. We then turn to the stochastic version of the problem, in which processing times are independent random variables whose squared coefficients of variation are at most~$Δ$. A variance-corrected version of the new LP relaxation is valid for all non-anticipatory policies, and we show that WSEPT is within a factor $1 + (1 + Δ)/(3 + \sqrt{7 + 2 Δ})$ of it for $Δ\ge 1$, for any number of machines. This is $O(\sqrtΔ)$, whereas all

title: Partition rank and analytic rank over finite field
summary: We prove that the partition rank and the analytic rank of a tensor over any finite field are equivalent up to a constant depending only on the order of the tensor. The proof combines Milićević's theorem on dense multilinear varieties with the differential Schur complement of Moshkovitz and Zhu. The new ingredient is a method for approximately eliminating multilinear equations.

title: A variant of the Erdős--Gyárfás problem for $K_9$ and $K_{12}$
summary: For a graph $H$, let $r_H(n)$ be the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of $K_n$ such that every copy of $H$ contains a color appearing an odd number of times. We prove that $r_{K_9}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ and $r_{K_{12}}(n)\le\exp(O((\log n)^{2/3}))$. These bounds on $r_H(n)$ yield linear graph codes of density at least $\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$ that avoid images of $K_9$ and $K_{12}$.

title: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
summary: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

title: The Hamilton cycle space in the Erdős--Rényi random graph process
summary: Let $G(n,m)$ denote the graph at step $m$ of the Erdős--Rényi random graph process on $n$ vertices. The process starts with the edgeless graph and adds one edge at each step, chosen uniformly at random from the missing edges. Let $τ_3$ be the first step at which the minimum degree of $G(n,m)$ reaches three. We answer a question of Christoph, Nenadov and Petrova [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 176 (2026) 254--267] by proving that, as $n$ tends to infinity through odd integers, with high probability the Hamilton cycles of $G(n,m)$ span its cycle space over $\Ftwo$ simultaneously for all $m\geτ_3$. On the same event, $G(n,m)$ is Hamilton-connected for every $m\geτ_3$.

title: On \(q\)-ary Minimal Linear Codes from Hierarchical Posets
summary: In this paper, we study several families of \(q\)-ary linear codes constructed from two-level hierarchical posets over finite fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q>2\). By using generating functions and additive characters, we determine their complete weight distributions, dimensions, and minimum distances. This paper focuses on constructing minimal codes that violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition. By analyzing the weight distributions and support sets of the codewords, we show that a large class of the constructed codes are minimal and strictly violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

title: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
summary: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $γ(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstraëte conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $γ(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstraëte's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.

title: Algorithms and topological invariants for dynamic systems. IV. Topological Equivalence of Functions and Hamiltonian Dynamical Systems
summary: This is the fourth part of a series on algorithms and topological invariants for dynamical systems. We study the topological equivalence of smooth functions and of Hamiltonian flows on surfaces, and the discrete invariants, Reeb graphs and cell decompositions, that classify them. We recall the notions of topological equivalence and structural stability, introduce two equivalences of functions (with and without the order of the critical values) and show that simple Morse functions on closed orientable surfaces are classified by their Reeb graphs with vertex odering, while simple Hamiltonian flows are classified by Reeb graphs with marked edges. For the disc and for the sphere we obtain a recursive description and a generating function for the numbers of such trees, and compute the numbers of topologically non-equivalent simple Morse functions and Hamiltonian flows with a given number of s

title: Ternary Perfect $2$-Burst-Correcting Codes
summary: A construction for a ternary perfect linear $2$-burst-correcting code is presented for every redundancy $r \geq 5$. The construction is recursive with seeds given for $5 \leq r \leq 7$. The construction of redundancy $r \geq 8$ is derived from a code of redundancy $r-3$ and it distinguishes between codes of even and odd length.

title: Consecutive sums and Reconstructing Problems
summary: We study several problems concerning consecutive sums of integer sequences and their relationship with Sidon sets. We also provide new lower bounds for an extremal function related to sequences with distinct consecutive sums, and consider reconstruction problems from multisets of consecutive sums.

title: Quantum walks and conformal mappings
summary: We study the most elementary discrete model of an electron moving along a line, known as Feynman checkers, quantum walk, or the six-vertex model with special complex weights, and provide a uniform asymptotic formula for the wave function in the whole xt-plane. In addition to the well-known appearance of the Airy function that describes the transition between the oscillating and exponentially decaying regimes, we observe a second transition governed by the gamma function when the electron speed approaches the speed of light. We prove two general theorems producing uniform asymptotic formulae involving the Airy and gamma functions, using conformal mappings associated with the underlying integral representations. They are applicable in several other situations as well.

title: Dimension-uniform Connectivity Laws and Hitting Times for Spherical Random Geometric Graphs
summary: Let $G_d(n,p)$ be the graph formed by joining pairs of $n$ independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ within a radius chosen to give edge probability $p$. For each fixed integer $K\ge0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, we prove that at $np=\log n+K\log\log n+t$, the probabilities of $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity both converge to $\exp(-e^{-t}/K!)$ uniformly over all $d=d(n)\ge3$. This is the same limit as in the Erdős--Rényi graph. Moreover, as the radius increases on a single sample, the first radii for minimum degree at least $K+1$, $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity, and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity coincide with probability tending to one uniformly over $d\ge3$. To our knowledge, this is the first critical-window law for connectivity in a random geometric graph that holds uniformly from fixed dimensions to dimensions growing arbitrarily with $n$.

title: The limit shape of uniform random antichains in $[0,1]^d$
summary: For each $d\ge2$, we study $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, conditioned to form an antichain: no point is strictly smaller than another in every coordinate. We prove that the point cloud converges in Hausdorff distance to the closure of the hypersurface \[\mathcal S_d=\left\{\mathbf x\in(0,1)^d: \sum_{i=1}^dΦ^{-1}(\mathbf x_i)=0\right\}\] in probability as $n\to\infty$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The proof also shows that the antichain probability $a_n$ satisfies $\log a_n=-\frac{n}{d-1}\log n+β_d n+o(n)$ for a finite constant $β_d$. We identify the limiting empirical distribution and hence the limiting permuton of uniform random $d$-dimensional permutations avoiding a single pattern of size $2$.
comment: 31 pages, 2 figures. Accompanying Lean formalization available at https://github.com/MinjaePark-Math/antichain-lean

title: Bounds for the small Davenport constant of extraspecial groups of exponent three
summary: Let $E_s$ be the extraspecial group of order $3^{2s+1}$ and exponent three. We prove $4s+2r+2\le d(E_s\times C_3^r)\le 4s+2r+3$ for $s\ge1$ and $r\ge0$. For $s\ge2$, the degree in the polynomial proof is optimal among weights depending only on group-element multiplicities modulo three. For $s=2$, we reduce the question in all ranks to an abelian subset-sum problem with a fixed set of forbidden values in a $77$-dimensional space. We show that this set, together with zero, contains no $76$-dimensional subspace. The equality $d(E_2\times C_3^r)=2r+10$ in all ranks is not established here.
comment: 7 pages. Verification code included as an ancillary file

title: Alpha-points of a putative binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
summary: A point $P$ of a putative $q$-analog $\mathcal{D}$ of the Fano plane is an $α$-point if the derived design of $\mathcal{D}$ in $P$ is a Desarguesian line spread. Kiermaier showed that for $q$ prime or even every hyperplane contains a point which is not an $α$-point. For $q=2$ we study the $45$ blocks of $\mathcal{D}$ inside a hyperplane $H$. Call a $5$-subspace of $H$ a $β$-flat if all its blocks pass through one point, its focal point. We show that at least $41$ points of $H$ are not focal points of $β$-flats. Consequently $\mathcal{D}$ has at least $85$ non-$α$-points, at most $42$ $α$-points, and at most $22$ $α$-points in every hyperplane.

title: Depth of leaves in closed linear $λ$-terms: exact recurrence, limit law and edge window
summary: Let $K_n$ (resp.\ $D_n$) be the depth of a uniform leaf (resp.\ node) in a uniform closed linear $λ$-term of size $n$. A bijective \emph{grafting identity} yields an exact polynomial-time recurrence for the full depth profile. By the method of moments, $K_n/n$ converges in law to the density $3x/\sqrt{1-2x}$ on $[0,\frac12]$, i.e.\ $2K_n/n\to\Beta(2,\frac12)$, with $\mathbb E[K_n^r]/n^r\to3(r+1)!/(2r+3)!!$; likewise $1-2D_n/n\to\Beta(\frac12,1)$. A backward Markov chain gives the corresponding local limits for $k\le(\frac12-\varepsilon)n$. The limit density diverges at $\frac12$, and the profile has a second scale: a window of width $\sqrt n$ around $n/2$, which carries a fraction of order $n^{-1/4}$ of the nodes, at a density $n^{1/4}$ times larger than in the bulk. We prove that a single explicit function describes both regimes: uniformly in $d$, \[ n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(D_n=d)=g\Bigl(\tf

title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
summary: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem, we obtain \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)>2^{Ω_k(n\log n)}\). Combined with the upper bound due to Mubayi and Suk, this yields \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)=2^{Θ_k(n\log n)}\), where \(B^{(k)}\) is the half-graph. This answers in

title: A construction of proper Jordan schemes of rank $5$
summary: Let $q$ be a prime power such that $m=q^2+q+1$ is a prime satisfying $m\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. We construct a proper symmetric Jordan scheme of rank $5$ on $2m$ vertices using a Singer difference set with parameters $(m,q+1,1)$ and the Paley graph on $m$ vertices.

title: Products of translates: bounds and constructions
summary: We study products of translates of the form $(A+d)(A+d)$ with $d\in D$, where both $A$ and $D$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that $|(A+a)(A+a)|\ge C|A|^{5/3}$ for some $a\in A$, and that $|(A+D)(A+D)|\le |A|^{2-c(α)}$ for some $c(α)>0$ when $|D|=|A|^α$ with $α<1$.

title: Compatible expansions and rigidity in subtraction games with a single pass
summary: We study normal-play subtraction games with one globally shared pass. An expansion of the subtraction set is pass-equivalent if it leaves the pass-available Sprague--Grundy sequence unchanged. We show that pure periodicity of the ordinary sequence, together with an eventual translation identity for the pass-available sequence, forces every pass-equivalent expansion to preserve the ordinary sequence. For two-element sets $\{x,y\}$, we classify the compatible additional moves: they are exactly $x+1,\ldots,y-1$ when $y\leq 2x$, and there are none when $y>2x$. We extend this result to sets in short intervals. An exact recurrence certificate also exhibits a three-element set for which pass-state rigidity fails.

title: Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
summary: Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection

title: A Constructive Lower Bound for the Growth Constant of Ternary Cap Sets
summary: Let $r_3(d)$ denote the maximum size of a cap set in $\mathbb{F}_3^d$. We prove that the exponential growth constant $Λ= \lim_{d\to\infty} r_3(d)^{1/d}$ is strictly greater than $2.22920646813$. The main advance comes from combining two-color recursive synchronization with cross-layer joint filling of a seven-dimensional local alphabet that contains collinear triples (lines). By encoding marked positions as $14$-step closed walks on a two-state directed graph, any zero-sum triple with a fixed outermost color is forced to choose the identical closed walk---and hence the identical record---at every recursive layer, at a net cost of $1000$ dimensions per level. Because the open seven-dimensional coordinates are deferred to the outermost layer, all positions of the same type across all layers can be pooled per record and filled jointly via grouped binary-flag nodes. title: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
summary: This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(ρ,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $ρ\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture. First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $ρ=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets. This mirrors the phenomenon observed by Alrabiah

title: An Exact Vertex Localization of Zykov's Theorem
summary: We establish a vertex-based localization of the exact form of Zykov's theorem. For a graph $G$ of order $n\geq1$, let $N(G,K_t)$ denote its number of copies of $K_t$, and let $c(v)$ be the order of a largest clique containing $v$. Write $Z_t(n,s)=N(T_s(n),K_t)$, where $T_s(n)$ is the balanced complete $s$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every integer $t\geq2$, \[ N(G,K_t)\leq \frac1n\sum_{v\in V(G)}Z_t(n,c(v)). \] Equality holds if and only if $G$ is $K_t$-free or $G\cong T_s(n)$ for some $t\leq s\leq n$. Moreover, the coefficients $Z_t(n,s)$ are pointwise best possible among all bounds of this form. Our result strengthens the previous vertex-localized bound \[ N(G,K_t)\leq n^{t-1} \sum_{v\in V(G)} \frac{\binom{c(v)}{t}}{c(v)^t} \] by accounting for the integer part sizes of Turán graphs. The comparison between the two upper bounds is strict precisely when some vertex $

title: A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
summary: In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case. The first two main results are a cyclic analogue of the Maesaka--Seki--Watanabe formula for truncated sums and an {integral--series identity} under an admissibility condition. As an application, we give a proof of $4^nζ(\{1,3\}^n)=ζ(\{4\}^n)$ by counting linear extensions of a poset. The third main result expresses a cyclic Schur multiple harmonic sum as a finite signed sum of Schur multiple harmonic sums with the same number of boxes and the same multiset of exponents.

title: Local Limits and Structures of Nearest-Predecessor Random Graphs
summary: We study the two-sided nearest-predecessor graph on $[n]$, where vertices arrive in a uniformly random order and each new vertex connects to its nearest earlier vertex on each side. We construct an infinite graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ from i.i.d. continuous insertion times and prove quenched Benjamini--Schramm convergence to it almost surely. The limit is almost surely one-ended and recurrent. We resolve an open problem of Ponomarenko by proving that the maximum degree is asymptotic in probability to $\log n/\log(3/2)$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain the probability generating function and a CLT for the number of edges crossing the boundary of $[n]$ in the infinite limit. We also study the $K$-nearest-predecessor graph, in which each new vertex attaches to its $K$ nearest earlier vertices without regard to side. For every fixed $K\geq1$, we construct the infinite limit, prove almost sure quenched B

title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
summary: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammo

title: Cylindrical dimers and monomial immanants
summary: For a bipartite graph on a cylinder, group its perfect matchings by homological height and sum their weights in each group. We prove that every minor of the resulting Toeplitz matrix has nonnegative coefficients in the edge weights, settling a question recorded by Lai. We first prove conjectures of Galashin and the author concerning directed cycles in cylindrical networks, and then deduce the dimer theorem from them. A related, stronger positivity property for superpositions of cylindrical matchings turns out to be equivalent to Stembridge's interval-product conjecture on monomial immanants. Using annular webs, we prove this conjecture for partitions with at most four columns. A stretching argument extends this to all partitions with parts in $\{n,2n,3n,4n\}$.

title: Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
summary: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones. For nine types it has dimension one, two or three, because non-negativity forces some wedge angles

title: General bounds for metric dimension of diameter-two graphs with applications
summary: We study the metric dimension of several classes of graphs with diameter two. First, we establish a general lower bound for the metric dimension of graphs with diameter two in terms of their order and maximum degree. We then apply our results to Grassmann graphs, Moore graphs, and bilinear forms graphs. For Kneser graphs, we obtain new upper bounds, while for $G_q(n,2)$ Grassmann graphs we establish new upper bounds provided by constructions of resolving sets. For Moore graphs of diameter two, we derive improved lower bounds, and for $H_q(n,2)$ bilinear forms graphs, we obtain new upper and lower bounds on their metric dimension.

title: Parity-safe digraphs with countably many ends are kernel-perfect
summary: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set that every other vertex points into, and a digraph is kernel-perfect if every induced subgraph has a kernel. A digraph without odd cycles in which no ray contains infinitely many vertices that each send an infinite fan of disjoint paths to that ray is safe. The conjecture that every safe digraph is kernel-perfect was proved earlier for digraphs with finitely many ends. We prove a stronger statement for at most countably many ends. Number the vertices of a ray, and let the type of a path that ends on the ray be the parity of the sum of its length and the number of its last vertex. A fan is mixed if it has infinitely many paths of each type, and a digraph is parity-safe if it has no odd cycle and no ray containing infinitely many vertices with a mixed fan to it. title: Commutative bishuffle algebras and Pattern Avoidance
summary: This paper introduces the notion of a commutative bishuffle algebra, that linearizes classical pattern avoidance. The free commutative bishuffle algebra on one generator has a basis of permutations, divisibility of monomials is pattern containment, and the classes of permutations avoiding given patterns are the monomial bases of its quotients by monomial ideals. This free algebra is not Noetherian, but we show that its quotient by the antisymmetrizer $e_k$ is Noetherian for every $k$, and we conjecture that the same holds for its quotient by any nonzero ideal stable under the symmetric groups, in analogy with the Specht problem. We develop Gröbner bases for ideals of the free algebra and prove that the elements $e_k\oplusτ$, with $τ$ ranging over any set of permutations, form a Gröbner basis for the lexicographic ordering and for its opposite. This gives an algebraic form of the theorem

title: The probability that two random generalized derangements have the same number of cycles
summary: Using singularity analysis, we show that the probability that two independently and uniformly selected generalized derangements of size $n$ have the same number of cycles is asymptotically the same as the corresponding probability for unrestricted permutations, namely, $\sim \frac{1}{2\sqrt{π\log n}}\;.$

title: Counting Eulerian Orientations in Regular Graphs
summary: Let $G$ be a pseudograph, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote the number of Eulerian orientations of $G$. Lieb and Wu, and later Schrijver, showed that if $G$ has degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, where each $d_i$ is a positive even integer, then \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \prod_{i = 1}^n 2^{-d_i/2} \binom{d_i}{d_i/2}.\] Schrijver conjectured that for simple $d$-regular graphs, $\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(K_{d+1})^{n/(d+1)}$, with equality attained by disjoint unions of cliques of order $d+1$. In this paper, we prove a multigraph bound that implies the known case $d=4$, and we also improve Schrijver's lower bound for $d$-regular graphs, using an inductive relation between $\varepsilon(G)$ and the number $\ell_i(G)$ of cycles of each possible length $i \geq 1$ in $G$. We define \[ \ell(G) = \sum_{i = 1}^n \frac{\ell_i(G)}{(d - 1)^i}\] and we prove with $λ= (d - 1)\log(1 + 1/(d - 1))$ that

title: Unary maps are restrictions of linear maps and $k$-ary maps are restrictions of homogeneous maps
summary: We study maps on a finite set $S$ under renaming elements of $S$ and extending $S$. We show that every unary map is linear and every $k$-ary map is homogeneous with respect to such renamings and embeddings.

title: Distinct Distances under Well-behaved Norms
summary: We improve our understanding of the Erdos' distinct distances problem under non-Euclidean norms, in two ways: (i) For norms that are definable in an o-minimal structure and whose non-line bisectors have a finite intersection, we obtain a lower bound of \(Ω(n^{5/6})\) for the minimum number of distinct distances. In particular, this improves the current best bound of \(Ω(n^{4/5})\) for all \(\ell_{p}\) norms with non-integer \(p > 1\). (ii) We derive the stronger bound \(Ω(n^{6/7-ε})\) under all semi-algebraic smooth norms. Our proof technique is based on deriving properties of bisectors under various norms.

title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
summary: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct. The proof translates universal inclusion into a spanning-embedding question for coprimality graphs on consecutive integer intervals. Edge-count identities, arithmetic-progression estimates, and prime-residue switching exclude all other inclusions; a prime-gap argument reduces the remaining finite range to fifteen explicit rational inequalities. We further show that, for each nonexceptional ordered pair, the graph orders at which edge counts obstruct inclusion have a positive natural density. This density is de

title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
summary: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.

title: The Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity
summary: In their 2007 paper on the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences, Liu and Wang conjectured that the Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity. We completely solve their conjecture by showing that this transformation preserves strong $q$-log-convexity. More generally, we provide a sufficient condition for a linear transformation, defined by a triangular array satisfying a certain three-term recurrence relation, to preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. As applications, we show that both the $r$-colored Eulerian transformation and the $m$-Stirling Eulerian transformation preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. In particular, we confirm a conjecture due to Liu and Zhu, which states that the Eulerian transformation of type $B$ preserves log-convexity.

title: The maximum number of edges in minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs
summary: A connected graph of order at least $2k+2$ is {\em $k$-extendable} if it has a matching of size $k$ and every such matching extends to a perfect matching. In particular, a 1-extendable graph is also called a {\em matching covered graph}. A $k$-extendable graph $G$ is {\em minimal} if $G-e$ is not $k$-extendable for every $e\in E(G)$. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 23 (1977), 127--138] proved that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge6$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(3|V(G)|-6)/2$, and this bound is sharp for every even order at least 6. Fabres, Kothari and Carvalho [J. Graph Theory 96 (2021), 490--509] proved that every minimal 2-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge12$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(5|V(G)|-20)/2$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (2026), 559--606] characterized minimal matching covered bipartite graphs $G$ with $|E

title: An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
summary: Thomassé conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.

title: On the 0-Rotatability of Regular Spider Trees of Leg Length 4
summary: A tree $T$ on $q$ edges is said to be $0$-rotatable if for every vertex $v \in V(T)$, there exists a graceful labeling $f : V(T) \to \{0, 1, \dots, q\}$ such that $f(v) = 0$. Rofa proved that all regular (symmetric) spider trees with leg length at most $3$ are $0$-rotatable and conjectured that the property holds for every leg length. In this note, we settle the first open case of this conjecture by proving that every regular spider tree $T(k, 4)$ with $k \ge 1$ legs of length $4$ is $0$-rotatable. Our proof combines Rofa's algebraic graceful labeling at the root with complementary labelings, an end-to-end leg-reversal construction placing $0$ at a leaf, and a two-leg reflection permutation placing $0$ at distance $2$ from the root.

title: Reconstruction and geometry of $4\times4$ quantum Sudoku
summary: We study the reconstruction and geometry of $4 \times 4$ quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality. Using a matrix representation, we parametrise the equivalence classes by five closed squares, with the sides of one square identified with the diagonals of the other four. The quotient by classical cell symmetries is a closed disc containing exactly two classical classes. Finally, measurement in the basis of the first block gives a fractional Sudoku that

title: The mean orders of even and odd permutations
summary: We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree. Following Goh and Schmutz, we determine the logarithm of this sum over the group order asymptotically, with an explicit constant. Hence the ratio of the sums of element orders of the symmetric and alternating groups tends to two from above. The proof rests on an exact identity for generating functions. It isolates cycles of length a large prime times a small factor. Inclusion and exclusion over small odd primes enlarges this family. Each Euler factor is bounded by its maximum modulus. All constants are certified in ball arithmetic. Exact values up to degree 150 suggest that the odd permutations have the l

title: Extremal adjacency and distance spectral radii of graph powers
summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $G^k$ denote its $k$-th power. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, \[ ρ(G^k)\geq ρ(P_n^k) \qquad\text{and}\qquad ρ_D(G^k)\leq ρ_D(P_n^k), \] where $P_n$ is the path of order $n$, and $ρ$ and $ρ_D$ are the adjacency and distance spectral radii, respectively. If $n\geq k+2$, equality in either inequality holds precisely when $G\cong P_n$. If $n\leq k+1$, every connected graph of order $n$ has complete $k$-th power, and both inequalities are equalities. The adjacency bound is proved by transferring a terminal vertex between pendant paths and applying a reflection rearrangement to a Rayleigh quotient. For the distance bound, a transfer of an entire pendant path is required; a Schur-complement comparison and estimates for the antisymmetric subspace of a path-power distance matrix yield the result. We also give examples showing why the

title: A new upper bound for the Erdős--Szekeres conjecture
summary: Let $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that every set of $\mathrm{ES}(n)$ points in the plane in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. In 1935, Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that $\mathrm{ES}(n)=2^{n-2}+1$, and in 1960, they established the corresponding lower bound. A breakthrough on the upper bound was achieved by Suk in 2017, who proved that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{2/3}\log n)}. \] In this article, we further improve the upper bound by showing that \[ \mathrm{ES}(n)\leqslant2^{n+O(n^{1/3})}. \]

title: Odd Chromatic Number of Graph Classes: Bounds and Structural Results
summary: A proper coloring of a graph $G$ is called an \emph{odd coloring} if, for every non-isolated vertex $v\in V(G)$, there exists a color that occurs an odd number of times in the open neighborhood of $v$. For a graph $G$, the minimum number of colors required for such a coloring is called the {\em odd chromatic number}, denoted by $χ_{o}(G)$. The odd chromatic number has been well-studied from both combinatorial and algorithmic perspectives, and several bounds on $χ_o(G)$ are known. In this paper, we establish tight bounds on $χ_o(G)$ for several graph classes. In particular, we obtain the following results: 1. For every block-cactus graph $G$, we prove that $χ_o(G) \leq \max \{5,ω(G)+1\}$, where $ω(G)$ denotes the clique number of $G$. 2. For block graphs and proper interval graphs, we establish the bounds $ω(G) \leq χ_o(G) \leq ω(G)+1$. 3. For a bipartite circle graph, we prove that $χ_o(

title: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$ through $59$
summary: It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A. There exist at least $25$, $2$, $3$, $7$ and $12$ nonisomorphic optimal unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$, $55$, $57$, $58$ and $59$, respectively.

title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8ψ_8$ series
summary: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8ψ_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.

title: Quaternary games with infinite misère quotients
summary: We study the four wild quaternary games left open by the earlier work of Plambeck and Siegel. For \texttt{0.3102} we discover a special regularity of its two--heap case, give a complete solution of the two--heap case, and deduce from it that its misère quotient is infinite. For \texttt{0.3122} and \texttt{0.3123} we rigorously prove, by slice--wise algebraic periodicity and hierarchical induction (computer--assisted), that their misère quotients are infinite. For \texttt{0.3312}, as well as many other wild quaternary games, we carry out computations and observations.

title: Bruhat Shellings of the Quasisymmetric Flag Moment Complex
summary: The quasisymmetric flag variety gives rise to a regular cell complex whose maximal cells are cubes indexed by fully supported noncrossing partitions. Two maximal cubes can meet along several faces. We describe each cube using the block arcs and parent connectors of its indexing partition, and determine its intersection with the union of the preceding cubes in Bruhat order. For each nonempty face, we determine the first maximal cube containing it by applying an outer-block merging operation to its Bruhat-maximal noncrossing-partition label. The first-carrier theorem provides an explicit description of how each cube attaches to the preceding subcomplex. More precisely, the intersection is a union of coordinate facets which, for every cube except the first, forms the closed star of a face in its boundary. Consequently, every linear extension of Bruhat order on the maximal-cell labels gives

title: Improved Lower Bound on the Hadwiger-Debrunner Numbers
summary: The celebrated $(p,q)$-theorem of Alon and Kleitman asserts that for any $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and any $p \geq q \geq d+1$, every family of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which among any $p$ sets, some $q$ intersect, can be pierced by $c(p,q,d)$ points. The minimum numbers $c(p,q,d)$ are called the Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers and denoted $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q)$ and determining them is a longstanding open problem. We prove that for any $d \geq 2$, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,d+1) \geq p^{d-o(1)}$, and more generally, $\mathrm{HD}_d(p,q) \geq p^{\frac{q-1}{q-d}-o(1)}$. Our bound is obtained by a family of parallelotopes, and is tight up to polylogarithmic factors among all families that have a bounded VC dimension. The proof uses the hypergraph container method.

title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
summary: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.

title: Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis
summary: Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunkštis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compr

title: Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points
summary: In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.

title: Nontrivial Expanding Kähler--Ricci Solitons and Automorphism Groups of Stein Domains
summary: We study complete nontrivial expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete real holomorphic soliton fields. Let $Ω$ be a relatively compact domain in a complex surface such that a neighborhood of $\overlineΩ$ admits a holomorphic immersion into Euclidean space. We prove that such a soliton exists if and only if $Ω$ is Stein and the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$ is noncompact. On such a Stein domain, a complete real holomorphic vector field is the soliton field of a complete nontrivial expander if and only if its flow has noncompact closure in $\operatorname{Aut}(Ω)$. In higher dimensions, we establish existence criteria using the adjoint representation of automorphism groups, boundary geometry, and homogeneous positive closed $(1,1)$-currents. We give sufficient conditions for the holomorphic $\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$-action on the universal globalization of a proper holomorphi

title: Sharpness of the Brjuno Condition for Hyperbolic Bishop Surfaces
summary: Let $μ\in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|μ|=1$, and assume that $μ$ is not a root of unity and is not Brjuno. Let $Q_γ$ denote the Bishop quadric with $γ= 1/\sqrt{2+μ+μ^{-1}} > 1/2$. Gong and Stolovitch conjectured that there exists a real-analytic surface in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with Moser--Webster invariant $μ$ that is formally but not holomorphically equivalent to $Q_γ$. We prove this conjecture.

title: On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}
summary: For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_δ$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.

title: Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries
summary: This is a reading note on a disc formula proof of hyperconvexity of bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$ with continuous boundaries.
comment: Reading note of an AI proof

title: Complex Oscillation and Non-Oscillation Results of Second-Order Linear Differential Equations
summary: In this paper, we investigate oscillation and non-oscillation results of second order differential equations \begin{equation} f''+(H_1e^z+H_2e^{αz}+q)f=0,\tag{+} \end{equation} where $H_1,H_2\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, $0<α<1$, and $q$ is an entire function of order less than $1$. First, we show that if equation (+) has a zero-free non-trivial entire solution, then either $α=1/2$ or $α=3/4$, which settles the Problem 9 posed in \cite{HITW}. Second, we prove that if either $q$ is transcendental, or $α=(2m-1)/(2m)$ for some integer $m\geq 2$ and $q\equiv 0$, then every non-trivial entire solution $f$ of $(+)$ satisfies $λ(f)=\infty$.

title: The $H^p$-Corona theorem on bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
summary: For $0<p\le2$, we solve the $H^p$-Corona problem on bounded pseudoconvex domains $Ω\Subset\mathbb C^n$ with $C^2$ boundary, obtaining the bound $C_Ωδ^{-q-1}|\logδ|$, where $q=\min\{n,m-1\}$ and $m$ is the number of generators. The range of $p$ is sharp even on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain admitting a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function and having only one weakly pseudoconvex boundary point.

title: Complex structures on products with $S^4$
summary: The main theorem of the present paper is that $S^4\times P$ admits a complex structure whenever $P$ is the fibre product, over a compact complex manifold, of the unit circle bundles of an even number of holomorphic line bundles. This theorem has lots of significant applications. For example, $S^4\times G$ admits a complex structure for every compact Lie group $G$ of even dimension. The same holds for $S^4\times V_{2s}(C^n)$ and $S^4\times V_{2s}(H^n)$ when $n\geq 2s\geq2$, and for $S^4\times V_{4s}(R^n)$ when $n\ge4s\ge4$. The theorem also gives complex structures on the product of $S^4$ with any even number of odd-dimensional spheres. Moreover, complex structures exist on $S^4$ times some moment-angle manifolds, including certain connected sums of sphere products. The construction uses a holomorphic $(C^*)^2$-action on $S^4 \times T^2$ endowed with the complex structure we constructed i

title: Totally geodesic sets and Caratheodory geometry in the polydisk
summary: A subset $V$ of the polydisk ${\mathbb D}^N$ is called totally geodesic if every pair of points in $V$ lie on a Kobayashi geodesic of ${\mathbb D}^N$ that lies entirely in $V$. It is called a Caratheodory set if its intrinsic Caratheodory metric agrees with the Caratheodory metric inherited from ${\mathbb D}^N$. We prove that for algebraic subvarieties of the polydisk these two notions coincide, and we obtain a complete geometric classification of such sets. The invariant metric geometry of the polydisk is unexpectedly rigid: every such set is, up to automorphism, built from only two basic geometric objects: disks and a distinguished family of two-dimensional algebraic surfaces that we call Roman surfaces. Roman surfaces arise independently in the study of the three-point interpolation problem in the polydisk.

title: An extension of Janowski functions with applications
summary: Janowski functions are regular functions of the form $p(z)=1+p_1z+\cdots$, which are subordinate to $L_0(a,b:z)=(1+az)/(1+bz)$ for real numbers $a,b$ such that $-1\leq b<a\leq 1$. In this paper, we expand the space of the constants, $a$ and $b$, of the superordinate function, $L_0(a,b:z)$, to a larger set of complex numbers and provide some applications.

title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
summary: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.

title: Freedom is all you need
summary: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
summary: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichmüller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies t

title: One exponential or two? Invertibility tests for Jordan epimorphisms
summary: How many exponential factors must one test to recognise a Jordan epimorphism? Let \(T\colon A\to B\) be a unital linear surjection between complex Banach algebras, with \(B\) semisimple. Using a spectral-isometry theorem of Aznay and Chabbabi, we show that it suffices for \(T\) to send every product of two exponentials to an invertible element to force $T$ to be Jordan. If only single exponentials are tested, \(T\) is a Jordan epimorphism if and only if its kernel is a two-sided ideal, or equivalently a left ideal. A resolvent estimate on a logarithmic spiral shows that a single exponential suffices when the source is a \(C^*\)-algebra or the group algebra \(\ell^1(G)\) of a discrete group. A separate argument, which does not use the spectral-isometry theorem, shows that a single exponential also suffices when the target is a \(C^*\)-algebra with a faithful family of tracial states.

title: Elementary Factorization For Continuous Orthogonal Matrices
summary: We prove that every nullhomotopic continuous map, from a finite-dimensional normal topological space X to the complex special orthogonal group, is a product of elementary orthogonal matrices with entries in the ring of continuous functions. The number of factors is bounded by a constant depending only on the size of the matrices and the covering dimension of X. The same factorization result holds for nullhomotopic special orthogonal matrices with entries in a unital commutative Banach algebra.

title: Weighted fixed-bidegree subelliptic estimates for the \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain
summary: We establish two types of \emph{a priori} subelliptic estimates for the twisted \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. The estimates feature a subelliptic gain in \((0, 1/2)\) and are uniform with respect to the bidegree. The boundary is assumed to satisfy a plurisubharmonic-type condition, characterized by the local existence, near each boundary point, of a bounded plurisubharmonic function whose Hessian blows up algebraically near the boundary, with potentially different exponents at different points. The twisting function is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the domain, has bounded gradient, and its critical set inside the domain consists of isolated interior points with finite vanishing orders.
