title: The Space of $k$-Positive Potentials
summary: In this paper, we study weak geodesics in the space of $k$-positive potentials on a compact Kähler manifold. We prove that any two smooth strictly $k$-positive potentials can be joined by a weak geodesic of class $C^{1,1}$. As an application, we prove that the pair $(\mathcal H_k,d_2)$ is a metric space.

title: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
summary: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n

title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
summary: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

title: An Elasticity Complex for Kirchhoff--Love Shells
summary: We develop an elasticity complex for Kirchhoff--Love shell theory, based on the linearized Gauss--Codazzi equations as compatibility conditions for shell strains. The resulting shell complex forms a fine resolution of the sheaf of infinitesimal rigid motions, so its cohomology groups are determined by the corresponding sheaf cohomology. Remarkably, the complex also reveals an Airy potential representation of equilibrium stress fields. The framework further identifies natural boundary conditions for both kinematic and dynamic variables. Finally, we establish a Hodge--Morrey--Friedrichs decomposition for strain and stress fields on shells with boundary.

title: An Isoperimetric Comparison for a Variational Threshold Associated with the Riemannian \(p\)-Laplacian
summary: We study a variational threshold $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ associated with a one-phase free boundary functional involving the Riemannian $p$-Dirichlet energy and a volume penalization on a bounded domain $K$ of a Riemannian manifold $M$. In the Euclidean case, this threshold is the smallest parameter for which the interior Bernoulli problem has a solution minimizing the energy; it bounds the Bernoulli constant from above, and the inequality is strict for balls. We characterize $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ as the infimum of a capacity-to-volume quotient and prove that this infimum is always attained. We then prove an isoperimetric comparison theorem: domination of the isoperimetric profile of $M$ by that of a model space implies a lower bound for $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ in terms of the threshold of a model geodesic ball. This extends a theorem of Daners and Kawohl. For geodesic balls in space forms, we give an explicit one-dime

title: Topology-Preserving Hodge--Laplacian Diffusion on Manifolds with Boundary
summary: Overview: We study deterministic and stochastic Hodge--Laplacian diffusion of differential forms on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. Absolute and relative boundary conditions select harmonic spaces representing ordinary and relative cohomology. We investigate the preservation properties of these diffusion processes, their compatible cellular discretizations, and their implications for reverse diffusion models. Numerical experiments on an annulus and a solid torus illustrate the theoretical results. Mathematical Significance: Using the de Rham complex and its constant-sheaf interpretation, we distinguish preservation of harmonic coordinates from preservation of a cohomology class. title: Hermitian connections and holonomy with parallel torsions
summary: Let $(M^n,g,J)$ be a connected Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, and let $\nabla$ be a Hermitian connection with nonzero parallel torsion. Assuming that its restricted holonomy acts irreducibly on $T^{1,0}M$, the author proved that the first Ricci curvature must vanish. In this paper we derive a Berger like complete list of its holonomy representations: the complexified adjoint representation of a compact simple Lie algebra, and the standard seven-dimensional complex representation of compact $\Gtwo$. Curvature of such a connection is proven to be parallel. Secondly, without irreducibility assumption, we derive an explicit local normal form for the metric whose Chern connection has parallel trosion, which includes holomorphic warpings and nontrivial holomorphic extensions of hyperkähler manifolds. title: All stable Schoen--Wolfson cones are minimizing
summary: In the late nineties, R.~Schoen and J.~Wolfson studied the problem of minimizing the area among Lagrangian surfaces in a Riemannian symplectic $4$-manifold. In their parametric approach, they showed that minimizers are smoothly branched-immersed away from a discrete set of points, where there exists a nonflat tangent cone minimizing the area among Lagrangian disk competitors. They also classified the stable singular cones into a family $C_{p,p+1}$ indexed by a positive integer $p$, but left open the question of which of them are globally minimizing. We settle this question by showing that for each $p \geq 1$, $C_{p,p+1} \cap B_1$ minimizes the area among Lagrangian disks spanning its boundary with degree one.

title: Yau's pinching problem and vanishing of Betti numbers
summary: We prove that a closed connected Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq4$, satisfying $\sec>\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$ at every point has vanishing real cohomology in degrees $1,..., n-1$. It is consequently a rational homology sphere if $n$ is odd or the manifold is orientable. Complex projective space shows that the coefficient is optimal and that the strict inequality is necessary in every even dimension. The required estimate for the Weitzenböck curvature term is established by integrating restricted Ricci operators over orthonormal frames and combining complementary degrees using Hodge duality. This also allows us to replace sectional curvature pinching by intermediate Ricci curvature bounds. For a nonflat metric, the weak Yau inequality, $\sec\geq\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$, gives the same cohomology vanishing unless the manifold is isometric, up to scaling, to a quotient

title: Submanifolds, restriction of differential operators and Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket
summary: In this article, we present new formulas for restricting the Hodge operator, the codifferential and the Hodge Laplacian to a submanifold. These formulas are concise, thanks to the use of tools for differential forms (Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket and generalized interior product). They also facilitate explicit calculations for practical applications.

title: On Gromov's Volume Growth Theorem
summary: Let $M^n$, $n\ge3$, be complete and noncompact, with nonnegative Ricci curvature. We derive the estimate \[ Vol (B(p,R))\le \frac{C_n}{c}(1+R)^αR^{n-2} \] from the radial lower bound $Scal(x)\ge c(1+d(p,x))^{-α}$, where $c>0$ and $0<α<2$. The proof extends Ge's heat-covariance argument by retaining the heat occupation of the set where a chosen scalar threshold fails. Varying that threshold with the source time makes all entropy errors integrable and yields the exact exponent $n-2+α$, without a logarithmic loss. We give explicit examples showing that this exponent is optimal and also allow failure of the curvature lower bound on a set of finite volume.

title: Disjoint Divisors and Splitting Rigidity under Nonnegative Orthogonal Ricci Curvature
summary: Let $X^n$ be a compact Kähler manifold with nonnegative orthogonal Ricci curvature. We prove that if $X$ admits two nonzero effective divisors with disjoint supports, then its universal cover splits. As applications, we study the MRC fibration of $X$, and show that when the dimension of a general fiber is $n-1$, the universal cover of $X$ splits as a product of a simply connected Riemann surface and a compact rationally connected manifold. When $X$ is rationally connected, it splits off a $\Pj^1$-factor if and only if it contains two disjoint nonzero effective divisors. Together with the results of Zhang and Zhang, these conclusions give a unified description of the universal cover for all possible dimensions of the general MRC fiber. We also establish metric existence criteria for certain projective bundles.

title: Elliptic regularization for anisotropic mean curvature flow
summary: We develop an elliptic regularization scheme for anisotropic mean curvature flow in arbitrary dimension, with general norms serving as surface tension and mobility. Starting from a non-fattening set of finite perimeter, we prove that the vertically rescaled minimizers and translating solitons converge in the Kuratowski sense to the unique generalized level-set motion, and locally in BV to the flat flow. Furthermore, by implementing a restarting and matching procedure prior to curvature identification, we establish for the limit flat flow a coupled phase-transport and surface-energy dissipation balance valid for arbitrary, possibly crystalline, anisotropies. When the surface tension is continuously differentiable (away from the origin) and strictly convex, we further prove that the flat flow is a BV flow and that its reduced boundary defines a unit-density anisotropic Brakke flow. title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
summary: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
summary: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $τ$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,τ}-(F,S(τ)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. title: Doubly Intermittent Singular Skew Products
summary: We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gouëzel skew products [Gouëzel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn. Sys. (2007)], in which the fibre maps are intermittency maps with a single indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. Through the construction of an induced full branch map, we prove various statistical properties of the skew products, including existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations.

title: On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$
summary: We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders. We also construct a subset of the set of left orders on any of the three groups, show the subset is a perfect set and give a new proof of the fact that the sets of the left orders on these three groups are uncountable.

title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
summary: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $π_v/β_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(π_v/β_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. title: A mean index criterion for multiple closed characteristics
summary: Let $n\ge2$. We prove that a compact strictly star-shaped $C^3$ hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ carries at least $n$ geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics if all iterates are nondegenerate and all mean indices are at least one. It suffices that all mean indices are positive and that the bound holds only for prime characteristics with negative mean Euler characteristic in the variational grading. The proof uses a minimum argument for the global Morse remainder and requires no individual index exclusion. For odd $n\ge3$, we obtain a smaller, dimension-dependent strict bound when good iterates of Maslov-type index $-1$ are excluded. Irrational ellipsoids show that the multiplicity bound is sharp.

title: Automorphism groups of mixing shifts of finite type
summary: We prove that nontrivial two-sided mixing shifts of finite type are flip conjugate if and only if their automorphism groups are abstractly commensurable. This resolves an outstanding question of Boyle, Lind, and Rudolph from 1988.

title: Bifurcation Structure and Coexisting Dynamical States in Two Inductively Coupled Josephson Junctions
summary: Inductively coupled Josephson junctions support coexisting stationary and running states whose selection depends on both circuit parameters and initial conditions. We investigate the model of a direct current-driven resistively and capacitively shunted junction pair as coupled nonlinear oscillators at zero external magnetic flux, allowing unequal bias, damping and inductive coupling parameters. Equilibrium equations, nullclines, and Jacobian spectra are combined with multiple-initial-condition simulations, finite-time Lyapunov spectra, and Poincaré returns to characterize changes in the system dynamics under varying initial conditions and parameter settings. The fixed-point bifurcation diagrams reveal the creation, destruction or annihilation of equilibria and non-monotonic changes in their number under asymmetric coupling. title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
summary: We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. title: Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms
summary: Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<χ<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-χ,χ]$. We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas. As a result, for every $0<χ<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$, the Artin--Mazur zeta function of all $χ$-hyperbolic periodic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its disk of convergence. Its leading poles are determined by the periods of the ergodic maximal measures. This answers the meromorphic continuation question of Buzzi.

title: Sierpiński Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals
summary: Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Eroğlu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric. We survey the machinery underlying these results and propose directions for further research.

title: Synchronisation under quasi-periodic forcing of circle diffeomorphisms with two attracting and two repelling fixed points
summary: We study the dynamics of circle diffeomorphisms, which have exactly two attracting and two repelling fixed points, under quasi-periodic forcing. For sufficiently small forcing, such a system exhibits uniformly hyperbolic behaviour. The results focus on systems with larger forcing, where every orbit intersects the basins of attraction of both attracting fixed points infinitely often. For such quasi-periodically forced circle diffeomorphisms, we identify a set of parameters of positive measure for which the corresponding skew-product systems admit a unique attracting and a unique repelling invariant graph, which capture the dynamics of Lebesgue almost every point on $\mathbb{T}^2$. title: Trajectory arclength reveals thermodynamic criticality
summary: Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition. We trace this non-analyticity to spontaneous magnetization and derive the leading critical finite-size correction, scaling as $N^{-1/2}$ with an explicit analytical prefactor. title: From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems
summary: Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus. We derive explicit synchronized periodic solutions and compute their Floquet multipliers, establishing the existence of non-gradient dynamics. Numerical explorations using bifurcation diagrams, Poincare sections, periodic-orbit continuation, a nd Lyapunov exponents reveal attracting periodic orbits, invariant-torus-like behavior, and strong evidence of chaos. title: Levi Dynamics and Largest Domains of Discontinuity on Flag Manifolds
summary: Divergent sequences in a semisimple Lie group have a bounded Levi part that is invisible to Cartan projections and limit flags. We show that this Levi part is a genuine dynamical invariant and determines much of the large-scale behaviour of discrete groups on flag manifolds. For every real flag manifold, we compute the complete moving-source destination relation of a divergent sequence, including the Levi contribution. This yields a stratified convergence principle, a boundary compactification encoding the relation, and an exact properness criterion. For discrete groups the relation organises the classical limit sets into a single flag, from Quint's limit set through the recurrent and Kulkarni sets to the Myrberg set, the complement of equicontinuity. Sequences with coalescing limit flags satisfy a diagonal formula, which gives a recurrence criterion for the largest domain of proper disc

title: Explicit Response Formulae and Request Problem for Smooth Expanding Endomorphisms
summary: In this paper, we investigate the higher order differentiability of physical measures, in the category of smooth expanding endomorphisms of compact manifolds, and we establish the explicit response formulae of any order. The proof is based on the elegant Keller-Liverani-Gouëzel perturbation theory of transfer operators. Furthermore, we provide the solutions to the high order request problem, which is regarded as the inverse problem to response formulae, that is, we make perturbations to realize prescribed responses up to any finite order, and we establish the existence of minimizers for a relaxed optimization problem associated with suitable cost functionals.

title: Exceptional Rays of Invariant Processes on Trees
summary: Let $A$ be an ergodic, non-constant random process on the $d$-regular tree $T_d$, with marginal distribution $X$. We prove that there always exist "exceptional" rays, whose asymptotic means are at least $\mathbb{E}(X)+δ$; furthermore, for edge processes, $δ> 0$ can be taken to depend only on the law of $X$. We compare different definitions of "maximal asymptotic means", relating them to different notions of speed of tree-indexed random walks.

title: On the linear stability of elliptic relative equilibrium in planar restricted $(n+1)$-body problem
summary: In this paper, we consider the restricted $(n+1)$-body problems, where the $n$ primaries forming an a homographic motion generated by the planar central configuration, and the massless particle is attracted by this $n$ primaries. We are interested in the linear stability of the elliptic relative equilibria of the massless particle under the pulsating coordinates. The main contribution of this paper first lies in the investigation of a general $(α,β)$-system (1.7). We obtain large-range spectral instability and small-range stability results valid for arbitrary eccentricity. The restricted $(n+1)$-body problem arises as a special case of this system. Accordingly, we derive several criteria for spectral instability and linear stability for this problem. title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
summary: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
summary: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. The conclusions hold on residual subsets of a nonempty $C^1$-open set and follow from Chaidez's contact blender and localized contact perturbations. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy. The proof compares long-bar counts with graph volume through contact tomography and filtered continuation. Under strong translated nondegeneracy, we show that super-exponential translated-pair growth in a compact interior window forces super-exponential growth of short bars born in the surrounding window.

title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-β\)-transformations
summary: We study the subshifts \(Ω_{-β,α}\) associated with the intermediate \(-β\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-βx+α\pmod1\), where \((β,α)\inΔ_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $Ω_{-β,α}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{β,α}=α/β\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((β,α)\) for which \(Ω_{-β,α}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(Δ_-\). The approximating parameters can be chosen so that both kneading invariants converge to those of the original map.

title: Rotationa Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
summary: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.

title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
summary: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincaré-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
summary: Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,ω$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. We prove that diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-1 homoclinic tangencies of all orders are dense in such regions. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders. These results entail genericity of one- or two-dimensional universal dynamics in $\mathcal N(L)$ (depending on the type of $L$). Moreover, we characterize the geometric complexity of the bifurcation sets corresponding to homoclinic tangencies. We prove that parametric families with paratangencies of arbitrar

title: Nonvanishing of mean indices and stability of symmetric closed characteristics on symmetric star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^4$
summary: H. Duan, H. Liu, Y. Long and W. Wang \cite{DLLW24} conjectured that if a compact star-shaped hypersurface in ${\bf R}^{2n}$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics, then each of them has nonzero mean index. They proved this conjecture for non-degenerate star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^6$. Motivated by their work, we study the symmetric counterpart of this problem. We prove that if a symmetric compact star-shaped hypersurface $Σ$ in ${\bf R}^4$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics, and every odd iterate of them is non-degenerate in the symmetric sense, then each of them has nonzero symmetric mean index. Based on this result, we further prove that if $Σ$ carries exactly two geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics and all their iterates are non-degenerate, then both of them

title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
summary: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently. We choose these quantities so that the drift of a scalar amplitude function alternates in sign on $m$ nested level curves, forcing a limit cycle between each consecutive pair. A perturbation transverse to the Hopf hypersurface creates one additional cycle inside the others. The one-turn displacement map shows that both local counts are sharp. For each $m$, we give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational inte

title: Bounds on periods of curves for split rational maps
summary: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be fixed complex rational maps of degree at least two, and let $(A_1,A_2)$ denote the endomorphism of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(A_1(x),A_2(y))$. We show that the periods of irreducible $(A_1,A_2)$-periodic curves with dominant coordinate projections are bounded, unless $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to the exceptional power, Chebyshev, or Lattès families. We also extend this result to periodic subvarieties for endomorphisms of $(\mathbb P^1)^m$.

title: Regularity of invariant measures of solutions for fractional stochastic partial differential equations with memory and nonlinear noise
summary: We are concerned with stochastic fractional partial differential equations involving memory and nonlinear multiplicative noise. Based on the well-known Dafermos method, a suitable variable defined by the integrated past history is introduced. This transformation not only overcomes the non-Markovianity of the original problem which prevents us from analyzing invariant measures for the associated Markov semigroup, but also facilitates the analysis of the well-posedness together with the Faedo-Galerkin approximations and Minty's technique. Moreover, we prove the existence of invariant measures by the classical Krylov-Bogoliubov approach, and further establish the regularity of invariant measures by virtue of a control argument.

title: A transitive $C^{1+α}$ surface diffeomorphism with positive entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy
summary: Let $0<α\le 1$. On a closed surface, every topologically transitive $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphism with positive topological entropy has at most one measure of maximal entropy.

title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
summary: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.

title: Infinitely many spectral gaps for Anderson--Bernoulli operators with sparse periodic backgrounds
summary: We consider discrete Anderson--Bernoulli operators with a periodic background. At a single coupling, every minimal period of at least three admits a background with at most four nonzero sites per period whose almost sure spectrum has infinitely many gaps. We give two constructions. The first uses at most seven nonzero sites per period and fixes the accumulation point at zero. For periods of at least five, the second uses exactly four nonzero sites per period and takes the lowest Dirichlet eigenvalue of the inserted chain as the accumulation point. In both constructions the gaps approach from the right. The widths of the selected gaps and their distances to the accumulation point are comparable to a common geometric factor divided by the period in the first family and by its cube in the second. Spectral intervals of comparable length separate successive gaps in each selected sequence.

title: Contact rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants
summary: We study $C^0$-rigidity and Poisson bracket invariants on closed contact manifolds. We prove that Poisson commutation is closed under uniform convergence, establish weak rigidity for pairs without common zeros, and obtain lower semicontinuity under quantitative control of Reeb derivatives. A three-dimensional counterexample shows that unrestricted weak rigidity fails. For partitions of unity, the contact bracket itself controls the Reeb derivatives. Using monotone homogeneous quasi-morphisms and the Cant--Kilgore--Zhang spectral invariant, we derive positive lower bounds for invariants of open covers and configurations of compact subsets. Applications include a quantitative contact big fiber theorem, bounds on Hamiltonian chord durations and Reeb travel times, and deformations of contact one-forms.

title: On rescuing diverging algorithms: crossing infinity in continuous Newton methods via a self-similarity detection framework
summary: We address the solution of systems of nonlinear algebraic equations via continuous Newton methods; these methods reformulate the discrete Newton update as an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) whose stationary points correspond to the desired roots. A fundamental challenge arises when the Jacobian of these ODEs becomes singular along the solution trajectory, inducing blow-up in the vector field --or in the state itself-- and causing the numerical integration to break down before reaching the desired root. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a directional self-similar blow-up detection and crossing procedure, wrapped around an adaptive step-size ODE solver with event detection. The method assumes local self-similar behavior near the blow-up; the self-similarity exponent, blow-up time, and amplitude are estimated on the fly from a short sequenc

title: The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
summary: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron. Solving this finite linear system for all scales at once gives exactly the 22 rules known from a geometric search; no rule exists at any scale other than 1,tau,tau^2,tau^3. The substitution becomes integer arithmetic on six-tuples and reproduces the bubbles of the geometric foam exactly. Whether a point of M is the centre of a bubble of size tau^{-k} is decide

title: The Dynamical Manin-Mumford Conjecture for automorphisms of Hénon type
summary: We prove the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture for polynomial automorphisms of the complex affine plane of dynamical degree $>1$ proposed by Dujardin and Favre. More precisely, we prove that an irreducible algebraic curve contains infinitely many periodic points of such an automorphism if and only if it is the fixed locus of a polynomial involution conjugating some iterate of the automorphism to its inverse.

title: Coordinate Ordering and Non-collinear Central Configurations
summary: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.

title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
summary: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, u

title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
summary: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlin

title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
summary: For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--Rödl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $σ_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence. In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem.

title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
summary: We study the resonances of the quantum baker map opened by a window of width $w$ centred at $q_c$. For $q_c=1/2$ the survivor set of the classical doubling map with a hole goes from zero to positive topological entropy along the Thue-Morse route, and we find numerically, for $N$ up to $2^{25}$, that the resonance spectrum follows this route step by step, also where the entropy is zero. Below the threshold $w_c=4a^*-1$, with $a^*$ the Thue-Morse constant, the surviving cycles have periods $2^ν$ and their thresholds accumulate doubly exponentially. Each cycle gives, as isolated orbits do, a multiplet of resonances close to modulus $2^{-1/2}$, with phases set by its action. Since a cycle is resolved only if its period is shorter than about $\log_2 N$, twice the Ehrenfest time, about $\log_2\log_2 N$ steps are resolved, four at our largest sizes. Near $w_c$ the 16-cycle perturbs the 8-multip

title: Recurrent sets and Lyapunov functions: from topological dynamics to weak KAM theory
summary: The aim of this survey is to clarify the intimate relations between Lyapunov functions and chain recurrent sets. The study of this subject comes from a seminal paper by Conley and has had recent advances by the so-called Weak KAM Theory for homeomorphisms. We provide a survey of the state of the art, presenting recent improvements and connections with the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, in order to illustrate the distinctions between recurrent sets in a non-trivial case as well as their dependence on a parameter, we discuss a compartmental model from mathematical epidemiology and a fast-slow version of a prey-predator model with Allee effect.

title: An arithmetic theory of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra
summary: We show geometric and dimensional properties of simultaneous rational-translation Lagrange equality spectra for both $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(δ)}$ using the projective cocycle steering method, which we introduce. In particular, we show the existence of a simultaneous Hall ray for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, a simultaneous Hall interval for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}(δ)}$, regimes of full and positive Hausdorff dimension, a scaling law, empty low spectra in certain cases, a compact set of full Hausdorff dimension in $(2Q\sqrt 3 - \varepsilon, 2Q\sqrt 3)$ where $Q$ is a common denominator of the finite set of rationals giving the translations, and the density of Lagrange equality sets in $\mathbb{R}$ for Lagrange constants in the Hall ray or Hall interval, respectively. Furthermore, we show that the Lagrange equality set for $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Bad}}$, for

title: Boundary of the Lagrange and Markov spectra near Hall's ray
summary: The Lagrange and Markov spectra, denoted by $L$ and $M$, respectively, are closed subsets of the real line with intricate fractal geometry related to Diophantine approximations. In 1975, Freiman proved that both spectra contain the ray $[c_F,\infty)$, where $c_F=4.527829566\dots$, and that this ray is optimal, as both spectra avoid a tiny interval $(ν_F,c_F)$. Using renormalization techniques and the thickness of Cantor sets, we prove that the boundaries $\partial L$ and $\partial M$ have positive Hausdorff dimensions arbitrarily close to $ν_F$. Furthermore, in connection with Berstein's conjecture, which predicts that $[4.1,4.52]\subset L$, we exhibit a gap in $L$ near $4.08$, the first known gap in the region $L\cap[3.945,4.52]$. We also prove that the boundaries of both spectra have positive Hausdorff dimension near $4.5213$ and $4.08$.

title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
summary: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. For a fixed storage metric $Q$, the resulting Koopman matrices are the Cayley transforms of $(J-R)Q$, where $J$ is skew-symmetric and $R$ is positive semidefinite. This set does not depend on the step size and is the closure of all Q-contractions. This set is LMI-representable; therefore, structure-preserving EDMD, including ports through a discrete-time Kalman-Yakubovich-Popov condition and Casimirs through affine constraints, is a semidefinite program. The constrained es

title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
summary: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(μ\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_μ\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_μ\) is upper semicontinuous at \(μ=0\) almost surely.

title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
summary: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability. We study rollout scheduling for training on one contiguous rollout per sampled state, asking whether adapting its length to local instability improves prediction. We find the schedule that uses the most trajectory data under an instability budget, a limit on how much instability any one rollout may accumulate. Under stated assumptions, we bound the resulting coverage gain and the coverage lost when the instability estimates are in error. Numerical checks illustrate the theory. Training experiments on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky compa

title: Real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices preserving an ergodic volume
summary: We classify real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices that preserve an ergodic smooth volume on a compact manifold. On an invariant open dense set of full volume, the action is analytically conjugate to the restriction of an affine action on finitely many copies of one double quotient. The conjugacy carries Haar probability to the given volume. Analytic germ superrigidity supplies local coordinates with measurable dependence on the center. The conditional measures on coarse Lyapunov manifolds determine the law of a displaced center. A two-point joining pairs charts whose evaluations agree there and gives the change of coordinates. The resulting analytic frame bundle carries a coframe whose vector fields integrate to the homogeneous model. This gives the open homogeneous classification in Zimmer's program.

title: Rigidity and nonrigidity for interval translation maps
summary: Almost every infinite-type interval translation map in the Bruin--Troubetzkoy family, and in Bruin's family with any fixed number of branches, is rigid for its invariant probability, where typicality is understood with respect to the intrinsic induction parameter measure. We prove this by exhibiting explicit repeated-word blocks in the induction and showing that their cylinders recur. In the opposite direction, we give a sufficient condition for nonrigidity of a primitive aperiodic substitution: the existence of a rational periodic vector of its incidence matrix in the return-word space whose coordinate sum is nonzero. The proof gives a uniform positive lower bound for symbol discrepancies at all sufficiently large times. For self-similar Bruin maps with primitive period substitution, the same condition also implies weak mixing. We apply the nonrigidity condition to an explicit self-simi

title: Correspondence between orbit equivalences and exact symplectomorphisms for Anosov flows
summary: We show that for a closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, two Anosov flows are orbital equivalent if and only if the corresponding Anosov Liouville structures are exact symplectomorphic.

title: Non-local ergodic measures in symplectic dynamics
summary: We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic. The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations.

title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NIP groups
summary: Let $μ$ be a global generically stable Keisler measure on a type-definable group in an NIP theory. Then $μ$ is idempotent if and only if it is the unique translation-invariant measure on its type-definable stabilizer subgroup. This resolves the NIP case of the Idempotent Measure problem studied by Chernikov, Gannon, and Krupiński.

title: Real-analytic actions of lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact $n$-manifolds
summary: We classify real-analytic actions of arbitrary lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact connected $n$-manifolds without boundary, $n\geq 3$, with no invariant-volume assumption. After finite-index restriction, the action has finite image, extends to a connected Lie group locally isomorphic to $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ with an equivariant finite cover when needed, or is obtained by analytic surgery with at least one torus piece. In the last case the lattice is commensurable with a conjugate of $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb Z)$. As a main input, we prove a general cocycle superrigidity theorem for real analytic germs.

title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
summary: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.

title: Measure-class classification of achievable Cantorvals
summary: An achievable Cantorval is a Cantorval that is the set of subsums of a convergent series of positive terms. We construct an explicit achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Lebesgue measure at least $2\prod_{j\ge 1}(1-2^{-j})=0.5775\ldots$. This answers a question of Gł{ą}b and Prus-Wi{ś}niowski and gives a counterexample to the conjecture of Nowakowski and Prus-Wi{ś}niowski that every achievable Cantorval is standard. The example is generated by a hybrid series of Pratsiovytyi, Vynnyshyn and Vynnyshyn. The lower bound comes from an isolated-digit criterion, which produces a Cantor subset of the boundary whose measure is an explicit infinite product; after rescaling, the boundary measure can be made arbitrarily close to $1$. We also prove that the boundary of every achievement set is either Lebesgue null or has positive measure near each of its points. Consequently, up to homeomorphisms

title: Thurston measure is stationary with exponential Teichmüller moment
summary: In 1967, Furstenberg proved that every lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center admits a probability measure whose stationary measure on the associated Furstenberg boundary belongs to the Lebesgue measure class. We prove an analogue of this theorem for the action of the mapping class group on Teichmüller space. Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class on the space of projective measured foliations is the stationary measure of a non-elementary random walk with a finite exponential moment in the Teichmüller metric.

title: Dynabase: A Database of Extreme Examples in Arithmetic Dynamics
summary: We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.

title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
summary: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $σ$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\inσ+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in

title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
summary: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
summary: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

title: Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy
summary: We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.

title: Preventing cycles in Lotka--Volterra systems
summary: We study cycles of heteroclinic connections between equilibria of Lotka--Volterra systems with negative self-interactions. We prove that generalized strict diagonal dominance makes the invasion, connection, and weak graphs acyclic for every intrinsic growth vector. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed, and the associated semiflow is gradient with respect to its equilibria. For the broader class of Volterra--Lyapunov stable matrices, we show that two equilibria are joined by a heteroclinic connection exactly when the species that enter have positive invasion rates at the source and the species that leave have nonpositive invasion rates at the target. We show by examples that the three graphs can differ, that the dominance threshold is sharp, and that generalized dominance is not necessary for acyclicity. We also give a quantitative criterion for cycle exclusion in terms of the symmetric

title: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
summary: This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \

title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
summary: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagat

title: Convergence of the Most Probable Transition Paths in Multiscale Systems
summary: This paper is devoted to study the convergence behavior of the most probable transition paths in a class of multiscale stochastic dynamical systems. First, based on Euler-Lagrange equations, we establish proximity and convergence results in the space of continuous functions endowed with the supremum norm. These results compare the most probable paths of the multiscale system with those of averaged system derived from the averaging principle. Next, we utilize a variational framework and analyze the Onsager-Machlup functionals using $Γ$-convergence. Together with the equi-coercivity of the functional family, we prove the convergence of both their minima and minimizers. Specifically, we show weak convergence of the minimizers in the Cameron-Martin space $H^1$, which implies their strong convergence in $L^2$.

title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
summary: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle. First, for a non-exceptional polynomial of degree at least two, we prove that every invariant curve arising from such a semiconjugacy is contained in a generalized circle. Second, in the rational map case, we construct invariant curves arising in this way that are not contained in any generalized circle and have arbitrarily many self-intersections, counted with multiplicity. Moreover, the rational maps can be chosen so that their restrictions to these curves have positive topological entropy.

title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
summary: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_δ$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown / Vershik / Ryzhikov / Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results. Furthermore, the power topologies on the space of bistochastic operators recording weak convergence in powers up to $k+1$, $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ are all distinct, as are the analogous power uniformities on the automorphism group of the standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability measure.
