title: Every Finite Incline Is Finitely Based
summary: We prove that every incline of finite additive height generates a Cross variety. In particular, every finite incline is finitely based. Moreover, we obtain a uniform bound on the number of variables needed to axiomatize subvarieties of decreasing Catalan semiring varieties, and give an effective construction of finite equational bases.

title: Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
summary: Let $G = *_λG_λ$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.

title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
summary: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.

title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
summary: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.

title: Products of supersoluble groups
summary: Let $G=AB$ be a finite group, where $A$ and $B$ are supersoluble. We prove that every nonabelian composition factor of $G$ is isomorphic to $\PSL_2(p)$ for some prime $p\ge5$ and that the nonsoluble length of $G$ is at most one.

title: On simultaneous left- and right-homometric sets on the positive affine line group
summary: On a non-abelian group $G$, the homometry problem comes in two flavors, depending on whether differences are computed on the left or on the right. A natural question is to determine whether simultaneously left- and right-homometric subsets of $G$ exist. This question has been answered positively in the case of dihedral groups by Genuys and Popoff. We here prove that no such subsets exist on the positive affine line group, if we impose that the subgroups generated by their left- and right-differences be non-abelian.

title: Berkovich's conjecture on noninner automorphisms of order $p$
summary: We prove a long-standing conjecture of Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 4.13): every finite nonabelian $p$-group $P$ has a noninner automorphism of order $p$. If $p$ is odd, the automorphism $α$ can be chosen with $[P,α,α]=1$. More precisely, given a maximal normal elementary abelian subgroup $E$ of $P$, we can choose $α$ to fix both $F$ and $P/F$ pointwise, where $F$ is either $E$ or a hyperplane of $E$ normal in $P$. If $p=2$, the automorphism can be chosen with $[P,α,α,α]=1$, and with $[P,α,α]=1$ when $Z(P)$ is noncyclic. The dihedral group of order eight shows that the hypothesis on $Z(P)$ cannot be omitted.

title: On a question of A.N. Skiba concerning the modularity of the lattice of $σ$-permutable subgroups
summary: Let $σ=\{σ_i\mid i\in I\}$ be some partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. A subgroup $A$ of $G$ is said to be $σ$-permutable in $G$ if $G$ has a Hall $σ_i$-subgroup for every $i\in I$ and $A$ permutes with every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ for all $i\in I$. We describe the finite groups $G$ for which the lattice $\Lper(G)$ of all $σ$-permutable subgroups of $G$ is modular. This answers the first part of a question of A.N. Skiba. We also prove that if every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, then $\Lper(G)$ is modular if and only if every two members of $\Lper(G)$ are permutable.

title: Blocks with one simple module and solvable groups
summary: Let $b$ be a block of a finite group with one isomorphism class of simple modules in characteristic $p$. We construct, over a sufficiently large complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, a Morita equivalence between $b$ and a block of a finite solvable group. The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.

title: Random homomorphisms from affine to spherical reflection groups
summary: The goal of this paper is to understand the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)$ of homomorphisms from an affine reflection group $\widetilde{W}$ to its associated spherical reflection group $W$. We do this in three ways: numerically, by deriving an explicit formula for $|\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)|$; probabilistically, by exploring the question what does a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}\to W$ look like?; and algebraically, by explicitly writing down all possible homomorphisms on the standard generators. For example, we show that as $n\to\infty$ the probability that a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}_n\to W_n$ is surjective tends to $\frac{3}{4}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n}$ or $D_n$, to $\frac{9}{16}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n+1}$, and to $1$ if $W_n$ is of type $A_n.$

title: Profinite groups with coprime automorphisms whose orbits generate nilpotent subgroups
summary: Suppose that a profinite group $G$ admits a finite group of coprime automorphisms $A$ such that for any $\varphi\in A$ every subgroup $\langle x^{\langle\varphi\rangle}\rangle$ generated by the $\langle\varphi\rangle$-orbit of an element $x\in G$ is nilpotent. It is proved that $[G,A]$ is pronilpotent, and if $A$ is soluble and the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(A)$ is locally nilpotent, then $G$ is locally nilpotent.

title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
summary: Let $Γ<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/Γ$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $Γ$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to Möbius conjug

title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
summary: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
summary: Let $Γ_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leqΓ_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
summary: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\inγ_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for a word with six syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.

title: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes of arbitrary finite groups
summary: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. In a previous paper it was shown that if $H$ is solvable, then there exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible. In this paper we remove the hypothesis that $H$ is solvable. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof depends on the classification of finite simple groups. Its main new ingredient is a result on quasiprimitive linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups which shows that the elements acting as field automorphisms can be ignored when one looks for vectors with small stabilizers. We also present a new family of examples, with nonsolvable $H$, in which the bound is attained.

title: On the prime index elements graph of finite groups
summary: For a finite group $G$, the prime index elements graph $\G(G)$, introduced by Anitha and Rajkumar, has vertex set $G$, two distinct elements being adjacent if the cyclic subgroup generated by one has prime index in that generated by the other. We show that $\G(G)$ is a bipartite blow-up of a weighted graph $\Hq(G)$ on the cyclic subgroups of $G$, which is a cartesian product of trees when $G$ is nilpotent, and use this to study several graph invariants. We characterize the groups for which $\G(G)$ is a star, a cograph, a chordal graph, or has a perfect code. We compute the sharp bounds for the independence and domination number. We give an exact formula for the strong metric dimension, bound the metric and strong metric dimensions in terms of the quotient graph, show that the upper bounds for the strong metric dimension are attained for cyclic p-groups, and all upper bounds for groups wh

title: Leavitt path algebras, growth series, Thompson groups
summary: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Martín Barquero, Martín González, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.

title: There are hard braids
summary: Let us call a trivial braid hard if it cannot be untangled by Reidemeister moves without increasing the number of crossings. Are there hard trivial braids? Our paper answers this question. Hard braids exist. For every number of strands starting from 4, for every even length starting from 16, we present examples of hard trivial braids of that size. Our smallest example is minimal. We prove that there are no hard braids on three strands. On four strands our shortest example, of length 16, is a shortest hard braid. The hard braids in that family can be untangled without increasing their length if we use Reidemeister moves and an infinite family of moves $σ_i^{\varepsilon}σ_j^{m}σ_i^{-\varepsilon} \leftrightarrowσ_j^{-\varepsilon}σ_i^{m}σ_j^{\varepsilon}$, which involve only three strands. We also build a harder family of hard braids which no moves confined to a bounded number of strands can

title: The Tamura-Shafer Problem for Monoids
summary: Let \(\Pow(S)\) denote the semigroup of all nonempty subsets of a semigroup \(S\), with multiplication induced from \(S\). We prove that every monoid \(M\) is reconstructible from \(\Pow(M)\), even among arbitrary semigroups: if \(\Pow(M)\cong\Pow(T)\), then \(T\) is a monoid and \(M\cong T\). The resulting isomorphism is uniquely determined by the singleton subsets of units and the two-point subsets \(\{1,a\}\) of nonunits. The main difficulty is to recover multiplication without assuming that an isomorphism of power semigroups preserves singletons. We resolve it by reconstructing finite multiplication cycles and the translation geometry of infinite mixed-power orbits. We also describe the induced split epimorphism between automorphism groups and exhibit examples where nonregular singletons are not preserved.

title: Claw-free difference graphs of finite groups
summary: Let $\D(G)$ be the difference graph of a finite group $G$: the graph on the non-isolated vertices of $\PE(G)-\Pg(G)$, where $x\sim_{\D} y$ if and only if $\gen{x,y}$ is cyclic and neither of $x,y$ lies in the cyclic group generated by the other. A claw is the graph $K_{1,3}$ and a graph is claw-free if it has no induced claw. We prove that for every finite group $G$, $\D(G)$ is claw-free if and only if it is a disjoint union of copies of the path $P_3$, if and only if the element orders of $G$ are prime powers or $6$, every element of order $3$ has at most one involution in its centralizer, and every involution has at most one subgroup of order $3$ in its centralizer (equivalently: $C_G(a)$ has a normal Sylow $2$-subgroup of order at most $2$ for every $a$ of order $3$, and $C_G(u)$ a normal Sylow $3$-subgroup of order at most $3$ for every involution $u$). Consequences: a nilpotent grou

title: On the Delandtsheer Conjecture
summary: We prove the Delandtsheer Conjecture of 1988 that a line-primitive automorphism group of a finite linear space is point-primitive.

title: No solvable group is isospectral to the symmetric group of degree 10
summary: We prove that no finite solvable group has the same spectrum as the symmetric group of degree 10. The proof analyzes the two possible Frobenius structures of a Hall $\{5,7\}$-subgroup and the actions of the corresponding subgroups on normal $\{2,3\}$-sections.

title: Parameterized Subset Sum for Integers and Solvable Permutation Groups
summary: We show that parameterized subset sum for binary-encoded integers belongs to $\mathsf{W}[2]$, where the parameter is the number of selected integers. This improves a result of Buss and Islam, who proved membership in $\mathsf{W}[3]$. The proof uses an fpt-reduction to weighted CNF satisfiability without changing the parameter. For every fixed integer $d\geq1$, we also show that parameterized subset sum for permutation groups of derived length $d$ belongs to $\mathsf{W}[2d]$. The proof combines positive CNFs for addition in small abelian groups with an affine decomposition of a solvable permutation action. This gives circuits of weft at most $2d$ and depth depending only on $d$ for product evaluation. For every fixed nilpotency class, we obtain the stronger bound $\mathsf{W}[2]$ by an fpt-reduction to subset sum in abelian permutation groups. The reduction uses Hall's polynomial coordinat

title: Sparse IRSs in Acylindrically Hyperbolic Groups that Surject Onto $\mathbb{Z}$
summary: For a non-elementary acylindrically hyperbolic group $Γ$ that surjects onto the integers, we construct an invariant random subgroup $Λ$ of $Γ$ for which the expected word-length of the shortest non-trivial element of $Λ$ is infinite. We refer to these as ``sparse" IRSs. The construction employs properties of renewal processes on $\mathbb{Z}$ as well as work of Dahmani, Guirardel, and Osin (arxiv:1111.7048v5) on the freeness of normal closures of certain elements in non-elementary acylindrically hyperbolic groups. We contrast this with the case of property (T) groups which cannot possess such IRSs. As an application, we answer a question posed in (arxiv:1612.09510v1) by constructing IRSs of $\mathrm{Isom}^+(\mathbb{H}^n)$ which have infinite expected injectivity radius, something which is impossible for higher-rank geometries due to work by Abert, Bergeron, et al. (arxiv:1210.2961v4)

title: The distortion of finitely generated subgroups in hyperbolic groups
summary: We show that the range of distortion functions of finitely generated subgroups of hyperbolic groups is essentially as broad as the range of time-complexity functions $T(n)$ of Turing machines. More precisely, we show that for each such $T(n) \geq n$ for which $T(n)^3$ is superadditive, there is a hyperbolic group $G$ with a finitely generated normal subgroup $N$ such that $\text{Dist}_N^G(n) \simeq 2^{T(n)^3}$. Our approach is to estimate the distortion of the kernels in Wise's HNN version of the Rips construction, and then to look at what these estimates yield when the $S$-machine groups of Sapir, Birget, and Rips are the inputs to the construction.

title: Finite groups with a fixed-point-free automorphism satisfying an irreducible identity
summary: For any given irreducible polynomial $f(x)=a_0+a_1\cdot x+\cdots+a_d\cdot x^d\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, we study the structure of finite groups $(G,\cdot)$ that have a fixed-point-free-automorphism $α$ satisfying the condition \[ \{g^{a_0}\cdotα(g)^{a_1}\cdotsα^d(g)^{a_d}\mid g\in G\}=\{1\}. \] We show that such a group $G$ is nilpotent of class at most $d^{2^d}$, provided that $|G|$ is coprime to an explicit, non-zero, integer invariant $ι(f(x))$ of $f(x)$. We do this by extending the solutions of the Frobenius conjecture. We also extend the solution of the restricted Burnside problem in prime exponent and the classification of the $n$-abelian groups.

title: Nonsolvable critical groups with the spectrum of $S_{10}$
summary: We classify the nonsolvable finite groups that are critical with respect to the spectrum of the symmetric group $S_{10}$. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: $S_{10}$ and $(A_9\times C_3)\rtimes C_2$, where the involution acts on $A_9$ by conjugation by a transposition and on $C_3$ by inversion. The quotient of any nonsolvable group with this spectrum by its solvable radical is almost simple. All possible simple socles are treated without assuming that the radical is nilpotent. The final cases, $L_3(4)$ and $A_6$, are excluded using the canonical subgroup $K=[R(G)\cap G^\infty,G^\infty]$, actions on chief factors, and the required element orders $9,20,30$. In the $A_6$ case, the final contradiction is the existence of an element of order $16$. Reproducible certificates accompany the character-table and matrix calculations.

title: On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group
summary: The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.

title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
summary: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

title: The commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface has finitely generated abelianization
summary: We prove that the commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface with at most one boundary component has finitely generated abelianization. The proof combines Gaifullin's finite-generation sufficient condition with the explicit generating set for the Torelli commutator subgroup due to Brendle, Margalit, and Putman.

title: On the Beauville Dimension of Finite Abelian Groups
summary: Unmixed Beauville manifolds of general type are rigid quotients of products of compact complex curves of higher genus by free diagonal actions of finite groups. Their biholomorphism classes are encoded by equivalence classes of group-theoretic data. For a finite abelian group $G$, we characterize when these data exist and determine the unmixed Beauville dimension $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)$, the minimum dimension of such a manifold arising from a diagonal action of $G$. We prove that $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)<\infty$ if and only if $\exp(G)$ is odd and greater than $3$, and the largest invariant factor of $G$ occurs at least twice. In that case, \[ \mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=\max\{\mathrm{rk}(G),\mathrm{rk}_3(G)+2\}. \] Specializing to $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=2$ recovers the classical result of Bauer, Catanese and Grunewald: the finite abelian Beauville surface groups are prec

title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
summary: For a crystallographic root system $Φ$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}Φ$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $ρ+ λ$, where $ρ$ is the Weyl vector and $λ$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $ρ$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

title: Trickle groups on a complete graph are linear
summary: Trickle groups were recently introduced by Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris, as generalizations of both cactus groups and right-angled Coxeter and Artin groups. We construct a representation of any trickle group $\mathrm{Tr}(Γ)$ with complete graph $Γ$ on a space having a basis in bijection with the vertex set $V(Γ)$, and show that it is faithful. This in particular shows that trickle Garside groups are linear. It also allows one to realize every finite trickle group as a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_{|V(Γ)|}(\mathbb{C})$. We do not use the results of Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris; instead we rather show that several properties of trickle groups that they obtained (and also some new ones) can easily be proven in the particular case of a complete graph using our representation. This includes the normal forms, the embedding of the trickle monoid inside the group in the case where $μ(x)=\infty$ fo

title: Tropical Geometry of $G_2$
summary: We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard. These form hexagons in incidence geometry. We classify all toric degenerations and their Newton-Okounkov polytopes. Mukai theory leads us to tropical canonical curves of genus 10. This article serves as a blueprint for studies of reductive groups in tropical geometry.

title: Dyson's Tenfold Way, Revisited
summary: In this work, we study semilinear representations of groups acting on degree two Galois extensions. Our results include a classification of irreducible semilinear representations, which generalises Dyson's Tenfold Way. Using this, we completely describe the semilinear representation theory of certain groups, such as symmetric groups, and of finite groups over cyclotomic fields. We also prove many results concerning semilinear representations over $\mathbb{C}$, which includes an induction theorem which simultaneously generalises Brauer's Induction Theorem and Serre's Induction Theorem. We are also interested in applications of our classification theorem to crystallography, and include a detailed study of the semilinear representation theory of magnetic wallpaper groups.

title: Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition
summary: We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S. We identify the Poisson and Furstenberg boundaries of these groups. This applies in particular to reductive algebraic groups over local fields.

title: Graded version of local-global principle for Steinberg and Chevalley groups
summary: In this article, an analog of a graded version of Quillen-Suslin's local-global principle was established for Steinberg groups $St(Φ,-)$ and Chevalley groups $G(Φ,-)$ over a reduced irreducible root system $Φ$.

title: Character codegrees in $π$-separable groups
summary: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_π(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $π$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(χ)=|G:\kerχ|/χ(1)$) are $π$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $π$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_π(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_π$-characters $\operatorname{B}_π(G)$.

title: On primes not adjacent to $2$ in the prime graphs of almost simple groups
summary: The prime graph $GK(G)$ of a finite group $G$ is the graph whose vertices are primes dividing the order of $G$ and in which two distinct primes $r$ and $s$ are adjacent if and only if $G$ has an element of order $rs$. The $2$-independence number of $GK(G)$ is the maximal size of independent vertex subsets in $GK(G)$ containing the vertex~$2$. We determine all almost simple groups whose prime graph has a vertex $r$ not adjacent to $2$ and find the $2$-independence numbers of all almost simple groups.

title: Linear Connectivity of Boundaries of Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
summary: To every right-angled Coxeter group one can canonically associate a hyperbolic metric space, called its maximized hyperbolic space. This space is Morse recognizing and is obtained from the Davis complex by coning off its standard product regions. We characterize, purely in terms of the defining graph, when the Gromov boundary of a maximized hyperbolic space is nonempty and linearly connected. As an application, we prove that among one-ended right-angled Coxeter groups, splitting over a subgroup of an unbounded product subgroup is a quasi-isometry invariant. We also establish several features shared by maximized hyperbolic spaces and curve graphs, including the existence of dead ends and visibility of boundaries. Moreover, when the boundary is nonempty, it is non-compact if and only if the defining graph contains an induced 4-cycle.

title: Divisible design graphs from a construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups
summary: In this paper, we present a new construction of divisible design graphs with new parameters, obtained by plugging a difference set into a known construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs of diameter 3 that is based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups.

title: Exact factorizations of countable groups into discrete and thin subsets
summary: For every countably infinite Hausdorff topological group $G$, we construct an exact factorization $G=AB$, where $A,B\subseteq G$ and every element of $G$ has a unique representation as $ab$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. Both factors are infinite, closed, discrete, and thin. A subset $C\subseteq G$ is thin if the intersections $hC\cap C$ and $Ch\cap C$ are finite for every nonidentity element $h\in G$. In any countably infinite group, an exact factorization into two infinite thin subsets can be constructed starting from any partial exact factorization with finite nonempty factors. Given a finite or countably infinite family of infinite subsets of the group, we can choose the extension so that each factor meets every member of the family in infinitely many points. If the topology on the group has a countable base and every nonempty open set is infinite, taking the nonempty members of the bas

title: A faster algorithm for commutator length in free groups
summary: We compute the commutator length $\cl(w)$ of a reduced word $w\in[F,F]$ of length $M$ in a free group. Given a target $g\ge1$, a deterministic algorithm decides $\cl(w)\le g$ and, when it holds, returns a decomposition into at most $g$ commutators, in $O(M^{3g})$ steps; trying $g=1,2,\dots$ gives $\cl(w)$ in $O(M^{3\cl(w)})$ steps. For $g=1$ the same test takes $O(M)$ expected steps on a uniformly random reduced input in $[F,F]$. All bounds are in the unit-cost model.

title: Enumerating orbits of finite classical groups on their Lie algebras
summary: We enumerate the orbits of a finite classical group in the adjoint action on its Lie algebra, giving exact generating functions and very good upper bounds. We treat the general linear, unitary, symplectic and orthogonal groups, in both odd and even characteristic. In even characteristic, we get very nice formulas for the number of orbits on nilpotent classes both in the finite and algebraically closed case. We discuss the connection with commuting varieties.

title: Permutation groups, derangements and connections
summary: What is the chance that a random shuffling of a deck of cards leaves no card in its original place? More precisely, what is the chance that a random permutation has no fixed points? A permutation with no fixed points is known as a derangement. Questions about derangements, like the ones above, go back centuries, but there are also several unsolved problems in this very active area of permutation group theory. Based on a minicourse given at "Groups and Algebras in Bicocca for Young Algebraists" in June 2026, this survey provides a general introduction to permutation group theory, with a specific focus on derangements. The survey features modern methods for studying permutation groups, recent developments and open problems concerning derangements and connections between this topic and other areas, such as combinatorics, graph theory, number theory, representation theory and topology.

title: Finitely generated groups with arbitrarily fast MIF growth
summary: A group $G$ is mixed identity free, or MIF, if for each nontrivial $w(x)\in G\star (\mathbb{Z}=\langle x\rangle)$ there is some $g\in G$ such that $w(g)\neq 1$. Associated to MIF groups is a natural growth function that measures how far in the Cayley graph one witnesses such inequations. We adapt a recent construction of the author with Hyde to show that for each function $f:\mathbf{N}\to \mathbf{N}$ there is a finitely generated group $G$ whose MIF growth function grows faster than $f$. This answers a question first considered by Henry Bradford. As a consequence, we also provide the first examples of finitely generated MIF groups that are not selfless, answering a question of Bradford and Sisto.

title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
summary: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $β_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leqβ=β_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $β\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.
