title: Kato-Milne cohomology over rational function fields in characteristic p>0
summary: Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. In this note, we describe the Kato-Milne cohomology of the rational function field F(x) in one variable x over F. In particular, we extend the Milnor-Scharlau exact sequence [12, Theorem 5.2] to characteristic p. As an application of this exact sequence, we further obtain the norm theorem [16, Theorem A.3] in characteristic p.

title: Sharp tails for arguments of Dirichlet $L$-functions
summary: Let $t$ be uniform on $[T,2T]$, let $χ$ be a Dirichlet character modulo $q$, and set $X=\Im\log L(1/2+it,χ)$ and $Q=\sum_{p\le T,\,p\nmid q}1/p$. For fixed $K,θ_0>0$, uniformly in $q\le T^{θ_0}$, $χ$, and $0\le V\le KQ$, each signed tail $\Pr\{\pm X>V\}$ has order $\sqrt Q\,(V+\sqrt Q)^{-1}\exp(-V^2/Q)$. In particular, for $S(t)=π^{-1}\argζ(1/2+it)$ and $0\le V\le K\log\log T$, each tail $\Pr\{\pm S(t)>V\}$ has order $\sqrt{\log\log T}\,(V+\sqrt{\log\log T})^{-1}\exp(-π^2V^2/\log\log T)$. For $|v|\le KQ$, the probability that $X$ lies in a fixed-width interval centered at $v$ has order $Q^{-1/2}\exp(-v^2/Q)$ whenever the width is sufficiently large. The upper bound holds for every fixed positive width. We also obtain matching bounds of order $\exp(k^2Q)$ for the means of $\exp(\pm2kX)$ for fixed $k>0$. The proof begins with a one-sided polynomial bound for each sign, using Alpöge's zero-

title: Shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-functions
summary: In this paper, we establish upper bounds for shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-function over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one under the generalized Riemann hypothesis. The result is used to derive bounds for moments of angular Hecke character sums.

title: Explicit exponent bounds for sums of consecutive powers
summary: Let $x^k+(x+1)^k=y^n$, where $x,y,k,n$ are positive integers with $k\ge2$ and $n\ge3$. We prove that $n<52k^2\log(2k)\log^2(50k)$ for odd $k$ and $n<216k\log^2(2500k)$ for even $k$. For odd $k$, an exact valuation formula reduces the problem to a linear form in two real logarithms. For even $k$, we use factorization in $\mathbb Z[i]$ and a bound of Yamada. When $k=5$, we prove that the original exponent $n$ is one of the 34 primes between $23$ and $181$, inclusive. Every solution satisfies $2x+1=u^n$ with $u>10^{1000}$. A gap between successive rational approximations to $2^{-4/n}$, together with the Thue--Siegel principle, gives at most four solutions for each of $n=23,29$ and at most three for each larger prime in this range. Thus there are at most 104 positive integer triples $(x,y,n)$ in the quintic case. All bounds are unconditional.

title: On the Number Theory of the Greeks. II. Gauss's Lemmas and Riesz Domains
summary: In the second part of our article on Euclid's four number theorem we start from the notion of incommensurability and take a closer look at irrationality proofs for algebraic numbers. Along the way we encounter Gauss's Lemma, integral closure and Dedekind's Prague theorem, and finally we arrive back at the four number theorem.

title: On the number theory of the Greeks. I. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
summary: In this article we present Euclid's fundamental theorem of number theory and give evidence for the claim that this theorem, which is largely unknown today, was as familiar to number theorists before Gauss as the Gaussian version of the fundamental theorem is to us.

title: A ring of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree $2$ with integral Fourier coefficients II
summary: We exhibit 24 homogeneous generators for the graded \(\Z\)-algebra of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree 2 over \(\Q(i)\) with integral Fourier coefficients, where the weight \(k\) is even and the character is \(\det^{k/2}\). We prove that 24 is the minimum number of algebra generators. For the subalgebra in weights divisible by 4, Kurihara reduced the generating set given in our earlier work to 11 forms. We show that 13 further forms generate the direct sum of the components in weights congruent to 2 modulo 4 as a module over this subalgebra. For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), we show that the ring of Fourier expansions modulo \(p\) is a polynomial ring over \(\F_p\) generated by the reductions of 4 forms of weights \(8,12,12,16\). We also record the diagonal Sturm bound \(\lfloor k/8\rfloor\) modulo every prime \(p\) and verify its sharpness in every even weight \(k\ne2\).

title: A bound for Stieltjes constants of the Riemann zeta function
summary: The coefficients appearing in the Laurent expansion of the Riemann zeta function are known as the Stieltjes constants and are denoted by $γ_n$. Several authors, including Berndt, Matsuoka, Williams and Zhang, and Saad Eddin, have investigated upper bounds for $|γ_n|$, with the best known result due to Pauli and Saidak \cite{MR4671618}. In 2003, based on numerical evidence, Kreminski \cite{MR1972742} conjectured that Matsuoka's bound \cite{MR827790} could be considerably improved. Motivated by this conjecture, we employ the saddle-point method to derive an asymptotic formula for the Stieltjes constants, with the saddle point expressed explicitly in terms of the Lambert $W$-function. The resulting formula yields an asymptotic upper bound of the correct order of magnitude. Moreover, the resulting bound is consistent with the conjecture of Farr, Pauli, and Saidak \cite{MR4280128}.

title: On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh
summary: Let $Π$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $ρ$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $ρ$ on the $Π$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $ρ$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $ρ$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\barρ$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.

title: Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
summary: We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $Ω$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the

title: Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
summary: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q

title: Congruences modulo powers of $2$ and $3$ for Lin's function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
summary: Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Confirming a conjecture of Singh and Barman (2025), Tang (2026) recently proved that $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{2m-1}n)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+1}}$ for all $m\geq1$ and $n\geq0$. Using elementary techniques, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{m+2}n)$, and we use them to determine $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ modulo one further power of $2$. More precisely, we show that the quotient of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ by the relevant power of $2$ is odd exactly when $n$ is an odd square, or $2$, $3$ or $6$ times an odd square, depending on $k$. title: Exact-Order Mellin Transfer and Prime-Support Filtrations
summary: We establish a unified exact-order Mellin transfer principle that converts the multiplicity of a critical Mellin pole into arithmetic prime-support depth. For an exact-order Möbius transform in lattice dimension $\ell$, a base pole of order $r$ at $s=\ell/2$ satisfies \[ \ord_{s=\ell/2}\widehat{\mathscr P_{N,\ell}H}=ω(N)-r. \] The complete Jordan--Mellin jet is explicit, and its first surviving coefficient selects the canonical weight $W(N)=\prod_{p\mid N}\log p$. After the corresponding jet normalization, this weight governs a kernel-independent moving-support law and a mod-Poisson regime. With simultaneous splitting marks in finite Galois extensions, the same weight yields a multivariate polynomial whose mixed coefficients are reciprocal compositum degrees; it recovers pairwise intersection degrees and, under a full-rank hypothesis, also governs the coupled saddle and large-deviation g

title: A two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erdős-Moser equation and Erdős's 1949 problem
summary: We give a two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erdős--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$. Writing $m=k/\log 2+3/2+γ_m/m$, Gallot, Moree and Zudilin showed that a solution yields a convergent of $\log 2/(2N)$, for a known divisor $N$ of $k$, followed by a large partial quotient. We show that an explicit two-sided estimate for $γ_m$, from our earlier centre-of-mass work, restricts this partial quotient, for each value of $\gcd(k/N,2m-3)$, to two consecutive values, or to three in the exceptional case that an integer lies in an explicit interval of relative length $O(1/m)$. This excludes the first index left open by their computation and, without extending their continued-fraction computation, raises the lower bound for a nontrivial solution from $m>2.71\cdot 10^{1667658416}$ to $m>6.26\cdot 10^{1667658425}$. The same criterion gives an effective form of the asymptotic res

title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
summary: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

title: Robust Estimators for Stochastic Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
summary: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) methods are popular for solving stochastic optimization problems, with model-based methods being a practically successful class of DFO algorithm. In most existing works, sufficiently accurate objective estimates (used for model construction and to test for sufficient decrease) are constructed by taking a sample mean of several noisy evaluations. In this work, we demonstrate that using robust estimators (specifically the median, trimmed mean, and median-of-means) can improve the sample complexity of model-based DFO methods. Our numerical results demonstrate that robust estimators are also a practical choice for algorithm implementations.

title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
summary: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We

title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective on Optimal Control
summary: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate th

title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
summary: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic

title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
summary: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
summary: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations

title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
summary: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
summary: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approxima

title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
summary: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control prob

title: Service location flexibility in dynamic vehicle routing
summary: Parcel lockers and delivery robots let a vehicle serve customers at nearby locations. We study this service location flexibility in the dynamic traveling repairman problem, where a single vehicle may serve each demand anywhere within a radius $r$ of its location. Arrivals form a Poisson process, demand locations are independent and uniform in the unit square, and on-site service times are i.i.d. with uniformly bounded second moments, where the radius $r$ may vary across systems as the on-site load $ρ$ tends to one. In this heavy-traffic regime, the optimal mean system time is of order $(1-ρ)^{-1}(1+\min\{1/r,1/(1-ρ)\})$, compared with $(1-ρ)^{-2}$ without service location flexibility [BvR91, PFB11]. Thus, flexibility reduces the order of optimal mean system time when $r$ stays fixed or shrinks more slowly than $1-ρ$. Moreover, when $r$ is on the order of $1-ρ$ or larger, the vehicle can

title: An augmented generalized factorization bound for generalized maximum-entropy sampling
summary: Li proposed an augmented factorization upper bound for use in branch-and-bound (B&B) algorithms aimed at the maximum entropy sampling problem (MESP). This bound improves on the factorization bound for MESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. GMESP, which selects $s$ of $n$ variables so as to maximize the product of the $t$ greatest eigenvalues of the corresponding principal submatrix of the covariance matrix, is a generalization of MESP (the case $t=s$), and the factorization bound for MESP generalizes to GMESP. We extend the augmentation technique of Li to improve on the generalized factorization bound for GMESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. We derive fundamental properties of the augmented bound, and we develop primal--dual constructions for use within B&B. We give checkable conditions under which the relaxation can be solved in closed form,

title: An $O(n^{-1/2})$ remainder for the Chow--Robbins stopping boundary
summary: We sharpen the asymptotic approximation to the optimal stopping boundary in the Chow--Robbins game, proving the inverse-square-root remainder conjectured by Elton. The proof combines an exactly harmonic integral for simple random walk with a Catalan first-passage renewal identity. Averaging the stopping defect over one spatial period removes its leading lattice dependence, and a coupling of states at equal depth transfers this cancellation to the renewal sum. Consequently, the explicit integer stopping rule can fail at no more than a constant times the square root of the number of observation times.

title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
summary: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min--max--min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offsh

title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
summary: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to bot

title: Distributed Time-Varying Resource Allocation in Open Networks
summary: We consider the problem of distributed resource allocation over a team of agents whose active membership changes over time. Each agent's allocation evolves according to its own temporal dynamics, while a shared equality constraint couples all active agents at every instant. For the case of quadratic local objectives, we show that the optimal solution is characterized by a linear system whose coefficient matrix couples a block-tridiagonal temporal structure with a block-diagonal Laplacian capturing the time-varying communication graph. Building on this structure, we develop a distributed forward-backward sweeping algorithm in which each agent resolves its own temporal coupling through a local forward-backward sweep, while the shared resource constraint is resolved through a distributed consensus iteration that is feasible at every iteration. title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
summary: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stabilit

title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
summary: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for

title: Transformers with Signatures: Towards Universal In-Context Learning in Path Space
summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables transformers to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations without updating their parameters. However, theoretical guarantees for transformers remain limited in general, and elusive in particular when target responses depend nonlinearly on the evolution of observed paths. We establish an ICL framework for path space, using path signature features. Building on the universal linear approximation property of signatures, we construct explicitly a causal softmax transformer with two attention heads per layer that emulates in-context Lasso. Under sparse signature approximation and suitable moment and concentration conditions, we establish finite-sample prediction error bounds. Our analysis goes beyond the IID data setting in the existing ICL theory, allowing dependence among demonstrations and the query. Experiments on in-context sparse recovery, nonlinear path re

title: A Unified View of Operator Splitting and Interior-Point Methods
summary: First-order splitting and interior-point methods offer contrasting computational trade-offs for convex conic quadratic programs, yet their linear systems look remarkably similar. We make this connection precise through the Moreau slack, an unconstrained variable from which multipliers and (ordinary) slacks satisfying exact or barrier-perturbed complementarity are recovered. The remaining feasibility equations define a unified residual whose roots are KKT points at zero barrier parameter and central-path points at positive barrier parameter. Applying splitting to this residual yields projection methods at zero barrier parameter and barrier splitting at positive parameter; Newton's method in the latter setting gives an implicit interior-point method. title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
summary: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Soft-Constrained AC-OPF in Multiphase Distribution Systems
summary: This paper presents a self-supervised learning framework for fast, soft-constrained AC optimal power flow (OPF) in unbalanced multiphase distribution systems. The soft AC-OPF objective balances operating cost, renewable energy curtailment, and penalties for violating operating limits. A neural network predicts distributed energy resource (DER) setpoints conditioned on operating conditions, switch configurations, and objective weights. The predicted setpoints are then processed through a DER projection and differentiable AC power flow to enforce device limits and network equalities. The framework is trained by directly minimizing the AC-OPF objective, without optimal-solution labels. Experiments on 123-, 240-, and 906-bus systems yield mean objective gaps of 0.32%, 0.92%, and 0.56%, respectively, relative to IPOPT, across wide operating ranges. title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
summary: Organizations use large language models (LLMs) to classify jobs that differ in uncertainty and the cost of errors. Querying additional models may improve accuracy, but it also incurs fees and increases congestion at shared servers. We study congestion-aware adaptive routing (CAAR) policies that adapt model selection and stopping decisions to observed outputs while accounting for the steady-state congestion they generate. The objective is to minimize the long-run average cost of misclassification penalties, query fees, and holding costs. We can represent CAAR policies as a mixture of decision trees, and derive exact holding costs for first-come-first-served servers with exponential service times and processor-sharing servers with general service times. title: Convergence of potential-preserving annealed Sinkhorn algorithm
summary: The annealed Sinkhorn algorithm is an iterative method for approximating solutions of optimal transport problems, in which the entropic regularisation parameter is progressively decreased. As this parameter decreases, one may preserve either the multiplicative scaling factors or the corresponding dual potentials. We study the potential-preserving iterates under positive, non-increasing regularisation schedules tending to zero. We prove that, if the schedule is non-summable, the iterates admit a subsequence converging to a solution of the corresponding optimal transport problem. The non-summability condition is sharp, as for every summable schedule in this class we construct an example in which the iterates converge to a plan violating the prescribed source marginal. title: On convergence rate bounds for Markovian push-sum algorithms
summary: In this work we establish an upper bound on the almost sure convergence rate of a broad class of push-sum algorithms, more precisely for those where message passing events follow a Markovian dynamics, or a Hidden Markov Model. In this context, having a computationally accessible quantity at hand is of top priority; we thus formulate tools to cut down the complexity of obtaining the stated bound. Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.

title: Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs
summary: We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/ε^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+ε)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $ε>0$ to $1/ε,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/ε$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.

title: Random Feature Neural Networks for Stochastic Optimal Control
summary: Random feature neural networks (RFNNs) sample their hidden parameters once and train only the output layer. We analyze RFNNs as feedback policies for finite-horizon stochastic control with trajectory-dependent objectives. A policy change alters later states, so the error that matters is the objective error of the induced trajectory rather than a pointwise regression error. We extend the quantitative random-feature approximation theory for PDE solutions and nonlinear regression to feedback control. We investigate the objective error of an RFNN policy through two sources, approximation of the policy by random features and estimation of the objective from finitely many paths. A stability estimate for the controlled trajectory turns a policy error into an objective error. title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors
summary: Value iteration is an important tool for approximating solutions of infinite-horizon optimal control problems, but in practice it is never carried out exactly: value functions are represented by finite-dimensional approximators, and the iteration is stopped after finitely many steps. This paper analyzes which closed-loop guarantees remain under these limitations for continuous-time nonlinear systems. We consider a value iteration scheme in which each iteration solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem with the previous iterate as terminal cost, and the associated controller applies the optimal input of this problem over each horizon in a sampled-data fashion. We show that if the convergence tolerance and the approximation error are small enough, the controller asymptotically stabilizes the system on sublevel sets of the computed iterate, and provide a suboptimality bound. title: A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming
summary: We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. The barrier has self-concordance parameter $\widetilde{O}(m)$, so short-step interior-point methods require only $\widetilde O(\sqrt m)$ iterations. We also show that our matrix Lee-Sidford barrier can be implemented efficiently by developing a randomized algorithm that solves SDPs with $m\leq n$ to accuracy $ε$ in $(n^{ω+o(1)}+n^2m^{3/2+o(1)})\operatorname{polylog}(1/ε)$ time, where $ω\leq 9/4$ is the matrix multiplication exponent, achieving the fastest known running time in this regime.

title: Learning and Dynamic Route Recommendation Under Unknown Traveler Compliance and Road Conditions
summary: Route planning during evacuations and other large-scale egress operations is inherently dynamic: the planner's recommendations affect future congestion on the roads, influence whether travelers accept their guidance, and determine what the planner can learn from the travelers' actual route choices. In this paper, we consider stochastic dynamic route recommendation to many travelers over a finite horizon under uncertain compliance and road conditions. In each period, a planner assigns routes that lead different origins' traveler groups to safe destinations, and travelers either follow the recommendation or revert to a preferred route. We model compliance using a logistic model and learn its unknown coefficients from observed route travel. title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
summary: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. title: Proper and Optimal Scoring Rules for Risk-Averse Agents
summary: Scoring rules are used to elicit probabilistic beliefs through payments that depend on reports and realised outcomes. We ask how these rules should be designed to induce truthful reporting and incentivise costly information acquisition when the agent is risk averse. For agents with entropic risk preferences in finite state spaces, we characterise proper scoring rules through an exponential transformation, derive optimal structures for information acquisition under bounded payments, and obtain explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case. The risk-neutral limit preserves properness and, in the binary case, optimality, while recovering the optimal betting structure for nonbinary states. For optimal design in the binary model, it suffices to focus on rules whose associated concave function is affine on each side of the prior. title: Fast Gradient-Based Framework for Spatial and Length Optimization of Geothermal Borehole Fields
summary: Common analytical design tools for Borehole Heat Exchanger (BHE) fields size the total drilling length for a given layout but do not optimize the positions of the boreholes. We introduce a framework (OptiGeoS) for the simultaneous, gradient-based optimization of the borehole length and the continuous borehole positions under groundwater advection. It couples the Moving Finite Line Source model with local BHE equations and evaluates the temporal convolutions by Fast Fourier Transforms. The gradients with respect to the length and the positions are computed analytically. A flow-dependent Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation confines each borehole to its own cell, which enforces the spatial separation and provides advection-informed layouts. title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
summary: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.

title: MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
summary: Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. title: Silver rate is sharp for gradient descent
summary: We determine the minimax convergence rate of gradient descent with predetermined real stepsizes on smooth convex functions up to an absolute constant factor. Let $p=\log_2(1+\sqrt{2})\approx 1.2716$. We prove that for every $L>0$, every integer $n\ge1$ and every stepsize schedule $h\in\mathbb{R}^n$ there exist a convex $L$-smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ in some finite dimension $d$, a minimizer $x_\star$ of $f$ and an initial point $x_0\neq x_\star$ such that the iterate $x_n$ of gradient descent with stepsizes $h$ satisfies $(f(x_n)-f(x_\star))/(L\|x_0-x_\star\|^2)\ge c\,n^{-p}$ with an absolute constant $c>0$. This lower bound matches the $O(n^{-p})$ upper bounds achieved by silver-type stepsize schedules and establishes the optimality of the silver rate up to an absolute constant factor. title: The response field approach to path integral control
summary: This paper investigates non-linear path integral control problems within the response field formalism of nonequilibrium field theory. The aim of this work is exploratory, based on the identification of correspondences between backward adjoint processes and the response field of non-equilibrium statistical physics, whose properties have not been set out in an optimal control setting. The response field is found to play an analogous role to the backward adjoint process under the stochastic maximum principle. In particular, the gradient of the optimal cost-to-go at the initial time, which is proportional to the optimal control, is given by the average of the response field at the initial time. title: First-Order Information from Noisy Comparison Oracles
summary: We study stochastic and deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization problems where neither the functions nor their derivatives can be computed or estimated and the only information about the objective is available via pairwise comparisons. We focus on a specific model of smooth comparison oracles, as in the Bradley-Terry and Thurstone models, in which the probability of a correct comparison depends smoothly on the function-value gap. We investigate what first-order information can be obtained from such comparisons in deterministic and stochastic settings, and how many comparisons are needed to estimate it. We show that the first-order information that such comparisons provide is a fixed positive multiple of the gradient of the objective. We propose a random-direction estimator of the comparison gradient and analyze its bias and variance. It reaches mean-squared error $\varepsilon^2$

title: The Optimal D.C. Bound Is Dominated by the Reciprocal of the Lovász Theta Number
summary: We resolve a question left open by Anstreicher and Burer (J. Global Optim. 33, 299--312, 2005). For the standard quadratic formulation of the stability number, we prove that the optimal difference-of-convex (D.C.) bound is at most the reciprocal of the Lovász theta number. The dominance is strict whenever the Lovász theta number is not exact.

title: When Simpler Beats Learned: Dual-Weighted Sampling vs. Machine Learning for the Pricing Subproblem in Graph Coloring
summary: The graph coloring problem can be solved to optimality by branch-and-price (B&P), but its performance hinges on the column generation (CG) step, where each iteration requires solving a maximum weight independent set (MWIS) pricing problem. The state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) pricing heuristic follows a prediction-sampling paradigm: a learned model scores each vertex of a graph, and independent sets are sampled from the induced distribution. We observe, however, that the scoring procedure does not need to be learned, and critically assess the role of ML by replacing the learned scores with the dual solution of the restricted master problem, resulting in Dual-Weighted Sampling, a proposed lightweight alternative that requires no feature engineering or training. title: From Distributional to Temporal Interactions in McKean--Vlasov Games and Control
summary: The paper examines the relation between time and population in stochastic games and control. The idea is to substitute the interaction described via the population law with the interaction described via the occupation measure of a single self-interacting trajectory. Thus we study how McKean--Vlasov fixed point games and Mean Field Control problems compare with their resulting self-interacting counterparts. Assuming appropriate dissipativity and regularity conditions, we find that the ergodic costs, value functions and optimal feedback sets are identical, and the fixed point equilibria are equivalent. In addition, we obtain uniform bounds on both trajectories and costs for finite horizon problems. title: Continuous-Time LQR from a Single Discrete-Time Off-Policy Batch
summary: We study discounted continuous-time linear--quadratic regulation (LQR) with unknown drift parameters and additive noise, using a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions. Discrete-time methods target a policy tied to the training interval, while shortening this interval can make learning from finite data more sensitive to noise. Learning an accurate continuous-time controller therefore requires balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while preserving stability throughout policy improvement. We develop a drift-only policy iteration algorithm, termed PhiBE-PI, using one quadratic state--action critic for policy evaluation and explicit greedy improvement. Reusing the batch makes later policies depend on the data. title: Scaled Relative Graph Separation for Unbounded Nonlinear Systems
summary: We investigate stability analysis of one-channel nonlinear feedback systems based on the recent notion of scaled relative graph (SRG). Our focus is on the SRG separation in the complex plane for feedback stability analysis that involves possibly unbounded open-loop nonlinear systems. Subject to a technical assumption, a homotopy-based SRG separation theorem is developed as the main result, where the incremental directed gap is utilized as a key instrument to quantify robust feedback stability along the homotopy path. Doing so enables us to incorporate commonly used integrators as unbounded systems in the SRG-based framework. Specializations of the main result to linear systems, along with illustrative examples, are also provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.

title: Group Buying through Bankruptcy Rules: Cost Sharing and Endogenous Pricing
summary: Group buying allows independent buyers to pool their demand and benefit from quantity discounts that would not be available to them individually. While collective purchasing reduces total procurement costs, it raises a fundamental allocation question: how should the resulting savings be distributed among heterogeneous buyers? We address this question by integrating cost-allocation and bankruptcy approaches into a unified group-buying framework. Starting from a continuous quantity discount function, we examine cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and develop an endogenous pricing representation in which each buyer's effective discount may depend on the demand profile of the entire group. We then establish a connection between group buying and bankruptcy theory by interpreting the aggregate savings from cooperation as the estate and each buyer's potential savings as its claim. title: Small-time global exact controllability of nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with bilinear controls
summary: We study nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with nonlinearity $κ|ψ|^{2p}ψ$, a fixed smooth real potential $V$, and bilinear controls. The proof combines two ingredients: the approximate controllability between nowhere vanishing states from our companion paper, and a new mechanism that steers any nonzero initial state to a nowhere vanishing state in arbitrarily small time. title: Near-Optimal Smooth Convex Optimization with a Comparison Oracle
summary: We study the minimization of a convex $d$-dimensional function with $L$-Lipschitz gradient when the only available information is a comparison oracle that reports which of two points has the smaller objective value. title: Controlled nonstationary G-diffusions: dynamic programming, weighted Harris contraction and entrance risk
summary: We study controlled nonstationary \(G\)-diffusions in a canonical-law formulation of covariance uncertainty. The principal structural result is an abstract weighted Harris--oscillation contraction theorem for translation-covariant nonlinear evolution families. A Lyapunov estimate for a dominating terminal-perturbation bound and a local space--time oscillation estimate for differences imply exponential contraction in a weighted quotient norm, without positive homogeneity, subadditivity or convexity. For elementary sample-and-hold feedback controls and a rectangular family of martingale laws, we construct a measurable controlled state map and prove deterministic- and stopped-time dynamic programming principles for the robust lower value. title: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies
summary: Designing simple inventory policies becomes increasingly difficult as operational features and system configurations expand. We develop an Agentic Inventory-Policy Discovery System based on explicitly defined simple operational formula (SOF) policy and template classes. Large language models (LLMs) revise symbolic structures, while a numerical engine fits parameters separately for each instance and evaluates the induced policies. Multicriteria parent selection, state-specific operational diagnostics, and reusable symbolic motifs guide structural evolution. A three-stage progression develops shared templates across instances and configurations with varying state dimensions. Experiments on 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions cover lead times, perishability, their combination, and lead times with limited customer patience. title: Universal Extra-Gradient Method for Stochastic Variational Inequalities
summary: We study the stochastic Extra-Gradient Method (EGM) for solving a stochastic variational inequality (VI) over a compact convex set. The main assumption is $(δ, L)$-continuity of the VI mapping, which includes Hölder mappings and their linear combinations. We develop new adaptive, line-search-free step-size rules for stochastic EGM. These rules can be interpreted as enhanced AdaGrad-type updates and require no prior knowledge of either the continuity modulus of the VI mapping or the variance of the stochastic oracle. The resulting methods are universal and attain the best complexity bound among the admissible continuity regimes. title: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems
summary: We prove memory/query-complexity tradeoff lower bounds for the feasibility problem, where the goal is to find a point within an $ε$-ball hidden in the unit $d$-dimensional ball, with access to a separation oracle. This problem admits three regimes: the low-accuracy regime $ε\geq 1/\sqrt d$ where memory does not play a role, the medium-accuracy regime $1/\sqrt d\geq ε\geq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ where prior works identified strong memory/query-complexity separations, and the high-accuracy regime $ε\leq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ for which much less is known. In this regime, low-memory algorithms with significantly faster convergence rates than gradient descent have been developed in [BZJ24]: for accuracy $ε$ and any $δ\in[0,1]$, these require $d^{1+δ}\ln \frac1ε$ memory bits and use $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{O(d^{1-δ})}$ oracle queries. title: Learned spatial opportunity cost admission for ride-hailing with calibrated thresholds
summary: Ride-hailing operators must decide whether to accept a request before observing future demand. Serving a ride earns revenue and changes where and when the vehicle can serve again. We develop learned spatial opportunity cost admission for a centrally managed fleet. The policy estimates demand from past requests and solves a rolling mean-demand plan. Dual prices account for using a vehicle at its origin and returning it to service at its destination. With positive regularization, the policy accepts a request when its planned service fraction reaches a common threshold. We fix the regularization parameter and select the threshold using validation revenue. For one vehicle on a single route, we derive the exact range of thresholds that attain optimal expected revenue. title: Finite-Dimensional Internal Stabilization of Steady States of the Gray-Scott System
summary: In this article, we establish the local exponential stabilization of every steady state of the Gray-Scott system with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, other than the trivial state $(0,1)^{\top}$, at any prescribed decay rate by finite-dimensional feedback controls supported in an arbitrary nonempty open subset of the domain and acting only on the first equation of the system. Our approach does not require the steady state to be spatially constant and accommodates non-self-adjoint linearizations with variable coefficients. The proof combines unique continuation, a nonvanishing property of the steady-state coupling, the Fattorini-Hautus condition, and Riccati-based feedback.

title: Optimal isotropic three-material conducting composites with an ideal conductor, in the plane and in space.Bounds and optimal structures
summary: The paper describes an optimal isotropic three-dimensional, three-material conducting composite. One material is an ideal conductor, the volume fractions are prescribed, and the objective is to minimize the effective conductivity over all admissible layouts. We first derive a lower bound for the effective conductivity as a function of the material properties and volume fractions. The composite energy is bounded below by a constrained polyconvex envelope, where quadratic and cubic null Lagrangians are imposed through Lagrange multipliers. We further assume that the fields in optimal structures are positive semidefinite. Together with the use of the cubic null Lagrangian, this assumption makes the bound exact. The development of the Performance Estimation Problems framework led to even deeper understanding and allowed computer-assisted derivation of exact worst-case guarantees. Due to convex nature of PEP programs, the framework is not applicable for systems that involve non-convex constraints. This includes a wide range of non-standard assumptions, some of them are highly relevant for practice such as generalized smoothness. summary: The proximal slack update in an augmented Lagrangian method for semidefinite complementarity constraints requires a joint matrix projection. title: Sharp Convergence of Extended Douglas--Rachford Splitting with Variable Relaxation
summary: We establish a sharp convergence theory for extended Douglas--Rachford splitting when the first operator is maximally monotone and the second is a convex subdifferential on a real Hilbert space. The resolvent stepsizes may be chosen independently, and the relaxation parameter may depend on the current and past iterates. For fixed stepsizes $α,β>0$, let $\vartheta=\min\{2,2α/β\}$. Assuming the sum of the operators has a zero, we prove weak convergence under $0<θ_k\le\vartheta$ and $\sum_kθ_k(\vartheta-θ_k)=\infty$. Within these pointwise bounds, the divergence condition is also necessary for a universal convergence guarantee when the relaxation sequence is prescribed in advance. Constant relaxation recovers the exact range $0<θ<\vartheta$, resolving a conjecture of Nilsson, Åkerman, and Giselsson. title: Feedback Exact Controllability of the Nonlinear Diffusion Equation with Controller in Coefficients
summary: One designs a feedback controller for semilinear parabolic equations with controller in diffusion coefficients which steers the initial data y0 in a given state y1 in a finite time.

title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
summary: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. title: Construction of Universal Safe Stabilizing Formulas with Weighted Centroid Methodology
summary: Control Lyapunov and control barrier functions ensure stability and safety, respectively, by imposing state-dependent affine constraints on the control input. Controller design can therefore be viewed as the problem of selecting an admissible input from the set defined by these constraints. This paper adopts this perspective and develops a weighted-centroid methodology for constructing explicit feedback formulas that are provably smooth. The selection method relies on the fact that weighted centroids of a convex set lie within the set. We establish conditions on the weight functions that guarantee smoothness and continuity for several classes of constraints, including single constraints, mirrored constraints, linearly independent multiple constraints, and two-constraint Gaussian constructions. title: The dimension of optimal plans in multi-marginal optimal transport
summary: For general cost functions, we determine the maximal dimension on which solutions to the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with absolutely continuous marginals are concentrated. The dimension is obtained via a novel characteristic integer associated with the Hessian of the cost function. Applications are given to important examples of multi-marginal problems like Wasserstein barycenters, Wasserstein cubic splines and Brenier's generalized Euler equations.

title: Mirror Descent at the Edge of Stability
summary: In many deep learning settings, gradient descent has been shown to operate at the edge of stability -- a regime where the largest eigenvalue of the loss Hessian hovers around $2/η$. We study this phenomenon in mirror descent, a generalization of gradient descent. As mirror descent is non-Euclidean, existing explanations of the edge of stability phase do not extend to this setting. We generalize the existing notion of sharpness to introduce mirror sharpness, which measures the curvature of the loss with respect to the mirror potential. Empirically, we observe that the mirror sharpness hovers slightly above the $2/η$ threshold. Furthermore, we derive a dual central flow ODE for mirror descent that models iterates in continuous time at the onset of edge of stability. title: An Exact Penalty Method for Large-Scale Equality-Constrained Nonlinear Optimization
summary: We present an exact penalty method for equality-constrained nonlinear optimization. Our approach transforms the smooth, constrained problem into a sequence of nonsmooth, unconstrained problems by penalizing the constraint violation by its Euclidean norm. An outer loop updates the penalty parameter and the subproblem tolerances, while an inner loop solves each penalized subproblem with a quadratic regularization method. The method also includes a local infeasibility detection mechanism, an extrapolation strategy for warm-starting subproblems, and nonmonotone acceptance rules. We establish global convergence to first-order stationary points under a bounded penalty parameter assumption, with a worst-case complexity of \(\mathcal{O}(|\log ε|\,ε^{-2})\) inner iterations. title: Parallel batch scheduling for optimizing hospital sterilization operations: arc-flow formulations, column generation and Lagrangian heuristics for flowtime minimization
summary: In a recent work by Schlembach et al., the problem of optimally managing sterilization operations in hospitals has been modeled as a machine scheduling problem with parallel batch processing and minimum flowtime objective, and heuristically solved by column generation. We draw upon this approach, developing arc-flow formulations and related column-generation procedures, using an exact dynamic programming algorithm to solve the pricing problems. We further derive Lagrangian relaxations based on minimum cost flows and shortest paths, with subgradient optimization and the volume algorithm guiding batch generation. A makespan bound for schedules minimizing total flow time provides a finite horizon when no operational limit is known. title: Robust Pair--Restricted Lipschitz Regression with Global--Local Transfer
summary: We develop a robust pair-restricted Lipschitz regression framework for grouped longitudinal data represented as finite trajectories in a space equipped with a prescribed or learned pseudometric. title: A feasible point method for derivative-free linearly constrained optimization
summary: This paper presents a framework for linearly constrained derivative-free optimization (DFO) in which the original objective function is evaluated only at feasible points. The method first analyzes the linear constraint system using certificates of infeasibility and implied activity to detect infeasibility or a singleton feasible set, or, when the feasible set has positive dimension, to identify the affine subspace spanned by the feasible set and obtain an equivalent reduced representation with a strictly feasible base point. It then transforms the resulting reduced problem into an unconstrained optimization problem by means of a pointed feasible retraction and an exact penalty function. title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
summary: A fundamental question in reinforcement learning is how many sampled transitions are needed to learn a near-optimal policy, and whether direct policy optimization can attain this statistical limit. To answer this question, we consider natural policy gradient (NPG), a widely used policy optimization method. We study tabular finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) with known rewards and unknown horizon-dependent transition kernels, accessed through a generative model. Our sample-based NPG algorithms update the policy by backward sweeps and do not estimate transition probabilities. Under three different batch-size and step size schedules, we establish last-iterate guarantees with sample complexity $\widetilde O(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$, where $S$, $A$, and $H$ denote the number of states, the number of actions, and the horizon length, respectively. title: Neural Schrödinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
summary: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schrödinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.

title: Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
summary: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
summary: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chvátal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. title: An ADMM-Based Approach to the Large-Scale Geomagnetically Induced Current Blocker Placement Problem
summary: We propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based approach for addressing the challenge of determining placements for geomagnetically induced current (GIC) blocking devices on large-scale transmission networks. Traditional formulations of this placement problem lead to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) that are difficult for state-of-the-art MINLP solvers, which often struggle to exploit problem structure and fail to produce high-quality solutions on large systems. To overcome these challenges, the proposed method employs a three-block ADMM decomposition enhanced with (i) partial linearization of the GIC-related nonlinearities, supported by conditions guaranteeing exactness, and (ii) heterogeneous penalty parameters that significantly accelerate convergence to high-quality local solutions. title: Jointly Recovering Destination Attractiveness and Spatial Preference Segments from Observed Tours via Inverse Optimization
summary: Quantifying destination attractiveness by counting visitors, the most direct approach, can favor accessible sites and understate destinations that travelers reach at considerable cost. Preferences may also cut across a priori socio-demographic groupings. This study develops an inverse optimization framework that recovers destination attractiveness and preference segments jointly from observed multi-stop trip tours and generalized travel costs, without prespecifying tour-level segment assignments or imposing a parametric distribution on the unexplained part of utility. Representing each destination visit as a link in an extended network turns utility-maximizing tour choice into an inverse shortest paths problem. title: Concentration of the half-space Airy line ensembles
summary: The half-space Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{hs};\varpi}$ ($\varpi\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$), introduced in arXiv:2505.01798, arXiv:2601.04546, are natural analogues of the Airy line ensemble and are expected to arise as universal scaling limits of models in the half-space Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) class. We prove that, at each fixed time $t\geq 0$, the height of the $k$th curve concentrates about $-(3πk/2)^{2/3}$ on the scale $k^{-1/3}\sqrt{\log(2+k)}$, with exponential tails.

title: From invasion to replacement: excursions of the Moran model
summary: An excursion-theoretic description of the continuous-time Moran model with recurrent mutation is developed. Exploiting its birth--death structure, the killed Moran process is characterized through its Green function, resolvent, Laplace transforms of hitting times, and spectral decomposition. The characterization of the killed process leads to a boundary-switching excursion representation in which returning excursions correspond to unsuccessful invasions of an allelic type, whilst switching excursions describe population-wide allelic replacement. title: Frieze's $ζ(3)$ and the Avram--Bertsimas constant under Haar conjugation

title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
summary: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. title: An easy proof of transience of one-dimensional Rademacher walk with power weights
summary: Using a version of a local limit theorem, we provide an easy proof that the Rademacher random walk with step sizes $n^α$, $α>1/2$, is transient.

title: Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
summary: We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. summary: We develop a boundary comparison method for Gaussian fluctuations of optimization costs on planar random points, including traveling-salesman length, minimum perfect-matching length, and the Held--Karp relaxation. Our criterion requires the difference between the changes in the full and local costs caused by the same replacement to be controlled at the boundary scale, allowing a smaller-order $L^2$ excess. Under this condition, the centered difference between the total cost and the sum of independent cell costs vanishes in $L^2$. title: A proof of the chemical recurrence conjecture in two dimensions
summary: At the microscopic level, the dynamics of a network of chemical reactions can be modeled, in the well-mixed case, as a continuous-time Markov chain. This process counts the number of particles in each of the $d$ species as a function of time, and its state-dependent, polynomial jump rates are determined by the structure of the underlying reaction graph. Networks of chemical reactions whose reaction graphs are the union of strongly connected components are called \emph{weakly reversible}. The long-standing \emph{chemical recurrence conjecture} states that if a network is weakly reversible, then the associated Markov chain is positive recurrent. We prove this conjecture for $d=2$.

Thus the bias rescales the horizontal and vertical coordinates of the unbiased limit. The topology of convergence records loop multiplicities and the order of traversal around each loop, up to reversal. title: Matching Under Metric Privacy
summary: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $Θ\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. title: Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions
summary: We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli (2013); a proof of polynomial mixing remained one of the major challenges in the field. title: Fuzzy vectors from first and second moments: Affine consistency, carrying and sparsest realizations
summary: When the probability law of a random vector cannot be identified, its mean and possibly singular covariance can often still be elicited. summary: We study Gaussian approximation over all coordinate rectangles for coordinatewise self-normalized sums of iid centered random vectors. title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
summary: Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different gr

title: Gibbs-type allelic partitions of $Λ$-coalescents: a rigidity theorem
summary: Let $Π^θ_n$ be the allelic partition induced by a $Λ$-coalescent with mutation rate $θ$ under the infinitely-many-alleles model. We characterise the finite measures $Λ$ for which the EPPF of $Π^θ_n$ is of Gibbs type: the only possibility is $Λ=c\,δ_0$, corresponding to Kingman's coalescent and the Ewens sampling formula. Starting from Möhle's recursion, we derive its EPPF form and organise the Gibbs constraints by the difference between sample size and number of blocks. The first two sectors yield identities valid for every $Λ$; the next gives a scalar obstruction and a forward recursion for the Hausdorff moments of $Λ$. Complete monotonicity settles the zero-index case, while positive indices are excluded by an exact polynomial-positivity certificate at sample size six. Consequently, every non-Kingman allelic law fails the standard Gibbs factorisation on a sample of size six. We also de
