title: Closed-Form Formula for $d_{\mathrm{critical}}(a_0)$ in Large Fully Connected Power Grids
summary: Kadloor and Santhi (arXiv:1011.4098) modeled cascading failures in a large fully connected power grid by a coupled four-variable recursion for the minimum surviving load $a_n$, the mean failed load $μ_{n-1}$, the redistributed load $\mathcal{D}_n$, and the stagewise failure probability $p_n$. They noted that the recursion was not tractable and identified the critical disturbance $d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ by simulation. We show that the recursion telescopes exactly into a one-dimensional monotone map $a_{n+1} = g(a_n)$. This yields the threshold in closed form: $1 - a_0 = d_{\mathrm{critical}}\,(1 + \ln(1 + 1/d_{\mathrm{critical}}))$, or explicitly in terms of the lower branch $W_{-1}$ of the Lambert W function. We prove a sharp dichotomy. For $d_m \le d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ the cascade halts with limiting load $a_0 + d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ at criticality and surviving fraction $1/(1 + d_{\

title: Wigner Matrices and the $α$-Determinant
summary: For a Hermitian Wigner matrix $M_n$ and complex $α$ with $|α|\leq1$, we study the $α$-characteristic polynomial $\det_α(zI-M_n)$, which interpolates between the characteristic polynomial ($α=-1$) and the permanental polynomial ($α=1$). Assuming finite fourth moments off the diagonal and second moments on it, we show that this polynomial, normalized by its expectation, converges in distribution off the segment $\sqrt{-α}\,[-2,2]$ to the Wick exponential of an explicit Gaussian analytic function, with the same Gaussian modes for every $α$. As consequences, all zeros lie near this segment with probability tending to one, the empirical zero measure converges to a rotated semicircle law, and analytic linear statistics of the zeros satisfy a central limit theorem. We also show that $\det_α(zI-M_n)$ is approximated, with vanishing relative error, in terms of the characteristic polynomial of $M_

title: Reflected Elastic Diffusions
summary: We study the reflected elastic diffusion (RED), the pathwise counterpart of Feller's elastic boundary condition for a one-dimensional diffusion on $[0,\infty)$ with time-homogeneous, continuous drift and diffusion coefficients. Given a diffusion $X$ reflecting at zero, we construct a Feller process $\widetilde X$ by killing $X$ at the first time its local time at zero exceeds an independent exponential random variable. We characterize the infinitesimal generator of $\widetilde X$ explicitly and prove that its domain satisfies a Robin boundary condition, thereby identifying $\widetilde X$ as a probabilistic representation of Feller's analytical characterization of the elastic boundary. title: Structure Preservation of $2$-Wasserstein Barycenters on the Real Line with Applications to Log-Concave Distributions
summary: We study to what extent the $p$-Wasserstein barycenter ($p$-WB) of arbitrary, not only finite, collections of distributions preserves their structure, focusing on shape constraints on the densities, such as monotonicity, unimodality, or log-concavity. This preservation is a generalized convexity property in Wasserstein space, which we call $p$-WB convexity. We investigate $p$-WB convexity of the families of $φ$-unimodal distributions: an absolutely continuous distribution $μ$ is $φ$-unimodal if composition with $φ$ turns a density into a concave function on the interior of the convex support of $μ$. This notion generalizes log-concavity and $s$-concave densities. We find a quantile representation of $φ$-unimodality and then use a novel closed-form expression of the quantile density function of the $2$-WB to decide on $2$-WB convexity. In higher dimensions or for $p\neq2$, we give counter

title: Density of states for random Schrödinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder
summary: We study the density of states of random Schrödinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder. Using an integration-by-parts supersymmetric representation, we prove smoothness of the density of states and Wegner estimates in the strong-disorder regime. We are particularly interested in mixed-sign correlation kernels, which serve as a toy model for the hyperbolic structures arising in the analysis of averaged squared Green's functions. Our approach applies to a broad class of correlation kernels and disorder distributions, including $α$-stable laws.

title: Solvability of one-dimensional sub-quadratic BSDEs with unbounded stochastic coefficients
summary: This study is devoted to solvability of the unbounded solutions of a class of one-dimensional sub-quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with unbounded stochastic coefficients and general time horizons. In a general sub-exponential moment integrability space linked with the stochastic coefficients, we first establish existence of an unbounded solution of the preceding BSDE when the generator $g$ has a one-sided linear growth in the state variable $y$ and a sub-quadratic growth in the state variable $z$, and then prove a comparison theorem of the unbounded solutions of such two BSDEs when either of generators satisfies an extended convexity/concavity condition in $(y,z)$ with unbounded stochastic coefficients, yielding naturally the uniqueness of the solution. Particularly, the unbounded stochastic coefficient before the state variable $y$ is supposed to take values

title: Asymptotic approximation for a certain class of statistics associated with generalized urn models
summary: The generalized urn model is defined in terms of a collection of random frequencies, which is treated as a collection of conditionally independent random variables given their sum. We consider a class of random variables that can be represented as series of functions of these frequencies. The general results concern asymptotic normality, estimates of remainder terms, and Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansions for such random variables. We then consider random variables defined in various versions of the generalized urn model. These models include the random allocation of particles of several types into finite or infinite numbers of cells, random sampling without replacement from a finite population, random coverage of a circle, random forests, and random permutations.

title: No coexistence in the two-type Richardson model when one side is stronger than the other
summary: We study the two-type Richardson model in two dimensions. We prove that there is no coexistence of the two species when their infection rates are different, establishing a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m and Pemantle from 1997. In our proof we analyze a second order approximation of the infected region and use a Mermin--Wagner style argument to push the strong type out of the weak one.

title: Local limit theorem for the Kemperman's oscillating walk
summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the local probabilities of the so-called oscillating walk on the latttice Z; this class of discrete time Markov chains was introduced by Kemperman. Our main result is a local counterpart of the convergence of a properly rescaled oscillating walk towards the corresponding skew Brownian motion. In particular, we show that the approximation of local probabilities by the density of the limiting distribution may fail in the points which are not far from zero.

title: How long must an honest confidence interval be after causal discovery? Benign and malignant weak edges
summary: After causal discovery, a confidence interval for a total effect valid uniformly over the model class must pay for structural uncertainty. We measure this price by the worst-case ratio of expected length to that of the efficient interval knowing the graph, for linear Gaussian models with a known superset of the adjacencies and k-triangle faithfulness. The global price is of order sqrt(n) once one edge can be malignant, so we study it locally, near a generic distribution with one edge absent. Our main result classifies this weak edge by Meek closures. It is benign if deleting it leaves the effect identifiable in the resulting MPDAG and Markov equivalent explanations agree; the local price is then bounded, and otherwise, for small k, of order sqrt(n). title: Bismut formula and applications for conditional McKean-Vlasov SDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
summary: We investigate the stability of Lions derivatives under transition-rate perturbations for conditional McKean-Vlasov SDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion with $H>1/2$. For bounded measurable terminal functions, we establish Lions differentiability, a Bismut formula, and a gradient estimate under bounded first-order drift derivatives with suitable Hölder regularity, without imposing additional higher-order regularity assumptions on the drift's Lions derivative. Fractional Volterra estimates accommodate switching-induced discontinuities, while the Bismut weight has a common representation in terms of the switching process for all admissible transition-rate matrices. title: Joint Cohort Laws and Mixed Cumulants with Spectral Asymptotics for Growing Gaps in Finite-Age Branching Processes
summary: We investigate the joint distribution and temporal dependence of birth cohorts in a discrete-time age-dependent branching model in which an individual may reproduce at several integer ages. Under an independent age-specific reproduction array, we derive a recursive joint probability generating function, an exact history-dependent transition kernel, and a martingale innovation representation. These identities yield explicit covariance formulae and finite coefficient recursions for mixed factorial moments and mixed cumulants. When reproduction is restricted to a finite maximum age $L$, the cohort vector admits a finite-dimensional companion-matrix representation. title: Dirichlet heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary
summary: Let $D$ be a $C^{1, η}$ open set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{B}: D\times D\to (0, \infty)$ a symmetric Borel function which blows up at the boundary of $D$. Let $\overline{X}$ be a conservative purely discontinuous Markov process on $\overline{D}$ with jump kernel $\mathcal{B}(x,y)|x-y|^{-d-α}$, $0<α<2$. In a recent paper, we obtained two-sided estimates on the transition density of $\overline{X}$. In this paper, we consider the process $X$ obtained by killing $\overline{X}$ upon approaching the boundary of $D$ or by a critical potential. We obtain sharp two-sided estimates on the transition density of $X$. The estimates capture the interplay between the blow-up rate of $\mathcal{B}$, the geometry of $D$, and killing.

title: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
summary: It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $σ(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $μ(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $μ(p)$ known as the time constant. We compute the near-critical asymptotics of the two quantities in high dimensions, showing that \begin{align*} σ^2(p) \asymp (p-p_c)^2 \qquad \text{ and } \qquad μ(p) \asymp \frac{1}{\sqrt{p-p_c}} \end{align*} for all $p>p_c$. Our results concerning the diffusivity confirm a conjecture of Biskup (2011). We also compute the asymptotic critical probabilities of slabs in the same regime, showing that $p_c( \mathbb{Z}^{d-1} \times \{0,\ldots,n\}) - p_c(\mathbb{Z}^{d}) \asymp n^{-2}$ as $n\to \infty$.

title: Coalescence and the Two-Point Covariance in the Directed Landscape
summary: In the directed landscape with Brownian terminal data, we express the spatial derivative of the two-point height covariance in terms of the probability that two geodesics coalesce before the terminal time and the exit law of a single geodesic. This formula arises as the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang scaling limit of a zero-temperature Brownian last-passage identity from our earlier work on the O'Connell-Yor polymer. To pass the coalescence probabilities to the limit, we show that two paths sharing an optimal exit almost surely lose total weight if they must stay disjoint before reaching it. At stationarity, we determine when two zero-direction semi-infinite geodesics first coalesce. We recover this distribution by differentiating the height-increment variance first in the starting separation, then in the boundary strength. title: Wavelet determinantal samplers: Optimal approximation rates adapting to regularity
summary: We construct wavelet-based determinantal samplers on manifolds and geometric graphs whose approximation rates adapt to the regularity of the observable. On a Riemannian manifold of dimension $m$, our wavelet DPPs satisfy variance reduction of order $n^{1-2s/m}$ for linear statistics of both $s$-Hölder and $H^s$ observables, where $0<s\le1$. Using these samplers, we further construct unbiased quadrature rules with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$ using at most $3n/2$ function evaluations, matching the classical optimal randomized integration exponent. For point clouds sampled from an $m$-dimensional manifold, we develop corresponding determinantal samplers on two standard classes of geometric random graphs: $\varepsilon$-graphs and symmetric $k$-nearest-neighbour graphs. title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel
summary: Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a flexible framework for modeling complex dependence structures through a covariance function, or kernel, whose parameters determine the variability, correlation, and smoothness of the underlying process. The Matérn kernel is among the most popular choices due to its flexibility in modeling different degrees of smoothness. Although the identifiability of Matérn kernel parameters under fixed-domain asymptotics is completely understood, identifiability alone does not establish the consistency or asymptotic behavior of the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) routinely used in practice. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a sharp asymptotic theory for the joint MLE of Matérn kernel parameters. title: Cumulants, Partitions, and Generalizations of Pólya's Characterization of the Normal Distribution
summary: Let $X_1,X_2$ be independent, identically distributed random variables with finite variance. Pólya (1923) proved the celebrated result that if $\sqrt{2}X_1 =^L X_1+X_2$ then $X_1$ is normally distributed. Pólya's theorem has been extended in many ways, e.g., to the case of random coefficients $R_1,R_2$ such that, under certain regularity conditions, if $(R_1^2+R_2^2)^{1/2}X_1 =^L R_1X_1+R_2X_2$, then $X_1$ is normally distributed. In this article, Pólya's theorem is generalized {\it via} the combinatorics of $Π_n$, the set-partitions of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. title: Identifiability of infinite location-scale Gaussian mixtures
summary: The problem of identifiability of the mixing measure for a location-scale mixture of Gaussian distributions is considered. We give sufficient and necessary conditions on the compact support of the mixing measure on unknown location and scale parameters for which the mixing measure's uniqueness can be guaranteed. This is achieved by an analytic and probabilistic framework that characterizes the null space of the Gaussian mixing operator, a linear mapping that transforms a space of mixing measures with compact support into that of Gaussian mixture distributions. This framework exposes a fruitful connection between the infinite location-scale Gaussian mixtures and the exiting behavior of a space-time backward Brownian motion from a compact domain, as well as the nature of the support of the heat potential associated with such a stochastic process. title: Mixing time and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the torus shuffle
summary: The torus shuffle acts on an $n\times n$ board of $n^2$ cards: each step chooses a row or a column uniformly at random and rotates it cyclically by one unit in a uniformly chosen direction. We prove that the half-lazy version of this chain has total variation mixing time of order $n^3\log n$ and logarithmic Sobolev constant of order $n^{-3}$ on each communicating class. The order of the mixing time is the one conjectured by Diaconis. The proof of the upper bound has two steps. First, the entropy of a function on the board is at most a constant times $n$ times its mean loss when a single row or column is completely rearranged. Second, this mean loss is at most a constant times $n^2$ times the Dirichlet form of the shuffle. title: A generalization of Lévy's stochastic area formula for Gaussian rough paths
summary: In this paper, we establish a generalization of Lévy's stochastic area formula for the canonical rough path lift of a $2n$-dimensional centered Gaussian process with independent, identically distributed components. The formula extends the identity obtained by Aihara, Akahori, Fujii and Nitta [1] for Brownian motion. We compute the expectation of the exponential of a functional involving stochastic areas and quadratic forms in the terminal values. The result is expressed in terms of spectral data of a Hilbert--Schmidt operator associated with the stochastic area and an $n \times n$ determinant. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for absolute integrability in terms of the covariance at the terminal time and the symmetric part of the quadratic form in the terminal values. title: Stable-like Operators related to Bernstein Functions in weighted Lebesgue spaces: Boundedness, Regularity, Embedding, and Martingale Problem
summary: We study variable-coefficient nonlocal operators associated with a Bernstein function $φ$ satisfying global weak scaling conditions. Let $j_d^φ$ denote the radial Lévy density of the corresponding subordinate Brownian motion. The kernels may be nonsymmetric, and the coefficients are measurable in the jump variable and satisfy a prescribed uniform modulus of continuity in the spatial variable. In the critical scaling regime, we impose an annular cancellation condition. For jump profiles satisfying $0\le V(y)\le Cj_d^φ(|y|)$, we prove that the operator $\mathcal L_V^a$ is bounded from $H_p^{φ,2}(w)$ to $L_p(w)$ for every $1<p<\infty$ and $w\in A_p(\mathbb R^d)$. For $V(y)=j_d^φ(|y|)$ and uniformly positive real coefficients, we establish maximal regularity for parabolic equations in mixed-norm spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in space and time. title: Systems of quadratic BSDEs with unbounded terminal data
summary: The paper is devoted to global solution of multidimensional backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with non-convex quadratic generators and unbounded terminal data. The generators of some individual BSDEs of the system are allowed to have interactions among their second unknown variables and can be non-Lipschitz continuous with general growth in the first unknown variable $y$ and non-convex/non-concave in the second unknown variable $z$. We extend the results of the authors' previous paper [JDE, 2023] by incorporating both the no convexity/concavity of the generators and the interaction among the second unknown variables of individual BSDEs, and update the assumptions of Theorems 2.10 and 2.27 stated in the authors' previous paper~[EJP, 2025] so as to fill in a gap in the original proofs.

title: Persistence and Breakdown of the Initial Gaussian Rate Function for 1D Quasi-Periodic Cubic NLS
summary: We study rare events for the spatial supremum of the solution amplitude in the 1D cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with weak nonlinearity and Gaussian quasi-periodic initial data. Under suitable polynomial decay assumptions in Fourier space and a Diophantine condition controlling small divisors arising from spatial quasi-periodicity, we prove that the initial Gaussian rate function persists uniformly on the \emph{critical logarithmic correction time scale} with a \emph{small enough} prefactor. Using the \emph{Akhmediev breather}, we obtain that the same Gaussian rate function \emph{fails} to hold uniformly on this time scale with a \emph{large} prefactor. This also implies that the initial Gaussian rate function cannot, in general, persist uniformly on arbitrarily long polynomial time scales.

title: Flag algebras and the exact largest probability of a linear inequality between iid random variables
summary: How large can $\mathbb P[X_1+X_2+X_3<2X_4]$ be when $X_1,\dots,X_4$ are independent with a common law $μ$ on $[0,\infty)$? Previous work gave lower bounds through explicit constructions and upper bounds through exchangeability. The best lower bound, $0.4006953723\ldots$, was conjectured by \citet{BF} to be the exact value of the supremum. We prove this conjecture and formalize the proof in Lean~4. The improved upper bound uses the fact that independence gives more than exchangeability: two subsamples are conditionally independent given their shared points. As in Razborov's flag algebras, this yields a semidefinite program on the sign patterns of a few sample points. title: The broken-sample problem revisited II: Detecting hidden linear dependencies
summary: We study the detection problem for shuffled linear regression, in which the covariates and the responses are either independent or linearly related through a latent correspondence. Consider independent standard Gaussian covariates \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb R^d\) and scalar responses \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\). In a shuffled linear model, \(Y_i=\langle X_{π_*(i)},β_*\rangle+σZ_i\), where both the permutation \(π_*\) and the regression coefficient $β_*$ are latent and $Z_i$'s are white Gaussian noise. The goal is to distinguish this model from one in which the covariates and responses are independent with the same marginal distribution. In the low-dimensional regime of $d \ll \frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$, we show that the detection threshold is given by $σ=o(1)$ for fixed $d$ and $σ^2 = Θ(\frac{1}{d\log d})$ for growing $d$; both thresholds are achieved in nearly linear time using moment-based test

title: Counting fluctuations in the GOE-GUE crossover
summary: We study bulk eigenvalue counting fluctuations in a Gaussian ensemble interpolating between the Gaussian orthogonal and Gaussian unitary ensembles. Realizing this ensemble as the distribution at a fixed time of Hermitian matrix Ornstein-Uhlenbeck flow started from the GOE, we prove a central limit theorem for the one-sided counting function, centered by the semicircle prediction. Its variance grows logarithmically, with a leading coefficient that interpolates between the GOE and GUE values. Specifically, at times $T_N \asymp N^{-1 + \vartheta}$ with fixed $0 < \vartheta < 1$, we prove that the one-sided bulk count is asymptotically Gaussian with leading variance $(1 - \vartheta/2)π^{-2}\log N$. Although the microscopic bulk correlations have their GUE limit throughout this regime, the leading counting variance retains a contribution from the initial GOE matrix.

title: Limit theorems for almost conditionally identically distributed random variables
summary: $ξ$-Almost Conditional Identically Distributed ($ξ$-a.c.i.d.) random variables are generalizations of conditional identically distributed (c.i.d.) and exchangeable ones. $ξ$-a.c.i.d. random variables arise naturally in applications in statistics, such as in recursive algorithms and heteroskedastic observations, and are parametrized by a sequence $ξ=(ξ_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ that quantifies departure from the c.i.d. property. In this work, we extend limit theorems for exchangeable and c.i.d. random variables to the more general setting of $ξ$-a.c.i.d. random variables. After proving a Strong Law of Large Numbers, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic directing measure of the sequence to be absolutely continuous with respect to a given $σ$-finite measure. title: Mean First Passage Times for Loop-Erased Random Walks and Erased-Loop Size Distributions on Graphs
summary: Loop-erased random walks provide a natural way to extract self-avoiding trajectories from ordinary random walks by chronologically removing loops. They are deeply connected with uniform spanning trees: the loop-erased path between two vertices has the same distribution law as the unique path connecting these vertices in a random spanning tree. In this work, we use this connection as a computational framework for finite graphs. First, using the classical transfer-current theorem, we obtain an explicit formula for the mean first passage time of loop-erased random walks. The resulting expression returns the expected length of the loop-erased path as a weighted sum over simple paths, where the weights are exact determinantal probabilities obtained from the spanning-tree kernel. title: Exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions
summary: We study exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions whose conditional mean consists of a linear term and a signed adapted perturbation. The linear term determines a product normalization, but convergence after normalization does not ensure a strictly positive limit. Multiplying the state by the inverse of each deterministic contraction factor gives a contraction-adjusted state. On paths where this state tends to infinity, we prove that the logarithm of the normalized state differs from the cumulative relative perturbation by an almost surely convergent quantity. The assumptions control the effective step sizes, the quadratic positive relative perturbation, and the conditional quadratic variation of the relative martingale noise. title: The shortest figure-eight geodesics on random hyperbolic surfaces
summary: We consider primitive unoriented figure-eight geodesics on a closed hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ sampled from Weil--Petersson measure. The shortest of these geodesics realizes the non-simple systole. He, Shen, Wu and Xue proved that its length is tight after centering at $a_g=\log g-\log\log g$. We prove that, as $g\to\infty$, the point process of centered lengths converges to a Poisson process on $\mathbb R$ with intensity $e^s\,ds/(8π^2)$. Its first arrival gives a reflected Gumbel limit for the centered systole $M_g$. We also prove convergence of the marked process in which each figure-eight carries the three cuff lengths of its supporting pair of pants, normalized by their sum. In the limiting process, the third cuff accounts for half the perimeter. The two winding cuffs, ordered at random, divide the other half uniformly. These splits are independent across points and independent

title: Limit distributions and bootstrap for smooth adapted Wasserstein distances
summary: In this paper, we provide limit theorems for the Gaussian-smoothed adapted Wasserstein distances. Let $\widehatμ_n$ be the empirical measure of independent paths with law $μ$ on $(\mathbb{R}^d)^T$. Let $P = μ* γ_σ$ and $P_n = \widehatμ_n * γ_σ$, where $γ_σ= N(0,σ^2 I_{dT})$ is a Gaussian measure with mean zero and covariance matrix $σ^2 I_{dT}$. We first assume that $μ$ is compactly supported. For every $1 < p < \infty$ and fixed $d, T$, and $σ> 0$, we show that $\sqrt{n}\,\mathrm{AW}_p(P_n,P) \Rightarrow Q_{P,p}(G)^{1/p}$, where $G$ is the Gaussian limit of the density fluctuation and $Q_{P,p}$ is the minimum adapted $p$-energy for the linearized continuity equation. We prove full-path bootstrap consistency and the convergence of the first and $p$-th moments. The limit and the bootstrap hold for noncompact laws as well, for all $1 < p < \infty$ under appropriate tail and structural cond

title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
summary: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials

title: Skew-Symmetric Factor Models
summary: The paper introduces and analyzes a factor model for (real) skew-symmetric data, which arise naturally in directed flows and in pairwise comparisons used for rankings. Working within a signal-plus-noise framework, we analyze spectral inference and establish a BBP-type phase transition in signal strength. Under Gaussian noise, we derive joint eigenvalue fluctuation limits. Above the separation threshold, the estimated signal strength is asymptotically normal whenever the population strength has multiplicity one. For a general multiplicity $k$, the joint limiting fluctuations of the corresponding sample eigenvalues above the threshold are given by the eigenvalues of a scaled $k\times k$ Gaussian unitary ensemble matrix. The skew-symmetric structure induces paired eigenspaces, and we characterize the canonical angles between the population and sample eigenspaces. Below the threshold, the co

title: Fermat costs and path-dependent first-passage percolation
summary: We introduce a path-dependent and space-inhomogeneous first-passage percolation (FPP) model in the continuum. Inspired by Euclidean FPP, it is defined through a sample of points drawn from a common density function on a Riemannian manifold. In Euclidean FPP, the cost of each step in a discrete path is given by its length raised to the power $α>1$. In our model, the power $α$ increases as the path progresses, governed by a control mechanism. Consequently, the resulting percolation cost is not a distance. However, we prove a shape theorem showing that, as the number of points goes to infinity, the percolation costs converge to deterministic space-time integrals along curves in the manifold. title: Epidemic random model under vaccination regime and non-permanent immunity driven by time-changed Levy noise
summary: A random version of the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Vaccinated (SIRV) epidemic model with non-permanent immunity and a population of non-constant size is studied. The compartments satisfy a system of differential equations in which the contact rate is a random coefficient, and the contact rate itself is driven by a stochastic differential equation with time-changed Levy noise. This noise is constructed from a conditional Brownian motion and a doubly stochastic Poisson random field, both governed by a stochastic clock. When the clock is independent of the Brownian and Poisson components, the two parts of the noise are a time-changed Brownian motion and a time-changed Poisson random measure. The equation for the contact rate decouples from the compartment equations and enters them as a random parameter, which allows the compartments to be treated pathwise. The existence, uniqueness, and

title: The minimax value of outcome feedback in budget-constrained adaptive sampling
summary: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has ze
comment: 16 pages. Ancillary files contain an exact rational certificate and a standard-library Python checker for the computer-assisted part of Section 6

title: Automorphisms Induced on Cartan Tori and Centers of Quantized Enveloping Algebras
summary: Let \(U=U_q(\mathfrak g)\) be the root-lattice form of the quantized enveloping algebra associated with a complex simple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), over a field \(\mathbb{k}\) of characteristic zero, with \(q\in\mathbb{k}^{\times}\) not a root of unity. We determine the groups of automorphisms induced by algebra automorphisms of $U$ on its Cartan torus $U^0$ and its center $Z(U)$. These groups are \[ \Aut_U(U^0)\cong\Hom(Q,\{\pm1\})\rtimes\Aut(Φ), \] \[ \Aut_U(Z(U))\cong\Hom((P/Q)[2],\{\pm1\})\rtimesΓ, \] where $Q$ and $P$ are the root and weight lattices, $Φ$ is the root system, $Γ$ is the automorphism group of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak g$, and $(P/Q)[2]$ is the $2$-torsion subgroup of $P/Q$. The proof uses characters of finite-dimensional modules and Weyl-group invariant fields to show that the automorphism of $Q$ determined by the toral restriction preserves $Φ$. Writing $ρ_0

title: A Finiteness Result for Commuting Squares and Quantitative Ocneanu Rigidity
summary: We introduce the spanning relative commutant condition (SRC) for nondegenerate commuting squares of matrix algebras. The condition requires that the second relative commutant span the next algebra in the lower row of the basic construction as a right module over the preceding algebra. We prove that if a sequence of SRC squares with fixed tracial inclusion data converges, then all but finitely many terms are isomorphic to the limit square. We also show that the standard commuting square of every finite-index inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of depth two satisfies SRC. This gives a commuting-square proof of Ocneanu's finiteness theorem for standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph. We then obtain the explicit bound $B(D)=10^{7D^5}$ for the number of SRC squares up to isomorphism when the upper-right tracial algebra is prescribed and has dimension $D$. The same functi

title: Principal subspaces of affine vertex algebras at admissible levels
summary: We classify generic principal subspaces of admissible affine vertex algebras for all simple Lie algebras. The nongeneric cases occur precisely at denominator two in types $B,C,F_4$ and at denominator three in type $G_2$. The proof uses geometry of nilpotent orbits combined with positive root null vectors. Surprisingly, null vectors needed for our classification are explicitly known and already studied in the literature. We then study the exceptional principal subspaces at the level of their $C_2$-algebras and arc algebras. For $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ at level $-\frac12$ and $G_2$ at level $-\frac53$, we prove classical freeness and obtain product character formulas. In type $C_n$ at level $-\frac12$, classical freeness fails for $n\ge4$. For $n=3$, we combine the functional model method of Feigin and Stoyanovsky, and a flat degeneration of the explicit realization of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)

title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
summary: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that $\operatorname{Inn}(V)$ is the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ and has finite index in $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Aut}(V)=\dim V_1$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ is finite if and only if $V_1=0$.

title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
summary: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electric

title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
summary: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-mod

title: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
summary: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary. This proves the 'if' direction of a conjecture of Rowell and Wang, motivated by topological quantum computation, which states that a simple object admits a localization if and only if it is weakly integral. For a simple weakly integral object of a unitary braided fusion category, the operator $R$ that we construct has an enha

title: Critical Ising and Temperley-Lieb-Jones States: Cone Haag Duality and the Trivial Algebra Object
summary: We compute the algebra object of two critical Ising states in the operator algebraic framework of fusion category symmetry. The boundary subalgebra is the even part of the Pauli chain, and its DHR category is the toric code. We treat two models. The first is the classical Ising model in two dimensions, through its row transfer matrix. The second is the Ising chain in a transverse field. For the critical transfer matrix state and for the ground state of the critical chain, the algebra object is exactly the tensor unit. In a second part we treat the critical Temperley--Lieb--Jones chains at $δ=2\cos(π/(k+2))$. For every $k\ge2$ the ground state selected by the vacuum block is pure and has trivial algebra object in the Drinfeld centre of the even part. At $k=2$ this recovers the critical Ising chain.

title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
summary: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtim

title: Simple Yetter-Drinfeld Modules and Extensions over Fractional Infinite-Dimensional Taft Algebras
summary: We classify all simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a fractional infinite-dimensional Taft Hopf algebra $T=T(\underline m,t,ξ)$, including the infinite-dimensional induced family and the finite-dimensional truncated and cyclic families. We determine their explicit structures and isomorphism criteria, and classify first extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules together with their middle modules. We also establish the primary decomposition with respect to $z^t$ and prove that every nonzero-eigenvalue component is wild when $m>1$.

title: Recursive Relations for Categorified Young Symmetrizers in Type $\mathbb{B}$
summary: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type $\mathbb{X}_n$ contains a symmetrizer complex $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{X}_n}$ which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type $\mathbb{A}$, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_{n+1}}$ can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_n}$ and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type $\mathbb{B}_n$ and $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$. Following the method of the result in type $\mathbb{A}$, we then use this to prove that the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{B}_n}$ is a polynomial ring.

title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
summary: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. title: Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons
summary: Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $Δ$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure constants. A key role is played by the subalgebra $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ spanned by the stated $n$-webs whose $m-1$ edge weights are zero. We show that $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ is a quantum cluster algebra whose seed coincides

title: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
summary: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, tho

title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
summary: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and e

title: Orthosymplectic R-matrix from Hasse diagrams
summary: We calculate R-matrix in the basic representation for the ortho-symplectic quantum supergroups in arbitrary polarizations, by a method of Hasse diagrams.

title: Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras
summary: We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra. We construct a nontrivial topological post-Hopf structure on $U_\hbar(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and determine its semiclassical limit. For the standard Lie bialgebra structure on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we classify all compatible post-Lie products up to isomorphism and show that the nontrivial class admits a quantization. Finally, we formulate the general quantization problem for post-Lie bialgebras.

title: On quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimensions
summary: Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.

title: Twisted enveloping algebras for permutation orbifolds
summary: We formulate a topological formal calculus for continuous distributions with values in linearly topologized spaces. We apply it here to construct permutation-twisted fields directly from products and branch specializations. For a vertex operator algebra $V$, the key structural observation is that modes of tensors with at most one non-vacuum factor topologically generate the permutation-twisted enveloping algebra. Combining this observation with the calculus and $Δ_N$, we obtain an explicit isomorphism $\mathscr{U}_σ(V^{\otimes N})\cong\mathscr{U}(V)$ for an $N$-cycle $σ$, with grading and canonical filtrations rescaled by $N$. For arbitrary permutations, the cycle factors are rescaled before taking their degreewise completed tensor product.

title: The Partial Trace Functor on Soergel Bimodules in Type $\mathbb{B}$
summary: We write down some observations about the partial trace functor between the categories of Soergel bimodules of type $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_n$ for future reference. In particular, we observe that, like in type $\mathbb{A}$, the partial trace sends Soergel bimodules to a semi-infinite $q$-graded sum of Soergel bimodules.

title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
summary: The Bravyi-König theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. We present two explicit constructions of codes based on copies of the quantum doubles of $D_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with $k$ logical qubits and a logical $C^{k-1}Z$ gate, which is at level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy. The physical circuits realizing the gates consist only of physical $Z$ or $CZ$ gates. The main new ingredient comes from the logical encoding, which depends crucially on non-Abelian group multiplication.

title: Computing $F$-Symbols from Modular Data
summary: We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free. Although the algorithm is implemented numerically, we describe a reliable means of recovering the exact $F$-symbols, assuming that in some gauge they lie in a given number field, and of certifying every pentagon and hexagon equation exactly. title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
summary: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion. We demonstrate the scalability of this gated implementation by identifying prime modular data at rank 100 that is not realized by any Chern-Simons theory. title: Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical
summary: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule. If the canonical map $H_0\to H/J(H)$ is surjective, then $H$ is generated by $H_0$ if and only if $H=H_0^3+J(H)^2$, where $H_0^3$ is the span of products of three elements of $H_0$. For finite locally free Hopf algebras of constant rank over a $k$-scheme in characteristic zero, including duals of liftings of a given Nichols algebra, the locus where this property holds is Zariski open and compatible with arbitrary base change. title: Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras
summary: This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace. We demonstrate that the algebraic structures of the generating subspaces are encoded by a quadruple that generalizes Lie--Rinehart algebras and their weak representations. This quadruple yields necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for constructing an associated Lie superalgebra $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{g},A,U)$. Based on this, we construct a family of universal vertex operator superalgebras $V_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell,0)$ and establish a reconstruction theorem fo

title: Perspectives on the hidden subgroup problem over unitriangular groups
summary: We investigate the quantum Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) over the upper unitriangular group $U_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$. While efficient quantum algorithms were discovered for some families of non abelian groups and nil-2 $p$-groups, no efficient algorithms are known for groups of nilpotency class higher than 2. The only techniques known for such groups scale exponentially in the size of the input. We first study the group $U_4(\mathbb{F}_p)$, the smallest upper unitriangular group exhibiting nilpotency class three. We analyze the application of the Pretty Good Measurement approach used for Heisenberg groups and show its limits. We then focus on the more general case $U_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ to adapt existing techniques to this particular structure. In particular, we derive an algorithm for cyclic subgroups as a subroutine for a general algorithm, although it is not efficient in the size of the group

title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
summary: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

title: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
summary: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-st

title: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
summary: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined. For finite $A, D, E$ type, the construction involves $q$-integers where $q=e^{\imathπ/h}$ with $h$ the Coxeter number and there is a conjugate pair of $*$-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connections (QLCs). In the case of type $A$, these are necessarily contained in a previously known 1-parameter space of connections. For affine $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$ type, there is only one QLC, with real coefficients. Using the quant

title: $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$
summary: We give explicit descriptions of the $m$-harmonic polynomials for dihedral groups via hypergeometric functions. Using these, we compute the parameters $m$ for which the Hilbert series of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ differs from the Hilbert series of $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $0$. We also give explicit descriptions of the generators of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ when this is the case.

title: iBraid group symmetries of iquantum groups via star product
summary: We establish ibraid group symmetries on universal iquantum groups of symmetrizable Kac-Moody type, proving a conjecture of Wang and Zhang. Building on the star product realization of quantum symmetric pairs $(\widetilde{\mathbf U},\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath})$, we relate these symmetries to Lusztig's braid group symmetries, extending the compatibility previously obtained via iHopf algebras in the quasi-split setting. Via the Letzter map $ψ$ from the iquantum group $\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath}$ to the horospherical algebra $\mathcal A\subset \widetilde{\mathbf U}$, we show that the ibraid group symmetry $\widetilde{\mathbf T}'_{i,-1}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath}$ transported to $\mathcal A$ coincides with Lusztig's braid group symmetry $\widetilde T_{\mathbf r_i}^{-1}$ on the subalgebra $\mathcal R_{\bullet,i}^{-,r}$. Finally, a mixed product formula, together with a paraboli

title: Exotic cluster structures on $Sp_{2n}$
summary: We modify the seeds of Berenstein, Fomin and Zelevinsky attached to reduced words for~$(w_0,w_0)$, for any simply connected simple complex algebraic group and any aperiodic Belavin--Drinfeld pair. In every type, moves of words act on the resulting seeds by mutations. After a change of coordinates introduced by Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the seeds are, for $SL_N$, seeds of the cluster structures of these authors, and for $Sp_{2n}$ they define regular complete cluster structures with the expected properties. This proves the aperiodic version of their conjecture for $Sp_{2n}$, with its uniqueness part in a refined form.

title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
summary: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
summary: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.

title: Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operators at higher rank
summary: We construct a rank-$m$ Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operator for generalized Macdonald functions. The operator acts on the horizontal Fock module of quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$, extended by an auxiliary polynomial space with $m$ components. A geometric realization is given by the tensor product with the dual tautological line on the equivariant $K$-theory of a Hecke correspondence studied by Negut. The eigenbasis is indexed by an $m$-tuple of partitions and an addable corner, whose content is the eigenvalue. We give an anti-normal factorization and prove that the Lax operator is self-adjoint for the transported Euler pairing. With unit framing weight, the rank-one specialization recovers the Nazarov-Sklyanin factorization. We then show that the Lax operator is conjugate to the companion matrix of a projected q-Miura operator of the deformed $W$-algebra of type $\mathfrak{gl}_m$. This als

title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
summary: The defect of a complex Hadamard matrix is the real dimension of the solution space obtained by linearizing the row orthogonality equations in the phases of the entries, with the first row and column fixed. It is known that defect zero implies isolation up to Hadamard equivalence. The converse, whether every isolated complex Hadamard matrix has defect zero, was open and is the square-matrix case of a conjecture of Banica, Ozteke and Pittau. We answer this question in the negative. We exhibit a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of order 13 with entries among the sixth roots of unity and show that it is isolated and has defect one. We prove isolation by showing that no nonzero solution of the linearized equations satisfies the second order condition obtained by the second author for directions of convergence of sequences of Hadamard matrices. title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
summary: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
summary: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_ξ(W)$ constructed in

title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
summary: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should

title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
summary: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,θ}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,θ}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<θ<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

title: The automorphism group of the super Jordan plane
summary: We complete the description of the automorphism group of the super Jordan plane $\mathcal B$ over a field of characteristic zero, extending the classification of super-automorphisms obtained by N. Andruskiewitsch and F. Dumas in \cite{AD}. We characterize a subgroup $\mathbb L$ stabilizing two one-dimensional vector spaces and obtain two semidirect product decompositions of it. This subgroup contains all super-automorphisms and its structure motivates our main result. Precisely, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}\mathcal B=\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B\rtimes\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$, where $\operatorname{Inn}\mathcal B$ and $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{super}}\mathcal B$ denote, respectively, the groups of inner automorphisms and super-automorphisms of $\mathcal B$. We also characterize the nilpotent elements of $\mathcal B$ and prove that every nonzero nilpotent has

title: Psyquandle Fares
summary: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
summary: We prove Schlösser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
summary: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks. Secondly, we provide an example showing that, unlike for finite braided tensor categories, non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting: For an odd vector space $V[1]$, the $2$-shifted $\mathcal{D}$-modules $\mathrm{DMod}^2(V[1])$

title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values

title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
summary: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space is

title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
summary: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model. Moore realizations correspond to transition expectations that factor on the prescribed hidden algebra. We establish a rank obstruction to such factorization and prove its sufficiency for isometric generators: factorization holds exactly when the induced hidden-memory channel has Kraus rank at most the hidden Hilbert-space dimension. The Kraus rank also gives the minimal intermediate Hilbert-space dimension. When the hidden and output dimensi

title: Global generation of coinvariant vector bundles on $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,n}$
summary: Using fusion closed-ness and strong generation properties, we identify collections of modules over vertex operator algebras (VOAs) whose induced vector bundles of coinvariants on the moduli space $\overline{\mathrm M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus zero are globally generated. These results specialize to \cite{Fak12} for affine VOAs at positive integer levels, and of \cite{DG23} for strongly rational VOAs that are generated in degree 1. To illustrate the results, and to show that fusion-closedness is essential, we give numerous examples, including Lattice VOAs, Simple Current Extensions of Affine VOAs, and various tensor products.

title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
summary: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq

title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
summary: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

title: Folding of cluster algebras
summary: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators. It sends cluster monomials associated with canonical lifted $\bfi$-box seeds to elements of the classical dual canonical basis for the quotient Cartan datum. For arbitrary positive braids in finite Cartan type, the folding is realized through quantum virtual Grothendieck rings and, after specialization at $q=1$, is induced by a single ambient Grothendieck-ring homomorphism.
