comment: 116 pages, with background material, detailed explanations, and many examples to help readers understand the results

title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
summary: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.

title: Ozone groups and fixed rings of double Ore extensions
summary: We determine centers of two families of four-dimensional double Ore extensions without torsion assumptions, restricting to $f\ne0$ in $\mathcal O$. On the PI locus of $\mathcal K$, we classify the ozone groups and obtain normal commutative fixed rings of generic degree two over the center, including a nonmonogenic example. For an odd-torsion subfamily of $\mathcal O$, independent odd orders $n\geq1,m>1$ yield ozone group $C_n^2\times C_2^2$, PI degree $2nm$ and fixed-algebra PI degree $m$, with unchanged center. A PI specialization of $\mathcal G$ has trivial ozone group.

title: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
summary: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-fil

title: Higher Categorical Bistellar Moves
summary: We construct $n$-categories $\mathscr{P}_n$ with generators given by simplices and relations given by bistellar moves between them, in any dimension $n$. We show that functors out of $\mathscr{P}_n$ into an $n$-category of theories, give the correct input for the orbifold construction for TQFTs, and subsume all previously known examples, which are all in dimensions $n \leq 3$. In particular, in dimension 3 the construction gives a highly nontrivial categorification of a kind of nonunital, noncounital, Frobenius algebra.

title: Quantum loop symmetric pairs and meromorphic abelian K-matrices
summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra, let $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not be a root of unity, and let $\mathbf{U}=U_q(L\mathfrak{g})$ be the corresponding quantum loop algebra, equipped with Hernandez' deformed Drinfeld coproduct. For every diagram involution $τ$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, we introduce a coideal subalgebra $\mathbf{B}$ in a topological completion of $\mathbf{U}$, obtained by adapting the Letzter-Kolb construction of quantum symmetric pairs to the Drinfeld generators of $\mathbf{U}$. We derive necessary constraints on the parameters defining $\mathbf{B}$ from a minimality condition on its intersection with the quantum loop Cartan subalgebra $\mathbf{U}^0\subset\mathbf{U}$. We show that $\mathbf{B}$ yields a topological realization of the quasi-split $\imath$quantum loop group $\mathbf{U}^\imath$ associated with $τ$, in the presentation recently obtained by Lu-Pan,

title: A lift of Baxter's cyclic summation identity with applications to quantum topology
summary: While studying the chiral Potts model Baxter discovered a cyclic analogue of Ramanujan's ${}_1ψ_{1}$ summation identity. This identity was subsequently interpreted by Faddeev and Kashaev as a pentagon relation for the quantum dilogarithm function, a key ingredient in cyclic quantizations of Teichmüller theory. Existing forms of the identity involve multivalued functions so one must either accept overall phase ambiguities or keep track of branches on a complicated covering space. In this paper we show how to remove the phase ambiguities with a much simpler choice of covering space. As an application we compute the Fourier transform of the holonomy $R$-matrices of the author and Reshetikhin. A corollary is a simpler proof that Kashaev's $R$-matrix is a specialization of the colored Jones $R$-matrix, which was first shown by Murakami and Murakami.

title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
summary: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group

title: Braided module categories from small braidings
summary: We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions. We construct a number of new examples coming from quantum groups, as well as the associated quantum moment maps.

title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
summary: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.

title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
summary: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space. The same conclusion is obtained for arbitrary affine-state insertions. Finally, we compute the cases of at most four currents and the nodal limit $q\to 0$, in which the type-1 and type-2 elliptic cycle coefficients degenerate to rational genus-zero cycle coefficients and the module trace reduces to the ground-state space.

title: Differential equations for twisted intertwining operators in abelian orbifold conformal field theory
summary: Let $ V $ be a vertex operator algebra with two commuting automorphisms $ g_1 $ and $ g_2 $ (possibly of infinite order and non-semisimple). We derive a Jacobi identity for a twisted intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is a $ g_1 $-twisted $ V $-module, $ W_2 $ is a $ g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module, and $ W_3 $ is a $ g_1 g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module. For any abelian group $ G $ of automorphisms of a CFT-type vertex operator algebra, under certain Noetherian assumptions, we derive differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ when $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ are intertwining operators among $ C_2 $-cofinite and discretely graded $ V $-modules twisted by elements in $ G $. For modules twisted by automorphisms with only

title: Almost unimodular quantum groups
summary: We define a locally compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ to be almost unimodular if its modular element is diagonalizable. This is shown to be equivalent to the almost periodicity of a novel weight on the dual von Neumann algebra, which we call the middle Haar weight. The point modular spectrum of this weight is related to the point spectrum of $δ$, and we prove that unimodularity of $\mathbb{G}$ is equivalent to traciality of this weight. When $δ$ is affiliated with the center of $L^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, we show that there is a canonical closed, normal, unimodular quantum subgroup $\mathbb{G}_1 \leq \mathbb{G}$ which assumes the role of the unimodular part of $\mathbb{G}$, and moreover the openness of this quantum subgroup is equivalent to the almost periodicity of $\mathbb{G}$. Additionally, we establish several permanence properties of almost unimodularity.
comment: 24 pages, no large language models were used in the development of this article

title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
summary: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
summary: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincaré duality algebras.

title: Dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions
summary: We prove that the Artin--Schelter Gorenstein and Artin--Schelter regular properties descend from a graded Ore extension to its coefficient algebra, for every twisting automorphism and every skew derivation. We then determine the dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions for all gradings compatible with the Ore structure. They are exactly the semidirect products of a dual reflection group of the coefficient algebra by the cyclic group generated by the degree of the new variable, meeting it trivially, and a nonzero skew derivation never contributes a new degree. For iterated Ore extensions we characterize the dual reflection groups by an order formula analogous to the theorem of Shephard, Todd and Chevalley, and we prove the binomial conjecture of Buzaglo and Rogalski for these algebras. We show that their covariant rings are complete intersections of growth type, whose Ext-algebras

title: Categorical orbifold theory
summary: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.

title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
summary: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permu

title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
summary: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.

title: Quantales Arising From Rings
summary: We study the quantale, or multiplicative lattice, of additive submonoids of an arbitrary ring, with particular focus on the question of which properties of the ring can be recovered from it. We show that this quantale, unlike the better-known quantale of ideals, captures significant information about the cardinality, characteristic, and center of the ring. Certain rings, such as non-prime finite fields, torsion-free rings, and those with characteristic 2, are completely determined by their submonoid quantales. We also discuss various other subobject quantales one can associate to a (semi)ring.

title: Principal angles between annihilators of real sedenion zero divisors
summary: We investigate the relative geometry of annihilators of zero divisors in the real sedenion algebra. Each nonzero zero divisor has a four-dimensional annihilator, whose geometry is associated with an axis in the imaginary octonions. For two prescribed axes separated by an angle $θ$, we establish the exact range of principal angles between their annihilators. The four principal cosines are necessarily $(p,p,q,q)$, where $\cos^2(θ/2)\leq p\leq\cos(θ/2)$ and $0\leq q\leq p$, and every admissible pair is realizable. We further derive an explicit quadratic formula for the principal cosines of any specified pair using two invariants of the associated quaternionic frames. A continuous deformation demonstrates that neither the axis angle nor the underlying quaternion subalgebras together determine the annihilator angles. Finally, we relate these results to the least singular subspaces of sedenion

title: Weighted Numerical Homological Regularities over Positively Graded Algebras
summary: Let A be a noetherian positively graded algebra. We investigate several weighted numerical homological regularities: weighted CM-regularity, weighted Tor-regularity (Ext-regularity), and weighted Ex-regularity, defined in terms of the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of canonical complexes associated with graded A-modules. Introduced by Kirkman, Won, and Zhang, weighted regularities provide finite invariants even when their unweighted counterparts are infinite. Through parametrized degree reweightings, they unify classical homological invariants, including unweighted numerical regularities, sup, inf, depth, projective dimension, and local cohomology dimension. This framework clarifies the behavior of homological regularities under degree shifts and reveals intrinsic relationships among these invariants, particularly those involving the a-invariant. We establish several inequalities a

title: The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras
summary: AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$. Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compa

title: Division rings of fractions of LV-algebras
summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $A=L_K(E,ω)$ be an LV-algebra of a row-finite weighted graph. We prove that $A$ embeds in a division ring if and only if $E$ has one vertex and its ordered loop weights satisfy $w_n=n$ and $w_j>j$ for $1\le j<n$. Under these conditions, $A$ has a universal division ring of fractions, which we identify with the free field on $2\sum_{j=1}^n w_j-n^2$ generators over $K$. We construct a free generating set explicitly by factoring the matrix of generators. We classify the resulting division rings over $K$ and bound the stabilization required to recognize invertible matrices. These results include mixed weights, for which the LV-algebra need not be a semifir.

title: Gorenstein homological algebra over comma categories
summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories with enough projective objects. In this paper, we characterize those functors $F:\mathcal{A}\to \mathcal{B}$ for which the Gorenstein projective objects in the comma category $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ admit an explicit description in terms of the Gorenstein projective objects of $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. As a main application, we obtain estimates for the global Gorenstein projective dimension of $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ in terms of those of $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ and the functor $F$, and derive exact formulas in several important cases. Our categorical approach also yields dual results concerning Gorenstein injective objects and dimension. Special attention is devoted to the module category over a triangular matrix ring $ \begin{pmatrix} A & 0\\ U & B \end{pmatrix}$, the product category $\mathcal{A}\times\mathca

title: The Kaplansky-Aupetit conjecture for C*-algebras
summary: We settle the Kaplansky--Aupetit conjecture when either algebra is a $C^*$-algebra. More precisely, if $A$ is a unital Banach algebra and $B$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra, or if $A$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra and $B$ is a unital semisimple Banach algebra, then every unital invertibility-preserving linear surjection $φ: A\to B$ is a Jordan homomorphism. In fact, it suffices to assume that $φ$ preserves the invertibility of products of two exponentials, or of individual exponentials when both algebras are $C^*$-algebras. Claude Opus 5.5 found the original proof when both $A$ and $B$ are $C^*$-algebras by adapting a resolvent estimate from a recent preprint of Colbrook and Stepaniants, while OpenAI's GPT-6.1 further generalized this to the case where only one algebra is a $C^*$-algebra.

title: Higher Coherence of Flat Algebras
summary: We establish higher-coherence results for flat algebras over commutative base rings. If $K$ is noetherian and a $K$-flat algebra $A$ admits an $A^{\mathrm e}$-resolution of length $n$ with projective term in degree $n$ and flat terms in lower degrees, then every product of copies of $A$ has right flat dimension at most $n-1$ and $A$ is left strongly $n$-coherent. A projective $n$-th relative bar syzygy gives the corresponding two-sided conclusion. If $K$ is coherent and $A$ is $K$-flat and relatively quasi-free, then $A$ is left and right strongly $2$-coherent. In contrast, we construct a countable commutative ring $k$ that is strongly $n$-coherent for every $n\ge2$, while the one-variable polynomial algebra $k[z]$ is faithfully flat and relatively quasi-free over $k$ but fails strong $q$-coherence for every finite $q$. Explicit modules witness failure at each positive degree. These resu

title: The norm axiom and factor hyperfields
summary: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form $\mathcal{H}_ρ(K)$: a valued field $K$ read up to relative error $ρ$. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient $K^\times/T\cup\{0\}$ of a field, the norm axiom forces $T=1+\mathfrak{m}_ρ$ for a valuation on $K$. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group $\mathbb{Z}$ we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfield

title: The axial radical
summary: An {\it axial algebra} is an algebra generated by a set $X$ of semisimple idempotents satisfying a prescribed set of fusion rules. Some axial algebras (such as primitive axial algebras of Jordan type $1/2$) have a Frobenius form, in which case one can define the radical $Rad(A)$ of the Frobenius form. Recently, Mamontov, S.~Shpectorov, and V.~Zhelyabin defined a radical $R(A;X)$ as the largest ideal not containing any axis of $X$, which is always contained in $Rad(A)$, and proved that $R(A;X) = Rad(A)$ when the Frobenius form is anisotropic. In this case they also proved that $A/R(A;X)$ is semisimple, yielding an elegant structure theory for primitive axial algebras with an anisotropic Frobenius form. Our objective is to recover these results, removing the assumption of a Frobenius form. We provide alternative characterizations of the radical, including a Jacobson-type radical (not the s

title: Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
summary: Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors. Under a compatibility condition, the pair of special classes $(Δ(C), \nabla(D))$ is then shown to be admissible balanced if and only if $(C, D)$ is. As an application, for rings $A, B$ and a $(B, A)$-bimodule $U$ of finite flat dimension over $A$ and finite projective dimension over $B$, the triangular matrix ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A & 0\\ U & B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is left virtually

title: Gorenstein and Ding injectivity over coherent rings
summary: For a commutative Ding--Chen ring $B$, we prove that Gorenstein and Ding injectivity coincide over $R=B[x,y]/(x,y)^2$ if and only if injective $B$-modules generate the unbounded derived category of $B$. We construct a commutative von Neumann regular ring $B$ whose unbounded derived category is not generated by its pure injective objects. For this $B$, the coherent ring $R$ admits a strongly Gorenstein injective module $G$ which is not Ding injective. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $G_{\mathfrak p}$ has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. The ring $R$ can be chosen to have cardinality $\aleph_ω$, the least possible among coherent rings over which Gorenstein and Ding injectivity differ.

title: Finite conformal models and the Kac--van de Leur conjecture
summary: We prove that every simple Lie superalgebra containing the centerless Virasoro algebra, with diagonal $L_0$-action, uniformly bounded weight multiplicities, and support in finitely many cosets of $\Z$, is isomorphic, as a parity-graded Lie superalgebra, to a member of the Witt, special, contact, or Cheng--Kac families. Thus the amended Kac--van de Leur list is exhaustive. Every such algebra admits a finite ordinary conformal model and is a quotient by the full center of a twisted coefficient algebra of a finite simple conformal superalgebra. For Lie superalgebras containing the centerless Virasoro algebra, we also prove that linear commutator growth is equivalent to uniformly bounded weight spaces, provided the grading is diagonal and integral and each weight space is finite-dimensional.

title: $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over commutative Noetherian rings
summary: We prove $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over every commutative Noetherian ring.

title: Polynomial identities of the two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra
summary: We describe a basis for the polynomial identities satisfied by the unique two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra $B$ over a field of characteristic zero. Modulo the right-symmetric identity, this basis consists of two irreducible identities of degree three. We construct linear bases for the multilinear components of the relatively free algebra of the variety $\mathcal V=\operatorname{var}(B)$ and determine their decompositions into Specht modules. Using the resulting $S_n$-module decompositions, we prove that the commutator subspace is right nilpotent in every proper subvariety of $\mathcal V$. Moreover, in any proper subvariety satisfying a nontrivial identity of degree $n\ge2$, the index of right nilpotence of the commutator subspace is at most $2n$.

title: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
summary: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Crampé in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, toget

title: Associative operators and their iterated lifts: classification and cocycle identities
summary: The inverse problem of an inhomogeneous functional equation asks for which right-hand sides the equation is solvable. For the Cauchy equation and for the quadratic equation a necessary condition is a cocycle identity, and the two identities have a common form. We take this form as a definition. An operator from functions of one variable to functions of two variables can be lifted to functions of several variables, one argument at a time. We call it associative when its two iterated lifts from one variable to three coincide, that is, when every function in its image satisfies the corresponding cocycle identity. Composition with an associative binary operation is the model case. The Cauchy difference, the d'Alembert operator and the Jordan-von Neumann operator are associative as well. We prove that all iterated lifts of the same length of an associative operator coincide. Over abelian grou

title: On coherence of enveloping algebras of infinite-dimensional Lie algebras
summary: We investigate when the universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{g})$ of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is coherent. We show that if $\mathfrak{g}$ is the loop algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$ then $U(\mathfrak{g})$ is coherent exactly when $\mathfrak{h}$ is nilpotent. As a consequence, we show that $U(\mathfrak{g})$ is not coherent if $\mathfrak{g}$ is complex, simple, $\mathbb{Z}$-graded, of polynomially bounded growth, and not isomorphic to the Witt algebra $W = \mathrm{Der} \mathbb{C}[t,t^{-1}]$ or its one-sided version. We also demonstrate that the homomorphic image of $U(W)$ used to prove non-Noetherianity of $U(W)$ in previous work of the first author and Walton is not coherent. On the other hand, we establish that two closely related connected graded rings are graded coherent. Finally, we prove that any exhaustively filtered ring is

title: Double determinants of quaternion matrices in the P-generalized determinant framework with applications
summary: Building on the P-generalized determinant over quaternions, we introduce the double determinant of arbitrary square quaternion matrices. We then apply the double determinant to obtain a determinant representation for the inverse of any invertible quaternion matrix, without the Hermitian restriction. Furthermore, we establish Cramer's rule for the unique solutions to the quaternion linear equations Ax=b and xA=b, as well as to the quaternion matrix equations AX=B, XA=B, and AXB=C. As an application, we use the determinant representation of the unique solution to AXB=C to design a color image encryption-decryption scheme. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the encryption algorithm effectively conceals the contour and color information of the original image, while the decryption algorithm restores the original image almost perfectly, thereby confirming the effectiveness and practical po

title: Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond
summary: Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres. Finally, we prove that $I_L$ is unmixed if and only if all its minimal primes have the same height, if and only if the rank of every maximal closed distributive sublattice through an atom of the diamond is $\mathrm{rank}(L)-1$; in this case $I_L$ is radical.
comment: 18 pages. Every comment is very welcome!

title: Two Knuth orbits of order 256 without primitive semifield coordinatizations
summary: We exhibit two Knuth orbits of semifield planes of order 256 in which every coordinatizing semifield is nonprimitive on both the left and the right. Each orbit consists of two isotopy classes. The first orbit contains 168 isomorphism classes of unital semifields and the second contains 32. We give binary multiplication matrices for a representative of each orbit and an exhaustive computation that verifies nonprimitivity and the counts directly from these matrices.
comment: 3 pages, 2 tables. C++17 source code and computational output included as ancillary files

title: Auslander bounds under recollements and arrow removal
summary: Auslander bounds measure uniformity in the eventual vanishing of extension groups and are closely related to homological conjectures, including the Auslander-Reiten conjecture and finitistic dimension conjecture. We study global and finitistic Auslander bounds of finite-dimensional algebras under recollements and arrow removal. For a recollement induced by an idempotent $e$ of an algebra $Λ$, we establish inequalities comparing the bounds of $Λ$ with those of the quotient algebra $Λ/ΛeΛ$ and the corner algebra $eΛe$. We also establish comparison results for cleft extensions and deduce that arrow removal preserves finiteness of both the global and finitistic Auslander bounds. Finally, we construct radical-square-zero algebras with $\findim(Λ_n)=0$ and $\mr{fab}(Λ_n)=\mr{gb}(Λ_n)=n$ for every $n\geq1$, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between finitistic Auslander bounds and finitistic dimen

title: Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories
summary: We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy

title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
summary: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. title: On generalizations of the Cohen structure theorem
summary: The Cohen structure theorem is an important tool in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. Recent work of Caviglia, Goswami, and Mesiti addresses the related question of which unital rings admit a maximal ideal for which the natural projection admits a section; for such rings, they prove a structure theorem in terms of semidirect products of rings. In this paper, we extract the underlying mechanism of their structure theorem to address when unital rings admit a nonzero proper ideal whose associated projection map has this property. We also address other settings involving ideals with conditions which are determined by ring theoretic properties of the corresponding quotient.

title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
summary: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.

title: When Is an OIRI-Algebra a Banach Lattice? Structure Theorems and Counterexamples
summary: This paper investigates the exact conditions under which a relatively uniformly complete semiprime $f$-algebra whose order ideals are ring ideals (an OIRI-algebra) admits a norm turning it into a Banach lattice or an AM-space. While recent literature claimed that this equivalence holds automatically in the presence of a weak order unit, we construct a concrete counterexample within a relatively uniformly complete vector lattice showing that this assertion fails in general. By analyzing the canonical embedding $ψ:A\rightarrow Orth(A)$, we prove that the equivalence between being an OIRI-algebra, admitting an AM-space or Banach lattice norm and satisfying $Orth(A)=$ $Stab(A)$ $=Z(A$) holds under the assumption that $ψ\left( A\right) $ is relatively uniformly closed in $Orth(A)$ (alongside a characterization via finite elements in the unitization $A^{\sharp}$). We also deduce immediate cons

title: Decomposition of trilinear forme
summary: In this work, we are interested in the decomposition of trilinear forms. We associate this decomposition with the decomposition into irreducible subspaces of the group algebra associated with the symmetric group. We have a correspondence between a ternary form and a symmetric trilinear form, in the same way that we have the correspondence between a quadratic form and a symmetric quadratic form. We are then interested in the decomposition of ternary forms into a sum of cubes of linear forms and as an application we find the Tartaglia formulae on the expression of the roots of equations of degree 3.

title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
summary: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $λ$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+λ=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.
comment: 14 pages -- some cosmetic corrections were made in the previous version

title: Stafford's conjecture on cyclicity of torsion modules
summary: We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero $A_n(k)$, every nonzero $d\in A_n(k)$ admits $F,R,S\in A_n(k)$ such that $1=dR+FdS$, a conjecture Stafford proposed in 1978. As a consequence, every finitely generated torsion right $A_n(k)$-module is cyclic. The proof maps $d$, by a symplectic change of variables, to a normal form $\tilde d$ and shows that the cyclic module $Q=A_n(k)/(\tilde dA_n(k)+x_1^N\tilde dA_n(k))$ vanishes. We first show that right multiplication by $x_1$ is surjective on $Q$. A comparison of lengths of localized modules over the associated graded ring then gives $\operatorname{gr}Q=x_1\operatorname{gr}Q$, so that the characteristic variety of $Q$ is disjoint from the hyperplane $\{x_1=0\}$. Finally, Gabber's involutivity theorem together with an argument about conormal directions at infinity from algebraic geometry shows that such a characteri

title: Free Products of Vector Lattices
summary: We study free products of vector lattices and their relation to free products of Banach lattices. We characterize the Archimedean vector lattices whose vector lattice free product with every Archimedean vector lattice is again Archimedean: these are precisely those whose finitely generated sublattices are projective. For finitely generated lattices, this connects the free-product property with polyhedral geometry through Baker--Beynon duality. We also show that the Banach lattice free product is the completion of the Archimedean vector lattice free product under the largest lattice norm making the canonical maps contractive. For finitely many factors, the Archimedean vector lattice free product is order dense in the Banach lattice free product. Moreover, it is shown that bounded families of injective lattice homomorphisms also induce injective homomorphisms between Banach lattice free pr

title: The algebraic classification of three-dimensional nilpotent left-symmetric dialgebras
summary: Left-symmetric dialgebras (LSDA) are to left-symmetric algebras what Leibniz algebras are to Lie algebras. We classify the three-dimensional nilpotent LSDA over the complex numbers. To do this we adapt the annihilator-extension (Skjelbred-Sund) method to dialgebras, using the annihilator with respect to both products on both sides, and we compute the second cohomology of all two-dimensional nilpotent LSDA. Up to isomorphism, besides the null and split algebras there are nine non-split algebras and families; the 2-step nilpotent families depend on four and three parameters. We give isomorphism criteria and separating invariants, identify the left-symmetric and diassociative algebras in the list, and complete the two-dimensional classification of an earlier paper.

title: Weak Hilbert's Nullstellensatz for skew polynomials over division rings
summary: We establish a weak Nullstellensatz for skew polynomial rings $R_n=D[x_1,\ldots,x_n;σ]$, where $D$ is a division ring and the commuting variables induce the same automorphism $σ$ of $D$. For $n\ge2$, we characterize the pairs $(D,σ)$ for which every maximal left ideal is generated by $x_1-a_1,\ldots,x_n-a_n$, with $σ(a_j)a_i=σ(a_i)a_j$. The criterion consists of right $σ$-algebraic closure of $D$ and right algebraic closure of the centralizers of all commuting $(n-2)$-tuples in each twisted fixed division ring $E_a=\{c\in D:σ(c)a=ac\}$ for $0\ne a\in D$.

title: The Cooperstein conjecture and additive alternating $d$-codes
summary: Let $\bigwedge^2 V$ be the second exterior power of a vector space $V$ over a finite field. The Cooperstein conjecture asserts a dimension bound for flats external to varieties consisting of points of bounded rank in $\mathrm{PG}(\bigwedge^2 V)$. This geometric problem can be translated into a question about linear spaces of alternating matrices whose nonzero elements have rank at least a prescribed value. For matrices of odd order, the sharp cardinality bound was already established by Delsarte and Goethals (1975). In this paper, we prove the Cooperstein conjecture for matrices of even order and, more generally, we prove its additive analogue by determining, for all admissible parameters, the maximum size of an additive subgroup of alternating matrices in which every nonzero matrix has at least the prescribed rank. Our proof uses Pfaffian equations to characterize alternating matrices o

title: Constructions of reversible linear and DNA codes through $T_{D,g}^n-$set and $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$right polycyclic codes
summary: In this paper we give a construction technique of $T_{D,g}^n-$set for reversible linear codes and reversible DNA codes with their code parameters. This technique yields many reversible MDS codes which significantly improves the $T^n-$set construction by Oztas et.al. in terms of obtained code parameters. Concatenation-based constructions are presented for reversible linear codes satisfying self-duality and linear complementary dual (LCD) conditions, giving necessary and sufficient condition for desired dual properties. We introduce a new notion of $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes. Also, a new construction technique is developed to obtain reversible linear $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes with good parameters (MDS codes) over any finite commutative rings.

title: On representation-theoretic and homological properties of distance algebras of finite graphs
summary: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology as bigraded Tor and Ext groups. We study the representation-theoretic and homological properties of the distance algebra $Σ_G$ of a finite connected graph $G$. We characterize the graphs for which $Σ_G$ is representation-finite, multiserial, biserial, or self-injective by an explicit graph-theoretic classification. We also compute the finitistic, self-injective, and dominant dimensions for several natural families of graphs. For a finite modular lattice $L$, we consider the distance algebra $Σ_L$ associated to the Hasse graph of $L$, and show that $Σ_L$ is Auslander--Gorenstein precisely when $L$ is a finite direct product of chains. We also present a family of minimal Auslander--Gorenstein distance algebras, namely, those associated to punctured hypercubes, whose finitistic (equivalently, s

title: On continuous unitriangular matrices on \(\mathbb R^2\)
summary: Let \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) be the group of complex \(2\times 2\)-matrices with determinant \(1\). We prove that each continuous map \(A:\R^2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) can be written in the form \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1&f_1\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_2&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_3\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_4&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_5\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \] where \(f_1,\ldots,f_5:\R^2\to\C\) are continuous functions.

title: Boxes in Infinite Words: Complexity, Automata, and Point Modules
summary: Motivated by the geometry of point modules over monomial algebras, we introduce a box-counting function associated to a right-infinite word over a finite alphabet. An extendable box is a family of finite words obtained by choosing letters independently at each position, subject to the condition that all choices admit a common infinite right continuation in the associated subshift. We prove several results for these functions for words of linearly bounded complexity. For $k$-automatic words, we show using techniques from first-order logic that the total box-counting function is $k$-regular. Finally, we apply our results to prove eventual affine growth of the number of positive-dimensional irreducible components in finite projections of point-module spaces associated to semiprime monomial algebras of at most quadratic growth.

title: Exceptional cubics on 7-manifolds
summary: A $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ on a $7$-manifold $\mathcal M$ determines a two-dimensional space of invariant totally symmetric cubic forms on each fiber of the rank-$27$ bundle $S^2_0T^*\mathcal M$ of traceless symmetric $2$-tensors. This space is spanned by the trace cubic $C_0$ and a cubic $C_\varphi$ that, up to a constant factor, is the pointwise integrand of the Yukawa coupling on the $G_2$ moduli space. We determine the exact infinitesimal stabilizers over $\mathbb C$ of all nonzero cubics in this family. For $C_0+λC_\varphi$, the stabilizer has dimension $78$ precisely at the two non-real values $λ_\pm=(1\pm i\sqrt7)/8$. Its dimension is $21$ for $C_0$ and $14$ in all other cases. At $λ_\pm$, the stabilizer is simple of type $E_6$, and the corresponding cubic is linearly equivalent to the complex Albert algebra cubic norm. The two cubics at $λ_\pm$, which we call critical, define co

title: Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
summary: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $π_0$ of $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $π_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},π_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)})$.

title: Algebras Generated by Two Idempotent Matrices: Classification up to Isomorphism and Applications
summary: This paper is a continuation of the earlier work by the author and Falguni Roy \cite{biswas2025comprehensive} on the algebra \(\operatorname{alg}(P,Q)\) generated by two idempotent matrices \(P,Q\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\). A complete classification of these algebras up to algebra isomorphism is presented, without imposing any additional restrictions on the idempotents. As an application, group invertibility in \(\operatorname{alg}(P,Q)\) is employed to obtain an explicit solution to a particular system of linear equations.

title: A new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras
summary: This paper introduces a new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras and investigates the corresponding bialgebra structures. To this end, we first study an invariant-c$2$c form on a compatible Lie algebra, namely a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form that is invariant with respect to one Lie bracket and is a commutative $2$-cocycle with respect to the other, which naturally arises from a quadratic differential Novikov algebra. Then we introduce the notion of compatible Lie-anti-pre-Lie algebras (compatible LAPL algebras in short), which serve as the underlying algebra structures of compatible Lie algebras endowed with invariant-c$2$c forms. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a compatible LAPL bialgebra, which is shown to be equivalent to a Manin triple of compatible Lie algebras with respect to the invariant-c$2$c form. We investigate triangular compatible LAPL bialgebra

title: Full $t$-Linkage, Cancellation, and Almost Krull Domains
summary: Motivated by open questions of Kabbaj and Mimouni, we determine the position of full $t$-linkage among the standard classes of integral domains and its relationship with almost Krullness. Full linkage for a star operation is equivalent to cancellation in the monoid of all nonzero fractional star ideals. For the $t$-operation, this full cancellation law, denoted by $\mathrm{TCL}$, lies strictly between the $t$-almost Dedekind and completely integrally closed classes; on the $\mathrm{PvMD}$ locus, we recover the known $t$-almost Dedekind characterization. We prove that $\mathrm{TCL}$ and almost Krullness are incomparable. A monoid algebra arising from Reinhart's example satisfies $\mathrm{TCL}$ but is neither almost Krull nor a $\mathrm{PvMD}$. In the opposite direction, we construct a locally factorial almost Krull domain with a maximal ideal $0\ne M=M_t=(M^2)_t\subsetneq D$. For this dom

title: Block Generalized Inverses in Skew Corner Pairs
summary: We view generalized inverses from another perspective, through invertibility in the skew corner bimodules $eRf$ attached to a pair of distinct idempotents $e, f$ of a ring $R$. Many generalized inverses are defined by a system of equations together with conditions on ranges and kernels, which makes them harder to visualize as inverses in the traditional sense. In the language of invertible blocks, however, they become genuine one or two-sided inverses of a suitable compression of the element. We will systematically show how block invertibility in a skew corner $eRf$ can be used to visualize Drazin's $(b,c)$-inverse, which contains the Moore--Penrose, Bott-Duffin $(e,f)$ inverses amongst others. On this foundation we develop a way to produce units of the corner ring from complementary blocks, and transport stable range one across two-sided Peirce decompositions for distinct idempotents.

title: Hochschild Cocycle and Universality of Merge
summary: The Hopf algebra Markov chain dynamical system, on the Hopf algebra of non-planar binary forests, that models the action of Merge on workspaces in Chomsky's Minimalist Model of syntax, satisfies a universal property, determined by the fact that the Merge operation is a Hochschild 1-cocycle. This universal property has an interpretation in terms of models of the syntax-semantics interface, as it shows that, if the side of semantics possesses a sufficiently rich compositional structure, then that structure is uniquely induced by the syntactic Merge, once the semantic values of lexical items and syntactic features are assigned. We illustrate how this universality works by showing, in particular, full compatibility of this Hopf algebraic formulation with Heim-Kratzer semantics.

title: A characterisation of almost gentle algebras
summary: A finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special biserial. We prove the corresponding characterisation for almost gentle algebras, that is, an algebra over such a field is almost gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special multiserial, which answers a question of Green and Schroll. As a consequence, the property of having a special multiserial trivial extension is invariant under stable equivalence.

title: Embedding of Barnes-Wall lattices into Cayley-Dickson algebras
summary: The family of Barnes-Wall lattices includes the balanced Barnes-Wall lattice $M_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$ and two ordinary Barnes-Wall lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, which are geometrically equivalent to each other. Embedding of these lattices into the Cayley-Dickson algebras of an appropriate dimension is considered. It is shown that for all $n \geq 2$ the lattices $M_n$ and $L_n$ are closed under multiplication and are generated by the sets of pairwise products of their elements. The lattices $L_n \cdot L'_n$, $L'_n \cdot L_n$, and $L'_n \cdot L'_n$, generated by pairwise products of elements of the lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$, also are studied.

title: Iso-Multiplication Modules over Noncommutative Rings: Triangular Classification and Rational Rigidity
summary: A right A-module M is called iso-multiplication if for every submodule N of M there is a two-sided ideal B of A such that N ?A MB. We construct noncommutative examples of isomultiplication modules which are not multiplication modules, including triangular algebras of arbitrary dimension. We classify all iso-multiplication modules over T_2(k) without a finitegeneration assumption. For a semiprime right Goldie ring we prove that the classical localization of an iso-multiplication module is multiplicity-free. Further consequences address composition length and local rings; we distinguish these from standard Morita, Ore-localization, and chaincondition results.

title: A DGLA approach to global extensions and deformations of Lie algebras
summary: In this paper, we study the global extension problem of Lie algebras from the perspective of dgLas and the Maurer--Cartan formulism. We propose a new equivalence relation of global extensions, generalizing the early work of Agore and Militaru. This new concept can be better adopted in the study of classical contraction and deformation problems for Lie algebras. Meanwhile, we construct dgLas that control based formal deformations of global extension structures under these equivalences. As byproducts, we obtain the classification of infinitesimal deformations in terms of the cohomology of the controlling dgLas and the corresponding obstruction theory. We relate the dgLa controlling deformation of global extensions under framed equivalence to that of non-abelian extensions constructed by Frégier, obtaining a geometric interpretation of the decomposition of global cohomology into as a disjoi

title: All unital reversible nonsymmetric rings of order 256
summary: A ring is reversible if $ab=0$ implies $ba=0$, and symmetric if $abc=0$ implies $acb=0$. Szabo proved that the smallest order of a unital reversible nonsymmetric ring is $256$. We classify all such minimal rings: up to isomorphism there are exactly $186$ of them, $19$ of characteristic $2$ and $167$ of characteristic $4$, and there are none of characteristic $8$ or higher. All of them are local with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$, the nilpotency index of the Jacobson radical is $4$ or $5$, and $120$ of them form $60$ pairs $R$, $R^{op}$ of non-isomorphic rings. The classification is obtained by a general method of deformation of graded algebras over $\mathbb{Z}/2^e\mathbb{Z}$, whose completeness is proved, and it is checked against the known examples: $\mathbb{F}_2Q_8$, Szabo's example and the ten rings in the family of generalized quaternion rings studied by Grau, Oller-Marcén and Szabo.
comment: 13 pages, 3 tables. Ancillary files: presentations of the 186 rings and Python code. Submitted to J. Pure Appl. Algebra

title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
summary: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we give exact counting formulas as functions of $|X|$ in terms of finite sums and generating functions. Such pairs correspond bijectively to actions on $X$ of the semigroup presented by two generators and the prescribed relation. The proofs use images, fibers, and the decomposition of functional digraphs into directed cycles with rooted trees attached. Several constructions apply beyond these sixteen identities: they give recurrences for homomorphisms between arbitrary prescribed functional digraphs and formulas for pairs satisfying $f^a=g^b$, where $a,b$ are fixed positive integers. We also derive an explicit inclusion-exclusion formula over subsets of $X

title: Spectral coincidence and generalized Hua inversion in rings and Banach algebras
summary: For additively coupled elements with invertible sum and selected commuting outer inverses, we study coincidence of the core idempotents and inversion of the Hua element. Intertwining forces coincidence for finite-Drazin data in unital rings and for generalized-Drazin data in complex unital Banach algebras. Under coincidence, the output splits into an invertible core and a complementary parallel sum, called the residue, yielding exact criteria for inverse existence and success of the prescribed candidate. Explicit ring examples show that strict generalized-Drazin input inverses need not force coincidence under intertwining, and that a common core with a Harte-quasinilpotent residue need not give a strict output inverse. For rings finite as modules over a commutative central subring with the same identity, we prove intertwining transfer and automatic bicommutation for commuting outer inver

title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
summary: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapstoχ_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat

title: Quaternion Matrix Tuples with Common Invariant Subspaces: Dimension and Nonuniqueness
summary: Let $M_n(\mathbb{H})$ denote the algebra of $n\times n$ quaternion matrices. We study common invariant right subspaces of tuples in $M_n(\mathbb{H})^r$ and determine exact real semialgebraic dimensions for two associated sets. If $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ are positive integers, $n=n_1+\cdots+n_s$, and $q=\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq s}n_an_b$, the set of tuples preserving at least one nested chain with successive increments $n_1,\ldots,n_s$ has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)q$. For $r\geq2$ and $1\leq k<n$, the set of tuples with at least two distinct common $k$-dimensional right invariant subspaces has dimension $4rn^2-4(r-1)(k(n-k)+n-1)$. The proofs use finite right-module coordinates and a common local-rank argument.

title: Cotorsion pairs in $η$-extensions with applications to $θ$-extension rings and tensor rings
summary: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_ηF$ be an $η$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $η$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $η$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $δ$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $η$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(Δ(\mathcal X),Δ(\mathcal X)^\per

title: Classification problems for diassociative and dendriform algebras: a survey
summary: Diassociative algebras (associative dialgebras) and dendriform algebras are vector spaces with two binary operations, introduced by J.-L. Loday in the study of Leibniz algebras; their operads are Koszul dual to each other. We survey the classification problem for these two classes, including the Zinbiel algebras, the commutative dendriform algebras, which are Koszul dual to Leibniz algebras. We recall the definitions, the main examples and the Loday diagram with its extension by left-symmetric algebras and dialgebras, and describe the methods used to classify algebras of small dimension: direct computation from lists of associative algebras, annihilator (central) extensions and geometric classification by degenerations. We then collect, by dimension, the known algebraic classifications of diassociative algebras, dendriform algebras and their commutative case, the Zinbiel algebras, point

title: Sum of Powers with Matrix Coefficients
summary: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We consider polynomial maps with constants $ω(x,y)=A_1x^k+A_2y^k$ on $M_n(F)$, where $A_1$ is invertible and $k\geq2$. We show that the necessary condition for surjectivity obtained by Saini and Singh (Polynomial maps with constants on matrix algebra, Linear Algebra Appl. 752 (2027), 256-277) is not sufficient in any dimension $n\geq6$. We also completely characterize surjectivity for $n=5$ and $6$.

title: NS-bialgebras, the NS-Yang-Baxter equation and dendriform D-bialgebras
summary: In this paper, we develop a bialgebra theory for NS-algebras via the Manin triple approach. We first study representations of NS-algebras and establish an equivalence among NS-bialgebras, matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-algebras. We then introduce the NS-Yang-Baxter equation (NS-YBE) and show that its symmetric solutions induce triangular NS-bialgebras. We further investigate the relationship between symmetric solutions of the NS-YBE and $\mathcal O$-operators of NS-algebras, and characterize pre-NS-algebras in terms of invertible $\mathcal O$-operators. As an application, we investigate the relation between NS-bialgebras and dendriform D-bialgebras via double constructions of Connes cocycles. In particular, we show that every NS-bialgebra induces a dendriform D-bialgebra structure on the direct sum of two copies of its underlying vector space.

title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
summary: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $Θ_0, Θ_1, Θ_2, \dots$ with $Θ_k \circ Θ_j = Θ_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. title: On Tensor Invertibility and Spectral Localization under the M-Product
summary: The growth of multidimensional data demands rigorous multilinear algebraic frameworks. While M-product tensor transformations mimic matrix operations over a commutative ring of tubal scalars, the presence of zero-divisors has historically limited theoretical analysis. To overcome these limitations, in this paper, we introduce a novel tubal determinant to rigorously define tensor invertibility and resolve the zero-divisor effect (McCoy defect). We also prove a tubal rank-nullity theorem using projective submodules and formalize tubal spectral analysis, yielding a novel Gershgorin hypersphere theorem. In addition to this, we find the Frobenius perturbation bounds for the pseudoinverse. Supporting the theoretical algebraic results, some numerical examples and visual illustrations are also provided in this paper. Finally, the theoretical results are applied experimentally for numerical illus

title: Dimensionalities on monoids
summary: We study equivalence relations on monoids in $\Rel$ that are lax morphisms. We call them \emph{dimensionalities}. We prove that the quotient of a monoid in $\Rel$ by a dimensionality is again a monoid. We prove that polygroupoids (and hence hypergroups) are exactly the symmetric $†$-Frobenius structures in $\Rel$. We use this characterization to prove that the quotient of a polygroupoid by a dimensionality that preserves the inverse is a polygroupoid.

title: Admissible Yang--Baxter equation for Nijenhuis perm superalgebras
summary: We develop a superization of the theory of admissible Yang--Baxter equations for Nijenhuis perm algebras initiated by Ma and Song. We introduce Nijenhuis perm superalgebras, their representations, and the dual representation, with Koszul signs chosen so that the contraction of the Yang--Baxter tensor matches the $\mathcal O$-operator equation exactly. We define Nijenhuis perm superbialgebras and characterise them by matched pairs. In the coboundary case, we show that every even supersymmetric solution of the $S$-admissible perm Yang--Baxter equation gives rise to a Nijenhuis perm superbialgebra, and we give sufficient conditions for a perm superalgebra to admit a Nijenhuis operator constructed from such a solution. Examples with purely odd components illustrate the role of the grading.

title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
summary: We determine the spaces of \(δ\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(δ\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(δ=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(δ=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
summary: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.
comment: correction of Lemma 2.1; comments are welcome

title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellensätze with Operator Coefficients
summary: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional oper

title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{silp-spli}$
summary: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.

title: Equivariant Levi restriction
summary: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $\bbC$, $L\subset G$ a Levi subgroup, and $\cL\subset\cG$ their Langlands duals. Macerato \cite{macerato2023leviequivariantrestrictionsphericalperverse} computed the $\cL(\calO)$-equivariant cohomology of the $!$-restriction to $\GrL$ of the regular spherical perverse sheaf on $\GrG$, and identified it with the functions on the partial Kostant--Whittaker reduction $T^*(G/U,\psiL)$, where $\psiL$ is the possibly degenerate Whittaker character of $U$ determined by $L$. We add loop rotation. Our main result is: the $\LO$-equivariant cohomology of the same object is the ring $\Dh(G/U,\psiL)$ of asymptotic $\psiL$-twisted differential operators on $G/U$. For a single $\IC_V$ the answer is the space of intertwiners $\bM_\hbar(\psiL)\to V\otimes\bM_\hbar(\psiL)$ of the universal Verma--Whittaker module. This interpolates between results of Bezrukavnik

title: Resolution of ladder representations for classical groups
summary: Atobe has introduced ladder representations of the $p$-adic groups $\mathbf{Sp}(2n)$ and $\mathbf{SO}(2n+1)$, which contain the strongly positive discrete series and Mœglin's representations attached to irreducible Arthur parameters, and has expressed their characters as alternating sums of costandard modules. We show that all the coefficients of this formula are $\pm1$, with the sign given by the dimension of the orbit of the Langlands parameter, and that these representations have coresolutions of Cousin type by costandard modules, whose Euler characteristic is Atobe's formula.

title: An explicit BGG-type resolution of the spin/oscillator module for osp(2m+1|2n)
summary: We construct an explicit resolution of the spin/oscillator representation of the Lie superalgebra osp(2m+1|2n) by parabolic Verma modules. The resolution appears as the Chevalley-Eilenberg chain complex of the Lie algebra of quadratic operators in the universal Heisenberg algebra of the vector superspace C^{m|n}. In particular, its differentials are given by unified linear algebra formulas and all have degree 2 with respect to the standard grading of Verma modules.

title: Uniform dominance of Golod local rings
summary: We prove that every Golod local ring $R$ is uniformly dominant. More precisely, we show that its dominant index is at most the embedding dimension of $R$. The proof is based on a numerical criterion for formality of bounded complexes whose homology is annihilated by the maximal ideal.

title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
summary: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schrödinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Schörkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix s
