title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
summary: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
summary: We propose Spectral Jet KAN (SJ-KAN) to reduce the cost of differentiation and the network complexity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. The input coordinates are embedded through Chebyshev bases whose spatial derivatives are known in closed form, and all differentiation matrices are computed once for the collocation points before training. A single linear layer compresses the Chebyshev bases into a few latent features, and a single nonlinear Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) layer maps these features to the physical variables. Because the basis derivatives are known in advance and the compression is linear, the spatial derivatives in the NS equations are carried through the network analytically by a fixed sequence of matrix products and elementwise operations. title: Defining the mathematical family tree with a minimal programming language
summary: I introduce MLISP, a Turing-complete language with nine single-character commands (a b c d f 0 i j k), and use it to define 88 mathematical structures and a family tree of 65 theories that they model, with three aims: Pedagogy: It presents the mathematical structures in a unified way, with standardized presentation tableaus that define them and axiomatized theories that describe them. title: Higher-symmetry selection rules for second- and third-harmonic radiation in the Bullough-Dodd model
summary: We investigate nonlinear excitations of the discrete shape mode about a static complex soliton of the integrable Bullough-Dodd model. Extending the linear stability analysis to third order in the excitation amplitude, we construct explicit spatially localised corrections to the shape-mode oscillation and determine its nonlinear frequency shift using the Poincaré-Lindstedt method. Although both the second and third harmonics lie inside the continuous spectrum of the linearised fluctuation operator, the corresponding inhomogeneous equations admit exact localised particular solutions. We demonstrate that the nonlinear sources have vanishing on-shell overlaps with the scattering states at both harmonic frequencies, suppressing the corresponding radiative responses. title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
summary: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
summary: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.

title: Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals
summary: Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. title: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization
summary: Here we present an approach to quantifying superposition of nonorthogonal reference states through quantum coherence. No change of basis achieves this: every orthonormal basis makes some superposition-free states appear coherent. We show that orthogonalization succeeds instead as a measurement mapping every reference state onto a multiple of a basis vector in each outcome; such measurements are exactly the free operations that convert superposition into coherence. The largest average coherence they extract from a state, which we call its degree of superposition, turns every coherence measure into a superposition measure with the same operational meaning. title: Uniform Ionization Bounds in Molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizsäcker Theory
summary: We study the molecular Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizsäcker theory. For each fixed number $K$ of nuclei, we prove that every minimizer of mass $N$ satisfies $N\leq Z+C_K$, where $Z$ is the total nuclear charge, and $C_K>0$ is independent of the nuclear charges and positions. This answers the molecular large-charge ionization question posed in [R. L. Frank, P. T. Nam and H. Van Den Bosch, CPAM, 2018]. For $N\geq Z$, we also compare the screened potentials and electronic radii of Thomas--Fermi--Dirac--von Weizsäcker minimizers with those of the corresponding neutral molecular Thomas--Fermi minimizers and establish a uniform bound on the ionization energy.

title: Derivation of BCS functionals and gap equations from quantum many-body fermionic system
summary: We consider 3D single-species spin-$1/2$ Fermi systems with general dispersion relation and general attractive interaction initially inside a finite box. Up to some critical temperature $T_c$ determined by the interaction and system size, we establish, for the expected discrete BCS gap equation, existence of positive maximal solution. We then prove the uniqueness of nonzero (not identically zero) nonnegative solution. That is, any nonzero nonnegative solution, if exist or obtained via other methods, must equal to the positive maximal solution. Building on such a well-posedness result and assuming quasi-freeness, we prove the emergence of the $SU(2)$ symmetry of the finite system. title: A Steady Theory for Highly Unsteady Thin Airfoil Motions
summary: A generalized steady thin airfoil theory is built not from steady flow, but from flows in which there exists a frame of reference where the absolute vorticity field is steady. We specialize this general idea to construct a foliation of a domain of phase space for thin airfoil motions in which staying on a leaf of the foliation maintains zero absolute vorticity in the fluid indefinitely. The phase space is described by the airfoil's total rotation rate, speed, and angle of attack. It is found using this definition that one of the preeminent unsteady stall conditions is equivalent to the traditional steady stall condition for this class of flows, various other classical results can be re-interpreted as steady in the absolute vorticity field, and insight is also provided into the surprising experimental results of McGowan et al. title: A decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels and its application to Williamson's diagonal form
summary: In this paper, we establish a decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels, which extends the main result in [K. D. Ikramov, On the Symplectic Eigenvalues of Positive Definite Matrices. Moscow Univ. Comput. Math. Cybern., 42(2018)1-4]. As an application, we present another proof of Williamson's diagonal form for positive-semidefinite matrices with symplectic kernels.

title: The replication-energy limit of PQG reduced-density-matrix theory from a single-fragment semidefinite program
summary: Variational two-electron reduced-density-matrix calculations are not size extensive: the energy per fragment can decrease when identical, strictly noninteracting fragments are replicated [M. Nakata and K. Yasuda, Phys. Rev. A 80, 042109 (2009)]. For the $P$, $Q$, and $G$ conditions (PQG) we prove the following. (i) The energy per fragment converges to the minimum of a semidefinite program (SDP) on one fragment. The limit is reached through negative interfragment covariances of order $1/(k-1)$ for $k$ replicas, which cancel the local electron number and spin fluctuations consistently with a global singlet. (ii) The energy per fragment is nonincreasing in the replica count. (iii) It reaches the limit exactly at a finite replica count. title: Modulation equations and coherence dynamics in a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon
summary: We derive modulation equations for the joint quantum amplitudes of a circulating fluxon and an exchange-coupled qubit chain whose endpoint interacts with the field. A unitary passage operator combines the translational packet, vacuum dressing, and discrete oscillatory modes. A resonant normal form separates the slow amplitude evolution from nonresonant corrections. Ordered emission and return amplitudes generate a second-order correction that changes the population and coherence of an internal qubit. The next ground-band coefficient gives compensating diagonal and near-resonant off-diagonal contributions to the accumulated error. We bound the state error a posteriori. title: Interface currents of magnetized differential systems: quantization and bulk-interface correspondence
summary: This paper concerns transport along an interface between two insulators modeled by self-adjoint differential systems $H$ of arbitrary order, coupled to a magnetic field either by Peierls substitution or, for operators of the form $L^*L+W$, in the factor $L$. Each bulk carries a constant field, which may vanish. The principal symbol of $H$ is either elliptic or has a kernel of constant rank, in which case finitely many bands remain bounded at large momentum, as in rotating shallow water, cold plasmas, Maxwell's equations and pseudospin-one materials. title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
summary: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $γ$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-γ)γ^{γ/(1-γ)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and, for every $0<γ<1$, strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. title: $μ$- and $q$-extension of special functions in quantum field theory
summary: Analytic calculations up to single-scale quantities in perturbative quantum field theory result into special numbers and functions, which are generalizations as iterative integrals over special alphabets. In this way one obtains polylogarithms, Nielsen integrals, the iterated integrals over linear denominator terms, cyclotomic letters, letters induced by quadratic forms, and square-root valued letters. The inverse Mellin transform relates special nested sums to these quantities, which are harmonic sums, generalized harmonic sums, nested sums implied by quadratic forms, cyclotomic harmonic sums, and nested sums containing central binomials. We construct the $μ$- and $q$-extensions of all these special functions. title: Analytic continuation of the T- and S-matrices to unphysical sheets in a multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model
summary: We consider a matrix multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model. First, we formulate conditions on the kernels of the potential matrix that guarantee for the T-matrix (and then for the S-matrix) the existence of analytical continuation to unphysical energy sheets. We also obtain explicit representations for the analytically continued T- and S-matrices on unphysical sheets in terms of these matrices themselves, but only taken in the physical sheet. From the explicit representations obtained, it follows that the resonances on a certain unphysical sheet are nothing but the points at which the corresponding truncation of the scattering matrix in the physical sheet has an eigenvalue of 0.

title: A thermodynamically consistent variational formulation and structure-preserving finite element methods for non-isothermal liquid--vapor flows with moving contact lines
summary: In this paper, we present a variational formulation and structure-preserving finite element methods for non-isothermal liquid--vapor flows with moving contact lines. Based on the dynamic van der Waals theory with gradient contributions and surface thermodynamics, the governing equations and hydrodynamic boundary conditions are derived from a generalized Hamilton's principle for nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Two equivalent variational formulations based on internal energy and Helmholtz free energy are developed, using entropy density and temperature, respectively, as the primary thermal variable. Using the resulting weak forms, compatible spatial operators and discrete thermodynamic chain rules, we construct two thermodynamically consistent fully discrete finite element schemes. title: Analysis of Geometric Eigenmode Splitting in Planar Microwave Resonators
summary: A traditional challenge in planar microwave resonator design is to find geometric mechanisms that can control individual resonant frequencies - or tune coupling between specific eigenmodes - without affecting other system parameters, such as the center frequency. Achieving this capability can be transformative for the design of microwave sensors, filters, antennas and resonant networks. Starting from first principles, we outline the development of an analytical method that guides practical design by suggesting specific perturbation shapes capable of achieving resonant mode-splitting while keeping the center frequency nearly stationary. This approach opens the door to novel designs that were previously difficult to discover or optimize. title: Split Hamiltonian structure for Vlasov--Maxwell equations and cylindrical pinch equilibria
summary: We study the linearized Vlasov--Maxwell equations for cylindrical pinch equilibria, including the classical Bennett pinch, Gaussian equilibria from our earlier work, and a rigidly rotating $θ$-pinch. Conservation of particle momentum along a symmetry brings the energy principle of Lin and Strauss into these geometries. We work on a graph space for the symmetry component of the vector potential. For the Bennett $z$-pinch the bare potential form has one negative direction, but the particle-number constraint removes it and the entire $z$-independent spectrum lies on the imaginary axis. For a $z$-pinch with variable axial drift, every $z$-independent growing mode is radial. We prove axisymmetric spectral stability for a Gaussian $θ$-pinch in an explicit range of axis slopes and for a center-peaked, rigidly rotating $θ$-pinch. title: Local and Global Bifurcation for Axisymmetric Stationary Relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell Equilibria
summary: We study bifurcation of stationary two-species relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell equilibria on bounded axisymmetric domains. Velocity-moment and elliptic spectral bounds give computable tests for simple crossings, their number and separation, while the local theorem gives a branch-direction formula. Explicit two-species families exhibit electric-only, magnetic-only, and joint field-norm escape.

title: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers
summary: Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. title: Stability of a Paraboloidal Steady Solution for the 2D Surface Growth Model
summary: In this paper we consider the stability problem of 2D surface growth model. To be specific, we prove that the small perturbation of the paraboloidal steady solution decays to zero in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The decay occurs both for the perturbation and its gradient, whose decay rates are $O(t^{-1/2})$ and $O(t^{-1}\log t)$, respectively. The proof is based on the linearization of the perturbation equation and the bootstrap argument to close the statement in nonlinear equation. Sufficient conditions for stability require the initial data and its gradient of the perturbation to be small in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and Wiener algebra $\mathcal{A}$. It is notable that the smallness in second derivative is not necessary, which is physically reasonable because large second derivative would lead to high surface energy and it is expected to be relaxed in short time. title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
summary: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. title: The marginal sine-Gordon field theory
summary: At $β_*^2=8π$ we construct the two-dimensional sine--Gordon vacuum from a noncompact real lattice field with nearest-neighbor kinetic energy, positive cosine activity and zero Dirichlet data. Its mass $M$ is the lower edge of the energy spectrum above the vacuum. In units of the length $a_{\rm exit}$ at which the flow leaves weak coupling it obeys $0<c_-\le M a_{\rm exit}\le c_+<\infty$ on compact positive endpoint intervals, with uniform constants. A prescribed response to a smooth background in a fixed square determines the nonlinear asymptotically free bare parameters at each sufficiently fine cutoff. title: On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
summary: We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.

title: An Implicit Discrete Adjoint Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Sensitivity Analysis and Shape Optimization in Multiscale Gas Flows
summary: Accurate and efficient gradient-based sensitivity evaluation remains challenging for performance optimization in multiscale flows with complex geometries. To address this challenge, this work develops a matrix-free discrete adjoint method for the steady implicit unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) through the exact linearization and transposition of its converged fixed-point operator. The method employs a hybrid differentiation strategy that combines local automatic differentiation (AD) of complex nonlinear kinetic kernels with analytically derived tangent and transpose operators for the coupled macroscopic--microscopic implicit updates and mass-conservation projection. This formulation ensures exact discrete consistency across both flow and geometric dependencies while avoiding global Jacobian assembly and the memory overhead of end-to-end reverse-mode AD. title: Long-time dynamics of open quantum systems: mathematical and physical aspects
summary: Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. title: Emulator-enabled calibration and uncertainty quantification of $β$-decay calculations within the energy density functional theory
summary: Predictions of $β$-decay half-lives of neutron-rich nuclei and their uncertainties critically impact our understanding of the astrophysical rapid neutron capture process. To provide quantified predictions within nuclear energy density functional theory, as customarily done, we perform Bayesian calibrations of two coupling constants: the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing strength and the isovector spin-density coupling. We apply an E-optimal experimental design for choosing the calibration sets. We employ the proton-neutron finite-amplitude method with Skyrme energy density functionals using emulators of half-lives and Gamow--Teller resonance energies. The calculated $Q_β$ values are fine-tuned to experimental values. title: Emergence of collectivity in the $0^+_2$ band of $^{92}$Zr
summary: The $2^+_2 \rightarrow 0^+_2$ transition in $^{92}$Zr was observed for the first time in a high-statistics decay study of the 10-day isomer $^{92m}$Nb. Its $E2$ transition strength of 8.9(7) W.u. is enhanced by 40% relative to the ground state band, providing evidence for a collective structure built on the $0^+_2$ state which is analogous to the deformed shape-coexisting configuration in $^{94}$Zr.

title: Bypassing the Nanoampere Limit: A Thick-Target Methodology for Ultra-Low-Energy Resonances in the $^{11}$B(p,$α$)2$α$ Reaction
summary: Precise measurements of the low-energy cross section for the $^{11}$B(p,$α$)2$α$ reaction is critical for nuclear astrophysics and fusion energy research, yet such measurements are experimentally demanding due to the reaction's extremely small cross section. Conventional thin-target experiments are fundamentally limited to nanoampere beam currents, which restrict count rates to impractical levels at ultra-low proton energies. To overcome this limitation, we report a correction-free thick-target methodology capable of operating at beam currents of 20-60 microamperes, corresponding to a gain of over three orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo simulations of the full reaction kinematics are employed to determine the absolute reaction yield, eliminating the requirement for empirical normalization factors. title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
summary: An improved camera-based 3D-velocity map imaging (VMI) system was demonstrated with a neuromorphic camera. We show a machine vision event-driven camera can achieve an unprecedented latency of 2 microseconds when detecting single ion/electron with a microchannel plate imaging detector, which boosts the speed of the momentum imaging system to more than 100 kHz, while the system with a conventional frame camera is limited to a few kHz. The high spatial resolution of the camera offers additional performance boost while maintaining excellent multi-hit capability and a high time resolution.

title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
summary: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. title: Study of two-photon femtoscopic correlations in Ag+Ag collisions at $\mathbf{\sqrt{s_{NN}}}$ = 2.55 GeV with HADES
summary: Two-photon correlations can provide unique femtoscopic information, complementing those obtained with charged particles. They also allow to estimate the direct photon yield in the low $p_{T}$ region. We present experimental results on $γ-γ$ correlations in Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.55 GeV, collected by the HADES experiment. Photons were measured using an electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL) and two-photon correlations were determined as one-dimen-sional functions $CF(q_{inv})$. We discuss the observed structures, along with their plausible origin. Finally, we estimate an upper limit for the correlation strength of direct photons for two confidence levels, resulting in values of the order $10^{-4}-10^{-3}$ .

title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
summary: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. title: Fluctuations and Correlations of Conserved Charges in Isobar Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 200 GeV with the STAR Detector
summary: We report measurements of second-order cumulants and correlations of experimentally accessible baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness proxies in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$~GeV with the STAR experiment. The results exhibit similar centrality dependences in the two isobar systems within uncertainties. The baryon-strangeness correlation $C_{BS}$ is compared with lattice-QCD and UrQMD calculations. Motivated by recent lattice-QCD predictions for QCD matter in an external magnetic field, several ratios of conserved-charge correlations are studied as functions of centrality. In peripheral collisions, the measured ratios exhibit the same ordering as the lattice-QCD prediction. title: $Λ$-deuteron scattering below the $Σ$-threshold

title: The Barrel Imaging Calorimeter of the ePIC detector at the Electron-Ion Collider

title: Precision Muon Physics
summary: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments

title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach

title: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework

title: Design of nSPIRAL: a Neutron Spectrometric Position-Weighted Radial Array Long-Counter
summary: We present here the design of a neutron long counter intended to measure neutrons originating from radioactive decays or nuclear reactions. summary: We derive a coupled set of relations between inclusive and semi-exclusive nucleon-knockout electron-scattering cross-section ratios measured for any two nuclei in short-range-correlation (SRC) kinematics and the microscopic neutron-proton, (np-), proton-proton (pp-), and neutron-neutron (nn-) SRC pair populations in those nuclei. title: Construction and Commissioning of the Warwick TPC Platform

title: Development of millikelvin scintillation photodetectors with CUPID

title: The Alpha Clustering Model of the EMC Effect

We make predictions for other nuclei such as $^{16}$O, $^{20}$Ne, and $^{48}$Ca and explore its consequences for a spin-dependent EMC effect and global analysis of nuclear parton distributions.

title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
summary: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.

title: Unpolarized proton PDF with physical quark masses and large momenta
summary: We present a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculation of the proton isovector ($u-d$) unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) at physical sea and valence quark masses, using Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears within the large-momentum effective theory framework. The calculation is performed on a (2+1)-flavor ensemble with a lattice spacing of $a=0.076$ fm and proton momenta up to $2.3$ GeV. We combine kinematically enhanced nucleon interpolating operators, the Coulomb-gauge method, and high-statistics measurements to improve the signal quality at large momenta and quark separations. We use the static regularization-independent momentum subtraction and hybrid schemes to renormalize the bare matrix elements. title: Proton Number Fluctuations in Au+Au and Ag+Ag Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$: A JAM Model Study
summary: Proton number fluctuations in low-energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive to nuclear interactions, baryon-number conservation, and fluctuations of the collision volume, all of which can complicate searches for critical phenomena. We investigate proton-number cumulants and factorial cumulants up to fourth order in Au+Au and Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$ using the JAM hadronic transport model in cascade and mean-field modes. We employ the Centrality-Independent Genuine Cumulant Analysis fRamework (CIGAR) to suppress the initial-volume fluctuations and compare its results with those obtained using conventional centrality-bin-width corrections. CIGAR closely reproduces the participant-number-based reference, whereas the multiplicity-based analysis exhibits substantial deviations. title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
summary: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 φ)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer Rényi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. title: Precise measurements of the 3H/3He charge form factor ratio and their impact on the 3H-3He charge radius difference
summary: Nuclear form factor measurements can be used to extract the nuclear charge radius. Extractions of the 3H-3He charge radius difference are limited by the modest amount of data for tritium elastic scattering at low momentum transfer. The experiment made a precise measurement of the 3H/3He form factor ratio at low momentum transfer which is combined with the absolute 3He measurements to provide improved 3H data. This provides an improved determination of the absolute normalization corrections of world data sets, giving improved precision for the low-Q^2 measurements that are most sensitive to the radius. title: How to isolate charm production mechanisms using charm-anticharm rapidity and azimuthal angle differences
summary: Charm production in hadronic collisions proceeds via many different processes, which makes it hard to calculate from first principles. Using PYTHIA simulations, we study correlations between charm and anticharm hadrons and show that hard-process charm, final-state splitting charm, and initial-state-shower charm populate markedly different regions of rapidity and azimuthal-angle difference. In particular, selections on the pair rapidity separation, $Δy$, can strongly enrich or suppress the near-side final-state splitting contribution and thereby provide experimental sensitivity to the different production processes. A comparison with existing LHCb $D^0\bar{D}^0$ correlation measurements from Run 1 motivates more differential studies using the substantially larger LHC data sets now available. title: Elliptic flow of $φ$ and $Ω$ via quark recombination mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
summary: Multi-strange hadrons, such as the $φ$ meson and $Ω$ baryon, serve as unique probes for the properties of the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. We check the scaling properties of $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$ and find the number-of-constituent-quark (NCQ) scaled $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$ are approximately equal. title: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(γ,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $γ$-Process Calculations
summary: The $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)^{168}\mathrm{Tm}$ cross section has been measured at the Shanghai Laser Electron Gamma Source (SLEGS) using quasi-monoenergetic laser-Compton-scattering $γ$ rays over the energy range from the neutron threshold to 14.61~MeV. title: Sensitivity of jet and dijet observables to medium effects in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV using X-SCAPE/JETSCAPE
summary: Establishing jet quenching in small collision systems, such as high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions at the LHC, is challenging because the expected modifications are small and can be obscured by event-selection effects, multiparton interactions, and multijet production. We examine the response of several jet and dijet observables to medium-induced changes in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV using the JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE framework. First, a simplified Bjorken-expanding brick medium is compared with a vacuum reference for several brick lengths and strengths of transport coefficients. Second, separately generated realistic vacuum and medium samples with fluctuating initial conditions and event-by-event hydrodynamic evolution are compared after selecting the highest-activity 20% of events. title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
summary: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. title: Flavor decomposition of the nucleon axial and tensor charges from lattice QCD
summary: We determine the nucleon axial and tensor charges using four ensembles of twisted-mass clover-improved fermions with approximately equal physical volumes of about 5.5~fm and four lattice spacings, $ a=0.05$~fm, 0.06~fm, 0.07~fm, and 0.08~fm. The mass of the degenerate up and down, strange and charm quarks are tuned to approximately their physical values. We compute both connected and disconnected contributions to determine the isovector and isoscalar charges and their flavour decomposition. For the nucleon isovector axial charge we find $g_A^{u-d}=1.263(34)(26)$, in agreement with the experimental value. For the isoscalar axial charge we find $g_A^{u+d}=0.458(16)(1)$, while for the corresponding tensor charges we find $g_T^{u-d}=0.951(21)(5)$ and $g_T^{u+d}=0.556(16)(5)$.

title: NuSTEC Review: Current Experimental and Theoretical Challenges of Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
summary: The precise measurement of neutrino properties is among the highest priorities in fundamental particle physics, involving many experimental and theoretical efforts worldwide. Since the experiments rely on the interactions of neutrinos in the nuclear environment, the planned advances in the scope and precision of these experiments require a commensurate effort in understanding and modeling the hadronic and nuclear physics of these interactions, as incorporated in neutrino event generators. This modeling is essential to every phase of the experimental analyses, and the theoretical uncertainties play an important role in interpreting experimental results. title: Evidence for quark+quark pairing in proton formation
summary: The question of pairing between quarks inside baryons is addressed by calculating the fragmentation functions that describe production of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in high-energy collisions and comparing attendant predictions with phenomenological global fits to available data and directly with data on hadron multiplicities. The fragmentation functions are obtained from nucleon parton distribution functions using the Drell-Levy-Yan relation and subsequently solving a coupled set of pion, kaon, and nucleon jet cascade equations. Strong empirical evidence is found for the presence of diquark correlations. In comparison with global fits, $d$ (down) quark to proton fragmentation ($d\to p$) exhibits the clearest signals. title: Probing deformed nuclei: Experimental insights into excited states of $^{152,153,154}$Gd isotopes through fusion-evaporation reactions
summary: The rare-earth region has been the focus of various studies aiming at the understanding of nuclear structure and providing information on the details of the reaction mechanism. The Gd isotopes belong to this group of nuclei and despite the available spectroscopic information, several open questions about their structure still exist, such as the inter-band transitions related to shape evolution or branching-ratios in deformed states. In addition, production cross sections of different reactions to Gd isotopes are largely unknown. In this work, we report on an experimental attempt to populate the excited states in the isotopes $^{152,153,154}$Gd by employing the heavy-ion fusion reaction $^{18}$O+$^{138}$Ba $\rightarrow$ $^{156-x}$Gd + $xn$ in the 58-64 MeV energy range (center-of-mass). title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
summary: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $ν_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space. In all cases, we obtain remarkably consistent NSM transition densities. title: Spin to Orbital Angular Momentum Conversion in the Neutron Nucleus Weak Interaction
summary: The neutron nucleus weak interaction generates a small parity non conserving rotation of the neutron spin as the neutron moves through matter. This parity-odd neutron rotary power can reach up to 2.2e-3 rad * cm-1 for slow neutrons in 139La, which possesses a p-wave resonance at 0.7 eV where the parity-odd asymmetry is greatly amplified. This spin rotation must conserve total angular momentum. Here we show that this conservation occurs through neutron orbital angular momentum generation. We experimentally demonstrate that a neutron prepared initially in a longitudinal spin-orbit state experiences no change in total angular momentum.

title: Secondary neutron beam production at Jefferson Lab
summary: We investigate secondary neutron production by an 11 GeV electron beam in the Hall A beam dump at Jefferson Lab and their transport to a downstream experimental area. This secondary beam could operate opportunistically with the primary electron-scattering programme. The neutron energy spectrum extends from thermal energies to several GeVs, offering a distinctive opportunity for irradiation at energy grater than 1 GeV. We considered three configurations: the current setup, the planned BDX facility, and an optimized BDX layout with a dedicated neutron extraction pipe. We also studied how radiators made of different materials and placed upstream of the beam dump increase neutron production.

title: The ATAR, a dense and compact vertex detector for the PIONEER experiment
summary: PIONEER is an approved experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) in Villigen, Switzerland that aims to measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs. muons with an accuracy of 0.01%. This is an order of magnitude improvement in precision compared to its predecessors and approaches the accuracy of the standard model prediction. The key elements of PIONEER are a high resolution calorimeter built concentrically around the high granularity active target (ATAR). The ATAR is composed of a stack of 48 low gain avalanche strip detectors (LGADs) to stop the beam pions and provide detailed information of the event topology. This will include precise timing (in the order of 200ps), spatial information (to an accuracy of about 60 micro meter) and pulse height information with a high dynamic range to separate pion stops from muons and MIPs. title: A trap-based platform for cooling and laser spectroscopy of fast ions toward radioactive-ion applications
summary: We report on the first experiments with the Stopping and Trapping of Radioactive Isotopes for Precision Experiments (STRIPE) segmented linear Paul trap. The intent for this apparatus is to serve as an efficient capture and laser-cooling trap for radioactive isotopes produced at radioactive ion beam facilities. We demonstrate the deceleration of 10 keV ion beams and their trapping and laser cooling into Coulomb crystals. title: Independent nuclear charge radius determinations: bound-electron $g$ factor versus muonic atom spectroscopy
summary: We present an alternative method to determine absolute nuclear charge radii competitively via the bound electron $g$ factor of H-like ions. The method is demonstrated for $^{118}$Sn by extracting its radius with a precision of 0.1%. This is the second most precise radius ever determined from an electronic system. We benchmark our result against a state-of-the-art value derived from the spectrum of muonic $^{118}$Sn. This comparison reveals a 3.2$σ$ tension, prompting a careful reexamination of the calculations and calling for additional measurements. Crucially, after decades, we now have two independent methods to measure absolute charge radii with similar precision.

title: Probing the initial geometry and the onset of collectivity with anisotropic flow in light-ion collisions with ALICE at the LHC
summary: Collective behavior, traditionally associated with heavy-ion collisions, has been observed in small collision systems at the LHC. The recent oxygen-oxygen and neon-neon collisions allow to bridge the gap between small and large collision systems and to study the collectivity in well-constrained initial states. Measurements of azimuthal anisotropies are sensitive to the initial-state geometry and enable detailed investigations of the nuclear structure of $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, highlighting the interplay between nuclear structure and collective dynamics in ultrarelativistic collisions. This contribution presents recent anisotropic flow measurements performed by the ALICE Collaboration in OO and Ne-Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.36 TeV using two- and multiparticle correlation methods. title: Correlations and fluctuations of flow with event shape engineering in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC
summary: Measurements of anisotropic flow provide some of the strongest constraints on the collective expansion and transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. In this paper, correlations and fluctuations of the anisotropic flow coefficients $v_{2}$, $v_{3}$, and $v_{4}$ are measured in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} = 5.02$ and $5.44$ TeV, respectively, with the ALICE detector. The Event Shape Engineering technique, based on the reduced flow vector $q_{n}$, is used to study flow correlations for different initial-state geometries. A strong anticorrelation between $v_2$ and $v_3$ and a positive correlation between $v_2$ and $v_4$ are observed. A small anticorrelation is seen between $v_3$ and $v_4$. title: Toward the Centennial of Wigner's Supermultiplet Symmetry: an Ab Initio Perspective
summary: As the centennial of Wigner's supermultiplet theory approaches in 2037, this review offers a modern perspective through the recently advanced ab initio Symmetry Adapted Model (SAM). We begin with the symmetry's empirical foundations in two-nucleon data and electroweak processes, and trace its emergence from the strong force through effective field theories, the QCD large-$N_c$ limit, the similarity renormalization group, and lattice calculations. We then follow its historical arc, from early limited engagement, through its revived interest, to the modern algebraic and first-principles resurgence. Central to this renaissance are new nullspace-based algorithms for the U(3) and U(4) coupling and recoupling coefficients, which remove a bottleneck spanning nearly nine decades and are released as the open-source libraries u3lib and u4lib. title: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
summary: We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. title: Hint of universality in $α$-cluster nuclei
summary: The empirical ground-state energies of the $α$-cluster nuclei are placed on the universal function that governs $N$-boson systems with a shallow state. The data fall on the finite-range-corrected universal curve, suggesting Efimov-type universality. No excited states, transition strengths, radii, or cluster geometries enter the analysis; the nuclei are treated as $N$ structureless bosons. A zero-shape $α$-$α$ Bargmann potential, describing the $^{8}$Be resonance, provides the pairwise interaction with no shape freedom. Simple three- and four-body forces, each a single Gaussian in the hyperradius, are fitted to $^{12}$C and $^{16}$O; microscopic calculations for $^{20}$Ne and $^{24}$Mg ($N=5,6$) follow as parameter-free predictions. A compact $0^+_2$ state near the Hoyle energy emerges in $^{12}$C without being targeted by the fit.

title: Neutron-alpha scattering on a quantum processor: Spin-orbit-split resonances and weak nonresonant channels
summary: We reconstruct elastic neutron--alpha phase shifts in all five channels through $l=2$ from trapped spectra measured on IBM's Boston quantum computer. Using a four-qubit implementation of the factorized geometric-time RODEO algorithm, we resolve the spin--orbit-split $p_{3/2}$ and $p_{1/2}$ resonances of $^5$He and the small nonresonant $d$-wave phase shifts. We fit 40 trapped energies per channel at five confinement strengths (200 energies in total), using a reciprocal effective-range function for the $d$ waves. The fits yield free-space phase shifts, the elastic cross section, and both $p$-wave poles. The broad $p_{1/2}$ pole is more sensitive to the fit order. title: Coulomb-Induced $K^- pp$ Molecular State
summary: We studied a new bound state in the three-body system consisting of an antikaon and two nucleons. The state is primarily induced by the Coulomb interactions between the $K^-$ and the two protons, and is modified by the strong $K^- p$ and $pp$ interactions. This spatially extended molecular state has binding energy and width that are of the order of keV, compared to the tens of MeV binding energy and width of the famous quasi-bound $K^- pp$ state caused primarily by the strong interaction.

title: Sampling nucleon short-range correlations in coordinate and momentum space for Au+Au collision simulations
summary: We develop a nuclear initialization scheme that jointly incorporates spatial nucleon correlations, high-momentum components, predominantly proton-neutron pair assignments, and correlated pair momenta, and implement it in the SMASH transport model. This construction enables controlled comparisons of the effects of different ingredients of short-range correlations (SRCs) on heavy-ion observables. The larger relative enhancement of $π^+$ production reduces the $π^-/π^+$ ratio. title: Weak magnetism effects on neutrino-nucleon interactions in hot nuclear matter within nonrelativistic Skyrme RPA
summary: Neutrino production, absorption, and scattering are important in explaining neutrino-driven core-collapse supernovae. At high densities or temperatures, relativistic effects, in particular weak magnetism (WM), may become increasingly important. Therefore, we extend the nonrelativistic random-phase approximation (RPA) framework for the study of neutrino-nucleon interactions in hot nuclear matter by incorporating the WM term into the nucleon weak current. In calculations with our recent Skyrme functional Sky3s, we confirm that WM increases interaction rates for the most important charged-current neutrino processes in supernovae and reduces those of antineutrinos. title: Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) optimization of residual correction of $α$-decay energy based on Weizsacker-Skyrme 4 model
summary: A physics-guided hybrid framework combining the Weizsacker-Skyrme-4 (WS4) macroscopic-microscopic mass model with the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) is developed to improve the accuracy of alpha-decay energy predictions for superheavy nuclei. Through ablation studies of 18 feature combinations, the optimal feature set is identified, reducing the overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.2743 to 0.1442 MeV, an improvement of 47.43%. The corrected model improves prediction accuracy across all four odd-even nuclear configurations while preserving shell effects and odd-even staggering patterns along the Po, Rn, and U isotopic chains. The framework is further applied to predict decay energy values for experimentally unmeasured nuclei along the Z = 118-120 isotopic chains.

title: New $γ$-softness in $^{196}$Pt from $γ$-rigid triaxiality
summary: The interplay between the $γ$-softness and the $γ$-rigidity is a key aspect in understanding nuclear collectivity. The agreement between experimental data and theoretical calculations demonstrates that the present approach provides an effective explanation for the observed features.

title: Antinucleon--nucleon interaction at next-to-next-to-leading order in covariant chiral effective field theory
summary: We construct antinucleon--nucleon ($\bar NN$) interactions at next-to-leading order (NLO) and next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in covariant chiral effective field theory. title: The recoil nucleon effect in nuclear systems
summary: Nuclear excitation energies are typically in the keV-MeV range, but rare eV-scale transitions remain a puzzle for nuclear theory. This work develops a two-body recoil model to describe $β^-$ decay on the basis of classic momentum conservation. Using the final states of $β^-$ decay with a keV-scale excitation energy, the model yields eV-scale recoil energy for a single nucleon. It indicates the recoil nucleon effect in nuclear systems: a single nucleon bound in a nucleus can be excited by absorbing the recoil momentum. The observed eV-scale isomers in $^{235}$U and $^{229}$Th can be attributed to the recoil neucleon effect. This effect could spark a eV-scale energy, and provide a solid theoretical foundation for predicting such extremely small energies. title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison
summary: We propose the three-dimensional Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods and construct fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon number $B=1,\ldots,4$ without imposing a symmetry ansatz, with high precision. title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
summary: We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory. We show that the energy-momentum tensor is well described by relativistic fluid dynamics even when the system is far from local equilibrium. title: Probing the structure of the two proton Borromean nucleus $^{17}\rm{Ne}$ through inclusive breakup data
summary: The proton-rich nucleus $^{17}$Ne exhibits a Borromean structure, $^{15}$O+p+p, since both $^{16}$F and diproton systems are unbound. The low-energy spectrum of this nucleus consists of a series of resonances that remain poorly identified. In this work, a three-body model is used to describe the structure of $^{17}$Ne, with special attention to the emergence of resonant states. The four-body continuum-discretized coupled-channel (CDCC) formalism is used to study the reaction of $^{17}$Ne on a $^{208}$Pb target near the Coulomb barrier. Comparing the calculated elastic and breakup cross sections with the recently available experimental data~\cite{OVEJAS2023138007} provides an excellent framework for probing the resonant structure of this nucleus.

title: Rigid triaxial roto-vibrator in a finite system
summary: We investigate the emergence of rigid triaxiality in a finite system, within the framework of the interacting boson model of nuclei. Appropriate Hamiltonians for a maximally-triaxial rigid shape are constructed. Closed expressions for wave functions, energies and E2 rates for states of the ground band are derived. Classical and quantum analyses reveal that for a fixed Hamiltonian, the system evolves from a $γ$-soft SO(6) structure for small $N$, to a $γ$-rigid structure for large $N$. Attention is paid to symmetry and spectral properties of both rotational and vibrational states.

title: Impact of Effective Nucleon Mass and Symmetry Energy on Nuclear Pasta Phases and the Unified Equation of State of Neutron Stars
summary: We investigate how the effective nucleon mass and symmetry energy affect pasta phase properties and the unified equation of state (EOS) of neutron stars. title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
summary: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $σ/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. title: Beam-Driven Active Plasma Dechirper for Energy Stabilization of High-Charge Bunches

Tilting a target with respect to a narrow beam and splitting it into several layers both raise the yield substantially: five-layer Mo and W targets give 6--8 times the surface-muon yield quoted for the J-PARC MLF graphite target, counted at the production target before capture and transport.

title: Muon Collider: Towards the Energy Frontier
summary: A muon collider has emerged as a compelling candidate for the next energy-frontier particle accelerator, combining the discovery potential of multi-TeV lepton collisions with a footprint and power consumption far smaller than existing or proposed hadron and electron-positron colliders. Advances over the past two decades in high-power targets, muon production and capture, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, high-field magnets, collider ring design, and machine-detector integration have transformed the concept from a long-term vision into a credible path toward a future flagship facility. This review summarizes the physics opportunities, the accelerator complex's design and status, the unique experimental environment, recent technical achievements, ongoing international R&D, and remaining steps toward realizing a high-energy muon collider by the middle of the century.

title: Surrogate-assisted beam distribution shaping at the CERN Proton Synchrotron and Super Proton Synchrotron

title: Multi-Gaussian Model for Intrabeam Scattering

title: Reactive feedback for suppression of the periodic transient beam loading effect in storage rings: theory and simulations
summary: In fourth-generation synchrotron light sources, harmonic cavities are often employed for bunch lengthening. title: Single-spike superradiant free-electron lasers
summary: Free-electron lasers (FELs) deliver high-brilliance radiation from the infrared to X-rays, enabling atomic-scale studies on femtosecond-to-attosecond timescales. title: Physics design of a dual-ring light source toward MHz-rate free-electron laser radiation
summary: Combining the high peak brilliance and short pulse duration of free-electron lasers (FELs) with the high repetition rate of diffraction-limited storage rings (DLSRs) is a promising direction for accelerator light sources. title: Longitudinal beam dynamics II. Lecture 2: intensity effects and beam instabilities
summary: In this lecture, dealing with intensity effects, the equations of longitudinal motion with induced beam voltage are analyzed. This matrix equation is then applied to find the thresholds, growth rates and spectra of an unstable multi-bunch beam. The lecture is concluded by a discussion of possible beam-instability cures.

title: Optimizing an RFSoC LLRF Controller for a Low-PRF, Short Pulse System
summary: The Advanced Light Source (ALS) LINAC operates with 3 GHz RF pulses at 0.7 Hz pulse repetition frequency (PRF) and 1.2 microsecond duration, imposing severe limitations on traditional PID and adaptive feedforward control schemes. title: Fast prediction of electron-beam parameters using transfer maps and machine learning in a digital model of a MeV $γγ$ collider
summary: Tuning the electron beam of a MeV-scale $γγ$ collider, first in the design and later in a digital twin of the machine, requires the beam parameters at the interaction point (IP) for many injector states. title: High-transformer-ratio plasma-based afterburner for extending X-ray free-electron laser photon energies to $\gtrsim$50 keV

title: Numerical Study of Two-Frequency Heating in ECR Ion Source

title: LH$μ$C Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
summary: The concept of the LH$μ$C, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. For the latter, a $μ$TRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives $\sqrt{s}=5.3$ TeV and peak luminosities of $8.8\times10^{33}$ and $7.2\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.

title: FCC-μe: High Energy, High Luminosity Muon-Electron Collider & Neutrino Factory at CERN
summary: The concept is presented of making at the FCC-$ee$ (or CEPC) facility $μ^+e^-$ collisions at the centre-of-mass energy between 1 and 2 TeV and the average luminosity above $10^{34}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, concurrently to the $e^+e^-$ collisions. Basic considerations are also given regarding the machine-detector interface and the performance of the FCC-$μe$ and associated neutrino factory. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying relevance of such anti-muon beams for any future high energy storage ring as well as for neutrino science.

title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams

title: Inverse modelling of a laser-plasma accelerator
summary: The electron beams of a laser-plasma accelerator depend non-linearly on the laser and gas settings. This dependence is explored using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, and machine-learning models trained on these simulations predict the beam from the settings. Here we address the reverse problem: given a measured beam, which settings produced it? We infer three of them: the gas pressure $p\_1$, the normalised vector potential $a\_0$ and the nitrogen concentration $c\_{N\_2}$. The solution is not guaranteed to be unique. We train an ensemble of mixture density networks that, for each beam, output several possible sets of settings with their probabilities and uncertainties, and test them on simulated beams with realistic measurement noise. As the atomic fraction of Zr increased, the surface morphology improved and the bulk and surface void densities decreased. At the optimal Zr content, the superconducting properties improved and a thinner surface niobium oxide formed. These results identify co-sputtered Nb$_3$Sn:Zr as a promising material to advance the performance limits of SRF cavities.

title: Polarization-dependent exchange effects in intrabeam scattering
summary: The emittance growth due to intrabeam scattering (IBS) depends on the scattering cross section and is therefore affected by the exchange interaction of identical particles. In this paper, we calculate the small corrections to the growth rates resulting from the exchange interaction. title: Comment on "Beam blow up due to beamstrahlung in circular e+e- colliders"
summary: The authors of the original article, Valdivia Garcia and Zimmermann (2021), state that they "derive analytical formulae for the equilibrium beam parameters, considering the varying electromagnetic field during the collision". Consequently, a significant portion of the formulae derived in the article bears a very tenuous relationship to reality. For practical purposes, we propose a different solution -- one that is far simpler and more accurate.

We then derive a swimming formula that linearly relates the swimming velocities to the prescribed surface velocity of a microswimmer and imposed background flows. As a showcase application of the derived swimming formula, we prove that the scallop theorem holds in this class of linearly viscous fluids. title: Three-mode chimera-like states in a minimal network of active camphor ribbons
summary: Chimera states are a remarkable manifestation of symmetry breaking, wherein identical units spontaneously split into coherent and incoherent groups. summary: A planar Chapman-Jouguet detonation that runs out of fuel must become a shock. title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases

summary: The spatio-temporal wavefield sampled by distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) contains intertwined information about signal strength, oscillatory structure and propagation. summary: Field seismic data often suffer from multiple degradations, including noise contamination, incomplete geometry, low-frequency loss, and reduced spatial resolution, requiring different restoration operations. title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
summary: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it. Data can satisfy the FAIR principles and still mislead a machine acting alone. We propose that Earth-science data become AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled), an agent-specific requirements layer that extends FAIR, within a three-part agenda: AWARE data, bounded tools, layered validation. The ingredients exist across community infrastructure. We outline a staged, measurable path to adoption, intended to reduce silent error.

title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
summary: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincaré beams. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.

title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
summary: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. title: The effects of closure parameter on the properties of kinetic range plasma turbulence
summary: Simulations of plasmas such as the solar wind require an accurate representation of kinetic physics given the lack of frequent collisions. title: Relativistic Harmonic Generation in Spatiotemporal Plasma Photonic Crystals
summary: Spatiotemporal photonic crystals offer a route to controlling the frequency, momentum, and energy of light. title: Statistical Signatures of Velocity-Space Turbulence in the Earth's Magnetosheath
summary: In collisionless plasmas, the particle distributions are often far from local thermodynamic equilibrium, providing a significant source of free energy that leads to complex velocity-space dynamics. Using measurements from the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission in a special campaign in the Earth's magnetosheath, we present the first statistical study of signatures consistent with velocity-space turbulence across a wide range of plasma conditions. We observe two main populations in the ion velocity-space spectrum -- an isotropic $-3/2$ spectrum and an anisotropic $-2$ spectrum organized by the ion $β$ and bulk flow.

title: How zonal states beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes stabilize micro-turbulence in tokamak plasmas
summary: The effects of zonal states (ZS) beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes (AEs) on micro-turbulence stability are investigated; taking toroidal Alfven eigenmode (TAE) and ion temperature gradient mode (ITG) as an example. title: The role of externally-driven density fluctuations in the enhancement of beam spray
summary: Speckled laser beams, commonly used to ionize and heat plasma for inertial confinement fusion and high-energy-density experiments, are shown to drive long-wavelength plasma-density fluctuations that induce beam spray in other laser beams. Beam propagation simulations show increased beam spray due to self-focusing and filamentation when heater-driven density fluctuations are included.

title: Galilean invariance of Hamiltonian guiding center theory

We show that the model is sufficient to capture the bulk envelope of the CME, and also insufficient to capture the complexity of the CME's evolution. We generated simulated arrival-time forecasts for the CME by extrapolating the constant-velocity propagation to determine the time of impact with Earth. title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields
summary: Auroras provide remote optical observations of energetic electrons precipitating into the upper atmosphere, and whose energy distribution encodes key information about large scale magnetospheric processes. Recovering the underlying electron precipitation field from ground-based camera images of auroras remains a challenging inverse problem. Existing auroral tomography techniques are often limited to simplified static settings, discrete spatial and energy grids, or strong assumptions on the electron energy spectrum. We propose to model the dynamic auroral electron precipitation field via a temporally conditioned neural network. The state of the precipitation field at each frame is represented by a per-frame latent code driven by learned discrete dynamics. title: Eclipse-minimising sun-synchronous orbits in a mean-Sun rotating frame
summary: A satellite in low Earth orbit normally passes through Earth's shadow on every revolution. A dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit largely avoids it: J2 precession keeps the orbit plane facing the Sun all year, but it follows only the Sun's average position, the mean Sun. In reality the Sun wanders up to 23 degrees around this average, enough to push the plane into shadow for part of the year. We introduce MSSI, a coordinate frame that rotates with the mean Sun. In it, a sun-synchronous orbit is a fixed ring and the real Sun traces the analemma, so the yearly eclipse question becomes static geometry. From that picture we derive how much of each orbit is in shadow, the yearly eclipse for every plane orientation, maps of which directions are never, sometimes or always eclipsed, and the margin a mission has. title: Verifying the High-Energy Tail in Bi-Kappa Particle Loading: Three-Dimensional Tests, Velocity Bounds, and Finite Precision
summary: The bi-Kappa distribution models anisotropic space-plasma populations with suprathermal power-law tails. title: Statistical correlations between turbulent structures and dissipation proxies in near-Earth space: the MMS 2023-2024 unbiased magnetosheath campaign
summary: The terrestrial magnetosheath provides excellent opportunities for the experimental study of space plasma physics. summary: Identifying pre-flare magnetic conditions that determine whether a flare will be eruptive (associated with a coronal mass ejection) or confined remains a major challenge in solar physics. title: Radiation Hardness Assurance of Optical Coatings for the COMPASSO Iodine Reference
summary: The COMPASSO payload demonstrates compact iodine-based optical frequency references on the International Space Station (ISS), requiring optical windows and antireflective coatings that remain stable in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) radiation environment. title: Towards Distributed Quantum Computing: Quantum Gate Teleportation via Satellite-Distributed Entanglement under Atmospheric Depolarization
summary: We investigate quantum gate teleportation as a primitive for satellite-enabled distributed quantum computing. title: Parker Solar Probe Flies Through the Sun's Magnetic Poles Near 10 Solar Radii
summary: During the peak of the Sun's magnetic cycle, the solar corona can be complex and dominated by dynamics, while hidden below, the dipole component of the its photospheric magnetic field steadily reverses with respect to the rotational axis. title: Detecting space objects with Earth-observation radar satellites
summary: Millimetre-to-centimetre orbital debris poses a hazard to spacecraft, but its abundance remains difficult to measure. title: The Physics of Interstellar Travel
summary: How can we send an uncrewed spacecraft to the nearest stars within a human lifetime? What propulsion methods are available? Will it survive impacts in the interstellar medium? What science will it do at its destination? How can it send back data over enormous distances? In this short semi-popular article, I examine various aspects of the physics of interstellar travel, its challenges and possible solutions. I focus on nuclear rockets, laser sails, dust impacts, and communication. These, as well as other issues such as navigation and onboard power, are explored in more detail in my book, The Physics of Interstellar Travel (2026).

summary: At scales much larger than the ion inertial length and ion-gyroscale, space-plasma turbulence is often described within the framework of incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). title: Exponential Growth of Turbulent Cross Helicity in Shear-Flow-Driven Turbulence

title: Exact approach to double- and triple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems
summary: The determination of multiple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems is of broad interest in quantum physics. By this exact equation, we identify the critical condition for the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state, as well as its relationship to the single-excitation one. Our study not only clearly demonstrates the universality of double- or triple-excitation bound state in open quantum emitter systems, but also reveals the possibility of mediating inter-emitter interactions via multiple-excitation bound states.

title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1

title: Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
