title: A new approach to Turán inequalities for classical orthogonal polynomials
summary: Let $f,g\in C^{2}\left( a,b\right) .$ In this paper we investigate properties of the function% \[ v_{g}\left( f\right) \left( x\right) =-\frac{f^{2}\left( x\right) }{g\left( x\right) }\frac{d}{dx}\frac{g\left( x\right) f^{\prime}\left( x\right) }{f\left( x\right) }% \] where $f:\left( a,b\right) \rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is a solution of the second order differential equation $f^{\prime\prime}+pf^{\prime}+qf=0.$ Criteria for the monotonicity of $v_{g}\left( f\right) $ are given which depend on the coefficients $p$ and $q$. It is shown that for classical orthogonal polynomials $p_{n}\left( x\right) $ the Turán inequalities are equivalent to the non-negativity of the functions $v_{g}\left( p_{n}\right) $ for a suitable function $g.$ This allows new and simple proofs of classical and recent Turán inequalities.

title: Weak-type $(p,p)$ inequalities for Riesz transforms
summary: For $1\le p\le2$, we obtain the sharp weak-type $(p,p)$ inequality for each classical Riesz transform on real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$, with the same optimal constant as for the Hilbert transform. The proof combines the Bellman function method of \cite{BHV} with Janakiraman's sharp strip potential \cite{Janakiraman}.

title: $L^p(\mathbb{R}^3)$-estimates for maximal averages along mixed homogeneous hypersurfaces with vanishing Hessian
summary: We study maximal averages over the surfaces parametrized by $c+Φ$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, where $c$ is a constant and $Φ$ is mixed homogeneous and real analytic away from the origin. Under the assumption that the Hessian determinant of $Φ$ vanishes identically, we classify the possible graphing functions for all positive weights. For surfaces in each resulting class, we establish sharp $L^{p}$-estimates for the corresponding maximal averages.

title: On VMO-Type Characterizations of Ball Banach Sobolev Spaces and Independence of Integrable Index of Special John--Nirenberg--Campanato Spaces
summary: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, $X$ be a ball Banach function space, and $W^{k,X}$ denote the corresponding ball Banach Sobolev space. In this article, we solve six questions in [Math. Z. 311 (2025)]. Specifically, we first prove that the constants in its VMO-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ are sharp uniformly over all ball Banach function spaces satisfying suitable assumptions. Next, we show that the BBM-type formula and the BSVY-type formula involving minimizing polynomials or ball averages fail in general. In contrast, we establish higher-order BBM-type formulas involving Taylor polynomials and further obtain a Taylor-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ under suitable assumptions. Moreover, we construct counterexamples to show that the characterization of $W^{k,X}$ via higher-order minimizing polynomials fails in general. title: A counterexample to the Jordan tuple conjecture of Ball and Helton
summary: This article constructs a pair of bounded commuting 3-symmetric operators with no Jordan-family extension. The operators are coordinate multipliers on a Sobolev space of functions with values in three dimensional complex Euclidean space with an equivalent Hilbert norm. Their quadratic symbol has no operator polynomial factorization, even with an auxiliary target Hilbert space. The construction transfers the nonfactorability of the matrix quadratic used by Russo to the symbol of a commuting 3-symmetric tuple. The factorization approach of McCullough--Russo and Russo then supplies the obstruction to a Jordan-family extension.

title: Weak--type $(1,1;\frac{1}{2})$--estimate for the bilinear Bochner--Riesz mean at the critical index
summary: We prove the weak-type estimate at the end-point $\big(1,1,\frac{1}{2}\big)$ for the bilinear Bochner--Riesz mean at the critical index $α_c=n-\frac{1}{2}$ in all dimensions $n\geq 1$. Our proof is motivated by Christ's method for the linear Bochner--Riesz operator at the critical index. We develop a bilinear analogue of the $TT^*$ method to address the end-point boundedness of the bilinear Bochner--Riesz operator. This approach provides a useful tool in addressing the end-point issues for bilinear operators.

title: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes
summary: We prove that the discrete Bilinear Hilbert Transform along the primes, \begin{align} \mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{P}}(f,g)(x) := \sum_{n \neq 0} \frac{Λ(|n|)}{n} f(x-n) g(x+n), \qquad Λ(n) := \begin{cases} \log p & \text{ if } n = p^k, \ k \geq 1 \\ 0 & \text{ otherwise} \end{cases} \end{align} extends to a bounded operator from $\ell^p \times \ell^q \to \ell^r$ whenever $p,q \in (1,\infty)$ and $\frac{1}{r}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}$ in the Banach range, $r \geq 1$, and a particular portion of the quasi-Banach range $r \in \left(\frac{2}{3},1\right)$; in the diagonal case, this extends up to the endpoint $(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{6})$. title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
summary: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.

title: Monotonicity properties of ratios of Ferrers and conical functions related to a Riemannian nonlocal eigenvalue problem
summary: Recently, for a given Riemannian manifold with certain curvature constraints, S. Kajántó and A. Kristály [KK24] formulated a variational problem (on either positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces) and computed the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in terms of the radii, curvature and weight. Moreover, they conjectured that a saturation phenomenon exists also in the case of positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces (not only in the Euclidean case), and this is based entirely on the incompatibility of a system of nonlinear equations involving special functions, like Ferrers functions of the first kind and conical functions of the first kind. In this paper, we provide a partial solution for both positive and negative curvature case.

title: Nondoubling Calderón-Zygmund theory across geometries
summary: We develop a Calderón--Zygmund theory without the doubling property, a metric or a martingale structure. Our measure spaces carry an exhausting family of admissible sets with recursive child partitions. A stopping-time construction gives a decomposition of an integrable function, with a bounded good part and bad terms that cancel on the parents of the stopping sets. We introduce the corresponding atomic Hardy and BMO spaces, establish their duality and interpolation properties, and prove weak-type $(1,1)$ and Hardy-space bounds for singular integral operators under a Hörmander condition and a size estimate between each stopping set and its parent. We apply this framework to arbitrary flow trees, whose associated flow measures need not be either locally or globally doubling. title: Weighted $H^p$--$L^q$ estimates for fractional operators with multiple kernels under a strengthened Hörmander condition
summary: We study a scale of strengthened fractional Hörmander conditions, indexed by $δ\ge0$ and adapted to the Hardy spaces $H^p$, $0<p<1$, which was recently considered by Han and Wu [Y.~Han, H.~Wu, \emph{The weighted $H^p$ estimates for commutators of fractional integrals}, Potential Anal. \textbf{59} (2023), 1827--1850] for fractional integrals with a single kernel. title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
summary: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. title: Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation
summary: In this paper Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation are discussed. The Bäcklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate Bäcklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation and solutions of the third Painlevé equation is also discussed.

title: What is... An Exceptional Set Estimate?
summary: Exceptional set estimates are a fundamental topic of interest in projection theory. We introduce the topic through discrete geometry, and use this perspective to motivate some key results in the realm of geometric measure theory. To appear in the "What is?" series in the Notices of the AMS.

title: On the spectrality of non-homogeneous self-similar measures
summary: We develop a finite-cylinder difference-set obstruction to the existence of an exponential orthonormal basis for a compactly supported probability measure. This obstruction uses the equal-scale and equal-mass structure of finitely many disjoint affine copies of the measure, together with Parseval's identity and an elementary atom bound for positive measures. We apply it to prove that the golden-mean self-similar measure generated by $x/2$ and $(x+2)/4$ is non-spectral. Together with a weight-rigidity argument, this excludes spectrality for every positive choice of weights in this iterated function system. We also analyze a logarithmically incommensurable example generated by $x/2$ and $(x+2)/3$, proving non-spectrality for all first-branch weights $p\in[1/3,5/6]$, including the natural weights. title: Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches
summary: Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
summary: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.

title: End-line Fourier restriction for hyperbolic surfaces in three dimensions
summary: We prove new bilinear adjoint Fourier restriction estimates for pairs of separated rectangles associated to a hyperbolic surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then employ these bilinear estimates to prove Fourier extension inequalities along the (sharp) parabolic scaling line for any smooth hyperbolic 2-surface that is either the graph of a polynomial or that obeys a mild finite type condition.

title: Sampling recovery for intersections of Lipschitz classes in the low-smoothness regime
summary: We study sampling recovery in $L_p(\mathbb T^d)$ for intersections of Lipschitz classes defined by smoothness conditions in two different metrics $L_p$ and $L_q$, where $1\le p<q\le\infty$. Our focus is on the low-smoothness range, where the $L_p$-smoothness does not exceed the classical continuity threshold $d/p$. We determine the exact orders of the sampling numbers for both linear and general recovery algorithms, including critical smoothness cases in which logarithmic factors appear or uniform convergence fails. To analyze sampling approximation in the low-smoothness range, we establish new inequalities for averaged moduli of smoothness with different integrability parameters and derive sharp estimates for these moduli and the corresponding semi-discrete measures of smoothness. These estimates provide error bounds for linear sampling operators acting on functions whose smoothness may

title: On discrete harmonic functions with non-negativity on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$
summary: An improvement of Liouville's theorem for discrete harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ was obtained by Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin. Namely, they proved that if a discrete harmonic function is bounded on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then the function is constant. In this paper, we study the corresponding problem if we replace the boundedness assumption with non-negativity. We establish this non-negativity result in some classes of discrete harmonic functions (polynomial growth and finite-translation-rank). Moreover, we prove that if a discrete harmonic function is non-negative on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then it has at most exponential growth.

title: A BMO Extension of Oskolkov's Criterion for Rectangular Trigonometric Fourier Sums
summary: We give a sufficient condition in terms of sectional BMO for almost everywhere Pringsheim convergence of rectangular trigonometric Fourier sums. For continuous functions, the condition includes Oskolkov's criterion, and an example shows that the inclusion is strict.

title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
summary: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.

title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
summary: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.

title: Patterns, Distances, and Structure in Sparse Sets
summary: A central theme in modern harmonic analysis, with strong connections to Ramsey theory, is the tension between randomness and structure: to what extent can a "large" set avoid prescribed configurations, and when must such patterns inevitably appear? The answer depends delicately on how size is measured, with notions such as Hausdorff dimension, Fourier dimension, and density leading to strikingly different phenomena. In this mini-course, we explore this theme through two complementary perspectives. On one hand, we study translation-invariant linear patterns, a natural class of Euclidean Ramsey-type configurations. On the other hand, we investigate distance sets of sparse subsets of Euclidean space, which encode metric configurations of pairs of points. title: On transformations in the Second Painlevé family
summary: We complete the classification of algebraic relations among solutions of equations in the second Painlevé family $P_{II}(α): y''=2y^3+ty+α$, where $α\in\mathbb{C}$. More precisely, we prove that if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generic solutions of $P_{II}(α_1),\ldots,P_{II}(α_n)$, respectively, and $tr.deg_{\mathbb{C}(t)}\mathbb{C}(t)(y_1,y_1',\ldots,y_n,y_n')<2n$, then for some $i<j$, we have that $α_i\pmα_j\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $y_i=T(y_j)$ for a classical Bäcklund transformation $T$. In particular, the classical Bäcklund transformations are the only Bäcklund transformations in the second Painlevé family.

title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem
summary: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.

title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
summary: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.

title: How to arrange four points in the plane
summary: Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[ D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[ \begin{cases} \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1, \text{a rhombus with angle }θ\in(π/3,π

title: On the packing-dimension analogue of Bourgain's constant
summary: For every $n\geq 2$, we construct a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose harmonic measure has packing dimension $n$. That is, the packing analogue of Bourgain's constant is zero, in contrast with Bourgain's constant, which is positive. Moreover, the elliptic measure of the same domain also has packing dimension $n$ for every uniformly elliptic matrix.

title: On the size of the defect set of an analytic matrix field
summary: In this note, we study the defect set of a symmetric analytic matrix field $M$ defined on an open set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge2$. A defect point $x \in Ω$ of $M$ is defined as a point for which no eigenframe can be chosen continuously in any neighborhood of $x$. We show that the defect set $S(M)$ is contained in a locally finite union of analytic submanifolds of codimension at least $2$. The proof follows fairly directly from results by Parusinski and Rond (Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 2020) and by Kurdyka and Paunescu (Duke Math. J., 2008). This result can be applied in the context of the Landau-de Gennes Theory to estimate the physical defects of a nematic liquid crystal.

title: Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge
summary: Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.

title: Polynomial eigenfunctions and recurrences of fixed length
summary: This paper solves the fixed-length recurrence problem posed by Horozov, Shapiro and Tater. For the rational Darboux transformations specified here, it also resolves the order and classification questions raised by their two conjectures. It classifies monic polynomial sequences whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients and for which multiplication by the variable involves a fixed number of consecutive polynomials. Orthogonality is not assumed, and only sufficiently large degrees need be prescribed. If the lowest recurrence index is $n-m+1$, with $m\ge3$, the differential order equals $m$ times the degree of the eigenvalue as a polynomial in $n$. title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
summary: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
summary: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(σ)$ to $L^q(ω)$ for the operator $H_σg(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,dσ$, where $σ$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $ω$ is a $σ$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $κ_{p,q}$ in $C_*\leκ_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $ω$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse mart

title: Pointwise Convergence and Approximation of Matrix-Transform Means of Vilenkin--Fourier Series
summary: We study convergence, divergence, and approximation of matrix-transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series. For bounded groups, we prove convergence along ${M_n}$ at Vilenkin--Lebesgue points without additional diagonal conditions. For arbitrary bounded or unbounded groups, every regular matrix-transform method admits divergence on any prescribed null set along any increasing sequence. We also obtain $L_p(G_m)$ approximation estimates in terms of the modulus of continuity.

title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
summary: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis boun

title: A short route to Diening's averaging criterion in spaces of homogeneous type
summary: We present a short, self-contained proof of the averaging-operator criterion for the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over unbounded spaces of homogeneous type. Building on techniques of Diening and Lerner, we establish a Jensen-type inequality with uniformly summable error, from which the criterion follows directly via a Calderón-Zygmund argument.

title: Exceptional parameters in the Erdős similarity problem
summary: The Erd\H os similarity conjecture says that for every infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$, there exists a set $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure which does not contain any affine copy of $x + tA$ of $A$ (with $t \neq 0$). Kolountzakis proved that for every infinite $A$, there exists $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure so that the exceptional sets $D_E(A)$ of scales $t$, and $\mathcal E_E(A)$ of affine maps $(x,t)$, for which $x+tA\subseteq E$, are both Lebesgue null. We show that these exceptional parameter sets are small in two finer senses. First, given any countable family of Fourier decay rates, a single $E$ can be constructed so that $D_E(A)$ is null with respect to every measure whose Fourier transform decays at one of these rates. Consequently, there are compact sets $K$ of measure arbitrarily close to $1$ for which $D_K(A)$ and $\mathcal E_K(A)$ have modified Fourier dimension zero.

title: Artin-style characterizations of the multiple gamma and sine functions
summary: We extend Artin's characterizations of the gamma function to the multiple setting by means of the Kubert identity. We obtain uniqueness theorems for positive continuous solutions of a difference equation $G(z + 1) = α(z)G(z)$ that also satisfy an Artin-type multiplication formula, remaining within the class of continuous functions under a modest initial condition. The results apply in particular to the Barnes multiple gamma functions and the Kurokawa multiple sine functions.

title: Directional maximal functions along algebraic curves
summary: We prove that the maximal operator over line segments in $N$ arbitrary directions on a real algebraic curve of degree $D$ in $\mathbb R^n$ has $L^2$ operator norm at most $C_{n,\varepsilon}D^{C_n}N^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, with $C_n$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Combined with polynomial partitioning, this gives the sharp bound $N^{\frac14}$, up to a polylogarithmic factor, for $N$ arbitrary directions in $\mathbb R^3$. The first main ingredient is a new quantitative strengthening of the property that the curve crosses each affine hyperplane at most $D$ times. This condition controls the overlap of variable-width neighborhoods of hyperplanes. The width attached to each direction is a small multiple of its distance to the osculating hyperplane at an endpoint of its arc. The problem is projectively invariant, and a projective almost orthogonality principle turns the overlap

title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
summary: For a real polynomial of degree $n$ with $n$ distinct real roots, assume that no two different nonconstant derivatives, including the polynomial itself, share a root. Recording the derivative orders of all roots from left to right gives a Rolle word. We present an exact, computer-assisted classification in degree six: $2706$ words are realizable, with a word and its reversal counted separately. Starting from $33592$ formal interlacing words, published necessary restrictions leave $13404$ candidates. Integer realization certificates and $53$ exact exclusion stages classify every candidate. The surviving set agrees exactly with the set of certified realizations. All verification uses integer and rational arithmetic. The accompanying code, certificates, proof notes, and per-word exclusion ledger make the computation reproducible. The result concerns degree six; it does not resolve the class

title: Packing sets by rigid motions and similarities
summary: For nonempty Borel sets $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $Θ\subset O(d)\times\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge2$, let $Θ(E)$ be the union of the rigid copies $gE+z$, where $(g,z)\inΘ$. We prove that $Θ(E)$ has positive Lebesgue measure whenever $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E+\dim_HΘ>\frac{d(d+1)}2$, where $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E$ is the spherical Fourier dimension of $E$. This resolves a conjecture on packing by arbitrary Borel families of rigid motions. Our proof develops a discrete-to-continuous framework by adapting a finite-field averaging argument to $\mathbb R^d$ using Sobolev estimates on the group of rigid motions. We also obtain analogous packing results for similarities. title: Sharp L^p and variation inequalities for maximal operators on finite connected graphs
summary: Let $G=(V_G,E_G)$ be a finite connected graph (here $V_G$ and $E_G$ denote the set of vertices and edges of $G$ respectively). The primary aim of this paper is to study the sharp variation and $L^p$ inequalities of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator $M_G$ defined on $G$ and its fractional variant $M_{α,G}\,(0<α<1)$). Set $${\bf C}_{α,G}^{p,q}=\sup\limits_{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)>0}\frac{{\rm Var}_{q,G}(M_{α,G}f)}{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)},$$ where ${\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)$ denotes the $p$-variation of $f$ on $G$. We denote by $K_n$ (resp., $S^n$) the complete (resp., star) graph with $n\geq4$ vertices. When $α=0$, we prove ${\bf C}_{α,S_n}^{p,p} =1-\frac{1}{n}$ for $0<p<1$. This solve a question originally posed by Liu and Xue in 2021. In the fractional case $0<α<1$, we prove ${\bf C}_{α,S_n}^{1,q}=1-n^{-α}$ and ${\bf C}_{α,K_n}^{1,q} =(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{-α}$ for $q=\frac{1}{1-α}$, which pro

title: Sharp weighted bounds for reverse fractional integral operators
summary: In this paper, we prove the one-weight reverse fractional integral operators \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^q(w^q)}\geq C_w\|f\|_{L^p(w^p)} \] holds for all nonnegative measurable functions $f$, with $\frac ns<p<1$ and $\frac1q=\frac1p-\frac sn$, if and only if $w^{p/(1-p)}\in A_{\frac{p(s-n)}{n(1-p)}}$. Furthermore, we show the lower bound \[ C_w\gtrsim_{n,s,p}[w]_{p,q}^{\min\left\{\frac{p(n-s)}{n(1-p)},\frac{p(n-s)}{sp-n}\right\}}, \] and the exponent is sharp. We also investigate when the reverse weak-type estimate \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-s},\infty}(w^{\frac{n}{n-s}})}\geq \frac{n}{s}\,v_n^{(n-s)/n}[w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}]^{(n-s)/n}_{A_1}\|f\|_{L^1(w)} \] holds if and only if $w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}\in A_1$.

title: Falconer's conjecture through descent and chaining
summary: OpenAI proved that a compact set $E\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ of Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d}{2}$ determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive length. We give a complete proof of this theorem which follows the overall architecture of the OpenAI argument, from the construction of the initial pair measures to the final Fourier estimate, but which modifies that argument substantially at the points where the geometric costs are paid and where the estimates are reassembled. The reductions are organized by the descent and chaining viewpoint of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause: one potential, built from two separated depths together with a penalty for insufficient separation, pays for every reduction on every interval of scales, the terminal intervals included, and a finite-record chaining lemma keeps the fixed power losses attached to the few reductions which incur them. title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
summary: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.

title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions
summary: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $μ$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $μ(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrecti

title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
summary: Let $γ$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_γ$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,δ)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$.

title: Monotone Rearrangement for Flattening Weights $F_2$
summary: We consider a subclass of the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ weights with added smoothness, which we refer to as flattening weights $F_2.$ We quantify how such weights arise as exponents of VMO functions and prove that monotone rearrangement does not increase the class modulus in $F_2.$

title: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large
summary: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. Moreover, $S$ can be chosen so that $|S\cap[x,x+1]|\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. This resolves the Erdős similarity problem in the large.

title: Improvement to characterizations of BMO in terms of endpoint bounds for commutators and some counterexamples
summary: In this paper, we extend the technique of Lerner, Ombrosi and Rivera-Ríos (Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 51(1): 107--119, 2019) for the necessity of the strong-type boundedness of commutators to the endpoint case, and give characterizations of BMO via the endpoint bounds for commutators of singular integrals with rough kernels and related operators, which improve the conditions of Accomazzo (Israel J. Math. 228(2): 787--800, 2018), Guo et al. (J. Geom. Anal. 30(4): 3995-4035, 2020). We also give a characterization of BMO via the endpoint bounds for commutators of non-degenerate Calderón-Zygmund operators by removing the real-valued restriction on pointwise multiplier, which extend the results of Hytönen (J. Math. Pures Appl. (9) 156: 351--391, 2021) to the endpoint case. Finally, we find counterexamples to illustrate that weighted endpoint estimate of commutator of fractional integral operator

title: Transforms between multivariate Laguerre and Meixner polynomials and their applications to gateways
summary: We establish gateways in both directions between the Laguerre process and a discrete Markov process for every inverse temperature $2θ\geq 1$. Here, a gateway is an intertwining relation between Markov processes with continuous and discrete state spaces. A key ingredient is a pair of generating function identities that relate two double generating functions for multivariate Meixner polynomials to a single and a double generating function for multivariate Laguerre polynomials, respectively. These identities reveal a close relationship between the two families of polynomials and yield integral transforms that underlie the gateway relations. Gateway relations provide a means of transferring properties between continuous and discrete processes. title: On the proof of Falconer distance conjecture
summary: We are able to catch the main idea from OpenAI's recent release and present a proof of Falconer distance conjecture in our own words. Arguments are judiciously simplified and carefully designed for graduate-level readers.

title: Weak $L^{2/3}$ bounds for the bilinear Hilbert transform
summary: For Schwartz functions $f_1,f_2$ on $\mathbb{R}$, define the bilinear Hilbert transform by $$ \mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)(x) =\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-t)f_2(x+t)\,\frac{dt}{t}. $$ We prove the weak-type estimate $$ \left\|\mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)\right\|_{L^{2/3,\infty}} \lesssim_{p_1,p_2} \|f_1\|_{p_1}\|f_2\|_{p_2} $$ for $1<p_1,p_2<2$ with $1/p_1+1/p_2=3/2$. The key ingredient is a new local supremum estimate for packet sums, which we use to establish the forest estimate.

title: Failure of endpoint estimates for lacunary bilinear spherical maximal functions on Heisenberg groups
summary: We prove that the lacunary bilinear Nevo--Thangavelu spherical maximal operator on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$ does not map $H^1(\mathbb H^n)\times H^1(\mathbb H^n)$ into $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb H^n)$ for any $n\geq1$. We obtain this result by lifting the Euclidean counterexample in our recent result (arXiv:2610.40100) to the Heisenberg group.

title: A Counterexample to Polynomial Approximation for Monotone Weights
summary: We give a counterexample to a question of Borichev on polynomial approximation with monotone weights. We construct an even continuous weight $W$, strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$, with superpolynomial growth and finite logarithmic integral, and an entire function $F$ of zero exponential type such that $F/W$ vanishes at infinity and belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$. Nevertheless, $F$ has positive distance from the polynomials in the weighted uniform norm and in every corresponding weighted $L^{p}$ norm.

title: Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data
summary: We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables. The norming constants $γ_j$ are allowed to be arbitrarily large under a mild moment condition $\mathbb{E}[γ_j^ν] < \infty$ ($ν> 1$). Our main result is divided into two parts. First, we develop a probabilistic Riemann--Hilbert framework to show that the system self-averages: despite large, independent fluctuations in the initial data, the random Toda lattice variables converge deterministically to an effective continuum model at a polynomial rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-δ})$ for $0 < δ< 1/2$. title: Second-Order Linear $q$-Difference Equations
summary: Second order $q$ difference equations arise in various areas such as basic hypergeometric series, orthogonal polynomials and the analytic theory of special functions. When the independent variable is scaled by powers of $q$ ($0<q<1$), such equations display asymptotic behaviour that differs markedly from their differential or classical difference counterparts. Our purpose is to give a complete, self contained treatment of linear, second order $q$ difference equations with divergent formal solutions, including explicit error bounds, exact resummations and Stokes phenomena.

title: Sharpness of the Martin-O'Bryant autoconvolution inequality
summary: We show that there does not exist a constant $c<1$ such that ${\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{2}}^2\le c\,{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{1}}{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{\infty}}$ holds for every nonnegative $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})\cap L^2(\mathbb{R})$.

title: Global zero distribution and pluripolar exceptional cones for complex linear differential equations
summary: We study the zeros of solutions of complex linear differential equations of arbitrary order $n\ge2$ with exponential-sum coefficients. Using the initial-value space $\mathbb{C}^n$ to parametrize the solutions, we show that solutions with initial vectors outside a complete pluripolar cone of Lebesgue measure zero share an explicit common leading term for the global zero count and a common joint limit in radius and angle. The rescaled radial distance from the disk boundary has an exponential limiting distribution, while the rescaled angular deviations from each main ray are Gaussian. Inspired by logarithmic tracts in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal{B}$, we pull exterior sectors back conformally to countably many curvilinear strips extending in finitely many directions and obtain zero-counting asymptotics in each strip, although the coefficients may lie outside this class. title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
summary: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables with $n+2$ monomials. For these functions, we show that the Budan--Fourier bound never exceeds Descartes' bound, and we compute it at the endpoints of the interval of definition. As an application, we

title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
summary: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. title: Translation continuity for the local bilinear circular maximal operator
summary: We prove a positive power translation-continuity estimate for the local bilinear circular maximal operator on the real line. More precisely, there is $η>0$ such that the operator applied to a translation difference in either input maps $L^8(\mathbb{R})\times L^8(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^4(\mathbb{R})$ with norm $O(|h|^η)$. This answers Question 6.3 in Borges's survey on bilinear spherical averages. The main step is a frequency-localized estimate for arbitrary bounded inputs. A $TT^*$ argument converts it into a linear maximal problem on the plane, associated with pairs of circles. We verify the corrected multi-parameter cinematic curvature condition of Chen, Guo, and Yang by proving an irreducibility and infinitesimal independence statement for the resulting quartic curves. Uniform algebraic sublevel estimates control the degeneracies. Interpolation also gives continuity for all finite exponen

title: Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials with non-scalar varying weights
summary: We study the $2\times 2$ matrix orthogonal polynomials $\mathbf{P}_N$ on the real line with respect to the varying weights $\mathrm{e}^{-N\mathbf{Q}(z)}\mathbf{B}(z)$, where $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are real symmetric matrix polynomials that commute with a Hermite-type matrix weight, $\mathbf{Q}$ is not scalar and $\mathbf{B}$ is positive definite. We are motivated by the non-Abelian Toda deformation of the Hermite-type weight, in the sense of Deaño, Morey and Román. The weight depends on $N$ through a matrix exponential that is not scalar, so that its two eigenvalues have different exponential rates. The matrix orthogonality reduces to two scalar orthogonality problems on the real line, with a varying weight that has an essential singularity at the origin. title: Pointwise estimates for an anisotropic product type singular integral on the sphere
On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
summary: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=π^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $σ$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. title: The solution of the Bochner--Krall problem
summary: We solve the Bochner--Krall problem posed by Krall in 1938, extending the classification beyond regular orthogonal sequences. We classify monic polynomial sequences for which multiplying each polynomial by the variable gives a linear combination of that polynomial and the polynomials of the immediately preceding and following degrees, and whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients. Orthogonality is not assumed. The general formulation allows sequences to start at any fixed degree. In every degree beyond a fixed threshold, each sequence agrees, up to an invertible affine change of variable and monic normalization, with a Hermite, Laguerre, Jacobi or Bessel family, the monomial basis, or a finite rational Darboux transform of a Laguerre or Jacobi family. title: Random Configurations and Fourier Decoupling
summary: We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.

title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
summary: It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-δ,δ]$ ($0<δ<π$) from its finite oversampling data $f(j),-n+1\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formulas have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. A recent sinh regularized formula achieved so far the best rate $$ O(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(π-δ)n)). $$ We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $ρ_{n,δ}$ satisfying $$ \frac{c_*}{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}\le ρ_{n,δ}\le \frac{C_*}{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\fracδ4)^{2n+1/2}, 0<δ\leqπ, n\geq1, $$ where $c_*,C_*$ are explicit positive constants independent of $n$ and $δ$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling

title: The bilinear Hilbert transforms are not of restricted weak type $(1,1,1/2)$
summary: For every real $α\neq0,1$, we show that the bilinear Hilbert transform \[ H_α(f_1,f_2)(x) =\text{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-αy)\,f_2(x-y)\,\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{y} \] fails to map $L^1(\mathbb{R})\times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ when restricted to characteristic functions of sets of positive finite measure. The counterexample is quantitative and can be realized by sets that are finite unions of intervals of a common arbitrarily small length.

title: Uncertainty principle on $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$
summary: This paper establishes an uncertainty principle on the mixed space $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ for $n \ge 2$. Leveraging the paraboloid restriction theorem on $\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ derived from Barron's global-in-time Strichartz estimates for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation, we construct measurable sets $S \subset \mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ and $A(R,δ) \subset \mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ that form a strong $L^2$ annihilating pair, satisfying the uniform inequality $\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)} \le 3(\|f\|_{L^2((\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus S)} + \|\widehat{f}\|_{L^2((\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus A(R,δ))})$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)$, where the measures of $S$ and $A(R,δ)$ can be made arbitrarily large while the constant 3 remains unchanged. title: Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
summary: We establish on $R^n\times R^m$ a Fefferman--Stein type distribution function inequality in which the nontangential maximal function of the product Poisson extension is controlled by the Lusin area integral function: \[ |\{N>λ\}|\le C\left(|\{A>λ\}|+λ^{-2}\int_{\{A\leλ\}}A^2\,dx\right). \] The central idea is to establish a local $L^2$ estimate for the radial maximal function. This yields a new proof of the corresponding one-parameter inequality, avoiding Green's formula and the treatment of sawtooth regions, and extends to the multiparameter setting.

title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
summary: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2πsx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.

title: Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
summary: We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i λ_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-π,π)$ which is not a Riesz basis.

title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
summary: Let $λ$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_λ(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}λ(n)e^{2πi nα}\right|\,dα. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_λ(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]

title: Nonlocal bilinear differential operators induced by a third order hypermetric in $\mathbb{R}^n$
summary: The third order hypermetric $ρ(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $Δ^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In this paper, we consider local and nonlocal fractional versions of bilinear differential operators generated by the geometry induced by $ρ(x,y,z)=ρ(0,x-y,x-z)$ instead of the usual $|(x-y,x-z)|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. We consider both the kernel approach and the Fourier multiplier version.

title: Optimal orders for Hilbert-valued Littlewood--Paley functions of symmetric semigroups
summary: We study the Littlewood--Paley $g$-functions associated with symmetric submarkovian semigroups and Hilbert-valued functions. For every $1<p<\infty$ and $2\le q\le\infty$, we prove \[ \norm{G_q^T(f)}{L_p(Ω)} \lesssim\max\{p',\sqrt p\}\norm{f-F(f)}{L_p(Ω;\mathcal{H})}, \] with the sharp order $\max\{p',\sqrt p\}$, where the implicit constant is independent of $p,q$, the underlying space $Ω$, the semigroup $(T_t)_{t>0}$, and the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. Compactly supported radial functions show that, for each fixed $q>2$, the large-$p$ order cannot be replaced by $p^{1/q}$ in a dimension-free heat estimate. In particular, for the case $q=2$, we answers affirmatively the question posed by Xu in his \emph{JFA} paper (2022) \cite[Problem~7]{XuJFA}. For every finite $q>2$, our lower bound gives a negative answer to the dimension-free question in Xu's \emph{JEMS} paper (2025) \cite[Problem~1

title: Rough structure. I. Exclusion among series-parallel graphs
summary: This is the first in a series of papers about rough structure theorems: graph properties that are implied by the exclusion of some graph as a minor, and imply the exclusion of some larger graph of the same type. Here we look at the structure of the series-parallel graphs that do not contain a given series-parallel graph as a minor. We prove that for every series-parallel graph $H$, there exists $m$ such that every simple two-connected series-parallel graph that does not contain $H$ as a minor admits a tree-decomposition of height at most $m$, where each "torso" is either an outerplanar graph or a planar dual of one. We prove similar theorems about the series-parallel graphs that exclude an outerplanar graph, the series-parallel graphs that exclude a dual of an outerplanar graph, the graphs of tree-width three that exclude a series-parallel graph, and the general graphs that exclude a fan

title: On the General Position Number of Cacti
summary: Given a graph G=(V,E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges, a subset of vertices $S \subseteq V$ is called a General Position Set (GPS) if no shortest path on G between any two vertices in S contains another vertex from S. The General Position Number (GPN) of a graph G is the maximum size of a GPS in G. The decision version of this problem, determining whether the GPN of a graph G is at least a given integer i, is known as the General Position Problem (GPP). The GPP is known to be NP-complete, making the computation of the GPN for general graphs computationally challenging. Hence, much of the existing research has focused on determining the GPN for special classes of graphs. One such class is that of cactus graphs (i.e., cacti), in which any two simple cycles share at most one vertex and no edge. For cactus graphs, several upper and lower bounds on the GPN have been

title: When do local bounds permit optimal edge-colorings?
summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $Δ(G)$, maximum multiplicity $μ(G)$, and chromatic index $χ'(G)$. A proper edge-coloring is locally bounded if each edge $e$ in $G$ with endvertices $u$ and $v$ is assigned a color at most $\max\{d_G(u)+μ_G(u),d_G(v)+μ_G(v)\}$, where $d_G(w)$ and $μ_G(w)$ respectively denote the degree of $w$ and the maximum multiplicity of an edge incident with $w$. The well-known Vizing's theorem guarantees a proper edge-coloring with at most $Δ(G)+μ(G)$ colors. Recently, the local version of this theorem was established for simple graphs by Christiansen, resolving a conjecture posed by Bonamy, Delcourt, Lang, and Postle, and extended to multigraphs by Conley, Grebík, and Pikhurko. In this paper, we define the local chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_{loc}(G)$, as the least positive integer $k$ for which $G$ admits a locally bounded proper edge-coloring w

title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
summary: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

title: Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}
summary: We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $λ^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$. As a consequence, $\cN_n$ is non-empty precisely when $n=1$ or $3\cdot2^j-1\le n\le2^{j+2}-1$ for some $j\ge0$, in which case it has $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ elements. This yields a formula for the number of nilpotent $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, which begins $1,9,73,585,4809,39113$. The case $d=0$ is a conjecture of Corless, established in an earlier paper. The main new ingredient is a r

title: Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs
summary: Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. For locally finite $2$-connected graphs, both trees can be chosen end-faithful. We also prove that every locally finite $3$-connected chordal graph has three independent end-faithful spanning trees. Counterexamples show that local finiteness is essential for the version with independent end-faithful spanning trees. We further show that every $3$-connected graph with a universal vertex or a finite vertex cover h

title: Three almost symmetric metatiles generate the Spectre tiling
summary: We present a system of three `metatiles' for the Spectre aperiodic monotiling, named `D23'. These are similar in concept to the {\HTPF} system for the hat tiling: the metatiles have their own substitution system which can be iterated as many times as desired, and then the lowest-order metatiles can be converted into Spectre tiles. One of the three metatiles has order-2 rotational symmetry, and the other two are `almost symmetric' with orders 2 and 3 respectively, in the sense that although the region covered by the tile's $n$-times deflation is not exactly identical to its rotation, within their intersection, the proportion of non-matching tiles tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$. This near-symmetry corresponds to cases of near-symmetry in the Spectre tiling itself. A curious property of this system is that one of the three metatiles disappears completely in the conversion to Spectres!

title: Power-Law Lower Bounds for Edges in Odd Induced Subgraphs
summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $g(G)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an induced subgraph of $G$ in which every vertex has odd degree. Motivated by Scott's question of whether $g(G) \geq cm$ for every graph with $m$ edges, we prove that $g(G) \geq cm^{4/7}$ for every finite simple graph with $m \geq 1$ edges, where $c > 0$ is an absolute constant. For bipartite graphs, we obtain the stronger bound $g(B) \geq cm^{2/3}$.

title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
summary: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$. The codes $I^{n-1}J$, where $I$ and $J$ partition the alphabet, attain this bound when $n$ divides $q$, and Blackburn conjectured that for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the best such code is a maximum non-overlapping code. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes $I^{n-1}J$ with $|I|=(n-1)q/n$ and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.

title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
summary: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.

title: The inverse Erdős--Fuchs problem for $k$-fold sums
summary: For every fixed integer $k\ge 3$, we construct an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{h\le n}r_{kA}(h)=Γ(1+1/k)^k n+O_k(n^{(1-1/k)^2})$, where $r_{kA}(h)$ counts ordered representations of $h$ as a sum of $k$ elements of $A$, with repetitions allowed. This improves Dai and Pan's bound for a linear main term. In the paired random model used here, fluctuations of the stated order occur infinitely often almost surely.

title: On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
summary: In this note, we prove an Erdős-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.

title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
summary: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
summary: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
summary: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and only if it is isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_4$, $C_6$, $C_{10}$, or $D_{2n}$ with $n$ as above. Finally, every split metacyclic group $C_m\rtimes C_q$ with $m>2$ and odd $q\geq3$ is not a $2$-Cayley regression

title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
summary: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.

title: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
summary: For a real number $α>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $ρ(G)=α$ and maximum degree $Δ(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=α-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=αI-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output. We also establish a reduction for a graph $G$ obtained by attaching pairwise disjoint rooted trees, each by a single edge, to a nonempty connected graph $H$. title: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
summary: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.

title: Totally odd clique immersions in graphs with bounded independence number
summary: We prove that every $n$-vertex graph with at least one edge and independence number at most an integer $a\ge2$, where $n\ge a$, contains a totally odd strong immersion of \[ K_{\left\lceil (n+a-1)/(2a-3/2) \right\rceil}, \] with every branch path of length at most $2a-1$. We also prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most $a$ and no totally odd strong $K_t$-immersion with branch paths of length at most $2a-1$ satisfies \[ χ(G)\le\left\lfloor \frac{(2a-3/2)(t-1)-a+2}{2} \right\rfloor \] where $t\ge2$. These bounds reduce the leading denominator coefficient in the general order bound from $9/4$ to $2$ and the colouring coefficient for independence number two from $3/2$ to $5/4$.

title: A characterization of Ramsey property with application to dynamical systems
summary: The infinitary Ramsey theorem says that in any finite partition {V^i;~i=1,2,\cdots,n} of the the family of k-subsets of N, there exists V^i having an infinite subset M of N such that any k-set from M is in V^i. This property of V^i is called the Ramsey property. We characterize this property in term of ultrafilter.

title: Essential and disjoint edge numbers for graphs and hypergraphs
summary: We study the extension to arbitrary forbidden sets of the property that every graph has a bipartition over which at least half of the graph edges are cross-edges, and obtain analogous results in the hypergraph setting.

title: A general triangle generation of the $d$-dimensional Genocchi numbers
summary: We establish a uniform recurrence relation for the rook numbers of generalized Genocchi boards of dimension $d\geq 3$. The recurrence for each row of the rook-number triangle is expressed in terms of the preceding row, with coefficients given by products of consecutive powers and finite sums involving Stirling numbers of the second kind. The proof decomposes the boundary of the board into blocks that correspond to the coordinates equal to 1. A coordinatewise counting argument then shows that the number of extensions of a fixed interior placement depends on a boundary partition only through the number of its blocks and the size of their union. We also express the coefficients as finite differences, recovering the previously established recurrences in dimensions three through five, and give the six-dimensional specialization. title: Failed Vertex Covering Graph Reconfiguration
summary: A failed vertex cover of a graph is a vertex set that leaves at least one edge uncovered. The associated token addition and removal (TAR) graph has the failed vertex covers as vertices, with two sets adjacent when they differ by one vertex. We characterize when two finite graphs have isomorphic failed vertex cover TAR graphs, allowing disconnected graphs, loops, and parallel edges.

title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
summary: For the Möbius function $μ$ and every fixed $0 < ε< 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} μ(n) μ(n + 1) \ll_ε \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - ε}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matomäki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Teräväinen and the author for Möbius on shifted primes. This also yields an improved result, \[ \sum_{p \le x} μ(p + 2) \ll_ε \frac{π(x)}{(\log x)^{1/2 - ε}}. \] Specifically, we refine the determinant approach from the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors. We replace the averaged prime weights of Lü-Wang-Wu with an exact partition of prime intervals. Once sieving out exceptional integers, this enables uniform c

title: Triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes
summary: We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems. We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. As an immediate consequence, we prove the asymptotic form of Lee's high-dimensional Dirac conjecture: every sufficiently large admissible $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least $(3/4+\varepsilon)n$ contains a Steiner triple system. We also provide constructions establishing lower bounds on this fractional decomposition threshold problem.

title: Enumerative Chromatic Choosability of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Small Partite Sets
summary: Chromatic choosability is a notion of fundamental importance in list coloring. A graph is chromatic-choosable when its chromatic number is equal to its list chromatic number. In their 1979 paper on list coloring, Erdős, Rubin, and Taylor showed that complete $m$-partite graphs with every partite set of size 2, denoted by $K_{2*m}$, are chromatic-choosable. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list analogue of the chromatic polynomial of $G$, $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable when $P_{\ell}(G,m) = P(G,m)$ whenever $m \in \mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we explore the question as to whether $K_{2*m}$ satisfies this stronger property. We establish a recursive lower bound on $P_{\ell}(K_{2*m},m)$ and prove that $K_{2*3}$ and $K_{2*4}$ are weakly enumeratively chromatic-choosable, mean

title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
summary: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

title: Star Triangulations
summary: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram. By transforming each such Young diagram to a binary sequence, we manage to also give a combinatorial description of the orbits of these star configurations under the dihedral group action, encoding each such orbit through a black-and-white bracelet. For each star configuration, we derive an explicit formula for the number of its full triangulations, expressed in terms of Catalan numbers and the parts of the associated Young diagram. title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
summary: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k

title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
summary: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribut

title: Extremal $K_t$-intersecting graph families for large $t$
summary: In this paper, we show that for every sufficiently large positive integer $t$ and every integer $n \ge t$, every $K_t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs on vertex set $[n]$ has size at most $2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}$. Furthermore, when the equality is attained, $\mathcal{G}$ must consist of all graphs on $[n]$ that contain some fixed copy of $K_t$. Our result settles a conjecture of Ellis, Filmus, and Friedgut for sufficiently large $t$. We also present a short proof for the odd-cycle-intersecting case, slightly different from the existing proofs in the literature.

title: On the factorization of Dirac hypergraphs
summary: A celebrated result from the 70s due to Baranyai states that the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings if $k\mid n$. We prove a minimum degree version of this result. Note that a necessary condition for a $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices to admit a decomposition into perfect matchings is that $G$ is vertex-regular and $k\mid n$. We show that, if this is satisfied and, in addition, $G$ has minimum $(k-1)$-degree at least $(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n$, then it indeed decomposes into perfect matchings. The constant $1/2$ is optimal, as below this threshold, $G$ might not even contain a single perfect matching. This settles a conjecture of Glock, Kühn and Osthus from 2021.

title: Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions and the Hirota-Miwa equation
summary: For $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ count Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and $c$ above it, and let $D_{k,n}=\det\bigl(a_{i+j,k}(x,c)\bigr)_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. Yu proved Cigler's conjecture $D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2$ $(n\ge2k+2)$ by writing $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant of Chebyshev polynomials modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$. Using a linear map found by Yu, we show that the recurrence is a reduction of the Hirota-Miwa equation for Casorati determinants. This gives a second proof, and the recurrence holds for $n\ge2k+2+\max(0,N-\lfloor k/2\rfloor)$ for the Hankel determinants of $n\mapsto L(X^n(U_k-xU_{k-1}))$ whenever the moment functional $L$ has the recurrence coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomials above height $N$.
