title: Stability analysis of stochastic differential equations with the Koopman operator
summary: This paper investigates the stability of stochastic systems through the lens of the Koopman operator framework. In particular, we establish the connection between the convergence properties of the Koopman semigroup and specific stability properties of the underlying stochastic system. Moreover, we demonstrate that specific Koopman eigenfunctions capture stochastic attractivity properties and we illustrate these results with two numerical examples. This work mirrors existing Koopman operator-based stability results for deterministic systems and extends them to the stochastic framework.

title: Rigidity of randomly perturbed expanding circle maps
summary: We extend the classical smooth linearization theory of expanding circle maps to randomly perturbed ones without requiring small perturbations, establishing two equivalent rigidity criteria of absolute continuity of random conjugacy and Lyapunov exponents along random periodic orbits. In the random setting, an essential difficulty is the uniqueness of absolutely continuous random invariant measures. For the first criterion, we overcome this difficulty by refining the memory-loss argument of Ott, Stenlund and Young, which gives the exponential convergence of probability densities, to establish the uniqueness of random invariant measures; for the second criterion, we bypass this difficulty by employing periodic-orbital averaging together with Jensen's equality condition to derive pointwise rigidity directly from the periodic data.

title: Hydrodynamic limit of the Toda lattice
summary: In this paper we consider the Toda lattice under random, spatially inhomogeneous initial data, meaning that its initial momenta and interparticle spacings are independent and their laws may slowly vary in space. When the density is strictly positive (but sufficiently small), we identify the model's hydrodynamic limit under Euler scaling. More precisely, we prove that spatial averages of each of the model's local conserved quantities converge to moments of a density $m_τ(λ,q)$ solving the generalized hydrodynamic equation predicted by Doyon arXiv:1902.07624 and Spohn arXiv:1902.07751. To do so, we justify the notion that the Toda lattice can be thought of as a dense collection of many "quasiparticles" that interact through scattering. title: Conditional limit theorems in dynamical systems
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems. We study the statistical properties of the dynamics within transient regimes by establishing a suite of limit theorems describing the behavior of trajectories under the condition that they remain outside a ``hole'', or region of no return. Under a spectral gap assumption for the associated open transfer operator, we first establish conditioning and Yaglom limits and identify the corresponding conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures. We then establish conditional exponential decay of correlations and the Strong Law of Large Numbers for both deterministic and quenched random systems. We also obtain a conditional Central Limit Theorem, Large Deviation Principle, and Berry--Esseen theorem, with additional assumptions in the quenched random case. We also derive standard (non

title: Averting `Gravity': Launch Control and the Limits of Collision Avoidance in Low Earth Orbit Operations
summary: As large constellations fill low Earth orbit, the risk of a runaway collision cascade has become a central concern of space operations. Debris population models treat collision avoidance as a fixed input, although the capacity to screen potential collisions and plan maneuvers degrades as debris accumulates. Using a stylized multi-layer queueing network model, we show that collision avoidance capabilities that saturate as the in-custody fragment count increases, can make the orbital shell bistable, with a low-debris and a high-debris equilibrium, and hysteretic. This has two major operational consequences. First, leaving the high-debris equilibrium requires a large cut in launch rates. Second, in the low-debris equilibrium, fragment counts respond with a delay as the launch rate rises past a tipping point. Removing bistability is desirable, and we show that fragment count-indexed admissio

title: Irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on projective $k$-lattices and Frobenius numbers
summary: The irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ induces an action on the space $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of projective classes of rank $k$-discrete subgroups in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and every starting point in $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $2\leq k<n$, we prove convergence of the orbit averages over expanding norm balls and give a complete, explicit description of their limits. In an overview, every limit is supported on the subbundle over the unique compact $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit in the Grassmannian. The conditional measures on the fibers are either uniform on finite sets or convex combinations of at most two homogeneous measures associated with split simple subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}_k(\mathbb{R})$ containing the principal $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$. title: Orbits of $p$-adic flows: balls, time-one maps and minimal group actions
summary: Let $f$ be a vector field on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ given by polynomials, or by power series converging on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, whose coefficients are divisible by $p^c$, where $c \ge 1$ ($c \ge 2$ when $p = 2$). Its flow exists for every $p$-adic time. I show that $t \mapsto \varphi_t(x)$ multiplies distances by exactly $\|f(x)\|_p$, in every dimension. This gives explicit flow-box coordinates, closed formulas for hitting times, return times and orbit averages, and a Newton iteration that computes them with quadratic convergence; in dimension one it recovers Mukhamedov's theorem that interpolated orbits are balls. I then show that the analytic maps $g$ congruent to the identity modulo $p^c$, coefficientwise, are exactly the time-one maps of such fields, and that the field is congruent to $g - \mathrm{id}$ modulo $p^{c+1}$. title: Replicating chaotic dynamics from sparse sensors with recurrent latent states
summary: Forecasting a high-dimensional nonlinear system from a few point sensors requires an estimate of the current state and a model of its evolution. Reduced-order models usually take the full state as input, so with only sparse sensors they require an auxiliary full-state estimate whose error is inherited by the latent representation. We instead build the latent state from sensor measurements alone, using a shallow recurrent decoder (SHRED) network that encodes a history of point measurements, and train an echo state network to advance that latent state autonomously. We show that the resulting latent dynamics replicate the long-term dynamical invariants of the underlying system rather than merely tracking its short-term trajectory. For the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, the autonomous latent model reproduces the leading Lyapunov exponents of the full system from 25 of 128 state components, u

title: Multifractal analysis of Takagi-type functions built from beta-expansion cylinders
summary: We study a family of Takagi functions obtained by placing a normalized tent on each beta-expansion cylinder, with amplitude $β^{-αn}$ at order $n$, where $β>1$ and $0<α\le1$. We characterize their pointwise Hölder regularity in terms of cylinder lengths and distances from the point under consideration. The characterization holds more generally for nested interval partitions with exponentially decreasing mesh, without requiring interval lengths at a given order to be comparable. For beta-expansion cylinders, we compute the full multifractal spectrum whenever the remainders of the expansion of $1$ have a finite upper exponential decay rate. The functions are monofractal when this rate vanishes, as it does for Parry, Pisot and Salem bases. When it is positive, the spectrum is affine on a nondegenerate interval. title: Dynamics-preserving graph sparsification
summary: Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes. We first study linear diffusion, where node values evolve according to the graph Laplacian. The dominant network sparsification method, effective resistance sampling, preserves all Laplacian eigenvalues within a uniform multiplicative bound. We show that with a limited edge budget, this is dynamically inefficient: diffusion is dominated by the slowest-decaying modes, so enforcing a uniform guarantee spends edges on fast modes that barely affect long-term dynamics. Based on this observation, we derive Diffusion Spectral Error (DSE), which evalua

title: Tropicalization and slow manifolds: A case study of the Michaelis--Menten reaction
summary: We present a case study of a recently developed approach to multiple-scale systems based on exponential scaling and tropicalization (Kristiansen and Sarantaris, \emph{On a tropicalization of planar polynomial ODEs}). Parameters and variables are scaled exponentially with respect to a small parameter $ε$, so that orders of magnitude become a genuine non-smooth singular limit $ε\to 0$. Tropical geometry, via subdivisions of the Newton polygon, classifies the asymptotic regimes and locates the candidates for slow manifolds on all scales of the variables simultaneously. Here we combine this framework with blow-up and geometric singular perturbation theory. {In particular,} the non-smooth singular limit is resolved by spherical and cylindrical blow-ups, and degeneracies caused by exponentially small terms with flat contact are treated by adding the exponential quantities as new variables {(fo

title: The orbital architecture of 14 Herculis system as a KAM-stable three-body configuration
summary: The 14 Herculis system hosts two massive giant planets on eccentric and mutually inclined orbits, making it a compelling test case for long-term stability in the spatial planetary three-body problem. We develop an analytical description of its dynamics using averaging, symplectic reduction of symmetries and KAM theory. For parameters compatible with the observed architecture, the secular quadrupole Hamiltonian possesses two elliptic relative equilibria that organise the nearby dynamics. The octupole contribution introduces a second slow angle and yields a properly-degenerate multiscale Hamiltonian. Under the corresponding smallness, non-resonance, and non-degeneracy conditions, families of quasi-periodic orbits coming from the relative equilibria of the quadrupolar approximation fill invariant 2-tori. Restoring the two fast mean anomalies and the cyclic angle conjugate to the angular-mom

title: Sums and Products in Dynamically Central Syndetic Sets
summary: Glasscock and Le introduced the notion \textit{dynamically central syndetic sets} in a minimal topological dynamical system under the minimal action of the semigroup $(\mathbb{N}, +).$ In this short note, we introduce these large sets in the semigroup $(\mathbb{N}, \cdot)$ and establish that dynamically central syndetic sets contain the Hindman configuration $\{x,y,x+y,xy\}$. Furthermore, we show that there are dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets that do not contain such configurations.

title: Reconstructing hidden attractors with reservoir computing
summary: Hidden attractors are difficult to locate as their basins of attraction do not intersect with any small neighborhood of an equilibrium point. We examine the possibility of reconstructing the hidden chaotic attractor from time series via reservoir computing, where the reservoir is built by a network of driven Kuramoto oscillators. We compare all-to-all coupling, nearest-neighbour ring coupling, and a ring with one modified oscillator equation which ensures that any attractor will be hidden. The numerical results suggest that ring coupling supports accurate reconstruction over a wider range of coupling and forcing strengths than all-to-all coupling. Searches near reservoir equilibria nevertheless show why agreement in short-term prediction and long-term statistics does not establish preservation of hiddenness. Numerics for the modified ring show that it has the highest performance which co

title: Feedback and Resource Competition in Incoherent Feedforward Loops: When Is Cumulative Dose Ordering Preserved?
summary: Biochemical coupling can change the expression levels and timing predicted by an incoherent feedforward loop (IFFL) model without changing cumulative dose ordering. We derive ordering conditions using shared-production identities and Metzler comparison bounds, with tail guarantees beyond finite computation. A nonlinear example exhibits delayed slope reversal at a fixed dose, on an $O(1/η)$ timescale as pathway mismatch $η$ vanishes. At one fixed joint fit, validated bounds establish decreasing cumulative output across 20-100 ng nominal burden, from zero to full target loading, at every positive finite observation time for a translation-blocking model and an RNA-decay model. Full loading at 20 ng reduces 48-hour cumulative output by 13.35% and 10.18%, respectively, while endpoint concentration in the first model changes by only +0.15%. title: Global phase-plane organization of a toxin-mediated plant-herbivore model
summary: Plant-herbivore interactions with chemical plant defence mechanisms can generate complex population dynamics through the nonlinear interplay between resource availability, herbivore pressure, and defence-induced feedbacks. In this work, we investigate the dynamical organization of a plant-herbivore model characterized by a non-monotone functional response accounting for inhibitory effects on grazing activity. In particular, we perform a qualitative and geometric analysis of the associated homogeneous system, characterizing the dynamical regimes supported by the model and the transitions between them. The results reveal the emergence of oscillatory behaviour through a Hopf bifurcation and the occurrence of stable periodic solutions. We further characterize the global phase-plane organization, providing a complete classification of equilibrium configurations and heteroclinic structures sup

title: Waist inequality and a Hurewicz-type theorem for mean dimension
summary: We establish a Hurewicz-type inequality relating mean dimension and conditional metric mean dimension. For every equivariant continuous map between dynamical systems, the mean dimension of the domain is bounded above by the sum of the mean dimension of the target and the conditional metric mean dimension of the map. In particular, any equivariant continuous map that decreases mean dimension must have infinite topological conditional entropy. The key ingredient is a new waist inequality, which we believe is of independent geometric interest beyond its application to dynamical systems. Compared with Gromov's original waist inequality, a distinctive feature of this inequality is that it applies to finite simplicial complexes of arbitrary topology, subject only to dimensional restrictions.

title: Strong Transitivity of Group Cellular Automata: Characterization and Decidability
summary: A discrete-time dynamical system is strongly transitive if every point can be reached, in finitely many steps, from every non-empty open set. We study this property for group cellular automata, \ie cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism, in every dimension $d\geq1$. We prove that no group cellular automaton over a non-abelian group is strongly transitive, and we develop a decomposition of group cellular automata over abelian groups, via quotients by power subgroups, which preserves strong transitivity. For linear cellular automata over $(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^n$ we use Pontryagin duality to characterize strong transitivity in terms of the characteristic polynomial $χ_A$ of the associated matrix $A$ of Laurent polynomials: the automaton is strongly transitive if and only if $\det(A)\neq0$ and no irreducible factor of $χ_A$ has an invertible

title: A new premodel for bounded type Siegel disks of some transcendental entire functions
summary: In the 1980s, Douady and Sullivan conjectured that the Siegel disks of rational maps with degree at least two are Jordan domains. Based on the study of Blaschke models, this conjecture was settled by Zhang under the condition that the Siegel disks are of bounded type, and by Zakeri for a large number of transcendental entire functions under the same condition. The entire functions studied by Zakeri have exactly one finite asymptotic value, which is the center of the fixed Siegel disk. Chéritat, and later with Epstein, also studied the Siegel disk boundaries of such type transcendental entire functions by developing Ghys-like models. In this paper, by introducing a new premodel, we prove that the fixed bounded type Siegel disk centered at the non-zero point $λ-1$ of $f_λ(z)=e^{1-λ}ze^z$ is a quasi-disk whose boundary contains the critical point $-1$. The asymptotic value $0$ is not contai

title: Growth of Sobolev Norms for Linear Schrodinger Equations with Denjoy--Carleman Potentials
summary: We consider the linear Schrödinger equation on a torus of arbitrary dimension with a real time-dependent potential satisfying a mixed space--time Denjoy--Carleman condition. More precisely, for an increasing concave weight \(ω(r)\asymp \log^σ(e+r)\), \(σ> 1\),we assume \[ \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\partial_t^q\widehat V(k,t)| \le Ae^{Bq^{p}}e^{-ρ_{0}ω(|k|)},\qquad p=\fracσ{σ-1}. \] The corresponding spatial class is strictly larger than every Gevrey class, while the moment factor gives the quantitative ultradifferentiable control in time needed by the finite normal form. We adapt the method of Delort and Fang--Zhang to this non-power Fourier weight. The essential new point is a quantitative operator calculus whose majorant is built from the moment sequence and an auxiliary factorial that closes the exact Leibniz convolutions. title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
summary: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. These approaches typically quantify drag reduction as a function of a single geometric parameter, such as spanwise spacing or groove cross-sectional area, evaluated over fixed riblet shapes. As a result, identifying optimal riblet geometries across a broader design space often necessitates exhaustive parametric studies. To address this problem, we propose an optimization framework for the systematic design of optimal riblet shapes. Accordingly, we reformulate the volume penal

title: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks
summary: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. We establish that this model achieves flocking within finite time and derive a quantitative relationship between the lower bound of flocking time and graph volume. Based on these results, we observe that imposing sufficiently small flocking time induces an increase in network volume, and that larger initial velocity variance requires greater volume under the same time constraint. In our experiments, we trained a transformer-based PPO policy to select network structures at each time step. Under the most stringent time constraint, the maximum average number of connections increased sharply, confirming a threshold effect. The negative c

title: The topology of the mean action spectrum
summary: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.

title: Klarner's sequences have density $0$
summary: We prove that the set of non-negative integers $n$ which can be obtained from $0$ by repeated application of affine maps $x\mapsto 2x$, $x\mapsto 3x+2$ and $x\mapsto 6x+3$ has density $0$. Moreover, we reach the same conclusion for five other sequences of similar type introduced by D. Klarner. More generally, we establish a criterion excluding stationary measures with bounded density on the profinite group $\mathbb Z_P\cong\prod_{p\mid P}\mathbb Z_p$. A density-to-measure construction using invariant Banach limits and a combinatorial argument involving rational orbits and affine words yield our density-zero results. The criterion also applies to an infinite family of mixed-slope affine semigroups.

title: Structural functional identifiability of unknown differential equation observation maps
summary: In many differential equation models of real-world systems, the mechanistic structure of the dynamics is known, but the map from the dynamics to the observations is not. This is potentially problematic, as it can prevent us from e.g. learning model parameter values from data. Examples where this occurs include measuring a fluorescent marker as a proxy for the dynamics of a cellular circuit, and using wastewater measurements to follow the development of an epidemic. The nascent field of hybrid modelling, in which machine learning components (like neural networks) are embedded within mechanistic models, provides the tools to learn such maps. Here, the system's dynamics keep their mechanistic form, while a neural network represents the unknown observation map and is trained alongside any unknown core system parameters. title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
summary: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side. To explain, we derive reduced-order models: the softmax is a Boltzmann distribution, gradient descent an Euler step on a nonlinear spring,

title: Hill's Lunar Equation as a Leaf: Riccati Reduction and Frobenius Theory for Second-Order PDEs
summary: The equations of Hill and Adams for the lunar perigee and node, Mathieu's equation and Lamé's equation arise as leafwise restrictions of one class of linear partial differential equations, the \emph{square-type foliated equations} $L^2u+A\,Lu+B\,u=0$, where $L$ is an analytic vector field and $A,B$ are analytic functions. Such an equation has a regular singularity exactly when the foliation defined by $L$ is analytically linearizable. At rational saddles, where every point of the indicial conic is resonant, we obtain convergent solutions whose exponents are holomorphic functions of a first integral; their variation describes the monodromy along the leaves and decides when classical Frobenius solutions exist. For a Hill equation, the characteristic exponent becomes the value of such a holomorphic function, given by a convergent series. This yields rigorous computer-assisted proofs of Hill

title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
summary: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification pr

title: Random compositions of quasiperiodic cocycles
summary: We consider the multiplicative process given by random compositions of linear cocycles over toral translations. Under appropriate generic assumptions, we establish effective large deviations estimates as well as the Hölder continuity of the associated Lyapunov exponent of the process. These properties in particular show the regularizing effect of randomness on quasiperiodic dynamics. The novelty of our approach allows for the study of such properties notwithstanding the lack of a spectral gap for the corresponding transition operator.

title: Cantor Julia sets of positive area in non-autonomous dynamics
summary: For every $a>0$, we prove the existence of a sequence of polynomials with rational coefficients whose non-autonomous iteration produces a Julia set of planar area $a$. We also construct a sequence of rational maps with rational coefficients whose Julia set has the same prescribed area. No individual map in this rational sequence is Möbius-conjugate to a polynomial, and no choice of Möbius coordinates at successive phases turns it into a polynomial sequence. In both cases, for every $n\geq1$, the Julia set obtained by starting the iteration at the $n$-th map, called the phase-$n$ Julia set, is a Cantor set and meets every neighborhood of each of its points in positive planar area. For every $A\in(0,1)$, we construct two sequences of quadratic polynomials, each with $\infty$ in every phase Julia set and with first phase Julia set of normalized spherical area $A$. In one sequence, every pha

title: Siphon faces in slow-fast mass-action networks
summary: When the species of a siphon in a mass-action network, however many, are fast and their invariant face loses transverse stability along the slow flow, trajectories follow the face past this loss before leaving it. We study three consequences. (i) If the transverse Metzler linearisation is irreducible, the entry-exit relation with its Perron root gives the exit. Under acyclic feeding between its strongly connected components, a max-plus recursion over the reactions gives it; in general neither the Perron root nor the diagonal blocks do. (ii) With one slow species, acyclic feeding and a transversal exit, a fold of the interior critical manifold followed by a drop onto the face gives a unique, exponentially attracting relaxation oscillation whose turning points tend to the fold and exit point. title: A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
summary: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz. In particular the answer is negative for general finite-energy data, and the open question is reduced to Lipschitz data.

title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
summary: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $σ$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

title: The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$
summary: In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.

title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
summary: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $μ$ and $μ(f)=0$. The system $(T,μ)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for Hölder observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.

title: Unconditionally Positive Nonstandard Finite Difference Schemes for $p$-Laplacian Reaction--Diffusion Equations
summary: We propose a conservative, semi-implicit nonstandard finite difference scheme for the reaction--diffusion equation $u_t=λ(|u_x|^{p-2}u_x)_x+f(u)$, $p>1$, where, as is customary, the $p$-Laplacian is regularized by a parameter $\eps>0$. The scheme combines a denominator function, a lagged diffusion coefficient, and a nonlocal treatment of the loss part of the reaction. For every time step and mesh size we prove that the scheme is well posed and positive, that it preserves an invariant region $[0,K]$ whenever the reaction admits one, and that it reproduces every constant equilibrium exactly. Without reaction, it conserves mass, satisfies a discrete maximum principle, and, for $1<p\le 2$, decreases a discrete energy. An example shows that the energy may increase for $p>2$. The truncation error is $O(k+h^2)$ at interior nodes. Numerical tests confirm first order in time and second order in s

title: Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space
summary: Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$. A $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{K}(X)$ is called an invariant random compact (IRC), and the action is IC-rigid if $δ_X$ is the only IRC supported on infinite compact subsets of $X$. In this paper we give a pair-correlation criterion implying both IC-rigidity and the Glasner property. As an application, we prove both these properties for finitely generated $\operatorname{Ad}$-Zariski-dense semi-groups acting on compact homogeneous spaces $G/Λ$, where $G$ is connected and noncompact with simple Lie algebra and $Λ<G$ is a cocompact lattic

title: State-Dependent Saving and Heavy-Tailed Shocks in a Stochastic Solow Growth Model via a Logistic Lévy Framework
summary: This work develops a stochastic Solow growth model in which the aggregate saving rate is state dependent and evolves on a faster time scale than capital. The saving target follows a mean-reverting process driven by symmetric $α$-stable Lévy noise, while the saving control adjusts toward this target and capital accumulates according to a Solow equation. After scaling, the model is a three-dimensional stochastic dynamical system with multiplicative heavy-tailed noise and a logistic saving function. We establish invariance of the economically meaningful state space for the discrete reflected model, derive the stationary distribution of the saving target in the Gaussian limiting case, and characterize how the tail index and logistic sensitivity affect the coupled dynamics. Monte Carlo simulations show bimodal capital and saving distributions, asymmetric first-passage behavior between low- an

title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
summary: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
summary: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.

title: Physics-informed neural network for model-based global computation of the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators
summary: The asymptotic phase is the central object of phase reduction theory for limit-cycle oscillators. It is a scalar coordinate defined throughout the basin of attraction of a limit cycle that advances at a constant natural frequency along every trajectory. Computing the phase from a given mathematical model requires solving a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire basin, which is challenging due to high computation costs and complex boundary conditions. In this study, we propose a physics-informed neural network to efficiently calculate the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators. By incorporating three types of loss functions, we train a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to satisfy the governing PDE for the asymptotic phase and the adjoint equation for the phase gradient. title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
summary: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every po

title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
summary: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane. When $n=d$ we find that as $n\to \infty$, the boundedness locus tends to the union of two unit circles centered at $\pm 2\sqrt{a}$. For arbitrary $n,d$, we identify a spine consisting of unit circles determined by the critical values, and prove that the boundedness locus tends to the spine as $n,d\to \infty$.

title: Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
summary: Medicaid covers nearly 78 million people, yet care quality varies across states, programs, and clinical domains. Using the 2024 CMS Child and Adult Core Sets (9,781 usable state-measure observations from 11,100 records), this study combined descriptive statistics, benchmark-gap analysis, correlation, and OLS regression to find where shortfalls cluster. Disparities were strongly domain-specific. Maternal and Perinatal Health scored lowest (28.0%), followed by Dental and Oral Health (38.5%) and Behavioral Health (44.4%), while Long-Term Services and Supports (82.8%) and Experience of Care (67.8%) scored highest. State performance correlated strongly with national benchmarks (r = 0.77, approximately), so rates should be read against each measure's benchmark. title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
summary: This paper studies contraction properties of stochastic dynamical systems governed by Itô stochastic differential equations. We consider two trajectories driven by a common noise process and measure their separation using Finsler distances, which encompass Riemannian and norm-induced distances. Two notions of contraction are then investigated: $L^p$-contraction, defined by exponential decay of the $L^p$-norm (or the $p$-th moment) of the distance, and almost sure contraction, defined by exponential decay of the distance along almost every sample path. Each notion is characterized by a differential condition that is necessary and sufficient for contraction under mild hypotheses. Relations between contraction notions and an associated incremental input-to-state stability result are also established. As an illustration, we apply the established theory to analyze noise-induced synchronizatio

title: Stability of Carathéodory Outer Measures Generated by Spatial Gauges
summary: We study outer measures generated by covering costs that depend on both the diameter and the location of a covering set. After establishing the metric and Borel-regularity properties of this construction, we investigate its stability under perturbations of the spatial gauge. For power gauges, we prove a uniform logarithmic criterion: if the exponent perturbation multiplied by $\log(1/r)$ converges uniformly to $λ$, then the induced measure is multiplied by $e^{-λ}$. Pointwise asymptotic equivalence, however, is insufficient: on $[0,1]$ we construct bounded gauges whose ratio is eventually equal to one at every fixed point, although their induced measures differ by a prescribed factor. In the converse direction, continuity of the ratio in the spatial variable on a Baire space yields equality of the measures on every compact subset of a suitable dense $G_δ$ set. The results identify a conc

title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
summary: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $μ$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $μ$) admit a common minimal model.

title: Variants of Expansivity, Shadowing and Spectral Decomposition
summary: In this paper, we first distinguish a very recently introduced notion of mean asymptotic expansivity from asymptotic expansivity. Then, we extend the spectral decomposition theorem due to Smale to bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. We also extend a measurable spectral decomposition theorem due to Shin to shadowable measures for bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms. Each of the chain transitive sub-systems obtained by Shin can be further decomposed into chain mixing systems by using the ideas of Richeson and Wiseman. Next, we use a probabilistic argument to recover both Smale-like and Bowen-like spectral decompositions for expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. Moreover, we investigate inter-relations among several variants of the shadowing property including the eventual shadowing property, the thick shadowing property,

title: Minimal sets of countable group actions on regular curves
summary: We study minimal sets of countable groups acting by homeomorphisms on regular curves. If the ambient action has a finite orbit, every infinite minimal set is an equicontinuous Cantor system. If there is no finite orbit, the minimal set is unique and remains minimal for every finite-index subgroup. A minimal set supporting an invariant probability is a finite orbit, an equicontinuous Cantor system, a circle isometry action, or a Cantor extension obtained by splitting a countable invariant subset of such a circle. Without an invariant probability, infinitely many nondegenerate components can occur. Their homeomorphism types determine the underlying space, and every nonempty countable family of types is realized. The two-generator free group admits an example with arc components on a dendrite, whereas its restricted wreath product with the integers admits none on any regular curve.

title: Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
summary: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

title: Instability of non-minimal critical points of Newton's equation with real analytic potentials
summary: We prove that any non-minimal critical point of a real analytic potential on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space possesses a nonconstant zero-energy Newton trajectory that converges to the equilibrium as \(t\to+\infty\). By time reversibility, this yields forward Lyapunov instability. We do not assume the critical point is isolated. The proof constructs angular minima via quadratic regularization, matching the regularization coefficient to the leading inertial term. A free forcing coefficient allows continuation past bounded accumulations of correction orders. For polynomial potentials, this produces a complete Hahn-series solution, and differential algebraicity gives a common Puiseux denominator. A fixed-denominator continuation estimate together with a finite Taylor transfer extends the construction to analytic potentials. The realization theorem for the resulting invariant formal pha

title: A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
summary: We study the polynomial Liénard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci. China Math. 69 (2026)].

title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Liénard systems
summary: This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Liénard system $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$, with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$. It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting for $a_2<0$; this system has no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar arcs obtained in potential coordinates. This result gives a positive answer to Conjecture 1.4 of Cen et al. (Sci. China Math., 2026).

title: Moment approximations in optimal transport: geometric estimates and a semiclassical limit
summary: We study finite moment approximations of linear optimization problems over measures. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the existence of discrete minimizers with a controlled number of support points, duality and $Γ$-convergence as the moment approximation is refined. This framework accommodates several transport problems, in which marginal constraints are replaced by finitely many moment constraints. For moment functions localized at scale $r_n$, we prove an estimate controlling $W_\infty$ by $W_p$ up to an additive error of order $r_n$, which also applies to discrete measures. For repulsive costs, we show that minimizers remain separated from the diagonal, uniformly in the number of moments, and we derive consequences for dual potentials. Finally, under a moment-correction assumption, we prove that the fermionic minimum energies converge in the semiclassical limit to the moment-c

title: An asymptotic ball algebra with countably determined spectra and a nonseparable character space
summary: Let $X=\partial\mathbb B_2\subset\mathbb C^2$ and let $\mathcal R$ be the restrictions to $X$ of functions in the ball algebra $A(\overline{\mathbb B_2})$. The unital uniform Banach algebra \[ \mathcal A=\{(f_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X)):\mathrm{dist}_{C(X)}(f_n,\mathcal R)\longrightarrow0\} \] is inverse-closed in $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X))$. Consequently one countable family of evaluation characters generates the spectrum of every element of $\mathcal A$. Nevertheless $Δ(\mathcal A)$ contains continuum many pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets and is therefore nonseparable. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Ohrysko, Wojciechowski and Graham.

title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
summary: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(π/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. title: Isometrically greedy renormings of bidemocratic unconditional bases of Banach spaces
summary: We show that if a greedy basis of a Banach space has the additional property that its dual basis is also greedy, then the space admits an equivalent norm under which the basis is isometrically greedy. This solves in the positive a question posed by Dilworth, Kutzarova, Odell, Schlumprecht and Zsák in 2014. As an application, we resolve a long-standing problem explicitly posed by Albiac, Ansorena and Wallis in 2017 by proving that any subsymmetric basis of a Banach space is isometrically greedy under a suitable renorming of the ambient space.

title: Critical Gaussian Asymptotics for Directional Superoscillations: STFT and Gabor Consequences
summary: We study directional Aharonov--Berry superoscillations in $\R^d$ with widening anisotropic Gaussian envelopes. We prove that the rescaled total $L^2$ mass has a sharp transition governed by the matrix $D=Q-(a^2-1)vv^T$. At criticality, $D$ has a one-dimensional kernel, and the mass obeys an exact $N^{d/2+1/4}$ law with an explicit Gamma-function constant. After anisotropic rescaling, the intensity converges globally in $L^1$ to a transverse Gaussian times a longitudinal quartic exponential. Moyal's identity gives the corresponding total STFT-energy law, but does not imply a local phase-space concentration theorem. We compare these global statements with the earlier quartic critical-window analysis of Berry and Shukla for periodic superoscillations. Supporting results include quantitative fixed-Gaussian STFT expansions, entire-growth convergence with a critical-step obstruction, and condi

title: The n-th Zbáganu constant
summary: In this paper, we introduce the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Banach spaces and investigate its basic properties. We establish some inequalities which give the relationship between the $n$-th Zbáganu constant and two other constants, namely the $n$-th Von Neumann-Jordan constant and the $n$-th James constant. In addition, we determine the values of the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Lebesgue spaces, Morrey spaces, and discrete Morrey spaces.

title: $L^p$-isometries on idempotents
summary: We study surjective $L^p$-isometries on spaces of bounded idempotents in an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. On each fixed positive finite-rank stratum, every surjective $L^p$-isometry, $1\leq p<\infty$, is implemented by a unitary or antiunitary operator, possibly composed with adjunction; no separability is required. The same conclusion holds for the operator norm, viewed as the $L^\infty$-norm. On a separable space, operator-norm isometries of the infinite-rank, infinite-corank sector admit the additional complement operation, as do surjective $L^p$-isometries between individual $L^p$-perturbation classes for $1\leq p<\infty$. For the extended $L^p$-metric on all idempotents, implementations may be chosen independently on finite-distance classes, subject to an explicit compatibility condition for matching infinite-rank classes. The proofs use similarity coordinates and metr

title: From Powers--Stormer to Loewner Inertia: Weighted Trace Functionals and Orthogonal Perturbations
summary: We study the weighted trace functional $\TT_{f,h}(A,B)=\Tr h^\circ(A-B)[f(A)-f(B)]$, where $h^\circ(H)=h(H_+)-h(H_-)$. The Jordan decomposition of $A-B$ yields exact common-roof decompositions for operator monotone and operator convex functions, including the Powers--Størmer and Ricard trace comparisons. The orthogonal cross term gives a finite rank-one realization of the classical conditional Löwner-matrix criterion for operator convexity. For powers, resolvent squares yield a coupling-dependent Mellin strip, endpoint identities, and quantitative bounds on off-sector spectral interactions. Linearization produces positive and inverse moment subspaces of power Löwner matrices. A confluent determinant calculation provides the remaining sign data in the known inertia classification. We give explicit equality conditions and a finite-copy application of the Powers--Størmer equality case.

title: Fixed and periodic points of bi-dual intersection operators
summary: We classify the fixed and periodic points, up to positive dilation, of the operators $\mathbb I_m=\mathbb I_{m,m+1}$ in the indexed bi-dual intersection family associated with centro-section integrals. For $n\ge3$ and $1\le m\le n-2$, a star body satisfies $\mathbb I_m^{\,r}K=cK$ for some $c>0$ and an integer $r\ge1$ if and only if it is an origin-centered Euclidean ball. No convexity, origin symmetry, or initial differentiability is assumed. An exact Grassmannian graph representation gives a decreasing weight and yields a strictly positive linear increment under continuous Steiner symmetrization unless the body is already symmetric. At a fixed point, a uniform radial Taylor estimate makes the same volume-preserving increment quadratic. Sobolev estimates for the spherical Radon transform and its adjoint supply the required regularity. Independently, a strict Lyapunov inequality reduces e

title: Schatten and weak Schatten classes of composition operator differences on Bergman spaces
summary: We investigate Schatten and weak Schatten class membership of differences of composition operators on the standard weighted Bergman spaces over the unit disk. We prove that the known sufficient condition for Schatten p-class membership is also necessary for 0<p<2, thereby completing the characterization for all p>0. We also characterize when differences of composition operators belong to weak Schatten classes for every p>0. Both results are expressed in terms of local-mass conditions involving the pseudohyperbolic distance between the inducing maps, and yield two-sided (quasi-)norm estimates.

title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
summary: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In

title: Incremental Roseland: Batch-wise Landmark Diffusion via Kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève Update
summary: Landmark diffusion (Roseland) computes a diffusion-map-style spectral embedding from the singular value decomposition of a degree-normalized data-to-landmark kernel matrix, at a cost far below that of full diffusion maps. It assumes, however, that all data are available at once. We introduce incremental Roseland (iRoseland), which casts the landmark affinity as a row-growing matrix whose SVD can be updated with a kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève (SKL) scheme. Degre correction is handled by a first order expansion about a reference mean kernel row and so that the landmark-side eigenbasis may be recovered from a single landmark-by-landmark eigendecomposition at each step. The presented method requires only a single pass over the data and runs in bounded-memory with state independent of the number of points processed. A forgetting factor lets the method track drifting distributions, an

title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
summary: We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.

title: Generalized and Convex Poincaré Inequalities via Transport-Divergence Inequalities
summary: We investigate the relationship between generalized $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and transport-divergence inequalities involving $χ^q$-type divergences. Extending the classical correspondence between the $(2,2)$-Poincaré inequality and quadratic transport-$χ^2$ inequalities, we prove that a $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequality is equivalent to a transport-divergence inequality for conjugates $(p,p')$ and $(q,q')$. We then study the convex counterpart of these inequalities. Using weak barycentric optimal transport and convex order, we establish an equivalence between convex $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and weak transport-divergence inequalities involving a projected $χ_q$ divergence. We further characterize the minimizers arising in this projection problem through a geometric condition on the relative density. In dimension one, we analyze the geometric consequences of $(q',p')$-Poincaré in

title: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem for certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings
summary: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem concerns global inversion of continuously differentiable mappings between Banach spaces. Here we consider a weaker notion of smoothness and work with continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings. We prove that a continuously Gateaux differentiable mapping with invertible derivatives such that the inverses are uniformly bounded, possesses a continuous right inverse on every compact set. We also provide sufficient conditions for global invertibility of certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings between Banach spaces.

title: $(α,β)$-lineability and spaceability of functions with a unique maximum
summary: Motivated by the classical work of Gurariy and Quarta on linear spaces of continuous functions with a unique point of maximum, we determine the largest possible dimension of such spaces in several settings. For a connected $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary, with $n\ge2$, the largest dimension of a subspace of $\mathcal{C}_0(M)$ whose nonzero elements attain their maximum at exactly one point is $n+1$ if $M$ is homeomorphic to $S^n$, and $n$ otherwise. We also establish the sharp bound $n+1$ in $\mathcal{C}(\mathbb R^n)$ and obtain results on extensions of prescribed finite-dimensional subspaces.

title: The random Riesz's lemma in random normed modules
summary: Riesz's lemma states that a normed space is finite-dimensional if and only if its closed unit ball is sequentially compact. The purpose of this paper is to establish a random counterpart of this lemma in a random normed module. Precisely speaking, based on the two recent developments in random functional analysis: one is the dimensional decomposition of a regular $σ$-stable $L^0$-module, and the other is the theory of random sequential compactness in a random normed module, we can finally establish the random Riesz's lemma, which states that a $σ$-stable random normed module is proper if and only if its random closed unit ball is random sequentially compact.

title: Commutants of diagonal operators
summary: The aim of this paper is devoted to the profound and comprehensive characterization when diagonal operators having the minimal, tiny or double commutant property on a separable Hilbert space, in terms of the topological and geometric properties of their spectra.

title: Bourin's Crossed-Heinz Inequality in the Operator and Frobenius Norms
summary: For positive semidefinite matrices $A, B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $0 < t < 1$, we establish Bourin's crossed-Heinz inequality for every dimension $n \ge 1$ in both the operator norm and the Frobenius norm. In the operator norm, we prove the sharp inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ by normalizing $\|A + B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ to $2$ and decomposing the normalized crossed-Heinz sum into $P_t P_{1-t} + Q$, where $P_t$, $P_{1-t}$, and $Q$ are self-adjoint contractions. In the Frobenius norm, we establish the sharp quantitative inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 + 4t(1-t)\|A - B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2$ via an exact nonnegative remainder decomposition, showing in particular that $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ holds with equality if and only if $A = B$.

title: Approximation numbers of Hankel Operators on Weighted Fock Spaces and the Berger--Coburn Phenomenon
summary: Let $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb{C}^n)$ be a real-valued weight whose real Hessian is uniformly positive definite and bounded. For $0<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and possibly unbounded symbols $f$, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for prescribed decay of the approximation numbers of Hankel operators $H_f$ from weighted Fock spaces $F^p(\varphi)$ to weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^q(\varphi)$ in terms of the non-increasing rearrangement of the IDA function of $f$. We also characterize membership in the approximation ideals $\mathfrak A_s(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ and their weak counterparts $\mathfrak A_{s,\infty}(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ for $0<s<\infty$. The symbol criteria involve Lorentz, Lorentz--Zygmund, and Copson--Lorentz spaces. Our approach also yields the converse to the sufficient condition in [15], thereby completing the characterization of prescribed singular value de

title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
summary: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

title: Banach-Mazur distance and related methods of comparing convex bodies
summary: The Banach-Mazur distance is one of the standard tools used in the study of mathematical objects such as convex bodies or normed spaces, and it becomes indispensable when investigating properties that are invariant under linear isomorphisms. It appears in convex geometry and convex analysis as a way to quantify the approximation of convex bodies. In functional analysis, it plays a basic role in the study of local properties of Banach spaces. The goal of this survey is to present a cohesive picture of these two perspectives. We supply an extensive collection of known results for reference and list open problems of varying difficulty, which could stimulate further research. We include in our discussion several distinct variations on the concept of the Banach-Mazur distance, some of them exploratory, that haven't received much attention to date in the literature. We follow the trend - which

title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
summary: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transpo

title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
summary: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $ρ$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

title: Fourier Algebras of HLS Groupoids: Lifts, Amenability, and Spectrum
summary: We investigate the Fourier algebra of a certain class of groupoids, called the HLS groupoids, within Paterson's continuous framework for locally compact groupoids. We develop the basic harmonic analysis of HLS groupoids by obtaining concrete descriptions of their topology, representations, and Fourier algebra. We then study the restriction maps from the Fourier algebra $A(\mathcal{G})$ of an HLS groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ to the Fourier algebras of its isotropy subgroups, and construct explicit norm-preserving lifts for these restriction maps. As applications, we describe the norm of every element of $A(\mathcal{G})$ in terms of the norms of its restrictions to the isotropy subgroups. We prove an analogue of Leptin's theorem characterizing when $A(\mathcal{G})$ has a bounded approximate identity. We also show that the Gelfand spectrum of $A(\mathcal{G})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathcal{G}$. Fin

title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
summary: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
summary: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(π/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\fracπ{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $π/2$ and $π/4$, respectively.

title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
summary: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

title: Numerical range of finite perturbations of a 2-periodic weighted shift
summary: In this note, we consider a weighted shift operator of weight sequence which is a finite perturbation of a 2-periodic weighted shift. We characterise the equality of the closure of its numerical range and its essential numerical range. We end up with some applications and comments.

title: Analytic Tools and Weighted Composition Operators on Paley--Wiener Spaces
summary: We develop a scale-explicit analytic framework for operator-theoretic problems on the Paley--Wiener spaces $B_σ^p$, $σ>0$, throughout the full range $0<p\leq\infty$. Using localized Paley--Wiener packets, we obtain sharp-order point-evaluation estimates, quantitative separation of distinct point-evaluation functionals, sampling estimates, and Carleson measure characterizations. As a principal application, we develop a comprehensive theory of weighted composition operators $W_{ψ,\varphi}:B_σ^p\to B_τ^q$, $0<p,q\leq\infty$, $σ,τ>0$. Boundedness forces every nonconstant symbol to be affine with real slope. A sharp dichotomy appears: when $p\leq q$, the weight is governed by the residual bandwidth $τ-σ|a|$; when $q<p$, the weight must also supply the missing integrability, with exponent $pq/(p-q)$, and boundedness coincides with compactness. We also obtain compactness criteria and essential-

title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
summary: Let $\mathscr{E}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$ and let $μ$ be a nonnegative finitely additive $σ$-finite measure on the Borel $σ$-algebra of $G$ whose values on $\mathscr{E}$ are finite but unbounded. Applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{μ(B\cap E)}{μ(E)}\right\}_{E\in \mathscr{E}}$ yields a finitely additive measure $\varphi_μ$, which can be viewed as a generalized normalization of $μ$ to total mass one. To obtain a nontrivial necessary condition on $μ$ for the resulting measure $\varphi_μ$ to be invariant, we establish two results of independent interest: we extend the Yosida--Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $σ$-finite measures and prove a theorem previously stated by Bingham and Ostaszewski concerning translates of sets of Haar measure zero. The first theorem yields a decomp
