title: Preserver Problems for Products of Operator Differences
summary: In this paper, we investigate surjective maps $Φ:\mathscr B(H)\to\mathscr B(H)$ preserving various operator quantities associated with products of differences, namely, $$α\big((Φ(A)-Φ(B))Φ(C)\big) =α\big((A-B)C\big) \quad \text{for all}~ A,B,C\in\mathscr B(H),$$ where $α$ denotes one of the following: the numerical radius, maximal numerical range, minimum modulus, surjectivity modulus, reduced minimum modulus, or spectral radius. Under suitable assumptions, we establish structural characterizations of these maps and determine their possible forms.

title: Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality implies superreflexivity
summary: We prove that if \(X\) is a Banach space for which Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality holds, then \(X\) is superreflexive. We also present an example of a superreflexive Banach space for which the vector-valued Stein property fails.

title: Entropy and frame measures for self-affine measures
summary: Let $M$ be a real expanding $d\times d$ matrix and let $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\R^d$ consist of $N\ge2$ distinct vectors. We study the existence of frame measures for the self-affine probability measure $μ$ generated by the maps $S_i(x)=M^{-1}(x+d_i)$ with equal weights $1/N$. Extending the entropy obstruction for self-similar measures with a common scalar contraction, we prove that $μ$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy of the first symbol given the spatial point is positive. In particular, this holds whenever $N>|\det M|$, without assuming absolute continuity or imposing arithmetic conditions. When $M$ has integer entries, $\mathscr D\subset\Z^d$, and $N=|\det M|$, the measure $μ$ admits a frame measure if and only if $μ$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor.

title: Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls
summary: We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic indepen

title: Linear Dynamics of Composition Operators on Zygmund Spaces of Rooted Trees
summary: We conjugate composition operators on the Zygmund and little Zygmund spaces of an infinite, locally finite rooted tree $T$ by the second-difference isometries. A path Green kernel gives row-finite matrices that characterize boundedness and yield exact operator norms. A rigidity result holds on the chain $\mathbb{N}_0$. Boundedness on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equivalent to $\varphi(n)=qn+b$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$. For these symbols, $\varphi(n)>n$ eventually characterizes Li-Yorke chaos of $C_\varphi$ on either Zygmund space, allowing noninjectivity and periodic vertices. If $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\mathcal{Z}_0(T)$ and $\varphi^k(T)$ eventually avoids every finite set, then for each $λ\ne0$, $λC_\varphi$ is Li-Yorke chaotic on either space exactly when the norms of its powers are unbounded. For $\varphi_q(n)=q(n+1)-1$ with

title: Schauder bases and local unconditional structure in Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series
summary: We prove that among the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series with $1\le p<\infty$, only $\mathcal{H}^2$ has local unconditional structure. Consequently, $\mathcal{H}^p$ admits an unconditional basis exactly when $p=2$. At the endpoint $p=1$, we also construct a Schauder basis of Dirichlet polynomials and give an explicit formula for each basis vector. Together, these results answer the basis questions posed by Aleman, Olsen and Saksman, as well as the question of Saksman and Seip concerning an unconditional basis for $\mathcal{H}^1$.

title: Isospectral Density Design and Distinct Global Shape Transitions in Weighted Yukawa Droplets
summary: We study Euclidean perimeter plus Yukawa repulsion with a fixed radial source density and a fixed ordinary volume. For each sufficiently small positive screening parameter, we construct two smooth, positive, strictly increasing densities whose constrained shape Hessians at the unit ball agree for every coupling. Their source masses, Yukawa moments, and ball self-energies also agree. Just above their common first global transition threshold, all minimizers form one rotation orbit of tetrahedral shapes for one density and one orbit of sectoral threefold shapes for the other. Both transitions are continuous, and the minimizing shapes are strictly convex. We obtain the two densities by fixing the boundary data that determine the Hessian and changing the higher derivatives that determine the reduced quartic energy. We compute a positive quartic coefficient, restore the three scalar observable

title: The numerical index with respect to a Lipschitz map
summary: We introduce the Lipschitz numerical range, radius, and index with respect to a norm-one Lipschitz map, unifying the Lipschitz numerical index of a Banach space and the numerical index with respect to an operator. For real-valued maps, we obtain metric formulas on finite metric spaces and graphs. In particular, a connected simple unweighted graph with at least two vertices is bipartite if and only if its real Lipschitz-free space, or equivalently its dual, has classical numerical index one. We also characterize finite metric spaces by universal numerical-radius attainment. Among complete metric spaces, we characterize length spaces by non-denseness of maps attaining their $g$-Lipschitz numerical radius for every norm-one $g$. Moreover, we derive upper bounds for the $g$-Lipschitz numerical index with $\ell_p$ targets, $1<p<\infty$, and lower bounds for the Lipschitz numerical index of sp

title: On König's non-existence conjecture for the one-dimensional fractional Bianchi-Egnell inequality
summary: König conjectured that the sharp stability constant in the Bianchi-Egnell inequality for the one-dimensional fractional Sobolev inequality equals the local stability constant and that the associated quotient has no minimizer outside the set of optimizers of the fractional Sobolev inequality. We prove both assertions for $s<1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, with an explicitly computable threshold. The proof is based on a reinterpretation of the Frank-Lieb rigidity mechanism. Due to the lack of smooth variational structure of the Bianchi-Egnell quotient, we work with a refined limiting inequality of Beckner-Onofri-type on the circle with vanishing first-order moments, which we derive from Toeplitz determinants.

title: Higher-Order Isometric Liftings of Convex and Concave Operators
summary: We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
summary: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$λ:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

title: Isometries for Hilbert's metric on vector lattices of continuous functions
summary: In this paper Hilbert's projective metric on the interior of the positive cone of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong order unit is studied. We show that every surjective isometry between two such projective cones is induced by a lattice isomorphism, possibly composed with the inversion map, and that the inversion occurs precisely when the vector lattice is a bounded inverse closed $f$-algebra. In particular, two such projective cones are isometric if and only if the underlying vector lattices are lattice isomorphic, and we determine the corresponding isometry groups. We apply these results to spaces of Hölder continuous functions, absolutely continuous functions, and continuous functions of bounded variation, for which we describe the surjective isometries explicitly. Finally, we show that the projective cones of these spaces of functions on an interval all have the same metric

title: Dynamical frames through Sz.$-$Nagy$-$Foias dilations
summary: We present a unified operator-theoretic treatment of dynamical frames based on defect operators, Stein equations, and the Sz.-Nagy-Foiaş dilation theory of contractions. An explicit realization of the minimal isometric dilation relates generating vectors to the wandering subspace and provides a geometric interpretation of standard frame constructions. For Parseval dynamical frames, polar decomposition yields a complete factorization of the generating families through the adjoint defect operator. General dynamical frames are described in terms of positive solutions of a Stein equation, leading to an equivalent formulation of the frame index. We also collect characteristic-function criteria for strong stability and joint strong stability. In the diagonal case, the characteristic function expresses the classical separation and Carleson conditions in operator-theoretic terms. The emphasis is

title: Stochastic Multivariate Taylor Measure Functions
summary: We introduce stochastic multivariate Taylor measure functions (SMTMFs), which extend the multivariate Taylor measure function framework through random Taylor coefficients and a possibly random Taylor parameter. We establish their measurability properties and derive sufficient conditions for the associated processes to be martingales, including criteria based on conditional covariance and continuous semimartingale decompositions. We construct standard Brownian motion as an almost surely uniformly convergent limit of finite SMTMFs using the Levy-Ciesielski representation. We also show that the completion of the finite stochastic MTMF space under the expected uniform norm contains Brownian motion, Brownian bridges, fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with integrable initial conditions. title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
summary: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;Λ^k\right)$, where $Λ^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
summary: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

title: Schatten isometries of Grassmann spaces
summary: We characterize all (not necessarily surjective) Schatten $p$-isometries of the Grassmann space of rank $k$ projections on a complex Hilbert space for every $p\in(0,\infty]$. We prove that every such isometry is induced by a linear or conjugate-linear isometry of the underlying Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with the additional possibility of composition with orthocomplementation when $\dim \mathcal H = 2k > 2$. Our result generalizes Wigner's theorem, which plays a central role in the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. It also extends previous results on Schatten $p$-isometries of Grassmann spaces, including characterizations of surjective isometries by Gehér and Šemrl for $p=\infty$ and by Qian et al. for $0<p<\infty$ and that of not necessarily surjective isometries by Gehér for $p=2$.

title: A remark on the entropy numbers of mixed smoothness classes
summary: We find the right orders of both the entropy numbers and the Kolmogorov widths of classes of multivariate functions with bounded mixed derivative, when the class is defined by the restriction in the uniform norm and the error of approximation is measured in the uniform norm. The case of functions of two variables was settled about 30 years ago and the case of three or more variables stayed open.

title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
summary: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, wi

title: Invariance of Arens module actions on the norm dual of a Riesz-normed f-algebra
summary: Let $A$ be an f-algebra and let $V$ be an order ideal of its order dual $A^{\sim}$ that separates the points of $A$. In a comment accompanying a theorem of Huijsmans and de Pagter (J. Funct. Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to b

title: Conic Frames, Cosine Measure, and Gaussian Frames
summary: Conic combinations play an important role across mathematics in areas such as optimization, non-negative matrix factorization, and sparse coding. Frames which span their underlying space using only conic combinations, known as positive spanning sets or conic frames, are of special interest in derivative free optimization. In particular, sets with large cosine measure, a measure of how spread out the vectors are, are favored. We focus on the asymptotics of the cosine measure of Gaussian frames and present tail bounds in a variety of regimes.

title: Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
summary: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
summary: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
summary: We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $ν$-Schur functions. In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $ν$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual an

title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
summary: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
summary: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation

title: On Block-Primitive Combinatorial Designs
summary: We settle a long-standing problem by proving that every block-primitive combinatorial design is point-primitive. Since block-primitivity and point-primitivity coincide for symmetric designs by duality, it remains to treat the non-symmetric $2$-designs. For these we apply the O'Nan--Scott theorems for primitive and for quasiprimitive permutation groups and prove that the automorphism group of every such design is almost simple on points and on blocks. Together with the classification of finite simple groups, this classifies all non-symmetric block-primitive $2$-designs except for two families of block stabilizers in even characteristic. The exceptions are as follows. One family is of subfield type, $PSL_2(q_0)$ with $q=q_0^{d}$, $d\geq2$, of order below the dihedral point stabilizer $D_{2(q\pm1)}$, and includes $S_3\cong PSL_2(2)$ and $A_5\cong PSL_2(4)$. title: On complemented skew braces
summary: We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

title: Half-factorial generating sets and the realization of Dedekind class groups
summary: We prove a cardinality obstruction to realizing an abelian group as the ideal class group of a half-factorial Dedekind domain. If an abelian $p$-group $P$ satisfies $\bigcap_{r\ge1}p^rP=0$ and admits a half-factorial generating subset, then $|P|\le\max\{\aleph_0,|P/pP|\}$. The proof separates generators of equal order by finite quotients. Its group-theoretic ingredient is a direct summand generated by selected members of an arbitrary finite generating set. The torsion subgroup of $\prod_{j\ge1}\mathbb{Z}/p^j\mathbb{Z}$ is uncountable and $p$-adically separated, but has countable quotient modulo $p$; hence it has no half-factorial generating subset. This gives a negative answer to the universal half-factorial Dedekind realization problem for every prime. Pure subgroups give counterexamples of every uncountable cardinality at most the continuum, so the least cardinality of a counterexample

title: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
summary: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most c

title: On four problems from the Kourovka Notebook: spectra, periodic automorphism groups, commutators, and operator simplicity
summary: We examine Problems 18.62(a), 18.63, 18.65, and 20.120 of the Kourovka Notebook. First, a family of semidirect products involving $\operatorname{PSL}_2(p^2)$ gives arbitrarily many pairwise nonisomorphic groups critical with respect to one simple-group spectrum, subject to explicit arithmetic congruences. Second, a completed-algebra construction using sparse torsion identities and a matrix Golod-Shafarevich-Vinberg inequality produces an infinite periodic group generated by two fixed-point-free automorphisms of order five of an abelian group. Third, we give a short matrix proof that the class of elements of order three in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ contradicts the assertion in Problem 18.65 as written. Finally, we spell out how P. Hall's 1962 wreath-power theorems answer Problem 20.120 under the usual normal-subgroup meaning of simplicity for a group with one distinguished automorphism. T

title: Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
summary: We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$. In particular, we obtain an instance of the virtual structure problem of Kleinert and answer the rational isomorphism problem for such groups.

title: Products of Trees, $Σ$-theory, Higher Baumslag-Solitar Groups
summary: We study the $Σ$-theory of groups equipped with multiple HNN decompositions in the case where the product of the associated Bass-Serre trees satisfies the hypotheses of Brown's criterion. We then obtain an explicit description of the $Σ$-theory restricted to the span of all characters dual to one of the HNN decompositions. One consequence is that Meinert's Direct Product Formula holds in this context. As a key ingredient for the proof, we present a purely topological result that allows reading off the essential connectedness and acyclicity properties of products of regular trees with height functions. As the main application of our theorem, we introduce higher Baumslag-Solitar groups. We prove that they admit a canonical system of HNN decompositions, and use it to deduce multiple results, such as the existence of normal forms, and a well-behaved structure of standard parabolic subgroups

title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
summary: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $χ\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(χ_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $χ(1)_p$ of $χ(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $χ$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2πi/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $χ_P$ is the restriction of $χ$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(χ_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $χ_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
summary: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.

title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
summary: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.

title: CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes, Bipodality and the Parallel Wall Property
summary: Coxeter cell complexes are a simultaneous generalization to cube complexes and the Davis complex of a Coxeter group. We show that 1-skeleta of CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes isometrically embed into a CAT(0) cube complex. When the resulting cube complex is finite dimensional, we show that the condition of bipodality (satisfied by both CAT(0) cube complexes and Davis complexes of Coxeter groups) implies local finiteness of the cubulation. To this end, we show a Parallel Wall Theorem for bipodal CAT(0) Coxeter cell complexes satisfying a uniform bound on the size of a collection of pairwise intersecting walls. In particular, our methods give a new, purely geometric proof of the Parallel Wall Theorem for Coxeter groups.

title: Hierarchical hyperbolicity of Coxeter groups
summary: We show that for every finite rank Coxeter system, the Coxeter group is hierarchically hyperbolic relative to its nonhyperoctahedral irreducible higher rank affine parabolic subgroups. This is sharp---the Coxeter group admits a hierarchically hyperbolic group structure if and only if it has no such parabolic subgroups, and we give a complete diagrammatic characterization of when this is true. Moreover, this condition is equivalent to the existence of a coarsely equivariant coarse median on the Coxeter group. We also show that the Coxeter group is virtually a colorable hierarchically hyperbolic group. This is achieved by passing to a congruence subgroup of the Tits representation. As consequences, the Davis complex is a hierarchically hyperbolic space and the group admits a coarse median of rank equal to its algebraic rank. Furthermore, the Coxeter group is quasimedian quasiisometric to a

title: $C^*$-selflessness for free Burnside groups
summary: The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.

title: Quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces via Sierpiński spaces
summary: We study quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces using Sierpiński spaces. We introduce K3 surfaces of Sierpiński type and prove that their limit sets are round Sierpiński spaces. For such K3 surfaces, the quasi-isometry class of the automorphism group is equivalent to the rational isometry class of the Néron--Severi lattice together with its integral roots. As an application of this rigidity, we construct infinitely many quasi-isometry classes of hyperbolic automorphism groups in Picard rank 4. This reveals a new phenomenon in Picard rank 4, sharply contrasting with the finiteness of quasi-isometry classes in Picard ranks at most 3 and at least 6.

title: Mathematical foundations for symmetric programming and reasoning
summary: We develop a mathematical abstraction for uniformly exploiting symmetries in programming and reasoning based on the mathematical proof principle `without-loss-of-generality' (w.l.o.g.). Given: group actions that describe symmetries of the input and the output; and a canoniser, which captures how arbitrary inputs get sent to canonical ones, our construction extends any function from the canonical inputs to the whole domain. We characterise the conditions on the canonisers which guarantee that the construction gives the unique equivariant (i.e. symmetry-preserving) extension. Furthermore, we adapt the construction to a dependently-typed setting, where it captures traditional symmetric w.l.o.g. arguments via the Curry-Howard correspondence. Finally, we extend the construction to algebraic data types, where the symmetries of the constructors both uniquely determine the symmetries of the data

title: The structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups of the real projective plane
summary: In this paper we study the structure of the finite subgroups of the braid groups $B_n(RP^2)$ of the real projective plane $RP^2$. It is known that the isomorphism classes of these subgroups are comprised of cyclic, dicyclic and binary polyhedral groups. Using specific elements of $B_n(RP^2)$, we construct embeddings of the cyclic and dicyclic subgroups, we show that there is a single conjugacy class of the maximal dicyclic groups, and for small values of n, we also construct embeddings of the bin- ary tetrahedral and octahedral groups. One interesting phenomenon that occurs is the existence of isomorphism classes of finite subgroups that admit embeddings in $B_n(RP^2)$ as both maximal finite and non-maximal subgroups. Up to conjugacy, we describe completely the lattice of the finite subgroups of $B_n(RP^2)$ for n = 3, 4, 5. Some of our results regarding the number of conjugacy classes of

title: Rohrbach's Conjecture for Finite Groups
summary: Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $α_1,\ldots,α_h$ with $α_1+\cdots+α_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{α_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{α_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]

title: A new proof of nonamenability for free Burnside groups of odd exponent
summary: We prove that the free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is nonamenable for every $m\ge 2$ and every odd exponent $n\ge 557$. This improves Adian's bound $n\ge 665$ and matches the infiniteness bound of Atkarskaya, Rips and Tent. Our proof combines their canonical form construction with a counting argument to obtain an explicit isoperimetric inequality.

title: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
summary: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$

title: The spectrum of free projective geometries over finite chain rings
summary: Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime ideal of residue order $q$, and $\mathcal{O}_r=\mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{p}^r$ which is a finite chain ring; the motivating example is $\mathbb{Z}/p^r$. The free projective geometry $\mathbb{P}^{d-1}_{fr}(\mathcal{O}_r)$ is the graph whose vertices are the nontrivial free submodules of $\mathcal{O}_r^{d}$, two of them adjacent when one strictly contains the other. For every $d$, $q$ and $r$ we reduce its adjacency matrix to explicit symmetric matrices (blocks) of size at most $d-1$. There is one block for each signature (a partition with at most $d/2$ parts, each at most $r$) and we show that every block, at every depth, is a single universal matrix $L(s,σ)$ evaluated at the number $s$ of parts of the signature $λ$ and at $σ=2rs-|λ|$. The same blocks give the spectrum of the subgraph induced on any set of levels, and for two leve

title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
summary: Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$. Our theorem supplies a key ingredient in forthcoming work of Ben Yaacov--Dikstein--Liu, which obtains local tests for sparse algebraic codes with guarantees even at arbitrarily small acceptance probability. These tests use $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and guarantee that any word accepted with probability at least $\varepsilon$ agrees

title: On the reduction of GAP Conjecture to certain classes of groups and around
summary: In this note we revise our approach from [Rostislav Grigorchuk. On the gap conjecture concerning group growth. Bull. Math. Sci., 4(1):113--128, 2014] to the reduction of the Gap Conjecture on Group Growth to the class of just-infinite groups. For this purpose we introduce the class of groups that we call \emph{(GAPSY)} as well as some other classes. The properties of these classes are discussed in the relation with growth, elementary amenability, and just-infiniteness. Additionally, we discuss the GAP type problems for cancellative semigroups. A number of (old and new) open problems and few historical remarks is included in the note as well.

title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
summary: Let $G=F\rtimes_φ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $φ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece.

title: Finiteness properties of Bestvina-Brady kernels for graph products with torsion
summary: We study Bestvina-Brady kernels associated to graph products whose vertex groups are either infinite cyclic or finite. Using a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ cubical complex constructed by Ruane and Witzel, on which the graph product with defining graph $Γ$ acts, together with an equivariant Morse function, we establish sufficient conditions for homological finiteness properties in terms of the topology of the flag complex $Γ^\blacktriangle$, the subcomplex $Γ^\blacktriangle_\infty$ spanned by the infinite vertices, and the ascending and descending links of certain vertices. We also prove a partial converse, showing that, under additional vanishing hypotheses on homology in the next degree, non-vanishing homology of these complexes obstructs higher finiteness properties of the Bestvina-Brady kernel. The main new features are the presence of finite stabilizers and the resulting additional link conditi

title: Second homology of some quandles
summary: We derive formulas from Eisemann's formula for the second quandle homology of quandles. We prove that for a finite injective quandle $Q$, the second quandle homology $H_2(Q)$ can be computed in a representation group of $Q$, which is a finite quotient of the enveloping group of $Q$, by giving a formula for that. We use this to compute $H_2(Q)$ for $Q$ the subquandle of $k$-cycles of $S_n$ and $Q$ the quandle corresponding to the conjugacy class of a diagonalizable element of $SL(n,q)$, with some exceptions. For $G$ a finite group with trivial Bogomolov multiplier, as many classical groups, simple groups and (with exceptions) quasi-simple groups, we derive a formula for $H_2(Conj(G))$ that can be computed in $G$ alone. The formula relies on conjugacy classes of $G$, centralizers in $G$ of representative of such classes and the derived group of $G$. If $G$ is moreover perfect this formula

title: Coset Geometries and Tameness of Certain Classes of Shephard Groups
summary: For the class of Shepard groups (which contain Coxeter groups, Artin-Tits groups, and many finite complex reflection groups), we investigate the structure of the coset incidence systems defined using the standard parabolic subgroups. For the class of tame Shephard groups, which is when all the standard parabolic subgroups are equal to the corresponding Shephard groups, then the intersection of standard parabolic subgroups is also a standard parabolic subgroup. We show that when the Shephard group is either finite, right-angled, or rank two, then it is tame; this is further evidence that all Shephard groups are tame. Finally, we mix the Burau and the geometric representations to produce a representation for all Shephard groups, but we show it is not faithful in rank two unless the Shephard group is finite or an Artin-Tits group.

title: On the orders of irreducible subgroups of finite classical groups
summary: Let $G$ be a finite almost simple classical group over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with socle $G_0$ and natural module $V$ of dimension $n$. Let $H$ be a core-free maximal subgroup of $G$. By a well-known theorem of Aschbacher, either $H$ is contained in one of eight subgroup collections that are defined in terms of the geometry of $V$, or $H$ is almost simple and the embedding of $H$ in $G$ arises from an absolutely irreducible representation of a covering group of the socle of $H$. We write $\mathcal{S}$ for the latter collection of irreducibly embedded almost simple subgroups. Determining the subgroups in $\mathcal{S}$ is an intractable problem, in general, which has only been fully resolved in low dimensions. However, many applications require some control on the subgroups in $\mathcal{S}$, expressed in terms of their order, or properties of their elements, for example. Extending a theorem of Lie

title: $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$
summary: We classify all controlled $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$ up to Morita equivalence. This provides a proof of Donovan's Conjecture for resistant $2$-generated $2$-groups.

title: Growth function of the cactus groups
summary: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.

title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
summary: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

title: Abelian covers and the index of the centre in a group
summary: Let $h(n)$ be the largest number of abelian subgroups needed to cover a group in which every set of more than $n$ elements contains two distinct elements that commute, and let $ζ(n)$ be the largest index of the centre under the same constraint. Erdős asked for the growth of $h$, Neumann proved that both quantities are finite, and Pyber bounded both $ζ$ and $h$ exponentially. We determine $h(n)$ for every positive integer $n$ and prove that $h(n)=1+\sqrt{ζ(n)}$ whenever the constraint admits a nonabelian group. The covers are built directly from the commutator geometry of a scalar quotient, and the comparison with $ζ$ is made afterwards. Beyond finitely many small cases, both maxima are attained by the same groups, those isoclinic to an extraspecial $2$-group of order $2^{1+2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}$, confirming Pyber's prediction for the central index in this range.

title: Positivity in symplectic groups and electrical networks
summary: We study the relation between electrical positivity introduced by Lam and Pylyavskyy $[9]$ and total positivity of symplectic matrices arising from circular planar electrical networks. A particularly convenient framework for our purpose is provided by a construction of an embedding of electrical network into the positive Lagrangian Grassmannian, see Section $1.1$. Employing this technique, we demonstrate that mentioned below two types of positivity do not coincide, see Theorem $2.2$. In Section $3$ we also derive explicit rational formulas recovering the parameters of the factorization from our symplectic matrix entries and minors, and prove uniqueness under explicit nonvanishing conditions.

title: A regular free action on the integral plane and a problem on left braces
summary: We construct a free subgroup of countably infinite rank in $\ZZ^2\rtimes\SL_2(\ZZ)$ that acts regularly on $\ZZ^2$. At each stage we adjoin an affine transformation taking the origin to the least point of a prescribed orbit. Disjoint domains for reduced words ensure that the stabilizer of the origin remains trivial. The orbit map gives a left brace with additive group $\ZZ^2$ and multiplicative group free of countably infinite rank. This group contains a nonabelian free subgroup and is therefore nonsolvable, answering both parts of Problem 20.126 of the Kourovka Notebook.

title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
summary: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values. The combinatorics of the polynomials are noncrossing partitions of type $B_d$. This give us a piecewise Euclidean cell structure built using the order complex of the noncrossing partition of type $B_d$. Along the way, we also give a compactification of this space of polynomials.

title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups
summary: We study progression-free sets in arbitrary finite groups. We transfer sharp upper bounds from abelian groups to nilpotent groups of class $2$, and from nilpotent groups to arbitrary groups. Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author's theorem on large subgroups of class $2$ gives \[ r_3(G) \, \leq \, C \, |G|\exp\left( -c\frac{(\log|G|)^{1/6}}{(\log\log|G|)^{1/3}}\right) \] for every finite group as $|G|\to\infty$. This improves the estimates obtained by using the abelian subgroup supplied by Pyber's theorem.

title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
summary: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.

title: A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups
summary: We characterize almost symmetric numerical semigroups in terms of their associated Young diagrams, showing that almost symmetry is equivalent to a simple numerical identity relating the genus, the type, and the number of small elements, and also to a combinatorial condition on the hook lengths of the diagram. We then introduce a symmetrization procedure that associates with each almost symmetric numerical semigroup a symmetric numerical set. This yields a map from the set of almost symmetric numerical semigroups to the set of symmetric numerical sets. We also present experimental data on the image of this map and on the proportion of its elements that are numerical semigroups. The results show, in particular, that the map is far from injective and that its image contains many numerical sets that are not semigroups.

title: Coxeter cubes on the graph associahedron and separable elements
summary: A Coxeter cube is a Boolean lattice inside a finite Coxeter group $W$ such that every square is a Coxeter square in the sense of Dyer and Wang. A Coxeter cube of full dimension based at the identity, which we call a based cube, is the same as a partition of the positive roots into inversion sets with one simple root in each block. These partitions were studied by Dimitrov, Gigliotti, Ossip, Paquette and Wehlau under the name of fine decompositions, and by Hohlweg and Pons as partitions of $w_0$. We show that the based cubes of $W$ form a point configuration in the graph associahedron $K(Γ)$ of the Coxeter diagram $Γ$ of $W$. The vertices of $K(Γ)$ are the based cubes whose blocks are parabolic. Every other based cube lies in the interior of an edge or of a cubical face, and we count the based cubes on each edge using the Coxeter arrangement. We also characterize the elements of $W$ that

title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
summary: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable. We extend the construction to the $p$-Basilica groups and, using polynomial activity, to the long-range group, whose derived subgroup we prove to be finitely generated. Under an additional hypothesis on finite quotients, we determine the closure of the product. Membership in the constructed product is decidable in the first Grigorchuk group.

title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
summary: We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof. Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics. We use this to establish an integral representation theorem for positive spherical functions in complete generality, extending the Harish-Chandra representation. A similar representation theorem is given for positive harmonic functions.

title: Automorphisms of the Reduced Finitary Power Monoid of $\N^d$
summary: Given an additive semigroup $S$, the collection of its nonempty finite subsets can be equipped with the setwise addition \[ X + Y = \{x + y : x \in X, \; y \in Y\}, \] forming a semigroup denoted by $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(S)$, which is called the finitary power semigroup of $S$. If $S$ is a monoid with identity $0$, the finite nonempty subsets containing $0$ form a submonoid $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(S)$, known as the reduced finitary power monoid, whose identity element is the singleton $\{0\}$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, $\mathbb{N}$ the set of nonnegative integers, and $\mathbb{N}^d = \{(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_d) \mid a_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$. For the one-dimensional case \(d=1\), Tringali and Yan (\textit{J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A}, \textbf{209} (2025)) established that the only nontrivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N})$ is the involution $X \mapsto \ma

title: An additively idempotent semiring of least order generating a limit variety
summary: We construct an additively idempotent semiring of order five that generates a limit variety and is not strongly nonfinitely based. The generated variety has exactly two maximal proper subvarieties, both hereditarily finitely based. We also prove that no ai-semiring of order at most four generates a limit variety. Consequently, five is the least possible order of a finite ai-semiring generating a limit variety.

title: A congruence-group counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7
summary: For every prime $p>24$, let $H$ be the kernel of $\SL_2(\Z/p^9\Z)\to\SL_2(\F_p)$. We prove that $H$ is not IYB, whereas $H\times C_{p^8}$ is IYB. The proof excludes a pre-Lie multiplication on the rank-three Lie ring with bracket $p[x,y]$ over $\Z/p^8\Z$ using three trace identities. It follows that the supersoluble group $H\times(C_{p^8}\rtimes C_2)$, with the involution acting by inversion, has IYB Sylow subgroups and is not IYB. Its nilpotent residual is cyclic and its Sylow $p$-subgroup has nilpotency class eight. For $p=31$, an action of order three gives a supersoluble counterexample of odd order $3\cdot31^{32}$. The same construction gives an IYB $p$-group with a specified central cyclic direct factor such that the quotient of the whole group by the unique subgroup of order $p$ in that factor is non-IYB.

title: On Lévy type subgroups of the symmetric group of $ω$ associated with simple density functions
summary: The Lévy group, introduced by Lévy in (Lévy (1951)), is defined by \[\mathcal{L} = \left\{σ\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : σ(k)\notin n\}|}{n} = 0\right\},\] where $aut$ denotes the group of all permutations of $ω$. This group happens to be closely connected with the notion of asymptotic density as it consists of permutations that map sets with an asymptotic density back to sets with the same density. Our aim is to replicate the construction by replacing $n$ in the denominator by $g(n)$ for a function $g:ω\to [0,\infty)$ with $g(n)\to \infty$ (weight), which leads us a class of Lévy type groups. Specifically we define simple Lévy group with weight $g$ as \[\mathcal{L}_g = \left\{σ\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : σ(k)\notin n\}|}{g(n)} = 0\right\}.\] As a natural consequence we first study its relationship with the notion of simple density functions (which had been introduced in \cit

title: On Distinct Powers in Finite Groups
summary: Sun conjectured that if a group $G$ has no elements of orders $2,3,...,n+1$, then every $n$-element subset $A$ can be ordered as $a_1,...,a_n$ so that $a_1,a_2^2,...,a_n^n$ are pairwise distinct. We prove the conjecture for finite groups when $n=4,5,6$. The proofs combine collision-counting arguments with reductions to finite-field assignment problems; the remaining finite cases for $n=6$ are verified exhaustively. We also prove the conjecture for every $n$ when no four elements of $A$ generate the same cyclic subgroup.

title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
summary: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large pri

title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
summary: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.

title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem
summary: Jones showed that Thompson's group $F$ produces all unoriented links, and introduced its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}$, which produces all oriented links; the same holds for the Brown-Thompson group $F_3$ and its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}_3$. The corresponding Thompson indices measure the complexity of a knot in these groups, much as the braid index does for braid groups. In this article we prove that the span of the Jones polynomial plus $1$ is a lower bound for the $F$- and $\vec{F}$-index, and we give lower bounds for the $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index in terms of the degrees of the HOMFLY-PT polynomial. We then compute the four indices (the $F$-, $F_3$-, $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index) for the prime knots with at most 13 crossings, by an exhaustive enumeration of tree diagrams (up to 13 leaves for $F$, 17 for $\vec{F}$, with the HOMFLY-PT polynomials of all the diagrams with 19 le

title: Smooth actions of Baumslag-Solitar groups on the interval
summary: We study representations of the Baumslag-Solitar group $BS(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid ab^ma^{-1}=b^n\rangle$ inside the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the interval $[0,1]$. We prove that for integers $n,m\in \mathbb Z\setminus\{-1,0,1\}$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds into $\mathrm{Diff}_+^1([0,1])$ if and only if $|n|=|m|$. Furthermore, we show that for any $α\in (0,1)$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds inside $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+α}([0,1])$ if and only if $1=|m|=|n|$ or when $1=m\leq n$.

title: Profinite groups with finite conjugacy classes of commutators
summary: It was shown in a recent work by Senise and Shumyatsky that if $G$ is a finite group such that $|x^G|\leq m$ whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, then $G''$ has $m$-bounded order. In this paper, we examine the following question: given a profinite group $G$ such that $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, does it follow that $G''$ is finite? We show that, in general, the answer to this is negative. The main result obtained in this paper is the following theorem: Let $G$ be a profinite group in which $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order. Assume that $π(G)$ is finite. Then: (1) The second commutator subgroup $G''$ is finite; (2) $G$ has an open normal subgroup of nilpotency class at most $3$.

title: Strong pseudo Frobenius numbers
summary: By Sylow's theorem, the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, but not every such integer occurs. Frobenius extended the congruence to the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ for every $a\ge0$. Kulakoff and Hall showed that this number is congruent to $1$ or $1+p$ modulo $p^2$ whenever $p^{a+1}$ divides the group order. A positive integer is a Frobenius $p$-number if it is the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ of some finite group for some $a$. There are integers congruent to $1$ modulo $p^2$ which are not Frobenius $p$-numbers, and it remained open whether there are also such integers congruent to $1+p$ modulo $p^2$. We show that no finite group has exactly $106$ subgroups of order $5^a$ for any $a\ge0$.

title: Lie algebras graded by the root system $AG_2$
summary: We study Lie algebras graded by the generalized root system $AG_2$, which is obtained from $G_2$ by adjoining the doubles of its short roots, over fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. We show that every such Lie algebra with a grading subalgebra of type $A_2$ is, modulo its center, the Tits-Kantor-Koecher Lie algebra of a structurable algebra equipped with an idempotent $t$ satisfying $t+\overline{t}=1$. Conversely, every structurable algebra with such an idempotent gives rise to an $(AG_2,A_2)$-graded Lie algebra. We describe the corresponding Peirce decomposition and characterize the additional algebraic structure required for an $(AG_2,G_2)$-grading. Using the classification of central simple structurable algebras, we determine the central simple examples when the characteristic is also different from $5$. Finally, we compare our constructions with the theory of Tits h

title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
summary: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, an

title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
summary: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.

title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
summary: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $Γ$ and $Λ$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $Γ$ to $Λ$ to a homo-morphism between

title: Extreme amenability and failure of the Lévy property for the trace-class special unitary group
summary: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a Lévy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the Lévy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.

title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
summary: The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$. In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $γ_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$. Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite

title: Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent
summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.

title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
summary: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

title: Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two
summary: We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group. The simplified graph and all its vertex-induced subgraphs have optimal thin-triangle constant zero for tree components and 3/4 otherwise. Every whole orbit component of the original graph has thin-triangle constant at most 2, while every component of every vertex-induced subgraph has constant at most 5/2. Both bounds are sharp in the primitive orbit and apply to the full geometric realization, including edge-interior triangle corners. The hereditary upper estimate also fol

title: Finite soluble groups with Sylow subgroups of class at most two are IYB-groups
summary: We prove that every finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups have nilpotency class at most two is an involutive Yang--Baxter group ($\IYB$-group). This answers a question of Cedó and Okniński \cite{CedoOkninski2025}. The main method of the $\IYB$-structures has been reflected in \cite{MengBallesterJimenez2026}.

title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
summary: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $Ω$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/μ_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/μ_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisi

title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
summary: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
summary: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact Kähler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely

title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
summary: By a $\textit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $ν$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $ν(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $ν(x)=\bot$, where $\bot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{\bot,\top\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of th

title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
summary: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2

title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
summary: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,ξ)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for plan
