title: Decorrelation Before Variable Selection: Left and Right Transforms and Their Trade-Off
summary: Decorrelation has two forms. A left transform keeps coefficients and changes noise; a right transform keeps noise and changes coefficients. Cholesky whitening alone keeps noise variables inactive when true ones come first; decorrelation preserving coefficients and noise loses information.

title: High-dimensional transfer learning with unaligned ordinal responses
summary: In this work, we study high-dimensional transfer learning with unaligned ordinal responses, allowing different domain-specific regression coefficients, cumulative links and thresholds. We develop the sample-split and full-target algorithms that pool source and target likelihoods and then estimate a target correction. Under suitable conditions, our algorithms achieve minimax-optimal rates for parameter estimation and excess risk. Simulations favor the full-target algorithm over the sample-split algorithm for finite-sample estimation and prediction. An application to a medical dataset further demonstrates the predictive gains of our full-target algorithm over the target-only and pooled baselines when transferring information from the five-category source data to binary hospital mortality.

title: The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
summary: We study vector-valued regression with predictors filling a tube around an unknown $m$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal{M}$ in $\mathbb{R}^D$. In the Manifold-Index Model, the mean response is $F=f\circΠ_{\mathcal{M}}$, where $Π_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the nearest-point projection onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $f:\mathcal{M}\to\mathbb{R}^p$ is a possibly non-injective link function. Multiscale ANisotropic lOcal Regression (MANOR) estimates tangent planes by multiscale PCA of predictors with similar responses, then refines them by pooling outer products of local slopes. The neighborhoods narrow tangentially while retaining complete normal fibers. We assume a Lipschitz link differential and bounded response noise. For $p\ge m$, under our geometric and sampling conditions, $n$ independent observations give mean tangent-space error of order $n^{-2/(m+4)}$ and integrated squared prediction error at the $m$-

title: Phase Transitions in Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation under $\ell_p$ Norms
summary: We study the problem of estimating the mean of a random vector in $\mathbb R^d$ under $\ell_p$ norms, assuming only the existence of a covariance matrix. In the Euclidean norm, the sample mean is already optimal in expectation, and robust estimators are usually needed only to obtain high-probability tails. Our results show that this picture changes for $\ell_p$ norms with $p>2$: robustification is already necessary even for the expected risk. We prove that the minimax risk exhibits a sharp phase transition, controlled by the interaction between the sample size $n$, the dimension $d$, and the norm parameter $p$. In the large-sample regime, the classical Gaussian rate remains achievable. In the complementary regime, heavy-tailed distributions create a genuinely non-Gaussian obstruction. Furthermore we show that the simple estimator: coordinate-wise median of means whose number of buckets c

title: Causality and order restricted inference in the Aalen additive hasard model
summary: We study a graphical model (DAG) with time to event as a response variable. We use the Aalen additive hazard model for modelling the effect on the response variable of covariates, combined with a multiple linear regression for earlier layers in a DAG. This enables modelling covariates affecting the event process both directly and indirectly. The indirect component effect is represented by a product $θ_1(t)β_2(t)$, where $θ_1(t)$ describes the effect of the independent covariate on the dependent covariate and $β_2(t)$ is the effect of the dependent covariate on the final time to response variable, in the additive hazard model. We estimate $β_2(t)$ by the order-restricted estimator recently introduced in Anevski and Merai (arXiv:2606.23882v2), thereby enabling disease models with early onset or late onset covariate effects. Combining our previously obtained results with the DAG allows for

title: Honest confidence sets under experiment-level failure
summary: An experiment-level failure replaces the joint observation law while preserving the target. We study honest confidence sets when a declared upper bound on failure probability equals the allowed noncoverage probability. For a Uniform support endpoint and a Gaussian mean on fixed compact parameter intervals, every honest deterministic procedure has full-range worst-case expected diameter under arbitrary or absolutely continuous joint failures. Independent randomisation gives sharp minimax risks of $(2+o(1))\log N/N$ for the endpoint in $[1,2]$ and $(2σ+o(1))(\log N/N)^{1/2}$ for the mean with known variance $σ^2$. A failure distribution shared by many targets forces average clean-state noncoverage to decrease with expected diameter. One-sided local Kullback--Leibler bounds then yield lower bounds with logarithmic factors. The endpoint experiment also has a sharp deterministic frontier as t

title: Weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift: process limits, estimated weights and efficiency
summary: Weighted split conformal prediction handles covariate shift by reweighting calibration scores with the likelihood ratio $v=dQ_X/dP_X$; its training-conditional coverage is a functional of the self-normalized weighted empirical distribution function $\hat F_m$, and we study the process $\sqrt m(\hat F_m-F_Q)$. It converges in $\ell^\infty$ to the Gaussian process $W(G(t))-F_Q(t)W(K^2)$, with $G(t)=\mathbb{E}_Q[v\mathbf{1}\{S\le t\}]$ and $K^2=1+χ^2(Q\|P)$, if and only if $χ^2(Q\|P)<\infty$ (for non-degenerate scores); $\sup v$ plays no role. The limit gives the joint law of the coverage across levels, consistent bootstraps, inflations asymptotically exact uniformly in the level, and Berry-Esseen-type rates. With estimated ratios, a uniform expansion remains valid when the estimate uses the calibration covariates; the estimation error enters through a covariance term that can reduce the va

title: Dependence measures as spectral risk measures
summary: For a bivariate copula $C$ with $(U,V)\sim C$, the conditional distribution functions $L_t=\partial_1C(U,t)$ are random variables with means $t$, so that measures of directed dependence become risk functionals. The absolute Lorenz curves of the variables $L_t$ form the rearranged copula $C^\uparrow$. In this picture Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ is a squared Sobolev seminorm and the rearranged Spearman correlation an $L^1$ norm of $C^\uparrow-Π$, and both arise from one spectral risk measure, applied either to the conditional laws of $V$ or to the laws of $L_t$. The resulting classes $ω_φ$ and $κ_φ$ of spectral dependence measures have mirror-image axiomatic properties. For every spectrum we determine the exact upper bound of $κ_φ$ in terms of $ξ$, and we prove sharp inequalities between $ξ$, $κ_φ$ and the values of $C^\uparrow$, which show how little global measures say about the ta

title: Two approaches of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift
summary: We investigate the problem of estimation for a tempered fractional Brownian motion with drift of the form: $X_t=μt + σB_{H,λ}(t)$, for all $t\geq 0$. Based on discrete observations of $X$ and by using the method of moments with the ergodic theorem, we construct estimators of the drift parameter $μ\in\R$ and noise parameters $ σ^2,H,λ\in(0,\infty)$. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators, including convergence in probability, almost sure convergence, and asymptotic normality. Finally, by using Gladyshev's results \cite{gladyshev1961new} we provide some consistent alternative estimators of $σ^2$, $H$ and $λ$, when $μ=0$ and $H\in (0,1)$.

title: Certified Algorithms for Gaussian Location Mixture NPMLEs via Discretized Gradient Flows
summary: We study the computation of approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators (NPMLEs) for Gaussian location mixtures in arbitrary dimension $d\ge 1$ via the Fisher-Rao gradient flow. We provide a certified algorithm based on an entropic proximal discretization of the flow which, given a sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, returns an absolutely continuous mixing measure $\tildeμ$ admitting an exact finite-dimensional representation and satisfying $\hat L_n-L_n(f_{\tildeμ})\le\varepsilon$. For almost every dataset $X_1,\cdots, X_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $n>2(d+1)(m+1)^2$, where $m$ is the number of support points of the NPMLE, the algorithm requires $O(n\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{d+2}(1/\varepsilon))$ time. En route, we also establish results on the well-posedness and convergence properties of the continuous-time Fisher--Rao flow. In particular, initializing the flow at the unifo

title: Sharp Gaussian Approximation for Q-Learning
summary: Gaussian approximation provides a foundation for online statistical inference in reinforcement learning. We establish sharp non-asymptotic Gaussian approximation rates in Wasserstein distance for asynchronous Q-learning with Polyak-Ruppert averaging. We prove an upper bound of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/4})$, where $n$ is the number of iterations, together with a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Q-learning is more challenging to analyze than linear stochastic approximation due to the nonlinearity of the Bellman operator. Asynchronous updates introduce further challenges due to Markovian noise. Our analysis separates the errors from Bellman nonlinearity, Markovian noise, and the finite-sample covariance discrepancy. In particular, we show that Markovian noise induces an unavoidable bias even when the Bellman operator is linear. The trade-off between this bias and the covariance d

title: Efficient Recursive Evaluation of Gaussian, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian Tail Probabilities
summary: Accurate computation of tail probabilities motivates efficient high-order implementations of the $G_n^{(1)}$ extrapolation transformation. We derive finite recurrence relations in the transformation order for Gaussian, gamma, and inverse Gaussian tail approximations. The Gaussian and inverse Gaussian numerator and denominator sequences satisfy four-term recurrences, whereas the gamma sequences satisfy a three-term recurrence. The derivation exploits the structure of the underlying differential operator and shows that the reduced numerator and denominator obey recurrences with identical coefficients. This construction avoids the repeated evaluation of higher-order derivatives and nested sums required by the explicit formulations. As a result, generating the approximation sequence through order $n$ requires $O(n)$ arithmetic operations, compared with $O(n^3)$ for the Gaussian and gamma dis

title: Minimax Estimation of Discrete Distributions under Hockey-stick Divergence
summary: We initiate the study of estimating a discrete distribution with respect to the hockey-stick divergence from independent samples. We provide non-asymptotic upper and lower bounds on the minimax expected loss in terms of the alphabet size, the number of samples, and the divergence parameter. The upper bounds are achieved by add-constant estimators, while the lower bound is derived via a Bayes risk argument. Both upper bounds and lower bounds reveal a transition between polynomial and exponential regimes as the parameters of the problem vary.

title: On the false discovery rate of one-sided p-values under Gaussian dependence
summary: We study the false discovery rate (FDR) of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for $K$ hypotheses at nominal level $q$ under Gaussian dependence of one-sided p-values. We ask whether the global null is least favorable after optimizing over correlation matrices. We show that the global null attains the worst-case FDR for $K\le3$ at every level. In dimension eight, an explicit mixed-null construction has FDR $21q/20$ for $0<q<1/2$. It exceeds the global-null maximum for all sufficiently small $q$, by a uniform extension of the known fixed-matrix small-level Simes bound. For $0<q<1/2$, we identify eight as the first inflation dimension in the monotone rank-one class and prove that $21q/20$ is its exact eight-dimensional maximum. In the same level range, the sharp multiplicative bound over all dimensions in this class is twice the omega constant $w = W(1)$, where $W$ is the Lambert $W$ function

title: The stable false discovery rate
summary: When a discovery depends on analysis choices, a list of selected hypotheses that controls the false discovery rate (FDR) gives little indication of how easily the finding could change: the selected set may be very sensitive to a variety of analyst choices, like the target FDR level, which machine learning algorithms are used in the pipeline, the choice of test statistics, and so on. We propose that scientists should measure and control a new metric called the \emph{stable FDR} (sFDR), and give methods to control it, including simple wrappers around existing FDR analysis pipelines. sFDR is a natural continuous extension of the FDR: we assign each hypothesis an allocation between zero and one, and the sFDR equals the expected fraction of null allocation to total allocation. If one runs multiple analyses of the same data by varying different reasonable choices, allocations can be determined

title: Asymptotic Divergence-Based Monitoring for Data Drift in Production AI Systems: A Discrete Case Approach
summary: We develop a complete asymptotic theory for monitoring data drift in production artificial intelligence (AI) systems whose inputs take values in a finite set of categories. The framework combines two complementary inferential tools. Under the no-drift hypothesis $H_0$, the two-sample likelihood-ratio statistic $G$ of Wilks follows a universal Chi_{r-1}^2 law, independently of the divergence chosen and of the sample sizes; the calibrated Population Stability Index (PSI) of Yurdakul and Naranjo (2021) shares the same Chi_{r-1}^2 limit and is asymptotically equivalent to the $G$-test under $H_0$. Under the drift hypothesis $H_1$, the plug-in phi-divergence is asymptotically normal with a variance computed in closed form for the one-sample, two-sample and symmetrized configurations, yielding standardized $Z$-statistics, detection boundaries, power functions and sample-size planning rules. We

title: Local asymptotic normality for Cox-Ingersoll-Ross drift parameters under high-frequency sampling and the strict Feller condition
summary: For the ergodic Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) diffusion with known diffusion scale and a fixed initial value, we prove local asymptotic normality (LAN) of the exactly sampled experiment for the drift parameters whenever the Feller index exceeds $1$, assuming only a vanishing mesh and a diverging observation horizon. This improves the previously known condition that the index exceed $(11+\sqrt{89})/2$. The proof cuts off the continuous score near $0$, recovers the remainder by exact conditional centering on each sampling interval, and transfers LAN by a conditional-likelihood argument.

title: Markov potential priors for prediction in Gamma models
summary: We consider Bayesian prediction in independent Gamma scale models with arbitrary known positive shape parameters. When the dimension is at least three, we construct a shrinkage prior toward any prespecified positive scale vector. The resulting predictive density strictly dominates the Jeffreys predictive density under Kullback--Leibler loss and is minimax. The prior is obtained by weighting the Jeffreys prior with a Markov potential. The transition is determined by the beta--gamma decomposition. The domination result is nonasymptotic.

title: Nonparametric Classification under Adversarial Attacks: Decision-Boundary Geometry and Optimal Rates
summary: Unlike in continuous regression, a small input perturbation in classification can move an input across a decision boundary and flip the predicted label. Decision-boundary geometry is therefore essential to understanding adversarial classification risk. Under anisotropic smoothness and margin conditions, we quantify this geometric contribution and establish sharp minimax rates for adversarial excess risk relative to the ordinary Bayes risk. These rates comprise a statistical term governed by the harmonic mean smoothness and a geometric cost of adversarial perturbations governed by the least smooth direction. As smoothness and the margin exponent vary, the adversarial term exhibits a phase transition from a fractional power of the attack radius to linear scaling, with a logarithmic correction in a critical regime. In addition, we construct an adaptive classifier that attains these rates ov

title: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
summary: We study the structural dimension of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with differen

title: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
summary: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we con

title: Bayesian Inference for Multivariate Stable Distributions via LePage Representation with von Mises -- Fisher Spectral Measure
summary: We develop Bayesian inference for multivariate $α$-stable distributions with von Mises--Fisher spectral measure, motivated by the hitting distribution of Brownian motion on the unit sphere. Inference proceeds via a LePage-type series representation with latent radial, spectral, and Poisson components; truncation bias is absorbed through a Gaussian error term, yielding a likelihood that is smooth in $α\in(0,2)$ with no special treatment at the Cauchy boundary $α=1$. The stability index $α$, spectral concentration $κ$, mean direction $η$, and spectral mass $Γ_\infty$ are estimated jointly by Markov chain Monte Carlo. At the Gaussian boundary $α\to 2$, the limiting covariance matrix equals twice the second moment matrix of the spectral measure, with explicit parametric form determined by $η$ and $κ$; in particular, the anisotropy of the limiting Gaussian distribution is controlled solely by

title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
summary: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates.

title: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
summary: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handw

title: High-dimensional limit theorems for adaptive variants of SGD I: Ballistic limits
summary: We develop the high-dimensional effective dynamics for adaptive, momentum-based variants of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). These effective dynamics are given by a Markov process. They key observation is that the non-Markovianity in the algorithm due to the exponential moving average and preconditioning can be treated using the method of averaging. Our approach applies to a broad class of algorithms including to Adaptive momentum estimation (ADAM), Momentum orthogonalized by Newton-Schultz (MUON), and its variants. It also applies to a broad class of learning tasks, such at tensor PCA, Gaussian projective models, teacher-student networks, and a multi-layer neural network trained on the XOR problem using a hybrid of MUON and ADAM as commonly done in practice. We demonstrate how to this technique can give precise, quantitative comparisons between algorithms. In particular, we find inter

title: Quantifying Dependence Effects on $k$-out-of-$n$ Reliability Relative to the Independent Benchmark
summary: Understanding how dependence among component lifetimes affects the reliability of redundant systems is a central problem in reliability engineering. In this paper, we develop a framework for quantifying the impact of multivariate dependence on $k$-out-of-$n$ system reliability relative to the independent benchmark. Using an orthogonal Legendre expansion of the copula density, we derive an exact decomposition that separates the dependence structure from the system architecture. This representation identifies how individual dependence contributions are transmitted to system reliability through explicit structural weights. An application to multivariate Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copulas demonstrates that higher-order dependence can produce distinct reliability effects even when all bivariate copulas remain unchanged. Our findings provide a systematic approach to quantifying and interpreting

title: Causal and conditional tail coefficients: asymptotics, inference and graph recovery
summary: The causal tail coefficient (CTC) measures the influence of an extreme value of one variable on another variable and has been proposed as a tool for causal discovery in heavy-tailed models. Despite its popularity, the asymptotic behavior of its empirical counterpart has not been well understood. We develop an asymptotic theory for the rank-based CTC estimator with an intermediate threshold under nonparametric conditions that are satisfied by all standard copula models. A key observation is that the CTC is determined by the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, which clarifies its interpretation and determines the asymptotic variance of the estimator. We establish joint asymptotic normality for the entire CTC matrix and prove consistency of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference. For heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear structural equation models, we show that

title: Characterizing M-estimators using canonical divergences from information geometry
summary: On Euclidean space, the losses that produce consistent M-estimators of a functional are its strictly consistent scoring functions (Dimitriadis, Fissler and Ziegel, 2024), and Osband's principle characterizes these through identification functions, which define method-of-moments estimators. We extend this characterization to the probability simplex. We define the residual, which on Euclidean space is a subtraction, as the inverse exponential map of an affine connection. It identifies the exponential barycenter of the connection: the arithmetic, normalized geometric and Fréchet means for the mixture, exponential and Levi-Civita connections. Its integral along geodesics is the canonical divergence of Ay and Amari (2015). A geometric form of Osband's principle decides which losses each connection admits. For the flat connections every strictly convex generator yields a consistent Bregman los

title: Training-point consistency of kernel ridge regression with varying correlation scales
summary: The scale parameter in kernel ridge regression plays a pivotal role in modeling the correlation structure of data. In modern applications, sampling density and the underlying correlation range often change simultaneously, making a fixed-scale assumption highly restrictive. However, establishing asymptotic theories under varying scale parameters is fundamentally challenging. To address this gap, this paper develops a unified theoretical framework for kernel ridge regression under varying scale parameters. We establish that, on uniform tensor grids with product exponential kernels, the consistency of the training-point risk holds if and only if the effective local sample size diverges to infinity. This sharp criterion universally covers all regimes along arbitrary deterministic scale sequences, seamlessly unifying the long-range, fixed-scale, and short-range. Furthermore, we provide an exp

title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
summary: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signatur
comment: Keywords: Path space regression, Signature transform, Rough paths, Functional data analysis, Kernel methods

title: High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance
summary: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.

title: Minimaxity in Robust Nonparametric Regression: from Heavy-Tailed to Sub-Gaussian Assumptions
summary: We study nonparametric regression over star-shaped function classes under strong adversarial contamination. The clean (original) observations $(\tilde{X} _{i},\tilde{Y} _{i})_{i=1} ^{n}$ are i.i.d. and satisfy $\tilde{Y} _{i}=f ^{*}(\tilde{X} _{i})+ξ_{i}$, where $f ^{*}\in \mathcal{F}$, $\tilde{X}$ is distributed as $\mathbb{P} _{X}$, and the noise is conditionally centered. An adversary may inspect the clean sample and replace at most $\lfloor εn\rfloor$ observation pairs. We assume that $\mathcal{F}\subset L _{2}(\mathbb{P} _{X})$ is star-shaped with finite diameter $d$. Under a Bernstein-type moment condition on function increments and a bounded conditional second moment for the noise, we establish the matching lower and upper bounds of order $\left((η^{*}) ^{2} \vee ε\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, uniformly over admissible star-shaped function classes, therefore characterizing the minimax ra

title: Homogeneous pursuit in $β$ model
summary: Data in forms of networks has been encountered in various prevalent fields at the arrival of big data era. To unveil and recover the true model with core units with numerous links, the $β$-model under sparsity constraint is proposed to meet the expectation of statisticians and engineers. Not only does this network model inherit spectacular property from the Erdős-Rényi model, but also exhibits degree heterogeneity through tuning sparsity parameter $s$. In this paper, we propose Homogeneous Pursuit (HP), an $\ell_0$-constrained maximum likelihood estimation method implemented through a primal-dual algorithm. To ease the harshness of computation, we find the surrogate function of the corresponding objective function to derive Majorization Minimization algorithm through the primal-dual process. Moreover, after meticulous evaluation, the algorithm brought about captures the property of fine

title: Unequal-probability distributional balance and the Horvitz-Thompson estimator
summary: Auxiliary information can improve estimation precision under probability sampling, but the relationship between the study and auxiliary variables may not be known well enough to specify suitable balancing variables. Distributionally balanced designs address this by targeting agreement between sample and population auxiliary distributions. We extend energy-based distributional balance to prescribed unequal inclusion probabilities by comparing the empirical sample distribution with an inclusion-probability-weighted population distribution. Under a regularity condition relating the study values divided by their inclusion probabilities to the auxiliaries, we establish an upper bound on the design variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator in terms of the expected energy distance. This bound motivates an algorithm that exchanges units between randomly paired candidate samples without increasi

title: Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time
summary: We revisit the problem of estimating $k$ linear regressors with self-selection bias in $n$ dimensions up to error $\varepsilon$ with the maximum self-selection criterion, as introduced by Cherapanamjeri, Daskalakis, Ilyas, and Zampetakis [CDIZ23, STOC]. Our main result is a $\mathrm{poly}(n,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time algorithm for the unknown-index variant of this problem, thereby improving upon the running times of the best known algorithms due to Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] and Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Zhou [KMZ26, COLT] with exponential dependence on $k$. Our algorithm succeeds in the presence of correlated noise between regressors, which captures the related setting of max-affine regression. Consequently, we also give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem, improving on the prior works of Ghosh, Pananjady, Guntuboyina, and Ramchandran [GPGR22, IEEE Transactions on Informatio

title: Isotonic least squares is robust to heteroscedasticity, unimodal least squares is not
summary: We compare the least squares estimator (LSE) with the $\ell_{1}$-estimator recently introduced by Baraud and Maillard~\citeyearpar{BM-2026} for estimating a regression function under a fixed design, when the errors are independent but possibly heteroscedastic and heavy-tailed. We show that the two estimators coincide on the class of nondecreasing (or nonincreasing) functions on an interval. As a consequence, the isotonic LSE inherits the non-asymptotic $\ell_{1}$-risk bounds of the $\ell_{1}$-estimator, which only require a moment of order $p\in[1,2]$ on the errors and depend on the average of their $p$-th absolute moments rather than on their maximum. This coincidence no longer holds on the nonconvex class of unimodal functions: we exhibit a heteroscedastic Gaussian example in which the LSE is inconsistent while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator converges at the parametric rate. Finally, we show

title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
summary: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

title: Automatic Threshold Selection Leaves Finite-Degree Bias in Network Power-Law Fits
summary: Minimum-distance fitting selects a degree threshold and a power-law exponent from the same network. We study the procedure that fits a continuous Pareto law with the Hill estimator and minimizes the Kolmogorov--Smirnov distance over retained ranks. For homogeneous linear preferential attachment and Norros--Reittu graphs with Pareto weights, we derive the joint limiting law of the selected rank, retained fraction of the threshold tie, and exponent error. The selector retains of order $n^{2/(α+2)}$ of $n$ vertices, where $α$ is the survival exponent. At this rank, integer spacing and finite-degree departures from a Pareto tail have the same order as sampling fluctuations. The exponent estimate is consistent and retains a shift on the scale used for confidence intervals. For integer degree laws whose tail sums have a first-order inverse-degree expansion, adding the retained tie fraction div

title: Parameter estimation in models with explosive drift and Gaussian noise
summary: We study drift parameter estimation for a positive stochastic process with singular mean-reverting drift driven by Gaussian noise. For Riemann-Liouville fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$, an observable fractional transformation reduces the model to a semimartingale with drift linear in the unknown parameters. Using the quasi-likelihood approach, we derive explicit estimators of both drift coefficients. For a broader class of Gaussian driving processes, we construct a strongly consistent estimator of the ratio $a/b$, which has a natural mean-reversion interpretation, and verify the required assumptions for several Gaussian models. The theoretical results are complemented by a simulation study investigating the effects of the observation horizon and the discretization step on the finite-sample accuracy of the proposed estimators.

title: Nonsense nonlinear correlations between independent random walks
summary: Sample distance correlation can remain large between independent random walks. For centred walks with independent, identically distributed increments of finite, positive variance, we prove convergence in distribution to the distance correlation of the joint occupation measure of two independent Brownian paths. This universal limit lies strictly between zero and one almost surely and has full support on the unit interval. We calculate the expected squared distance covariance of the limiting measure and show that ordinary permutation calibration rejects independence with probability tending to one at every fixed nominal level. Gaussian simulations illustrate the persistent dispersion of random-walk correlations and the failure of permutation calibration.

title: Posterior contraction rates for banded approximations of Gaussian processes
summary: Gaussian process regression models are widely used in modern statistics and machine learning due to their flexibility, interpretability, built-in uncertainty quantification, and strong theoretical foundations. However, training Gaussian processes (GPs) has a computational cost of $O(n^3)$, while the memory and prediction costs are also $O(n^2)$. For large datasets commonly encountered in practice, this becomes infeasible and necessitates the use of approximate posterior methods. In this work, we propose a class of approximations based on sparse covariance matrices, where the kernel matrix is sparsified according to the spatial proximity of the design points. To understand the processes taking place in the outermost layers of the Sun, but also, indirectly, in its interior, we conduct high spectral and spatial resolution, high cadence observations of diagnostically important spectral lines. The intensity and the polarization of the electromagnetic radiation in the observed spectral lines are a result of the joint action of absorption, emission, and scattering processes, further altered by the Zeeman and Hanle effects. Spectropolarimetric inversions are the techniques devised for the inference of the physical parameters in the solar atmosphere through the interpretation of spectral line shapes and line polarization. title: On Modelling the Far-Side Unsigned Magnetic Flux Evolution of Long-Lived NOAA Active Regions
summary: The evolution of magnetic flux in solar active regions is central to space-weather forecasting and solar-cycle studies. The fit uses only disk-centre, flare-free intervals, and flux is the dependent variable, so the relation can be applied directly to intensity measurements. title: Rotating Polytropic Twins and the Fragmentation Problem
summary: Polytropic n=1 stellar configurations with strong differential rotation have been considered. The so-called twin configurations: stars having almost identical integral characteristics, but clearly structurally different have been found. Hydrodynamic 3D modeling has been performed for two such structures and has shown that these configurations also differ in the dynamic aspect: one of them remains practically stationary, while the other turns out to be unstable with respect to the development of the bar mode and fragmentation. The gravitational wave signal accompanying the fragmentation process has been calculated.

title: Magnetic Power in Binaries: From Coalescing Binary Neutron Stars to Close-in Exoplanetary Systems
summary: A binary system containing two magnetic components ("stars") can be modeled as a circuit powered by the orbital motion, with the magnetic field lines linking the two stars serving as wires. We derive analytic expressions for the average and episodic magnetic powers from such systems, providing a quantitative description on how the powers depend on the magnetic orientations of the two stars. summary: The $Gaia$ high-resolution spectroscopic observations using Radial Velocity Spectrometer offers a unique opportunity to study stellar Ca II infrared triplet (IRT) activity. Our results show that, for dwarf stars, compared with the canonical method, the baseline method not only yields far more objects with valid activity measurements, but also avoids many extremely low and unreliable values (e.g., log$R'_{\rm IRT} \lesssim -6$).

title: Electrical transport of surface-bound electrons on annealed solid neon
summary: We study the dc transport of electrons bound to the surface of solid neon using the conventional Sommer-Tanner method. First, we find that the capacitive cross-talk for the thickness of solid samples on the order of a millimeter varies substantially with the temperature and is strongly affected by the sample annealing. Second, we find that, even for the annealed samples, the observed response of electrons differs significantly from that of the surface-bound electrons on liquid helium and cannot be satisfactorily described by conventional models. Despite this, we managed to extract the resistance of the electron system from its in-phase response and investigate the temperature dependence in a wide range between 1.4 and 20 K. title: State Diagram of Dual-Free-Layer Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions for Artificial Spiking Neurons
summary: The performance of perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) depends critically on interfacial properties and layer thicknesses, small variations of which can substantially modify their magnetic and transport characteristics. This work investigates, experimentally and numerically, a perpendicular MTJ with two free layers, a configuration that preserves the precessional dynamics of the device while simplifying its fabrication. Quasi-static state diagrams measured under magnetic fields and DC or pulsed bias reveal static parallel, antiparallel, and bistable regimes, as well as a dynamical windmill regime in which the reversal of one layer triggers that of the other, giving rise to spiking neuron-like signals. title: Ferroelectric control of the $K$--$Γ$ valley landscape in R-stacked bilayer WSe$_2$
summary: In bilayer WSe2 the valence-band maxima at K and Γ lie within a few thermal energies of one another, and gating redistributes holes between a light and a heavy valley of different mobilities on a landscape that stays fixed. We show that rhombohedral (R) stacking moves the landscape itself. The three-fold symmetry of R stacking forbids interlayer tunneling at K but not at Γ. The K coupling is therefore exactly zero, not merely small. A fit that leaves the coupling free returns an upper bound of 0.017 meV, three orders of magnitude under k_BT at room temperature, while the Γ coupling is 361.8 meV. The polarization creates a potential step between the layers and splits the K doublet. Each K state stays on a single layer, so the K edge shifts by half of that splitting, 41.7 meV, which any tunneling would reduce. Γ barely responds. title: Quadrupole Origin of the Orbital Hall Effect in an $sp^3$ Centrosymmetric Lattice: Robustness and Tunability under Disorder
summary: We investigate how disorder affects orbital Hall transport in the centrosymmetric spinless $sp^3$ tight-binding model on a square lattice, widely used as a minimal model for the orbital Hall effect [1]. In the pristine system, the intrinsic orbital Hall response is related to the quadrupolar orbital texture generated by $s$-$p$ hybridization. Using the Kubo-Bastin formalism expanded in Chebyshev polynomials, we analyze the effect of vacancies, orbital-dependent Anderson on-site disorder, and selective $V_{spσ}$-bond disorder on the orbital transport. For Anderson disorder and vacancies, the longitudinal charge conductivity decreases faster than the orbital Hall conductivity over the range studied, leading to an increase of the orbital Hall angle and, in the Anderson case, saturation at stronger disorder. title: Chiral Majorana Charge Kondo Criticality
summary: Unambiguous identification of chiral Majorana edge modes remains challenging because the transport signatures proposed for them can also arise from conventional mechanisms. Here we identify the chiral Majorana charge Kondo (CMCK) critical point as a more discriminating many-body route to detect chiral Majorana edge modes. This criticality arises in a charged island hosting a single chiral Majorana edge mode, where Majorana self-conjugacy locks normal and anomalous tunneling amplitudes, so that each physical lead provides two Kondo screening channels without fine tuning. Ordinary subgap states generically break this locking and drive the system toward conventional charge Kondo (CK) behavior. In the simplest two-terminal geometry, CMCK and conventional CK share the critical conductance $G^*=e^2/2h$, but their leading conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/3}$ and $T$, respectively. title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
summary: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. title: Current-driven chiral RKKY interaction in altermagnets
summary: The Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction between magnetic moments usually requires spin--orbit coupling and broken inversion symmetry. We show that in a spin-split metal without spin--orbit coupling a charge current generates a DM interaction between localized spins. Using Keldysh Green's functions (GFs) with a drifting Fermi sea, we compute the Ruderman--Kittel--Kasuya--Yosida (RKKY) interaction between two magnetic impurities in a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with an additional exchange splitting. To linear order in the current, the correction is a Fermi-surface term, and all its components are obtained in closed form in terms of Bessel functions, valid for arbitrary values of the two independent spin splittings, $β$ and $J_\perp$. title: The Goldstone--Wilczek Charge on the Rim
summary: A solenoid flux $Φ=2πα$ threaded through the center of the Kaplan--Sen lattice disk binds a ground-state charge $Q_{\rm core}=α-\mathrm{round}(α)$, and the edge carries exactly the opposite charge. The edge charge is the Goldstone--Wilczek charge of the edge ladder, $Q_{\rm edge}=-\tfrac12η$, with $η$ its spectral asymmetry. At $Φ=π$ one unit of charge crosses the disk. We ask how the rim operator, the Schur complement of the disk Hamiltonian on its boundary sites, registers this transfer. Its count of negative eigenvalues never changes over the flux cycle. Instead, the unit of charge enters the rim through a simple pole: the extremal eigenvalue of the rim operator passes through infinity in the same flux interval as the charge jump, with $ΔQ_{\rm edge}=\tfrac12Δ\,\mathrm{sign}\,λ_{\rm ext}$. title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
summary: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. title: Ultrastrong coupling between magnetoplasmons and higher cyclotron-resonance harmonics induced by spatially inhomogeneous electromagnetic fields in two-dimensional electron systems
summary: Finite-wave-vector electromagnetic fields provide a route to accessing nonlocal collective dynamics in two-dimensional electron systems. Here, we theoretically investigate the magnetoplasmon response of a two-dimensional electron system subjected to a spatially nonuniform electromagnetic field in a perpendicular magnetic field. By combining Maxwell's equations with the Kubo formula, we derive the nonlocal magnetoconductivity tensor and obtain the self-consistent dispersion relation for collective modes. We show that a finite in-plane wave vector enables higher-order cyclotron transitions, allowing higher harmonics of the cyclotron resonance to contribute to the nonlocal conductivity. These harmonics hybridize with the magnetoplasmon mode, producing avoided crossings in the collective-mode spectrum characteristic of Bernstein modes. title: Universal Analytical Description of Magnetoexcitons in Two-Dimensional Semiconducting Materials
summary: Matching the Coulomb and logarithmic limits of the Rytova--Keldysh model gives a universal zero-field spectrum for monolayer exciton $s$ states, $E_n\simeq-\mathrm{Ry}^*/[n-1/2+f_n(ξ)]^2$, where $ξ$ is the screening parameter. Analytical radii determine diamagnetic coefficients and the magnetic crossover scale. Zero-field deviations peak near $1\%$ across the full screening range $0\leqξ\leq100$. For the sampled hBN-encapsulated monolayers, magnetoexciton energies agree with numerical spectra to sub-meV rms up to $100\T$ and capture the measured orbital shifts. Shared parameters link optical and magneto-optical spectra.

title: First-Principles Investigation of the {ScSe2} TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
summary: We present an ab initio investigation of the {ScSe2} monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its $3d$ orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by {Se}$-4p$ states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

title: Metal to Semiconductor Transition in Niobium Sulfoselenide Alloy Films by Compositional Control
summary: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered significant interest due to their tunable bandgaps, optical anisotropy, and mechanical flexibility. This study explores the relationship between stoichiometry, structural phase, and electronic transport in niobium sulfoselenide (NbSxSe2-x) thin films. In this study, low-dimensional TMD films were grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to investigate the effects of varying chalcogen (sulfur and selenium) content in NbSxSe2-x alloys. We focus on tuning electrical resistivity along with the transition from metallic-to-semiconducting behavior through compositional control. These MBE grown films were characterized using in-vacuo x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze the chemical composition. title: Defect Engineering of the Water-Carbon Interface: Insights from First-Principles Calculations
summary: Interactions at solid-liquid interfaces are fundamental to hydrovoltaic and catalytic technologies. While carbon nanomaterials have been extensively studied, the role of abundant defects in amorphous carbon remains poorly understood. Here, using first-principles calculations, we systematically investigate how various defects (topological, point, line, edge, and doping defects) modulate water-carbon interactions. We find that armchair-edge defects with dangling bonds reduce the energy barrier for water dissociation by up to 30 times compared with pristine carbon, while di-vacancies exhibit a near-zero Gibbs free energy for hydrogen evolution, enabling potential hydrogen evolution reaction activity on a purely carbon-based interface. title: Linear Response Theory of Nitrogen K-Edge X-ray Absorption of TCNQ
summary: The linear response of the density is computed in the frequency domain within the generalized Kohn--Sham framework of adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory, employing hybrid exchange-correlation functionals. It is shown that the generalized Casida equations imply a Dyson-like equation for the linear-response of the full frequency-dependent one-electron reduced density matrix of the reference GKS system. We implement this formalism in the \textsc{Crystal} code and apply it to the nitrogen K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) of 7,7,8,8-tetracyano-$p$-quinodimethane (TCNQ), the acceptor in the charge-transfer salt TTF-TCNQ. We interpret the spectrum through a step-by-step construction by building blocks of increasing complexity. title: Prediction and characterisation of cation topology of pentanary high-entropy alloy (MoWNbTaV)S$_2$
summary: High-entropy transition-metal dichalcogenides offer properties tuned by composition, yet two basic questions remain open: which arrangement of the metals forms under synthesis conditions, and how it can be recognised in experiment. Density functional theory (DFT) cannot sample the vast space of possible arrangements, and the ground-state energies usually employed to screen them do not take into account the temperatures at which these materials are made. This work solves both issues for the pentanary (MoWNbTaV)S\textsubscript{2} monolayer with a Gaussian approximation potential trained on DFT data by iterative learning. Gibbs free energy calculations reveal that vibrational entropy reshapes the stability ranking, while five selected configurations retain their trigonal-prismatic framework during nanosecond molecular dynamics up to \qty{1300}{\kelvin}. title: Voltage-Controlled Dielectric Cavity Magnonics in Epitaxial Fe Films on SrTiO3 Single Crystal Substrates
summary: Cavity magnonics relies on the hybridization between collective spin excitations and well-defined photonic or mechanical cavity modes, enabling fast and efficient coupling of spintronic devices to microwave circuits and optical information carriers. In this work, we present a hybrid material heterostructure that combines an intrinsic dielectric microwave cavity with a ferromagnetic medium, establishing magnon-photon interaction with coupling rates in the order of 0.1-1 GHz. Demonstrating effective voltage-control of the hybrid mode spectrum at cryogenic temperatures, we achieve a highly tunable photo-magnonic material, that could provide significant advancements for high-performance and power-efficient cryogenic RF-applications, including hybrid quantum technology, superconducting electronics and nonlinear microwave devices for unconventional computation and signal processing.

title: Atomistic theory of the $d$-wave phonon angular momentum splitter effect
summary: Phonons offer a bosonic route to angular-momentum transport in solids, but how their momentum-space textures manifest in transport remains unclear. Here we develop an atomistic theory of the phonon angular momentum splitter effect in an antiferromagnetic square lattice with checkerboard-modulated elastic couplings, analogous to the spin-splitter effect in $d$-wave altermagnets. We calculate the transport and accumulation of phonon angular momentum driven by a temperature gradient and find that the transverse response separates into Hall and $d_{xy}$-wave splitter contributions. The splitter contribution requires both the antiferromagnetic order and the checkerboard elastic modulation and exhibits a characteristic $d_{xy}$ angular dependence, whereas the Hall contribution is nearly isotropic. Their combination enables directional control of the edge phonon angular momentum accumulation.

title: Silver/alumina-capped Janus particles: a dispersible hyperbolic metamaterial
summary: Hyperbolic metamaterials (HMMs) made of alternating layers of metal and dielectric have been heralded as promising materials for super-resolution imaging and spontaneous emission enhancement sought after in biological applications. However, the practical utilization of HMMs has been limited, primarily by the solid and stiff nature of the underlying substrate, usually a silicon wafer or glass substrate. An ability to transfer HMMs to colloidal substrates would introduce dispersibility to HMMs and potentially enable their use in medical applications while extending the curved HMM geometry to discrete particles. Here, spherical particles with alternating metal and dielectric layers are used to fabricate hyperbolic metamaterial-capped Janus particles (HMMJPs). title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
summary: Perovskites are promising materials for chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) due to their compositional flexibility and tunable redox properties. However, cation substitution opens a vast compositional space, making screening for new high-performing materials computationally demanding. Here, an autonomous active-learning framework combining a Wasserstein autoencoder (WAE) with a deep ensemble surrogate model was used to search for perovskites with a high hydrogen production capacity (HPC). In seven independent runs of 50 cycles, the mean HPC of the acquired compositions rose from 0.41 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$ in the starting set to 2.05 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$, and the best compositions reached 2.65-2.99 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$. title: Physically Informed Data-Driven Modeling of Low-Pressure Carburizing (LPC): A Self-Calibrating Boundary Condition for Carbon Flux
summary: This paper formulates an extended framework for a hybrid physically informed data-driven model of low-pressure carburizing (LPC), in which diffusive carbon transport in austenite is described by a physical equation, whereas the effective carbon flux across the gas-metal interface is treated as an unknown boundary forcing to be identified from experimental and process data. The basis for this formulation is that, in LPC, the most uncertain part of the model is not bulk diffusion but the transient surface kinetics of carbon uptake by the metal. In contrast to direct empirical relationships of the 'process regime-result' type, the proposed scheme uses machine learning as a closure operator for the boundary condition in the diffusion problem. title: Decoupling Exciton Energetics from Wavefunction Geometry in Imide-Based Defect Double Antiperovskites
summary: The excited-state properties of imide-based defect double antiperovskites AE$_5$AsPn(NH)$_2$ (AE = Ca, Sr; Pn = Sb, Bi) are investigated using spin--orbit-coupled quasiparticle calculations, the model Bethe--Salpeter equation (mBSE), and analytical descriptions of lattice-polarization effects. Across five tetragonal ($P4/mmm$) and monoclinic ($Cm$) structural models, the calculated exciton binding energies range from 140 to 210 meV. Chemical substitution modifies both the binding energies and the hydrogenic estimates of exciton spatial extent. By contrast, the structural distortion from tetragonal $P4/mmm$ ($D_{4h}$) to monoclinic $Cm$ ($C_s$), which removes inversion and fourfold rotational symmetry, produces comparatively modest changes in binding energy but appreciably reshapes the real- and momentum-space exciton distributions. title: One-Step Self-Assembling Lipopolymer Coatings Enable Direct Longitudinal Biosensing in Native Biological Matrices
summary: Sample-driven cross-reactivity remains a fundamental bottleneck for sensitive and selective biosensing in complex biological environments, particularly in microfluidic systems where high surface-to-volumes ratios amplify non-specific interactions. Here, we address this challenge with a one-step, biomimetic surface functionalization strategy based on engineered lipid-based nanocarriers that self-assemble within minutes into immunoassay-ready, antifouling interfaces that couple pegylated-lipid passivation with biorthogonal, site-specific probe conjugation. This approach enables rapid, tuneable, and reproducible surface functionalization, which suppresses sample-specific cross-reactivity even in undiluted serum, and supports direct, label-free digital biosensing assays directly in native biological environments. title: Frustration-Stabilized Hexamerons and Their Topological Magnons in Janus MXene
summary: Frustrated magnets on triangular lattices favour noncollinear order, and when inversion symmetry is broken they can host localized topological textures on top of that order. Here we show that the Janus MXene MnHf2C2FI is such a system. Combining first-principles calculations with atomistic spin simulations, we find that magnetism is confined to the Mn layer, where a strong antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange together with a sizable Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction stabilizes a frustrated 120 Neel ground state. On top of this ground state we identify a metastable hexameron: a composite of six merons and antimerons, one vortex-antivortex pair on each of the three sublattices, whose sublattice-resolved topological charges compensate. title: Tailoring Phonon Transport in Bi-based Quaternary Half-Heusler alloys for Thermoelectric Applications
summary: Quaternary half-Heuslers (QHHs) are substitutionally disordered derivatives of conventional halfHeusler (HH) compounds, which offer a potential route to modify phonon transport and enhance thermoelectric performance. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric properties of the quaternary half-Heuslers ZrHfRh2Bi2, ZrHfIr2Bi2, Zr2RhIrBi2, and Hf2RhIrBi2 using first-principles calculations and anharmonic lattice dynamics. Among four compounds, ZrHfRh2Bi2 and Zr2RhIrBi2 exhibit semiconducting electronic structure and others are semimetallic in nature. Both the semiconducting compounds show favorable electronic transport properties. title: Quantum effects on the Peierls stress for screw dislocations in α-Fe
summary: The large discrepancy between the Peierls stress calculated using atomistic methods and that measured in experimental studies is well known. Despite significant research efforts over the past decades, our understanding of this mismatch remains limited. This work presents a multiscale study on the kinetics of screw dislocations in α-Fe at 0.7K, employing the phonon description of temperature and using the Concurrent Atomistic-continuum (CAC) method as the simulation tool. Our simulations are shown to preserve the Bose-Einstein distribution of phonon modes and reproduce the nucleation and propagation of kink pairs. title: Structural, optoelectronic, mechanical, thermodynamic and thermoelectric properties of kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4: A first-principles study
summary: The structural, optoelectronic, mechanical, thermodynamic, and thermoelectric properties of kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4 were investigated using density functional theory. The mBJ and HSE06 approaches yield band gaps of 0.88 and 1.55 eV, respectively. Optical calculations reveal high absorption, with the onset in the 0.8-1.0 eV range. Hydrostatic compression from 0 to 30 kbar decreases the lattice parameters and increases the band gap. The elastic constants satisfy the Born stability criterion, and B/G $>$ 1.75 indicates plastic behavior. Phonon calculations confirm dynamic stability. In the temperature range from 0 to 1000 K, the Helmholtz free energy decreases, the vibrational entropy increases, and the heat capacity approaches a plateau above 500 K. title: Axial Thermal Transport in Transition Metal Chalcogenide Nanowires from Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
summary: Transition metal chalcogenide M6X6 nanowires (M = Mo or W; X = S, Se, or Te) are promising one-dimensional (1D) building blocks for nanowire bundles and arrays, but how elemental composition controls their intrinsic axial heat transport remains unclear. Here we develop a multicomponent neuroevolution potential (NEP) from first-principles reference data and use homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations to quantify the thermal conductivity of six MX6 nanowires. The Mo6X6 series show a nonmonotonic composition dependence, whereas the thermal conductivity of the W6X6 series decreases monotonically with increasing chalcogen mass. Frequency-resolved thermal conductivity and phonon mean-free path analyses show that axial heat conduction is dominated by low-frequency phonons. title: Transition-Metal Substitutions in MOF-5: A Hybrid-DFT Study of Oxygen Electrocatalysis
summary: Hybrid density functional theory calculations were used to investigate the stability, electronic properties, and catalytic activity of transition-metal impurities substituting Zn sites (M\(_{\rm Zn}\)) in the MOF-5 metal-organic framework [Zn\(_4\)O(BDC)\(_3\), BDC = 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate], with M = Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu. Most substitutions introduce \(3d\) states within the MOF-5 band gap and induce localized magnetic moments. Partially occupied \(3d\) states promote orbital hybridization and charge transfer with oxygenated intermediates, activating the dopant sites toward oxygen electrocatalysis. The oxygen reduction and evolution reaction (ORR and OER) activities were evaluated using the computational hydrogen electrode model. title: Interfacial Transition Waves and Domain Wall Self-Pinning in Bi-stable Mechanical Metamaterial
summary: The understanding of transition waves in mechanical metamaterials currently derives from architectures fitting one of three archetypes as distinguished by the stability and order parameter: multi-stable with scalar or vector order parameter, and bi-stable with scalar order parameter. However, a fourth archetype is conspicuously absent: bi-stable with vector order parameter. Completing the tetrad, in this article, we numerically examine the transformation dynamics unique to bi-stable mechanical metamaterials with vector order parameter. We report two types of interfacial transition waves, whose propagation is restricted to the narrow region of configurational boundaries (e.g., domain walls). We show that the wave speed may depend on its polarization. title: First-principles-based Prediction of Phase Fields: Part II. Solid Solution Tunability in Refractory Complex Concentrated Alloys
summary: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs) offer a high-dimensional composition space for designing either robust single-phase solid solutions or controlled multiphase microstructures. However, most RCCA studies have examined isolated compositions, often near the equimolar point, rather than determining how solid-solution stability varies across the surrounding composition space. Here, we use rapid thermodynamic phase-field calculations to map the topology of solid-solution stability in RCCAs composed of Cr, Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, V, W, and Zr. Benchmarking the model against 109 experimentally reported quaternary-to-senary compositions produced through diverse processing routes yields an overall classification accuracy of 80%. title: Tuning the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in CoFeB thin film heterostructures
summary: The Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI) is essential for stabilizing chiral spin textures in spintronics, yet achieving consistent quantitative measurements across different techniques remains a significant challenge. Heterostructures consisting of magnetic thin films sandwiched between non-magnetic heavy metals have been shown to possess substantial DMI; however, these vary in both magnitude and handedness for supposedly identical samples, indicating the sensitivity of DMI to both interfacial properties and measurement techniques. Here, systematic tuning of the DMI in ultra-thin magnetic heterostructures of Pt/CoFeB/Ta/Pt is achieved by varying the thickness of a tantalum sub-monolayer with thicknesses ranging from $0.1\,\mathrm{nm}$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{nm}$. title: Prediction of lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heusler compounds by machine learning and transfer-function calibration
summary: High-throughput searches for half-Heusler thermoelectrics increasingly rely on lattice thermal conductivity ($κ_L$) from first-principles calculations, or from machine-learning models trained on them. These calculations describe an ideal single crystal, whereas measurements are made on polycrystalline samples, in which grain boundaries and defects scatter heat as well. The resulting gap between calculated and measured $κ_L$ has been noted for individual compounds but not, to our knowledge, quantified across a materials class, so the values used for screening carry an unknown, systematic bias. Here we quantify and correct this bias for cubic half-Heusler compounds with 18 valence electrons. title: When the magnetic force theorem fails: dressed exchange in the induced-moment magnets FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd
summary: Effective spin Hamiltonians for itinerant magnets are commonly parameterized by magnetic-force-theorem (MFT) exchange constants, which are subsequently used to compute the behavior of complex and delicate spin textures, for example skyrmions. We show that for systems containing atoms with large spin susceptibility, such as Pd or Pt, this approach misses important parts of the energetics. For FePt, it even predicts the wrong ground state. Benchmarking against fully self-consistent spin-spiral density-functional calculations - in which the electronic structure, including the induced Pd/Pt moments, relaxes for every spin configuration - we quantify the missing energetics for the ordered L1$_0$ alloys FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd. title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
summary: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Solidification of AlCoCuFeNi High-Entropy Alloy Nanowire
summary: Molecular dynamics simulation of the solidification behavior of an AlCoCuFeNi high-entropy alloy nanowire was performed using an embedded atom model potential at cooling rates of 10^11, 10^12, and 10^13 K/s. title: Confinement-induced bound state and effective potential for microwave-shielded ultracold molecules

title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
summary: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
summary: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
summary: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. title: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases
summary: We investigate nonequilibrium coherence spreading in quenched homogeneous bosonic gases both analytically and numerically. Our ensemble-averaged Gross-Pitaevskii trajectory approach and kinetic analysis confirm the linear-in-time growth of the squared coherence length, and explicitly give the spreading-law dependence on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When the ratio is relatively small, the squared coherence length grows at a universal rate determined by the ratio of Planck's constant to the particle mass, insensitive to interaction strength and initial momentum distributions. However, our further calculations uncover fundamental limitations to such universality and establish its phase boundaries governed by low system energies, weak interparticle interactions and many-body integrability. title: Shapiro spikes in driven quantum fluids
summary: Periodic driving of a Josephson junction produces resonant transport signatures known as Shapiro spikes, conventionally described by effective circuit models. Here, we demonstrate Shapiro spikes in a neutral quantum fluid using simulations of a potential-biased atomic Josephson junction. The dc-current resonances follow the expected Bessel-function scaling, including the suppression and revival of individual resonances with increasing modulation strength. We uncover their microscopic mechanism by showing that the phase-winding frequency develops finite plateaus at integer multiples of the drive frequency. These phase-locked states are sustained by quantized-vortex nucleation and the associated $2π$ phase slips. title: Ultracold polar molecules for quantum science and technology
summary: Ultracold polar molecules present a rich platform for experimental quantum science leveraging their unique properties. Of particular relevance is the intrinsic electric dipole moment of the molecule, which results in strong coupling to microwave fields and can be used to engineer long-range, anisotropic, and tunable dipole-dipole interactions. Such interactions can generate entanglement between molecules and enable the study of novel quantum many-body phenomena in parameter regimes inaccessible in other systems. Modern experiments in optical tweezers and optical lattices have demonstrated controlled interactions between molecules in coherent quantum states, and recently bulk gases of molecules have been cooled to quantum degeneracy. Motivated by these landmark advances, we present this article to explain many of the key concepts relevant to current research in the field.

title: Observation of Scaling of Higher-Order Flow in a Unitary Fermi Gas

By suddenly releasing the confinement, we resolve anisotropic flow harmonics up to the seventh order. title: Vortices in a two-dimensional fermionic superfluid
summary: Quantized vortices are a hallmark of superfluidity. They have proven to be an indispensable probe for systems ranging from superfluid helium to type-II superconductors. By continuously tuning the velocity of two moving obstacles, we observe quantized steps in the absolute vortex charge. title: Synchronization in one-dimensional arrays of photon condensates
summary: We investigate the synchronization of coupled photonic Bose-Einstein condensates in dye-filled microcavity arrays, subject to a potential gradient. We show that in the absence of noise the desynchronisation threshold is the result of a dynamical instability. For a two-site system, we analytically derive the maximal potential difference that allows for a synchronized solution as a function of the system parameters and find that it crucially depends on the thermalization rate. For systems with $N$ sites, we find a $N^{-3}$ power law scaling for the critical potential difference. When quantum fluctuations are included, stochastic phase slips broaden the sharp transitions, yet the phase velocity and first order spatial coherence still reliably identify the instability threshold.

title: Single-anchor Delta-learning with the cluster Gutzwiller approximation: predicting phase boundaries of strongly correlated bosons in optical lattices
summary: The cluster Gutzwiller method is widely used to study strongly correlated bosonic systems in optical lattices because it explicitly treats quantum fluctuations within a cluster.
