title: Bayesian-optimized magnetic-field-gradient sensing with a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate
summary: Building on our previous study of the expansion dynamics of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate, we propose a scheme for magnetic-field-gradient sensing that relates the maximum rotational deflection angle of the spin-density distribution to the magnetic-field gradient. We analyze the dependence of the sensing performance on key parameters and perform a systematic parameter optimization. A Bayesian optimization algorithm is introduced to efficiently identify the optimal parameter combination, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of magnetic-field-gradient sensing. Numerical simulations under the adopted noise model show that, compared with the parameter set used in our previous work, the optimized gradiometer improves the sensitivity by a factor of five. title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
summary: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. title: Altermagnetism-induced Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov superfluids and momentum-selective pairing channels in optical lattices
summary: We study the superfluid phases of a two-dimensional degenerate Fermi gas in an optical lattice subject to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetic term that couples to the in-plane spin component. The single-particle Hamiltonian generates anisotropic Fermi surfaces for the two pseudo-spin species while maintaining zero net polarization. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach, we show that this anisotropy favors Cooper pairing at a finite center-of-mass momentum, producing a competition between Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) and Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) pairing and leading to FFLO superfluids. We further examine the effect of a Zeeman-induced spin polarization and find that triplet and singlet pairing channels coexist and compete, resulting in a momentum-selective pairing pattern. title: Condensate: an interactive simulator of two-dimensional quantum fluids
summary: Condensate is an interactive simulator of two-dimensional quantum fluids that runs in a web browser on phones, tablets and computers, with no installation. A split-step Fourier solver runs on the graphics processor through WebGPU at up to $1024^2$ grid points, with a double-precision CPU engine as a fallback and reference. title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
summary: We propose an interaction-driven route to Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial noninteracting bands in a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and an attractive Hubbard interaction. The large Zeeman splitting renders the noninteracting bands topologically trivial and suppresses spin-flip hopping. These otherwise off-resonant spin-flip processes are resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, generating occupation-dependent spin-orbit coupling that coherently couples neighboring spin-down fermion pairs to onsite doublons. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. title: Inhomogeneous Synthetic Fluxes in Optical Lattices
summary: Synthetic gauge fields in optical lattices are usually engineered to realize a uniform magnetic flux. Here, we propose a scheme to generate spatially inhomogeneous fluxes and demonstrate how such fluxes reshape the single-particle spectrum. Within Wannier--Stark-assisted tunneling, onsite modulation produces a plaquette flux that depends on the orientation of the static tilt, whereas laser-assisted tunneling (LAT) does not. Using LAT, two coherent Raman processes with different momentum transfers imprint a dimerized Peierls phase that alternates the flux between neighboring plaquettes of a square lattice while keeping the mean flux fixed. A bond-selective Raman phase extends the scheme to the kagome lattice, where a parameter $ξ$ redistributes the flux between triangles and hexagons at fixed flux per unit cell. title: An Intrinsically Gapless Topological Phase with Dipole Symmetry
summary: We show that the boundary fractionalization familiar from gapped topological insulators can enforce bulk gaplessness in a dipole-conserving system. In a one-dimensional fermion model with charge conservation, dipole conservation, and particle-hole symmetry, we realize an intrinsically gapless symmetry-protected topological (igSPT) phase combining a dipolar Luttinger liquid with half-quantized boundary charges. This boundary structure obstructs a unique gapped bulk preserving these symmetries and lattice translation. Remarkably, the two charge-neutral edge configurations remain exactly degenerate even at finite size due to dipole conservation and particle-hole symmetry. title: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
summary: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the $n$-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all $n$-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. title: Intrinsic Zak Phase of Solitons: A Geometric Correspondence with the Center-of-Mass Position
summary: The center-of-mass position of a nonlinear soliton in a lattice is commonly attributed to the interplay between nonlinearity and lattice confinement. Here, we reveal its geometric origin by establishing an exact relation between the soliton position and an intrinsic Zak phase. Unlike the Zak phase of a linear Bloch band, this intrinsic Zak phase arises from the nonlinear self-consistent band of the lattice reconstructed by the soliton density. We construct a composite periodic function to define this phase and demonstrate that its topological winding during nonlinear Thouless pumping dictates the quantized soliton displacement. Our results establish band geometry as a fundamental descriptor of nonlinear soliton position in a lattice and provide a geometric framework for their topological transport.

title: Cluster Condensation and Symmetry-Protected Thermal Rigidity of Bose gases on the Haldane Sphere
summary: We show that a spinless Bose gas on a Haldane sphere with a small monopole charge \(q\) realizes, in the lowest Landau level (LLL), an exactly solvable SU(2)-protected cluster condensate: a Hafnian condensate of two-boson singlets for \(q=1\), analogous to resonating-valence-bond singlet coverings, and a four-boson singlet condensate for \(q=3/2\). Unlike topologically protected quantum Hall states, the exactness of these states relies only on SU(2) symmetry and repulsiveness, with no pseudopotential fine-tuning. Their SU(2)-protected degeneracy renders the single-particle correlations exactly temperature-independent even as the clusters dissociate, a thermal rigidity absent in conventional Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs). Increasing the interaction drives a transition to a vortex BEC with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry.

title: Dual-Space Analysis of Vortex Configurations and Rotational Energy in a 2D Optical Lattice
summary: We investigate the effects of a stationary two-dimensional periodic optical lattice on a rotating Bose--Einstein condensate confined by an isotropic harmonic trap. Within the mean-field description, the condensate is modeled by the two-dimensional Gross--Pitaevskii equation in the rotating frame and solved numerically using an imaginary-time split-step Crank--Nicolson method to obtain stationary vortex states. We examine how the lattice depth, lattice wave vector, particle number, and angular velocity influence the vortex configurations, real-space density, momentum-space density, and energetics of the condensate. We find that the stationary periodic lattice significantly modifies vortex nucleation and spatial organization: vortices emerge progressively with increasing angular velocity and, for sufficiently strong lattice strength, undergo rearrangement and merging. title: Interaction-Enabled Bulk-Boundary Correspondence without a Global Band Gap
summary: A challenge of growing interest is how to make topology observable when conventional gap-based frameworks no longer suffice. In bulk-edge correspondence, this challenge arises when the global band gap closes and localized boundary modes disappear, even though the bulk topology remains intact. Here we show that interactions unlock a novel emergent boundary response from this spectrally hidden topology without reopening the global band gap. These interaction-induced excitations originate from a bulk-band minimum, yet reconstruct the characteristic boundary channels of a gapped topological parent sharing the same Bloch eigenspaces. title: Influence of the Coulomb Interaction on the Radiation of a Few Body System
summary: Understanding energy absorption in laser-plasma interactions is crucial for applications ranging from inertial confinement fusion to particle acceleration. At the most fundamental level, this energy exchange is governed by the motion of individual charged particles in the laser field. However, when multiple particles are present, their mutual Coulomb interaction can modify the dynamics and, consequently, the energy absorption. In this work, we investigate this scenario by solving the classical equations of motion for two coupled charged particles interacting with an intense laser field. Within the plasma approximation, we find that the Coulomb interaction between the electrons does not significantly affect the energy transfer during the laser-matter interaction. title: Quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation with spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates
summary: We investigate quantum-enhanced two-phase estimation in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate, where spin-exchange collisions generate a spin-nematic squeezed state in the $m_F=\pm1$ modes. title: Superradiance fingerprints of moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel
summary: Hybrid moiré excitons form a dense array of electrically tunable single-photon emitters, entailing cooperative optical responses with intriguing consequences. title: Polarization instability of unpolarized excited states in trapped two-component Bose--Einstein condensates
summary: A binary Bose--Einstein condensate in an elongated trap supports unpolarized excited states, in which both components share the same spatial profile. Within mean-field theory we show that the interspecies repulsion at which these states demix rises with the excitation level. Since each component keeps its atom number, the components separate by moving in opposite directions in the trap, and demixing sets in when the interaction energy released by the separation balances its cost in kinetic and trap energy. We show that the threshold also marks the onset of an exponential, non-oscillating growth of the separation, which divides the cloud into domains of opposite polarization, with walls at the density nodes and further walls interlaced with them. title: Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials
summary: We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbarψ_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}Δψ+ V(x)ψ+ \hbar^2 λ|ψ|^2ψ$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. title: Spontaneous Chirality and Collective Chern Bands in a Dipole-Conserving Bose System
summary: We demonstrate spontaneous chiral dipole order and an isolated collective Chern band in a time-reversal-symmetric microscopic bosonic lattice model with exact dipole-moment conservation. In a controlled large-occupation limit at zero temperature, frustrated dipole exchange and three-particle conversion stabilize two time-reversed chiral condensates. The two dipole Goldstone modes remain gapless, while a separate finite-frequency band carries Chern numbers $-1$ and $+1$ in the opposite domains. title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
summary: We theoretically describe and experimentally observe the reversibility of a nonequilibrium state in a unitary Fermi gas confined in a time-dependent trap. title: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum
summary: The long-term performance of high-finesse optical cavities depends on the stability of their mirror coatings under vacuum and under continuous exposure to high circulating power. title: Pair-Condensation Peak in Radio-Frequency Dimer-Projection Spectroscopy of a Unitary Fermi Gas
summary: Radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy has recently emerged as a powerful probe of strongly interacting Fermi gases, yet its frequency-resolved spectrum remains largely unexplored. title: Minimal model of sticky collisions in modulated optical traps
summary: Collisional loss of ultracold bialkali molecules is predicted to occur through photo-excitation of collision complexes. However, recent measurements in modulated optical traps report an unexpected lack of excess survival, at odds with theoretical predictions and earlier experiments. We develop a minimal quantum scattering model that treats collisions as a coherent process occurring in the presence of the modulated trap. We demonstrate that quantum reflection from the long-range potential fundamentally alters loss dynamics, removing the tension between recent experiments and predicted sticking times. This framework provides new testable predictions such as a strong dependence on collision energy, initial molecular state, and long-range interactions, that are absent in the currently used phenomenological model.

title: Preparation of a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator on a superconducting quantum processor
summary: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) are lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, hosting topological order and fractionalized anyonic excitations. title: Tunable Three-Body Interactions in Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
summary: We show that microwave shielding, which enables collisionally stable ultracold polar molecules, also leads to genuine nonadditive three-body interactions comparable to the shielding interaction itself. Their magnitude, sign, and geometrical dependence can be flexibly controlled through microwave parameters and orientation. The nonadditive three-body interactions can stabilize novel many-body phases, and should be accounted for in quantum simulation with microwave shielded molecules.

title: Subsonic terahertz plasmon instability in space-time plasmonic crystals
summary: We investigate collective plasma-wave dynamics in a two-dimensional electron fluid subected to a travelling periodic modulation of the effective plasma velocity. title: Theory of Convective Diffusion
summary: We obtain a hydrodynamic theory of diffusive-scale dynamics in one-dimensional systems with interacting sound modes in the absence of self-interactions. title: Beyond the Kubo formula: unification of adiabatic and isothermal response in quantum systems
summary: The static limit of the Kubo susceptibility describes the adiabatic response of an isolated quantum system, in which energy-level occupations remain unchanged, and generally differs from the isothermal susceptibility, where these occupations readjust to thermal equilibrium. title: Gapless and Non-Equilibrium Topology in Blockaded Ladders

A nonlocal $φ^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.

summary: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-Rényi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution th

title: Dynamical Variational Theory of Stochastic Reaction Networks
summary: Discrete stochastic population dynamics describe systems ranging from biochemical reaction networks and gene regulation to epidemic spreading, ecology, and population genetics, where finite populations generate strong intrinsic fluctuations. Predicting their dynamics, including mean populations, fluctuations, time-lagged correlations, response functions, and steady states, remains challenging: the chemical master equation admits no general analytical solution, numerical solutions scale poorly with system size, and standard approximations fail at low copy numbers. Using a field-theoretic representation of the reaction dynamics, we develop a dynamical variational approximation for stochastic reaction networks based on the Plefka expansion from spin-glass physics. For reaction systems with general stoichiometry and time-dependent rates, the expansion yields tractable non-Markovian effective

title: Semiclassical Averaging and Temporal Fluctuations of Quantum Dark Solitons in the Lieb-Liniger Model
summary: We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant $c$ tends to zero and the particle number $N$ and ring circumference $L$ tend to infinity, with the mean density $\bar n=N/L$ and scaled circumference $Λ=L\sqrt{c\bar n}$ fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time $τ=c\bar n t$ are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. Th

title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
summary: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $χ$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger

title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
summary: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with th

title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation
summary: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact b

title: Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams
summary: Can a machine provably discover new quantum phases of matter? We show that the answer is yes under physically motivated assumptions. For any smooth family of geometrically local Hamiltonians, we construct an efficient quantum algorithm that outputs the phase diagram to prescribed accuracy and provides a verifiable certificate for every transition it reports. The algorithm takes as input only a classical description of the family together with unverified preparations of reference ground states; no order parameter, symmetry-breaking pattern, or training data are supplied. It succeeds provided that at least one preparation is correct in each gapped region of parameter space. The algorithm explores parameter space by quasi-adiabatically or adiabatically transporting each reference state, detecting the approach of a phase boundary by tapping the transported state with a frequency-filtered loc

title: Quantum many-body scars and zero modes in the spin-1 Kitaev chain
summary: We study the spin-1 Kitaev chain and, by analyzing its Hilbert-space connectivity in the Cartesian basis, show that it hosts an exponentially large number of exact zero-energy modes protected by chiral symmetry. For even-length periodic chains, their count is lower-bounded by the Jacobsthal number $(2^{L+1}+1)/3$, where $L$ is the chain length. We then construct an exponentially large number ($2^{L/2}$) of zero modes with an analytic expression that have a maximally mixed density matrix for a contiguous bipartition using the operator-state mapping. We further identify an embedded tight-binding structure governing defect dynamics that supports PXP-like quantum many-body scars (QMBS) in multiple sectors previously not reported. The associated forward-scattering approximation (FSA) Hamiltonian takes a universal form across the scarred sectors studied. A simple physical picture of defects pr

title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
summary: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling. Here we construct a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance. Under suitable conditions, we prove a time-uniform $O(λ^2)$ bound on the difference between the predicted and exact reduced density matrices, where $λ$ is the system-bath coupling strength. Our construction completes the Redfield generator by imposing detailed balance while matching its dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance. In this approach, TR-KMS detailed balance is compatible with resonance matching, whe

title: When Time-Reversible Sensor Records Require Hidden Dissipation
summary: A binary sensor record can be time reversible yet require dissipation in every compatible finite-state Markov model. For a four-state sensor with correlated dwell times, two observed switching statistics give an exact equilibrium criterion and, when equilibrium is excluded, a positive lower bound on entropy production independent of hidden-state number. An explicit four-state construction provides an upper bound on the minimum dissipation. For a noisy Poisson sensor, the bounds differ by less than a factor of two and vanish at a kinetic matching point while the sensor remains dissipative.

title: A provably efficient classical algorithm for simulating OTOC$^{(1)}$ in 1D
summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are quantities of broad interest in many-body physics due to their connection with information scrambling and quantum chaos. Recently, estimating higher-order OTOCs in random quantum circuits was proposed as a promising avenue for quantum advantage, yet the classical hardness of this task remains poorly understood. Even for first-order OTOCs, where growing evidence suggests classical tractability, no efficient classical algorithm with rigorous guarantees has been established to date. In this work, we introduce "window propagation," the first provably polynomial-time classical algorithm for approximating first-order OTOCs in 1D Haar-random brickwork circuits, at arbitrary depths and with inverse-polynomial mean-squared error. We also conduct numerical experiments comparing our simulation results to exact computation on up to $512$ qubits for Clifford

title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
summary: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

title: A Monte Carlo study of closely packed two-patch particles with frustrated interactions
summary: Recently it was found that closely packed two-patch particles exhibit rich orientational ordering behaviors, e.g., nonmonotonic changes of the nematic order parameter and double BKT phase transitions [arXiv:2509.03981]. In this work, we show that, with repulsive patch-patch, attractive patch-nonpatch and intermediate nonpatch-nonpatch interactions, there exist frustrations in the system of closely packed two-patch particles. To investigate the ground states of the system, we design a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm with single-defect propagation. The simulation results show that the ground states are disordered and the correlation functions decay exponentially with the distance. These results demonstrate that in 2D close packing one could design patchy particles to explore orientationally disordered systems.

title: Virtual Autopurification in Translationally Invariant Quantum States
summary: We introduce virtual autopurification (VAP), a protocol for virtual purification that operates entirely within a single translationally invariant system. Virtual purification suppresses thermal fluctuations and decoherence noise by amplifying the dominant pure component of a mixed state, but its standard implementation requires multiple copies of the state and global entangled measurements. VAP avoids the multiple-copy overhead by constructing virtual copies from spatially separated subregions and performing entangled measurements only between them. Assuming clustering of correlations, we show that VAP reproduces the expectation values of the standard virtual purification protocol, with discrepancies that decay exponentially in both the buffer length and the inter-subregion distance. title: Phase transitions in work fluctuations in correlated N-particle resets
summary: Systems of $N$ independent uncorrelated particles subjected to the same stochastic change in the environment have recently been studied both theoretically and in experiments, to elucidate the interesting phenomenon of dynamically emergent interparticle positional correlations. However, the thermodynamic cost of creating such correlations, as well as its interplay with the initial distribution of the $N$ particles has not been studied. In this paper, we study systems of $N$ particles that are simultaneously subjected to a switch of an external potential, either stochastically or periodically, beginning from arbitrarily correlated initial states. We map out the distribution of thermodynamic work for such a system in the full parameter space of the problem that includes the number of particles $N$, arbitrary initial correlations between particles and arbitrary initial reduced single particl

title: Amplifying or Redistributing Coupling: Synchronization in Sparse Adaptive Oscillator Networks
summary: Synchronization -- different units falling into a common rhythm -- matters in systems ranging from electrical generators to populations of neurons. But what happens when the connections that coordinate their timing can also change? If two units become more closely aligned and their connection strengthens, that extra influence can either increase the total coupling received by a unit or take a larger share of a fixed total. We examine these alternatives in a mathematical network of oscillators, each representing a repeating cycle, connected by sparse directed links. We compare constant connections with two adaptive rules that favor phase-aligned neighbors: unconstrained Hebbian coupling and homeostatic normalization, which keeps the total incoming effective coupling of each oscillator constant. Exact relationships establish this conservation and show that the mean Hebbian weight relaxes t

title: Neither graphs nor hypergraphs: structural moments of higher-order interactions determine stochastic social-impact dynamics
summary: Whether higher-order interactions can be reduced to simpler representations is a question about the dynamics they drive, not only about their structure: what can be discarded is whatever the dynamics does not see. We make this precise for binary-state stochastic dynamics in which each agent, when updated, interacts with a randomly selected group and changes state according to the fraction of disagreeing members, as in generalized voter and social-impact models on hypergraphs. We ask which statistics of the group-interaction process determine the resulting Markov dynamics. For response functions that are polynomials of degree $q$, the answer is a hierarchy of size-weighted inclusion moments, which we call structural moments, involving at most $q$ neighbors at a time, regardless of how large the groups are. title: From dynamic strain aging to Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi dynamics of propagating Portevin--Le Chatelier bands
summary: Type-A Portevin--Le Chatelier bands are propagating strain localizations whose velocity exhibits strong intermittent fluctuations. We derive a coarse-grained connection between the dynamic-strain-aging model of Hähner and Rizzi and the Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi (ABBM) mean-field model of avalanche dynamics. A propagating band is reduced to a single phase coordinate while retaining the elastic feedback of the tensile machine. This feedback generates the increasing drive and restoring terms of the ABBM description. A finite-time adjoint calculation determines the stress mobility of the band and is checked independently by direct stress continuation. The mobility is approximately proportional to the hardening parameter, whereas the band speed scales approximately as its square root. title: Geometric Decomposition of Entropy Production Based on General $f$-Divergences
summary: We construct a general class of excess--housekeeping decompositions of entropy production based on $f$-divergences for overdamped Langevin systems. The excess entropy production rate equals the relaxation rate of the $f$-divergence toward a relaxation target and also admits an optimal-transport representation, while the housekeeping velocity preserves the same relaxation target. Our framework recovers the Hatano--Sasa and Maes--Neto{č}n{ý} decompositions as special cases, and unifies their relaxational and optimal-transport aspects within a common structure. Moreover, our framework yields physically meaningful decompositions beyond these two by taking a desired distribution as the relaxation target.

title: Free energy distribution for two non-crossing directed polymers on the cylinder
summary: We consider the partition sum $Z_L(t)$ of two non-crossing continuum directed polymers of length $t$, in a common random medium with the geometry of a cylinder of circumference length $L$. In the limit $t \to +\infty$, the $k$-th cumulant of (minus) the free energy $\log Z_L(t)$, grows as $c_k(L) t$, and we compute the amplitudes $c_k(L)$. To this aim we first study the integer moments $\langle Z_L(t)^n \rangle$, whose long-time behavior is determined by the ground-state energy of the one-dimensional attractive Lieb--Liniger model in the symmetry sector associated with the Young diagram $(n,n)$ (a two-component bosonic nested Bethe ansatz). This ground state energy is obtained using the nested Bethe-Ansatz involving $2n$ physical rapidities and $n$ auxiliary rapidities. title: Blanket theory for dense networks
summary: We show how Blanket theory provides a constructive method for calculating cavity functionals in dense spin networks. Building on the description through interfaces and magnetization shells, we develop the calculation from the low-temperature fluctuations around the ground state. In this regime, dilute defects reveal the mechanism of random energy model (REM) universality for linear energies, while their sharing and renewal across layers organize the energies and Gibbs weights into a hierarchy. Because the same configurations determine the covariances of the fresh cavity fields, this construction identifies the fields and weights with an Aizenman-Sims-Starr random overlap structure. The cavity contributions can then be evaluated through recursive fractional means, yielding an explicit free-energy functional parametrized by layer magnetizations and hierarchical exponents, with coefficients

title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
summary: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. title: Localized active phase in the coevolving voter model with fixed links
summary: The coevolving voter model (CVM) describes the evolution of node states and network topology through copying and rewiring dynamics. It traditionally assumes that all ties can be rewired, overlooking unbreakable real-world relationships like family or close friendships. To address this, we introduce fixed links that cannot be rewired and study how these structural constraints modify the collective dynamics of the CVM. In addition to the active and frozen phases of the CVM, we find a new localized active phase in which activity is sustained, beyond a percolation transition, by a giant component of fixed links. The existence of this new phase is predicted by a moment-closure approximation that goes beyond the standard pair approximation. The finite-size manifestation of this phase is an asymmetric fragmented phase. In addition, the active-frozen transition of the CVM, manifested as a fragme

title: Finite-time stochastic resetting in bounded domains: competing targets, energetic cost, and optimal search strategies
summary: We investigate the first-passage dynamics and energetic cost of a Brownian particle subject to finite-time stochastic resetting in a bounded one-dimensional domain with two absorbing boundaries. Unlike conventional instantaneous resetting, the particle is returned to a prescribed resetting position through a finite-duration process driven by a linear trapping potential. By solving the corresponding backward equations, we derive analytical expressions for the mean global first-passage time and the splitting probabilities. Our results show that the finite duration of the return process can substantially modify the dependence of the mean global first-passage time on the resetting rate. title: Cumulant Generating Function of the Hill-Lane-Sudderth urn model
summary: We consider the Hill, Lane and Sudderth urn, in which a black or white ball is added at each step with probabilities depending on the current proportion of black balls. We solve the equation for the limiting normalized cumulant generating function when the urn function is invertible on the outer branches beyond the fixed points and the corresponding inverses are Lipschitz. The solution has a parametric representation through three quadratures of the urn function and a limit of compositions of radicals, with no derivatives or inverses of the urn function in the final formula. We prove an error bound that does not accumulate along the partition and remains valid when starting from the initial singularity. Four examples with exact solutions illustrate the two orientations of the construction, the non-affine case and the presence of zeros.

title: Charged Schrödinger blocks in $1+1$ dimensions from the quartic Casimir and endpoint equations
summary: We construct charge-two Schrödinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension $1/2$, with homogeneous Schrödinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair. title: Kinetic theory of dry granular particles under simple shear: steady flows and relaxation dynamics
summary: We develop a kinetic theory for dry granular particles under simple shear flow using the Enskog approximation combined with Grad's moment method for moderately dense granular gases with the volume fraction $\varphi\le 0.5$. The collisional moments and stresses are expressed in terms of generalized hypergeometric functions, retaining all orders in the dimensionless shear-rate parameter within the adopted Grad closure. Within this framework, we derive a complete set of equations governing the kinetic stress and the collisional contribution to the stress tensor. The steady-state solutions reproduce the shear viscosity over a broad parameter range and improve the predictions of the kinetic temperature relative to the anisotropic Gaussian theory at the parameter values examined. Temperature still shows appreciable deviations under strongly inelastic conditions. Additionally, the theory captur

title: Persistent Hydration and Ionic Mobility: When the Ion Is Not the Only Transported Species
summary: Small-ion transport in water remains only partially understood despite more than a century of theoretical work. The difficulty is especially acute for strongly hydrated ions such as Li$^{+}$, Mg$^{2+}$, and Ca$^{2+}$, whose first hydration shells can persist on timescales comparable to or longer than translational motion. We develop a molecular framework in which the ion, its first hydration shell, and the outer solvent are treated as dynamically coupled components. Local hydration structure and exchange are represented through a potential of mean force and coordination dynamics, while collective solvent response is described through molecular memory functions. The theory clarifies why hydration cannot generally be represented by an additive friction or a single enlarged radius, and provides a route beyond conventional continuum and molecular descriptions.

title: Quantum resources and the onset of the quantum Monte Carlo sign problem
summary: The Monte Carlo sign problem poses a fundamental obstacle to classical simulation of quantum many-body systems, yet its connection to quantum resources remains poorly understood. We probe this connection by systematically tuning the degree of nonstoquasticity in random k-local Hamiltonians. In numerical tensor-network studies, we find the sign complexity and the quantum resources of entanglement and nonstabilizerness of the ground state to be strongly suppressed in a broad regime up to substantial nonstoquasticity. As nonstoquasticity is further increased, the considered quantum resources experience sharp crossovers into a regime where they are strongly enhanced. title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
summary: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. summary: Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition. title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
summary: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll Δ_χ\ll Δ^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory. For the three-dimensional Ising model, Monte Carlo simulations yield a perimeter coefficient in good agreement with a Padé interpolation of our $\varepsilon$-expansion result.

title: Color Through Time: Distributions, Sparsity and Dominance in Western Painting
summary: We investigate the evolution of color in Western painting using a large corpus of digitized artworks. Each painting is represented by its distribution over a fixed palette of colors in a perceptually uniform space. We compare the color distributions of historical periods and artistic movements through their Jensen-Shannon distances, and introduce two interpretable descriptors, sparsity and dominance, that quantify how many colors are used and how unevenly they are represented. We find a historical transition from dark, earthy palettes toward a broader and more saturated chromatic range, unfolding through distinct shifts from the nineteenth century onward. Periods evolve smoothly over time, whereas artistic movements display increasingly distinct chromatic signatures beyond chronology. title: Memory kernel and closure for systems driven by intermittent forcing with power-law waiting times
summary: Many systems are driven by an intermittent forcing that takes on a random value for a random time interval. For such renewal step noise, the master equation for the driven variable has a memory kernel whose coefficients are the totally time-ordered cumulants, or $G$-cumulants, of the noise. In the case of Poisson switching, these correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the jump distribution, and the kernel can be summed exactly. title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

title: Reversing the text is not reversing the path: a fixed-text measure without a zero, and an assembly-order comparison that vanishes identically
summary: For an ensemble of trajectories the fluctuation theorems give the entropy production its meaning and zero. The same expression has recently been evaluated on one fixed text, $Δ= [\log P(x) - \log P(\tilde x)]/L$ with $\tilde x$ the text in reversed order, read as an entropy production separating causally from arbitrarily ordered prose. No theorem fixes where the zero of a fixed-text quantity lies: the expression carries over from an ensemble, its zero does not. We supply a zero from an exact antisymmetry. Scoring a text's $n$ sentences in all $n!$ orders, reversal carries $π$ to $π\circ \mathrm{rev}$, a measure-preserving involution, so $Δ(π) = -Δ(π\circ \mathrm{rev})$ identically and the values are centred at zero for any score. title: Dynamical theory of the East model. II. A path-probability formalism
summary: We develop a dynamical theory of the East model---a one-dimensional, hierarchically constrained kinetic Ising model---based on path-probability densities. This theory yields an infinite but closed set of equations for single-spin path-probability densities, which, after Laplace transformation, become algebraic difference equations. To render the theory tractable, we introduce a systematic factorization approximation in which the joint probability densities of consecutive flip intervals are factorized into lower-order joint probability densities. We implement the first-order single-interval factorization approximation, obtain a closed set of four equations for the persistence functions, and solve them numerically. The resulting time correlation functions and relaxation times agree closely with Monte Carlo simulations and with the two-domain-basis approximation of the Zwanzig--Mori formali

title: Polymer adsorption on vicinal surfaces
summary: While polymer adsorption is theoretically well established on flat surfaces --- and somewhat understood on rough surfaces --- the common and practically relevant case of nearly flat stepped surfaces remains poorly studied. Here, we address this gap via extensive simulations of flexible polymer chains grafted at the step edge of vicinal surfaces. For wide terraces, the polymer-step interaction yields a stable step-attached (SA) phase, alongside the desorbed and terrace-adsorbed (TA) phases, all of them separated by continuous transition lines that meet at a multicritical point previously unanticipated in polymer thermodynamics. This scenario is observed for terrace widths $\mathcal{W} \gtrsim 3 R_g^{(2D)}$, being $R_g^{(2D)}$ the radius of gyration of TA polymers. Simpler phase diagrams, absent this multicriticality, are found for $\mathcal{W} \lesssim 3 R_g^{(2D)}$, where a simple crosso

title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
summary: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate. The nonadiabatic dynamics is formulated in terms of an operator-valued distribution obeying a quantum-classical Ehrenfest--Smoluchowski equation which exhibits nonlinear classical diffusion and non-increasing free energy, thereby retaining detailed balance. In contrast, a quantum-classical Liouville--Smoluchowski model with quantum-classical linear diffusion develops unstable long-time behavior and fails to reach a stationary thermal state. title: Effects of probe size, shape, and probe-surface interactions in imaging multilayer island growth, coalescence, and formation of a smooth film
summary: Recent studies of deposition onto weakly interacting substrates have revealed multilayer island growth, followed by smooth-film formation upon island coalescence. However, for C60 films, the roughness peak measured by atomic force microscopy (AFM) was significantly lower than that obtained by X-ray reflectometry (XRR), suggesting tip-sample convolution effects. We investigate this problem using kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations of such films and models of probe-surface interactions for AFM imaging modes. To model the non-contact mode, surface profiles are transformed by averaging heights over regions matching the probe-tip width. A roughness peak remains if the probe width L is smaller than the average island distance, but its height decreases with L and its position is slightly displaced. title: Bypassing the Entropy Production Speed Limit of State-to-State Transitions with Adaptive Resetting
summary: State-to-state transitions in colloids and cold atoms (trap compression, bit erasure) are often achieved through driving, whose speed and entropy production are constrained by a fundamental bound. We show that this bound can be surpassed by changing the transport mechanism. Adaptive resetting enables transitions through nonlocal jumps, with rates learned from reset-free trajectories. A hybrid protocol, combining resetting with a switch to the target potential, surpasses the diffusive bound in three transformations. Finally, we derive a speed limit governing coupled diffusion-reset dynamics.

title: Molecular memory reduces timing noise in stochastic gene expression
summary: Fluctuations in gene expression affect the timing precision of downstream events triggered when a gene product reaches a critical threshold. The first-passage time (FPT) to this threshold characterizes the timing of such events. In conventional single-step birth--death models, reaction waiting times are exponentially distributed and hence memoryless. In this setting, FPT noise exhibits a U-shaped dependence on the threshold, attaining its minimum near one-half of the steady-state mean. However, mRNA production and degradation often involve multiple sequential steps, leading to hypoexponential distributions of mRNA production times and mRNA lifetimes. Here, we investigate how molecular memory arising from multistep mRNA production and degradation affects FPT statistics in bursty gene expression. title: Predicting Quantum Mpemba Effects from Quantum Speed Limits
summary: Can anomalous Quantum Mpemba Effects be anticipated before a system comes close to its stationary state? We employ Quantum Speed Limits as geometric indicators of Quantum Mpemba Effects, arguing that Mpemba physics is already imprinted in speed limits by benchmarking dissipative qubits and open spin chains. Our results show that short-time speed limits can predict Quantum Mpemba Effects at low cost and with reasonable precision over broad parameter regimes. This predictive power implies a useful application of speed limits for open many-body quantum systems.

title: Confinement Alters Energy Relaxation in Subrecoil Laser Cooling
summary: Controlling atomic motion through laser cooling requires both reducing kinetic energy and confining atoms to a finite spatial region. Here, we investigate how harmonic confinement modifies the long-time energy relaxation in subrecoil laser cooling. Using a stochastic scattering-rate model, numerical simulations, and an analytically tractable renewal approximation, we show that confinement qualitatively changes the asymptotic relaxation law. For a scattering rate that vanishes at low momentum as $R(p)\propto |p|^α$, the change arises because confinement reshapes the phase-space geometry of rare, long trapping events. In free space, such events require only small momentum. Under harmonic confinement, however, position and momentum are coupled along phase-space orbits, restricting long-lived low-scattering trajectories to the vicinity of the phase-space origin. title: Strong eigenstate thermalization in Singer-cycle Clifford circuits
summary: Eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides a central framework for understanding thermalization in isolated quantum systems. Recently, the infinite-temperature ETH has been established for almost all Floquet eigenstates in linear feedback shift register quantum circuits. Here we introduce brickwork Clifford circuits with $L$ qubits where the induced transformation of Pauli operators is represented by an irreducible symplectic matrix over the finite field $\mathbb F_2$ of the maximal order $2^L+1$, known as a Singer cycle. For these Singer-cycle Clifford circuits, we prove a strong version of ETH: all Floquet eigenstates are thermal at infinite temperature without exceptions. We derive uniform bounds on both diagonal deviations from thermal expectation values and off-diagonal matrix elements of arbitrary observables supported on a fixed number of sites. title: Contact-number hyperuniformity at glass close packing in infinite dimensions
summary: We investigate contact-number fluctuations of harmonic spheres near glass close packing (GCP), the amorphous jamming endpoint reached by compressing an ideal glass. Using replica theory, we show that the Gardner-unstable region shrinks toward jamming as the spatial dimension increases, allowing GCP to be approached along a stable one-step replica symmetry breaking branch in the high-dimensional limit. By coupling an external field to the local contact number, we derive the variance of the total contact number and the wave-number-dependent structure factor directly from the microscopic interactions. At GCP, the structure factor vanishes quadratically at small scaled wave numbers, demonstrating contact-number hyperuniformity. title: Structural balance in complex networks: from measurement to dynamics, emergence and implications
summary: Structural balance theory, introduced in social psychology to describe how friendly and hostile ties organize into consistent patterns, has been reinterpreted through statistical physics and complex networks. In the classical formulation, a triad with positive or negative links, representing friendship and hostility, is balanced when the product of its signs is positive; a balanced network splits into at most two internally friendly, mutually hostile groups. This review synthesizes how the triadic formulation has been extended to a statistical-ensemble perspective in which balance is encoded by immanent three-body interactions described by a proper Hamiltonian, balanced configurations correspond to low-energy states, and balance measures serve as order parameters for transitions between consensus, polarization, and disorder. title: Dynamics and transport in LiF using classical and machine learned interatomic potentials
summary: We perform molecular dynamics simulations of molten Lithium Fluoride, comparing the classical Buckingham and Born-Huggins-Mayer potentials with machine-learnt interatomic potentials - the MACE-MP-0b3 (small) foundation model potential, and a fine-tuned version thereof. We find that the MACE-MP-0b3, out-of-the-box, is able to accurately reproduce the experimental shear viscosity across the liquid state comparable with polarisable potentials despite not itself being polarisable. Previous viscosities computed using classical potentials are under-predicted, which has previously been attributed to a suppressed melting temperature. Prompted by this we compare the melting points of these potentials. title: Magnetic tuning of odd elastic instabilities in chiral active crystals
summary: We investigate the dynamical properties of an odd active crystal whose elementary units follow an inertial dynamics and experience a Lorentz force induced by an external magnetic field. The continuous injection of energy associated with active chirality gives rise to odd elasticity, manifested through transverse forces between the crystal constituents. We show that the interplay between the magnetic field and these transverse forces produces a distinctive long-wavelength instability at vanishing wavevector, which is absent in both non-magnetic elastic crystals and passive crystals subjected to a magnetic field. Moreover, the magnetic field provides a means of tuning the collective oscillations of the crystal, enabling the emergence of exceptional points and tuning the dynamical instability induced by odd elasticity at finite wavevectors. title: Shortest-path percolation and structural robustness of quantum internet networks
summary: We study shortest-path percolation on spatial networks that model the quantum internet based on optical fibers. In this process, the removal of paths describes the consumption of the entangled links used for communication. We compare finite and unrestricted path-length bounds for networks whose average degree either increases with system size or remains approximately constant. We show that networks become more robust as the average degree increases, whereas networks with approximately constant average degree exhibit a data collapse for the fixed finite bounds considered. Using Monte Carlo sampling of the shortest-path-length distribution, we estimate an equivalent path cost, a finite bound that approximately reproduces the degradation of the network in the unrestricted case. For networks with fixed average degree, this cost grows approximately as the square root of the number of nodes. I

title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
summary: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. title: Renormalization group study of critical behavior of $O(m)$ model with cubic anisotropy and extended defects: two-loop approximation
summary: We study the impact of quenched extended defects correlated in $ε_d$ dimensions and randomly distributed in the remaining $d - ε_d$ dimensions on the critical properties of a $d$-dimensional $O(m)$-symmetric system with cubic anisotropy. Exploiting the field-theoretic renormalization-group approach within the minimal subtraction scheme, we compute the two-loop renormalization-group functions. Applying resummation techniques to analyze the asymptotic series, we estimate the marginal values of $ε_d$ above which disorder becomes relevant for the physically important cases $m = 2$ and $m = 3$ in $d = 3$. We report numerical values of the critical exponents for the disorder-induced universality classes.

title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
summary: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schrödinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
summary: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schrödinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $β=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. title: Current-driven resistive switching in high-field heavy fermion metal UTe2
summary: In UTe$_2$, superconductivity persists up to 70 T for fields tilted by roughly 20-40° from the b axis toward c. Its normal state is a field-polarized (FP) state, which emerges above a first-order metamagnetic transition when the field component along b exceeds $\sim$35 T. Despite being the parent of this high-field superconductivity, the FP state remains poorly understood, including whether it shares underlying physics with the low-field paramagnetic (PM) state from which it is abruptly separated. Using microstructures fabricated by focused ion beam, we reach current densities of 30-60 kA/cm2 and observe a current-induced high-resistivity state in both the PM and FP regimes over a wide range of field angles in the bc plane. title: Interaction-driven phase transition between bosonic Moore-Read and Laughlin states in a multiple flat-band model
summary: Lattice models with multiple nearly flat bands provide additional degrees of freedom for realizing fractional Chern insulators and studying competition between distinct topological orders. Here we report numerical evidence for the interaction-driven phase transition between the non-Abelian and Abelian topologically ordered states at fixed filling factor in a multiple flat-band lattice model. We construct a six-site Kekulé lattice model with two low-energy nearly flat bands whose Chern numbers are $1$ and $0$, respectively. At one boson per unit cell (a site filling of $\frac{1}{6}$), the weak two-body repulsion favors a Moore-Read state predominantly occupying the lowest band, whereas stronger repulsion favors a Laughlin-like state with substantial occupations of both lower bands. title: Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo for twisted bilayer graphene: Interaction effects in the presence of remote bands
summary: Twisted bilayer graphene hosts strong correlation effects within topological flat bands separated from remote dispersive bands. This separation motivates projection onto the central bands, which greatly reduces the computational complexity of many-body calculations, including momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. However, the interaction-induced Mott gap obtained in the projected model can be comparable to the noninteracting flat--remote band separation, raising the question of whether the projection remains valid. title: Learning Spin Hamiltonians from Interacting Magnon Spectra
summary: A neural network that learns an inverse map inherits the approximations of the forward solver used to generate its training data. We demonstrate this in the inference of spin Hamiltonians from synthetic neutron-scattering spectra and show how a fast many-body solver can overcome the limitation of linear spin-wave theory (LSWT). Using the truncated Hilbert-space ladder (THL) method, we compute the dynamical spin structure factor (DSSF) nonperturbatively within the one- and two-magnon space. title: Canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop transition in honeycomb $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$ revealed by angle-dependent torque magnetometry up to 35 T
summary: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. title: Resilience of emergent Hamiltonian quantum memories in the presence of noise
summary: Emergent Hamiltonians can freeze an entangled state prepared through coherent evolution, since that state is an eigenstate of the Hamiltonian under which it is then stored. We show that the freedom left in this construction allows the storage spectrum to be adapted to a noisy environment without changing the stored state. For a product of Bell pairs prepared from a density wave in an engineered chain, a selection rule prevents local density noise from connecting the target to any of its degenerate partners, so that rescaling the storage Hamiltonian by a factor $α$ moves every transition this noise drives. title: Max-Cut on Token Graphs
summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-ε$
summary: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $ε^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-ε$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $ε^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. summary: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
summary: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. title: The magical memory cost of entanglement spectrum compression
summary: How much quantum memory is needed to faithfully retain the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after separating out Bell pairs through local unitaries? Smoothed entanglement spread bounds this memory cost from below, while diverging nonlocal magic forces unbounded memory at any fixed positive fidelity. Chaotic circuit dynamics exhibit a transient memory peak whose height increases with system size, followed by declining cost despite continued entropy growth. title: $1/N$ corrections to $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in QED$_3$, QED$_3$--GNY and scalar QED$_3$
summary: Three-dimensional Abelian gauge theories have broad applications in deconfined quantum criticality, Dirac spin liquids and cuprate superconductivity. For $\langle TJJ\rangle$, we study both global flavor currents and the topological $U(1)$ current, which measures the magnetic flux of the dynamical gauge field. title: Conformal defects in a quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain: an exactly parametrized Ising defect line and a relevant vacancy

summary: The quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain of coupled hexagonal plaquettes recently introduced by Majumder is exactly solvable in terms of free Majorana fermions and undergoes a topological transition at the exchange anisotropy $J_x=\sqrt{2}\,J$. title: Stabilizer models of achiral abelian topological orders
summary: We construct continuous-variable stabilizer codes realizing every achiral 2D abelian topological order, both bosonic and fermionic. Starting from an arbitrary signature-zero integer $K$-matrix, we show that the corresponding topological order can be obtained by condensing a lattice of dyons with trivial pairwise mutual braiding in an $\mathbb{R}^N$ gauge theory. We implement this condensation microscopically by gauging a non-on-site 1-form symmetry of the $\mathbb{R}^N$ toric code.

summary: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly. Surface-code benchmarks under fixed-sign coherent noise yield accurate logical error estimates at small bond dimensions, while random-sign simulations up to distance $d=9$ and on the $[[72,12,6]]$ bivariate bicycle code match the Pauli-twirling approximation results. title: Molecular Kondo Ball Based on an Endohedral Fullerene
summary: We theoretically predict a molecular Kondo ball in TiSc$_2$N@C$_{80}$/Al(111), where a Ti-centered $S = 1/2$ local moment is encapsulated within a closed fullerene $π$ cage that serves as an itinerant-like electronic reservoir for Kondo screening. title: Local spin constraints and symmetry in single-$Q$ spiral magnets

title: Implementation of LDA+Gutzwiller with Newton's method
summary: In order to calculate the electronic structure of correlated materials, we propose implementation of the LDA+Gutzwiller method with Newton's method. We compare the calculated results by applying the previous linear mix method and Newton's method. We have applied our code to study the electronic structure of several typical strong correlated materials, including SrVO$_3$, LaCoO$_3$, and La$_2$O$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_2$. summary: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. summary: In quantum dynamics, it is generally believed that interference effects lead to a sign problem for classical Monte Carlo sampling methods, rendering sampling ineffective. title: Multiple Field-Induced Transitions, Magnetocaloric Response and Anisotropic Magnetotransport in Orthorhombic RAlGe (R = Dy, Ho)
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the magnetic, thermodynamic, and magnetocaloric properties of single-crystalline DyAlGe and HoAlGe, both members of the RAlGe Weyl semimetal family. title: Competing Magnetic Orders and Continuously Varying Exponents in $U(1)$ Spin Liquids
summary: Unequal couplings to a common emergent gauge field provide a continuous way to tune competing magnetic instabilities in an effective description of $U(1)$ spin-liquid mixtures. summary: Layered ferromagnets with strongly correlated electrons provide a platform for exploring the interplay among magnetism, spin-orbit coupling, and nontrivial band topology. $\mathrm{Ni}_{1/4}\mathrm{TaSe}_2$ is a correlated van der Waals ferromagnet with a transition temperature of 58 K that lies close in composition to a superconducting phase that emerges upon Ni depletion. We observe spin-polarized states crossing the Fermi level and signatures of broken time-reversal symmetry in the ferromagnetic state. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry.
