Collider examples illustrate the importance of interference in indirect searches and the information available when the zero is kinematically accessible.

title: Analysis of the triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules
summary: In this work, we construct the diquark-antidiquark type local currents to interpolate the triply-charm tetraquark states, and investigate the spectroscopy of the scalar, axialvector and tensor triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules comprehensively. As a byproduct, we obtain the masses of four vector triply-charm tetraquark states.

title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$μ$C
summary: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $μ^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$μ$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$μ$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $μ^+$ and jet plane. We have also comp

title: Probing Compressed Dark Sectors at a Muon Collider through Dilepton Signatures and Machine Learning
summary: The inert doublet model (IDM), a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM), provides a scalar dark matter (DM) candidate that belongs to the additional Higgs doublet. The model faces challenges in achieving the correct relic abundance for compressed spectra and DM masses in the high-mass range. In this work we investigate the prospects of detecting dark matter candidates at future high-energy muon colliders. Focusing on the process $μ^+ μ^- \to AH$ with subsequent decay $A \to H Z^*$ and $Z^* \to \ell^+\ell^-$, we explore the sensitivity of machine learning techniques, specifically Boosted Decision Trees (BDT) and XGBoost, to distinguish the signal from Standard Model backgrounds. We demonstrate that the combination of advanced multivariate analysis with high-luminosity muon collisions enhances the discovery potential for inert scalars in compressed mass spectra scenarios.

title: Flavor-Modulated Neutrino Communication: Channel Model, Modulation Schemes, and Link Budget for Through-Earth Links
summary: We investigate the physical limits of transmitting information through the Earth using neutrinos, modeling the link as a discrete-input, Poisson-output classical channel whose crosstalk is set by the three-flavor evolution operator in a layered, matter-filled Earth. For the maximum-likelihood receiver, we derive closed-form Bhattacharyya and Chernoff error exponents for Poisson counts, accurate to within 0.4\% of the exact Chernoff limit. We examine three modulation schemes: source-flavor keying (SFK), oscillation-phase keying (OPK), and matter-path keying (MPK). For an Earth-diameter link with a neutrino-factory-class source (\(3 \times 10^{13}\) decays/s) and a 200 kt detector, the mean charged-current event rate is \(1.31 \times 10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), yet the information rate is only \(1.36 \times 10^{-4}\) bit/s for SFK and \(5.2 \times 10^{-6}\) bit/s for OPK. This reduction oc

title: Interplay of elliptical laser polarization and scattering geometry in laser-assisted pair production of doubly charged Higgs bosons in the Higgs Triplet Model
summary: We study the pair production of a doubly charged Higgs boson via $e^{-} e^{+}$ in the presence of a polarized laser field in the Higgs Triplet Model (HTM), mediated by the photon and the $Z$ boson exchange. A unified formulation based on generalized Bessel functions is developed for a monochromatic plane wave with arbitrary ellipticity, encompassing linear, circular, and elliptical polarization states. The numerical analysis shows a strong interplay between laser polarization and scattering geometry, affecting both the characteristic multiphoton domain and the relative strengths of individual harmonic contributions. At a fixed cycle-averaged squared laser potential, the peak ratio normalized to linear polarization exhibits distinct geometry-dependent trends, including a reversal of the polarization hierarchy between different incidence configurations. The dependence on the collision ener

title: A resolution-based framework for coherent and decoherent jet energy loss in NLO pQCD
summary: We investigate the role of medium resolution and color decoherence in jet energy loss in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Within an NLO pQCD framework, implemented using NLOJet++, we calculate inclusive jet production in $pp$ collisions and extend the calculation to $AA$ collisions by incorporating nuclear PDFs, Glauber geometry, and medium-induced jet energy loss in the Higher-Twist formalism. To account for the finite resolution of the QGP, we introduce a sequential coherent clustering procedure based on the pairwise invariant mass of final-state partons. The resulting coherent clusters act as independent color sources when resolved by the medium, with the transition governed by an effective resolution scale $Q_{\rm med}$. We validate the coherent clustering procedure using PYTHIA simulations and investigate the nuclear modification factors of inclusive jets, reclustered jets, soft-dr

title: Heavy Quark-antiquark Systems in a Galilean Covariant MIT Bag Model
summary: This work presents a Galilean covariant extension of the MIT bag model to describe heavy quark-antiquark systems within a non-relativistic framework. Using a 5-dimensional formulation of Galilean covariance, a Dirac-like equation governing quark dynamics inside a confining bag is constructed, and the corresponding boundary conditions are derived. Analytical solutions for the spinor wavefunctions and eigenfrequencies are obtained. Numerical results show some agreement with experimental masses and hyperfine splittings for heavy mesons, particularly charmonium and bottomonium states. However, the approach is less reliable for light-quark systems, indicating the limitations of the non-relativistic approximation.

title: Unstable particle collisions in space and time
summary: A proper quantum description of colliding beams reveals the spacetime structure of collision processes, going beyond the conventional picture of classical point-like particles undergoing short-distance scattering. This familiar picture emerges as an approximation in the classical beam limit and under specific conditions. Resolving the t-channel singularity in processes initiated by an unstable particle requires going beyond the short-distance treatment because this singularity is associated with a long-distance effect: the decay of the unstable particle, followed by the propagation of its decay products until they scatter with the other beam. In this article, we develop the theory of spacetime collisions to allow the systematic study of the classical expansion accessing quantum corrections, and we apply it to unstable-particle collisions. title: Exploring Screening Masses of Light and Heavy Spin-$3/2$ Baryons in a Symmetry Preserving Contact Interaction Model
summary: We present a study of the screening masses of spin-$3/2$ baryons within a symmetry preserving contact interaction framework. Extending previous finite-temperature investigations of light baryons, we analyze 16 systems composed of $u$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ quarks, including light, heavy-light, and fully-heavy configurations with both positive and negative parity states. Whenever available, our results are compared with previous contact interaction calculations and other theoretical predictions. Our analysis shows that the screening masses generally increase with temperature, while the thermal evolution of the relative splitting between positive and negative parity states exhibits a clear dependence on the flavor content. title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
summary: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it
summary: Lithium-7 in old stars is about three times below the prediction of standard big-bang nucleosynthesis, and deuterium lies slightly above it. Precise measurements of deuterium, helium-4, and the effective number of neutrino species now disfavor most previously proposed particle solutions. We find that relics that decay or evaporate with lifetimes of a few hours, mostly into electron antineutrinos of about a hundred MeV and into electrons or photons, still lower lithium-7 while respecting these measurements. Such relics include gauge bosons of $L_e-L_τ$ or $B-3L_e$ and heavy neutral leptons with a dipole coupling or mixing with $ν_τ$, with masses of a few hundred MeV, and populations of evaporating Q-balls that carry lepton number. The decaying particles substantially alleviate the lithium problem, while Q-ball populations reach the $2σ$ range of lithium-7 adopted by the Particle Data Grou

title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
summary: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. title: $Zγ$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
summary: We study the production of $Zγ$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%. We also give the invariant mass distribution up to $Q=1000$ GeV for $13.6$ TeV LHC. In this case, the resummation reduces the seven-point scale uncertainty from $25\%$ at NLO to about $16$\% at NLO+NLL for $Q=1000$ GeV. We also present th

title: Constraint on anomalous $W^-W^+γ$ coupling in $\ell^\pm γ\slashed{E}$ final state at NLO QCD
summary: We study the anomalous $W^-W^+γ$ triple gauge couplings in the $pp\to \ell^\pmγ\slashed{E}$ channel at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV with next-to-leading order QCD corrections. Eight polarization asymmetries of the reconstructed $W$ boson, measured in four disjoint regions of $Δη_{\ellγ}$ and combined with the $m_{Wγ} \ge 1$ TeV distribution, are used to constrain the two CP-even and two CP-odd couplings. The bounds improve only marginally with increasing luminosity, far below the statistical expectation, while they degrade substantially when the systematic uncertainties are relaxed, showing that the sensitivity is systematically limited. A simultaneous four-parameter MCMC fit is performed to obtain marginalized limits. Relative to the CMS $WW+WZ$ combination, our bounds are significantly tighter for the CP-odd coupling $\widetildeλ_γ$ and competitive for $λ_γ$. The CP-odd results are also compared

title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
summary: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $μ^+μ^-\toγγγ$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events. The results demonstrate that the hardware-implemented quantum autoencoder effectively discriminates NP signals from the SM background. Concurrently, we derive the expected constraints on the aQGCs coefficients and compare them with those obtained from conventional methods.

title: $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings at the Large Hadron Collider
summary: Constraining the $Z$-boson couplings of the $b$ quark, or even ruling out the possibility of an opposite-sign coupling, is considered very challenging at the LHC. Utilizing signatures of new physics resulting from contact operators accompanying the modification of $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings from Standard Model predictions, we show that the ATLAS measurement of $pp\to Zh$ already ruled out the opposite-sign couplings by more than 9.5 standard deviations. We also argue that $pp\to Zhb$, which receives a contribution from the same contact term, would lead to even better sensitivity. Furthermore, we show that with future data this indirect method can provide the strongest constraints on $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings, and can even probe the anomaly in these couplings left over from the LEP era.

title: Towards Consistent Thermal Resummation: Improved Partial Dressing for Precise Electroweak Phase Transition Predictions
summary: Reliable predictions for the electroweak phase transition depend critically on a consistent resummation of thermal fluctuations. However, existing prescriptions often entail sizable uncertainties, motivating the development of a robust and systematically controlled resummation scheme. In this work, we develop an improved partial dressing (IPD) scheme that resolves intrinsic inconsistencies in the original partial dressing prescription, including the overlapping momentum problem and the associated divergences in the gap equations. By consistently incorporating momentum-dependent self-energies and reorganizing the daisy resummation, the IPD scheme provides a more systematic framework for thermal resummation. title: Photon-Mediated Axino-Bino Scattering Process for the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event
summary: We for the first time investigate the photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering process to explain the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy recoil event. We calculate the signals from non-relativistic halo and boosted dark matter (DM), including natural xenon isotopes, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. For a fixed Standard Halo Model (SHM) distribution, a simplified three-bin Poisson analysis yields a best-fit benchmark with mass $m\simeq506\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and mass splitting $δ\simeq326\,\mathrm{keV}$ at the adopted upper coupling bound $g_γ=10^{-3}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. It predicts approximately one accepted event, with $70\%$ in the middle bin. A boosted benchmark with $m\simeq82.87\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $δ\simeq0.626\,\mathrm{MeV}$ provides a comparable fit. title: NNLO QCD corrections to radiative and hadronic $Υ(1S)$ decays
summary: We present the complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to radiative and inclusive hadronic $Υ(1S)$ decays in the color-singlet framework at leading order in the heavy-quark velocity expansion. For radiative decay, the NNLO correction reshapes the photon energy spectrum and lowers the partial width in the fiducial window $0.65\leq 2E_γ/M_Υ\leq0.92$, bringing the central prediction into good agreement with reconstructed CLEO data. For inclusive hadronic decay, the NNLO correction provides a large negative shift that lowers the predicted width from its inflated NLO value to a level fully consistent with the experimental determination. title: Concerning Factorization at Lepton Colliders
summary: We uncover super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders. They arise from Glauber interactions involving colored partons produced by electromagnetic splittings of the incoming leptons. A three-loop analysis establishes the resulting factorization breaking, which we reconcile with the use of lepton PDFs below the soft veto scale. We conjecture that soft--collinear factorization fails for exclusive observables even in pure QED by identifying a genuine Glauber region in massless QED. This reveals a far richer infrared structure than naively expected.

title: Interpretation of the LZ Event via Inelastic ALP-Dark Photon Transition with Photon Exchange
summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a nuclear recoil event at $248\pm23$~keV with a global significance of about $2.6σ$. We for the first time explain it via the inelastic process with photon mediator. We consider a dark matter (DM) axion-like particle (ALP) $a$ converts into a heavier dark photon $γ'$ via the nuclear electromagnetic current, and study the photon-mediated endothermic transition $aA\rightarrowγ'A$. We derive the kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and boosted ALPs. A three-bin Poisson fit to the LZ data includes the xenon isotopes, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. Halo DM, which has mass $m\simeq1.2$~TeV, mass splitting $δ\simeq346$~keV, and near the upper coupling bound, reproduces the event with about $61\%$ in the middle bin. title: New unintegrated gluon density in proton and nuclei tested with small $x$ processes at modern colliders
summary: We present a new unintegrated, or transverse momentum dependent (TMD) gluon density in proton and nuclei. Parameters of the new function have been obtained from a fit on inclusive soft charged hadron production and structure functions at low scales, and from comparison with data on a number of processes at higher scales results taken at LHC and HERA, such as heavy quarks production, prompt photon photoproduction and Higgs boson production. A modification employing the geometric scaling approach has been made to extend the obtained parton density to the case of light and heavy nuclei. As a test of the nuclear TMD distribution we perform a calculation of the charged hadrons multiplicity spectra in pPb collisions at the LHC energies.

title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
summary: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. title: Parity restoration in a sterile-neutrino scenario: bounds from atomic parity violation to the LHC
summary: In a four-fermion-interaction scenario beyond the Standard Model (SM), in which right-handed (sterile) neutrinos take part in TeV-scale composite dynamics, the $Z$ boson acquires an energy-dependent right-handed coupling $\GR(q^2)$ that is expected to vanish at low energies and to restore parity symmetry at high energies. We derive the contribution of $\GR$ to neutral-current parity-violating observables. At first order in $\GR$, every low-energy parity-violating coupling is obtained from its SM value by the replacement $\sin^2θ_W\to\sin^2θ_W(1-\GR)$; in particular the nuclear weak charge is shifted by $ΔQ_W=4\sin^2θ_W\,Z\,\GR$, while the $Z$-pole effective mixing angle is shifted by $-\tfrac12(1-2\sin^2θ_W)\GR$. title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
summary: We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim \barφ^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2ν\barφ}$) bulk potentials, where $\barφ$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n\to\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. title: Helicity amplitudes and angular distributions in $D\to b_1(1235)(\toωπ)\ell^+ν_\ell$
summary: Using the helicity amplitude technique, we derive the decay intensity for the charmed meson semileptonic decays $D\to b_1(1235)\ell^+ν_\ell, b_1(1235)\toωπ$ with $\ell=e,μ$. Based on the theoretically predicted hadronic transition form factors, the branching fractions for $D^0\to b_1(1235)^-\ell^+ν_\ell$ and their lepton flavor universality ratios are calculated. The predicted branching fractions of the positronic channel span $(2.6$--$8.8)\times10^{-5}$, with most theoretical predictions being consistent with the previous BESIII measurement $(7.2\pm1.8^{+0.6}_{-0.8})\times10^{-5}$ by assuming $\mathcal{B}(b_1(1235)\toωπ)=1$. We further explore the partial decay widths and angular distributions of $D\to b_1(1235)\ell^+ν_\ell, b_1(1235)\toωπ$ and find distinct behavior among various hadronic transition form factors. title: Small-$x$ helicity evolution with gluon saturation
summary: We include gluon saturation in the revised small-$x$ helicity evolution at large $N_c$. Keeping the unpolarized dipole $S$-matrices, set to one in the double-logarithmic approximation, we derive the evolution equations for the polarized dipole amplitudes $G$, $G_2$ and their neighbor amplitudes. The equations reduce exactly to the known ones for $S=1$ and contain new terms proportional to $1-S$, including one in the equation for $G_2$ arising because the real and virtual contributions that cancel for $S=1$ are weighted differently by the $S$-matrix of the small daughter dipole; this term is ultraviolet finite and acts only for a saturated daughter dipole. Inside the saturation region the growth rate of $G$ drops from $3.66$ to $2\sqrt{1-λ}$, in units of $\sqrt{α_sN_c/2π}$, with $λ$ the growth exponent of the saturation scale, while $G_2$ oscillates without growing. title: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics
summary: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics. We also perform a perturbation analysis about an exact solution studied in earlier work. The equations represent a system that is subject to a periodic driver, and we use Floquet theory to help determine its properties. Numerically, we compare the exact solution to the analytic approximation, and we exhibit several examples of how the non-linear effects influence particle trajectories, with particular emphasis on trajectories near the linear limit.

title: Radiative-recoil corrections at order $α^2 (Z α)^5$ to energy levels of muonium and positronium
summary: We have calculated radiative-recoil corrections at order $α^2 (Z α)^5$ to the energy levels of spin-1/2--spin-1/2 Coulombic bound systems. The corrections we consider involve two exchange photons with two-loop radiative corrections on the electron line. We obtain precise results for all values of the mass ratio. Our results are relevant for upcoming improved measurements of the muonium ground-state hyperfine splitting and 1S-2S interval.

title: Wormholes do not contribute to supersymmetric partition functions
summary: We show that wormholes connecting multiple asymptotic boundaries always spontaneously break at least some of the symmetries preserved by their boundary conditions. Their configurations then form nontrivial orbits of the broken symmetry, and for the case of a fermionic symmetry, the contribution of each orbit vanishes. We conclude that wormholes do not contribute to moments of supersymmetric partition functions. This extends results on supersymmetric indices by Iliesiu, Kologlu, and Turiaci. We emphasize that supersymmetric partition functions can still have a nonzero ensemble variance. In SYK-like examples that we analyze, this arises due to the contribution of ``non-geometric wormhole'' configurations that preserve all continuous symmetries.

title: The Gradient Structure of Perturbative RG Flows
summary: Weyl consistency conditions show that perturbative renormalisation group flows in two, four and six dimensions are almost gradient flows. The obstruction is an antisymmetric contribution to the metric on the space of couplings, which has resisted removal since the work of Jack and Osborn more than 35 years ago. We show that a conformal Ward identity on the sphere allows it to be removed by a choice of scheme. The beta function is then the gradient of a potential $A$ with respect to a symmetric metric, to all orders in perturbation theory. The Ward identity gives this result in any dimension $d$, in theories with and without a Weyl anomaly. At leading order the metric is fixed by the two-point functions of the perturbing operators, so unitarity makes it positive definite at weak coupling. title: Level repulsion and the quantum viscosity of near-extremal black branes
summary: Below the gap scale of the AdS$_2$ throat, quantum fluctuations make the shear viscosity of near-extremal black branes grow as $(CT)^{-1/2}$ in the disk approximation of JT gravity, and the one-loop $η/s$ diverges. To cure this divergence, we include the non-perturbative completion of JT gravity as a matrix integral. The Kubo formula then probes universal features of level correlations. At finite extremal entropy $S_0$, level repulsion makes the DC viscosity vanish. A finite, universal viscosity survives in a double-scaling limit in which the probe frequency $ω$ is held in a fixed ratio to the level-spacing scale $ω_{\rm sp}\equiv e^{-S_0}/C$. At fixed $ω$, with $ω_{\rm sp}\llω\ll e^{S_0/3}ω_{\rm sp}$ the Schwarzian growth then saturates at $η_{\max}\simeq0.174\,(ω/ω_{\rm sp})\,η_{sc}$, where $η_{sc}$ is the semiclassical viscosity, and the viscosity decreases at lower temperatures. title: Bulk Wilson Loops from $\mathscr{I}$
summary: A Carrollian description of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on partially complexified future null infinity was recently proposed by Opreij, Skinner and Wang in arXiv:2604.09771. In this paper, we give a new form of the Carrollian Yang-Mills kinetic action on real future null infinity, and recover the logarithmic two-point function found by arXiv:2604.09771. We then extend the Carrollian description of Yang-Mills beyond scattering amplitudes by studying the expectation value of a null polygonal Wilson loop in Minkowski spacetime. We propose a boundary operator given by the trace of a cyclic product of holomorphic frames on the good cuts associated with the polygon's vertices. At order $g^2$, we show analytically that the boundary calculation reproduces the rational bulk integrand obtained from a self-dual Lagrangian insertion.

title: Banana D-modules
summary: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.

title: Polarized IKKT holography: bulk realization of BPS operators
summary: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

title: The $a$-function in fractional dimensions
summary: We consider the $β$-functions for both scalar, and supersymmetric chiral scalar, field theories with a general $n$th-order self-interaction, in their critical dimensions, which are in general non-integer. We perform a full computation up to fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case, and a partial one in the scalar case. We then demonstrate the existence of an $a$-function, related to the $β$-functions by a gradient flow with a positive-definite metric, through fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case; and show that all our fourth-order results in the scalar case are consistent with a similar property holding there too.

title: Gauging background isometries of the ILST null string
summary: We present a general gauging of a subalgebra, $\mathfrak h$, of the isometries $\mathfrak g$ of the background geometry for the ILST string (e-Print: hep-th/9307108 [hep-th]). We discuss which of the isometries in $\mathfrak g$ survive the gauging as symmetries. The gauged symmetry does not in general involve transformations of the vector density V. There is thus a corresponding contraction of the algebra of constraints as compared to the flat background and it no longer represent the full Carroll-Weyl algebra. This algebra of constraints is derived and discussed, partly in an appendix. The gauging of isometries sets the stage for a reduction, or quotient construction, leading to a new null string on the space of orbits of the gauge group. We illustrate this by deriving the ILST string in $AdS$ background as a quotient of a model in SO(d,2) background by a SO(d,1) isometry, in group spac

title: Perturbative $S$-matrix Unitarity in Higher-Derivative Theory of Fermions
summary: We construct a higher-derivative fermion theory with four-Fermi interactions. In quantum field theory, it is conjectured that good high-energy behavior of tree-level scattering amplitudes implies renormalizability, a notion referred to as the tree-unitarity criterion. To investigate whether this criterion is satisfied in a higher-derivative fermion theory, we examine the structure of the $S$-matrix in detail. Owing to the higher-derivative kinetic term, the mass dimension of the spinor field differs from that of a conventional fermion, rendering four-Fermi interactions renormalizable at the cost of introducing ghost states. We show that, unlike bosonic ghosts, fermionic ghosts inevitably give rise to negative-norm states regardless of the sign of their energy eigenvalues. We further demonstrate that, in contrast to conventional four-Fermi theories, the higher-derivative four-Fermi theory

title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
summary: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

title: Unified Yet Non-fundamental: The Origins of Steven Weinberg's Early Conception of Effective Field Theories
summary: This article traces the origins of Steven Weinberg's early conception of Effective Field Theories (EFTs) in the 1960s. I argue that Weinberg's path to his first EFT prototype was decisively shaped by his longstanding unificatory commitment. From his early days as a physicist onward, he strove to rely on first principles, whether fundamental or not, to bring order to the diversity of particle phenomena. This explains why he ultimately came in 1966-68 to introduce a new kind of field theory that instantiates a non-fundamental symmetry principle in the most complete manner in order to systematically account for low-energy nucleon-pion interaction processes. In doing so, Weinberg was, for the first time, led to conceive of EFTs as covariant model expansions in some characteristic scale, independently of their (more) fundamental counterpart(s). title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
summary: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. title: A matrix model of an M5--brane on a plane--wave background
summary: We construct the maximally supersymmetric deformation of the recently proposed $\mathcal{A}_6$ matrix model on a plane--wave background. We derive the same theory independently, by reducing the light--cone M5--brane on a five--sphere in this background to its lowest harmonics, including the dynamics of its chiral two--form and of its fermions. We then classify all its classical vacua. We show that one of them is the fivebrane giant graviton, and that its fluctuations form a single $\mathfrak{su}(2|4)$ multiplet, which reproduces the $\ell=1$ level of the spherical transverse fivebrane identified in the large $N$ limit of BMN theory. Moreover, the dynamical tensor supports new families of vacua, where the flux balances the size of the brane, and whose spectrum contains that of a fuzzy membrane. Finally, we show that BLG theory sits inside the model, both on a Coulomb branch of the massles

title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
summary: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

title: Dynamical Temperley-Lieb algebras from Quiver CFTs
summary: The one-loop dilatation operator of a superconformal planar gauge theory can be written as a sum of local generators. The algebra these generators satisfy is a powerful organising principle for the spectrum. For SU(2)-like bosonic subsectors we show that this algebra can be read off directly from Feynman diagrams, which we identify as a natural graphical language for it. For N=4 super Yang-Mills this simply reproduces the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra of the XXX spin chain. After orbifolding and marginally deforming to N=2 superconformal quiver theories, the same recipe yields dynamical generalisations of the TL algebra. In these theories, the faces of the diagrams are coloured according to the quiver nodes, and separated by domain walls corresponding to bifundamental fields. title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
summary: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
summary: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $μ^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. title: A full-color four-point form factor
summary: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
summary: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
summary: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. title: Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo method for bipolar charge transport in graphene
summary: We develop a Pauli-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo method for bipolar charge transport in graphene, with an explicit treatment of phonon-assisted interband scattering, including electron-hole generation and recombination. The method employs a valence-vacancy representation to describe coupled electron and hole populations without explicitly simulating the highly populated valence band. It preserves the discrete occupation bounds during both free flight and scattering while conserving net charge. The numerical properties of the method are assessed through sensitivity and refinement studies and comparison with an independent deterministic discontinuous Galerkin solution of the same kinetic model. The two approaches show very good agreement for the time evolution, carrier distributions, and steady-state transport observables across the investigated transport regimes. The results also demons

title: Feshbach resonances of the second order in a Friedrichs model
summary: We consider an extended version of the matrix Friedrichs model that may produce Feshbach resonances of the second order. In this model, under enlarging of the coupling constant, a pair of eigenvalues of the unperturbed Hamiltonian embedded into the continuous spectrum first transforms in resonances of the first order. At some moment later on, these two resonances merge into a single resonance but of the second order, and we fix conditions for this event. Being based on the operator interpretation of resonances, we found that, in the case under consideration, the operator roots of the transfer function have a very particular structure.

title: Phase-dependent atomicity and PPT edge states for cyclic-sign covariant qutrit maps
summary: Decomposable positive maps cannot detect entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT). We obtain a necessary and sufficient criterion for decomposability in the entire seven-real-parameter class of Hermiticity-preserving cyclic-sign covariant maps on $M_3$. The criterion reduces to a one-variable inequality and, for positive maps in this class, characterizes indecomposability exactly. We apply it to a phase-dependent family obtained by adding a completely positive map to the Choi map. Every map in this family is positive, and we find the exact phase-dependent threshold for indecomposability and atomicity. At three phase values, the maps remain indecomposable for every finite deformation strength. Each indecomposable map gives an indecomposable entanglement witness through its Choi matrix. title: On a class of affine Temperley-Lieb modules
summary: We prove that the class of all affine Temperley-Lieb modules, equipped with the recently introduced "diagrammatic" tensor product, forms a quasitensor (i.e. monoidal braided) category. When the Temperley-Lieb parameter $q$ is not a root of unity, we consider the infinite subcategory generated by the simple quotients of reducible standard modules, and we argue that it is a semi-simple ribbon category. We present some evidence that, under the fusion rules and the associativity maps, each simple module in this subcategory is equivalent to a pair of $U_q(sl_2)$ heighest-weight modules.

title: Effective Hamiltonians and asymptotic band coupling
summary: By a multiple-scale asymptotic expansion, we derive effective macroscopic models for a large class of tight-binding Schrödinger equations with slow spatial variations. For wave packets that are spectrally localized to some point $(K;E) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}$ in the unperturbed tight-binding dispersion relation, our effective models produce long-time approximations of the tight-binding dynamics, accurate to any prescribed order in the asymptotic parameter. Our framework allows the point $(K;E)$ to be degenerate, meaning that multiple (but not necessarily all) energy bands of the tight-binding Hamiltonian can attain the value $E$ at the frequency $K$. We construct an effective Hamiltonian on the relevant degenerate subspace, which quantifies the coupling between the degenerate and other bands. Several applications and numerical simulations illustrate the theory.

title: From Giant Vortex States to Bright Solitons in Rapidly Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates with Attractive Interactions
summary: We study the ground state of a Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) with attractive interaction of strength $ a_Ω$, confined by a two-dimensional anharmonic trap rotating at angular velocity $ Ω$. We prove the occurrence of a phase transition, as $ Ω\to\infty $, from an annular giant vortex state to an angularly localized bright soliton. More precisely, we distinguish three regimes according to the relative sizes of the radial and angular concentration scales. In the weak coupling regime $ a_Ω= \mathcal{O}(Ω^{-1/2}) $, the limiting angular profile is governed by a variational problem on the unit circle showing rotational symmetry breaking: below a given sharp threshold, the condensate remains uniformly distributed in the annulus and has a giant vortex profile with a vortex-free bulk and macroscopic circulation; above it, rotational symmetry is broken. title: Complex chaotic Boltzmann machines as deterministic representations of quantum states
summary: Neural networks and tensor networks have opened new ways to explore quantum systems by parameterizing families of wave functions through the structure and parameters of a network. Here we extend this perspective to a dynamical representation: we introduce a complex chaotic Boltzmann machine that assigns a deterministic system to a pure quantum state. We extend Suzuki's construction to incorporate both Born probabilities and relative phases. The probabilities set the trajectory velocities in a hypercube, while the phases define a complex field that lifts its Poincare sections. The evolution is determined by the network parameters and initial conditions, without random choices during flights or configuration changes. title: Quantum conditional relative entropy and quasi-factorization
summary: One of the characteristic features that distinguishes quantum systems from classical ones is the inability, except for some special cases, of defining a conditional expectation map for a given quantum state, namely a map that restricts observables to a given sub-region (or more generally, a sub-algebra of observables) while preserving expectation values. Of the many consequences of this lack of conditional expectation, we consider the problem of defining the quantum conditional relative entropy, i.e., the relative entropy between two quantum states conditioned to a sub-region or sub-algebra. We discuss how, when the conditional expectation map is not defined, there are multiple, non-equivalent ways to define a quantum conditional relative entropy quantity, and we present some of their properties. title: Dynamics of a spherical ferromagnet on a non-conducting incline in an external magnetic field
summary: Magnetic particles of various shapes and sizes are used in biomedical applications, robotics, nanomagnetism, electrotechnology, and education. Yet despite years of study, a theoretical description of the rolling motion of a solid magnetic sphere still eludes us. One of the reasons is that coupling magnetic fields with mechanical degrees of freedom creates a highly non-linear motion with non-holonomic constraints, which makes modeling these systems analytically or by simulations non-trivial. The Lagrange-d'Alembertian approach to holonomic systems remains one of the most versatile methods to prove central theorems and solve problems in analytical mechanics and electrodynamics. While non-holonomic systems are not accessible by the original theory, recent developments generalize the principle to certain dissipative systems. title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
summary: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

title: Moments, Equilibrium Equations and Barycentric Coordinates
summary: In a previous article, we applied the classical theory of moments to establish equilibrium equations for rather general finite systems of interacting particles. An equilibrium of such a system occurs if and only if the corresponding ``zeroth'' moment $μ_0$ and the first moment $μ_1$ vanish. Our focus then was on the relationship between $μ_0$, $μ_1$ and the second moment $μ_2$ in order to produce systems of equilibrium equations solely dependent on mutual distances, including a generalization of the Albouy-Chenciner equations for central configurations in Celestial Mechanics. In the present work, we explore in depth the condition of simultaneously vanishing $μ_0$ and $μ_1$ on its own. title: The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
summary: We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ have purely imaginary energies $\pm i\hbarω(n+1/2)$. In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for $T>0$ and the growing antiresonant branch converging for $T<0$. title: Reset Quantum Channels
summary: We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in t

title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
summary: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising can

title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
summary: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.

title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
summary: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. title: Nematic equilibria on a Möbius strip: topology and extrinsic curvature
summary: We investigate the equilibrium configurations of a nematic liquid crystal confined in a thin tubular neighbourhood of a Möbius strip. Assuming degenerate tangential anchoring and a director uniform across the thickness, we derive an effective two-dimensional Frank energy that accounts for both the intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of the mid-surface. The non-orientability of the substrate imposes identification conditions that couple the reversal of the local frame to the head-to-tail symmetry of the nematic director. We show that the resulting topological classification depends on the parity of the number of half-twists: the sector index is a winding number for even parity, whereas only its parity is physically meaningful for odd parity, in which case the net director rotation is not quantised. We analyse the narrow-strip limit and solve the full two-dimensional equilibrium problem by f

title: Curvature Integrability in Twinor Theory: An Ambitwistor Approach to the Twinor Googly Problem
summary: The twinor analogue of the googly problem is addressed through an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels, retaining both chiralities, sources and torsion without requiring chiral null surfaces. Under the stated quotient, evaluation and descent assumptions, holomorphic affine sections reconstruct the twinor field equation $DY=J$. Correspondence-space cohomology realizes the contracted chiral and ladder equations, including the ladder's soldering coupling and mass-normalization source. For a prescribed non-normal conformal connection, infinity-twistor parallelism recovers the energy--momentum equation, supplemented by independent spin-current equations. These constructions give a conditional auxiliary formulation; constitutive sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical input.

title: Elliptic analogues of KP and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions
summary: We develop a tau-function framework for soliton solutions on elliptic backgrounds associated with the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy and its B-type counterpart (BKP). Starting from discrete KP (dKP) and discrete BKP (dBKP) equations of elliptic type, we construct Casorati and Gram determinant tau functions for the elliptic dKP through Darboux and binary Darboux transformations, and elliptic Pfaffian tau functions for dBKP through the Moutard transformation. Moreover, the higher-order discrete KP and BKP hierarchies together with their tau functions are constructed via Pfaffian identities. Then, through Miwa transformations, the continuous elliptic KP, modified KP, and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions are provided. Suitable constraints on spectral parameters or wave numbers yield reductions to the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV), focusing and defocusing modified Korteweg--de Vries

title: Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
summary: We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.

title: Exploring the limit of partonic collectivity in small collision systems at the LHC
summary: The existence of a partonic phase in small collision systems has been investigated previously through measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_{2}$) of mesons ($π^{\pm}$, K$^{\pm}$, and K$_{S}^{0}$) and baryons ($\rm{p}(\overline{\rm{p}})$, $Λ(\overlineΛ)$) in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV and pp collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV recorded by ALICE. The results have revealed a grouping and splitting behavior of $v_{2}$ for baryons and mesons at intermediate transverse momentum ($p_{\rm{T}}$), establishing that partonic collectivity, as observed in heavy-ion collisions, is also present in these systems. In this Letter, the $p_{\rm{T}}$-differential $v_{2}$ of various hadronic species is investigated in p-Pb collisions for the multiplicity intervals $N_{\rm ch} \geq 50$, $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$, and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, as well as in pp collisions

title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
summary: Ultrarelativistic $^{16}$O+$^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions recently performed at the Large Hadron Collider have imaged quadrupole and octupole correlations between nucleons through the collective flow of emitted hadrons. We establish a quantitative link between these correlations and the low-energy constants (LECs) that enter chiral inter-nucleon interactions. Emulators built using the subspace-projected coupled-cluster method enable a global sensitivity analysis of the ground-state quadrupole mean-square eccentricity, revealing that quadrupole correlations respond linearly and additively to all 16 LECs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. The sensitivities differ markedly in $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, and are complementary to those of the binding energy and charge radius, the bulk observables to which nuclear interactions are typically calibrated. title: Triaxial $μ$-PIC for resolving Multi-Hit Ambiguity
summary: The micro pixel chamber ($μ$-PIC), a type of micro-pattern gaseous detectors (MPGD), features pixel electrodes structured similarly to a sliced proportional counter. Conventionally, $μ$-PIC electrodes are connected to orthogonal strip electrodes to reduce the number of readout circuits; however, this configuration introduces multi-hit ambiguity when tracing winding tracks or during high-rate operations. A well-known solution to this problem is the adoption of an additional readout axis. To this end, we designed a new electrode structure using Garfield++ simulations and fabricated a triaxial $μ$-PIC based on through-glass-via (TGV) technology. This triaxial $μ$-PIC achieved a high gas gain of $1.1\times 10^4$ and the energy resolution of 22\% (FWHM) at 5.9~keV, Furthermore, the false-hit probability was less than 0.78\% at a 95\% confidence level for two clusters separated by a distance o

title: Analysis of Xe-131 Prompt Gammas
summary: The prompt gammas of Xe-131 from thermal neutron capture were measured for the first time at the Fission Product Prompt gamma-ray Spectrometer by irradiation of isotopically enriched Xe-130 in a high-purity quartz ampoule. Through gamma-gamma coincidences, 42 new prompt gammas were measured and 14 new nuclear states determined.

title: Heavy quarkonium spin transport in a hot medium
summary: We investigate the in-medium spin transport of heavy quarkonium using an open-quantum-system approach based on potential nonrelativistic QCD. We express the heavy quarkonium dilepton decay angular distribution in terms of late-time quarkonium spin-dependent distribution functions. Working in the quantum-optical regime, where the inverse quarkonium size is much larger than the binding energy and the binding energy is comparable to or larger than the medium temperature $T$, we derive a spin-dependent quantum master equation incorporating both dissociation and regeneration, followed by the corresponding projected semiclassical Boltzmann equations. At leading order in the coupling, we retain the recoil corrections of relative order $T/M$ that contribute to the leading spin-dependent collision kernel. Here $M$ denotes the heavy-quark mass. At zeroth order in fluid gradients, we show that the

title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$γ$S
summary: Elastic and inelastic Compton-scattering cross sections of the deuteron were measured at HI$γ$S using a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic $γ$-ray beam (61.0 MeV). Scattered $γ$ rays from a liquid deuterium target were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. High-resolution NaI(Tl) detectors at backward angles enabled separation of elastic and inelastic events. A $χ$EFT analysis of the data yields new neutron scalar polarizabilities, $α^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \pm 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ and $β^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \mp 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ (in units of $10^{-4} \mathrm{fm}^3$) reducing statistical uncertainties by 12 %.

title: MR-ToF-assisted In-Source Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy at IGISOL
summary: Multi-Reflection Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer (MR-ToF-MS) assisted in-source laser resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS) has been implemented at the Ion Guide Isotope Separator On-Line (IGISOL) facility, University of Jyväskylä. Exotic nuclei, produced via fusion-evaporation reactions, are stopped and neutralized in a hot-cavity catcher, and selectively laser-ionized through a multi-step resonance ionization scheme before being transported to the MR-ToF-MS device. This combination of techniques is aimed at optically probing the very exotic N=Z nuclei in the immediate vicinity of $^{100}$Sn. The laser system, hot-cavity ion source, isobaric purification and detection stages are described. A representative hyperfine-structure spectrum of the proton-rich silver isotope $^{101}$Ag is presented as a case example.

Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). title: Elliptic and triangular flow responses in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions from hydrodynamics and kinetic theory
summary: Recent light-ion collisions at the Large Hadron Collider provide an opportunity to investigate the system-size dependence of hydrodynamization and whether the structure of light nuclei can be extracted from collective flow data. Both objectives require an accurate understanding of how the collision dynamics converts initial-state geometry into final-state momentum anisotropies. To this end, and to assess the impact of the experimental results, we compare simulations of O+O and Ne+Ne collisions in hydrodynamic and kinetic theory simulations across opacities. In both ultracentral and peripheral collisions, Ne+Ne-to-O+O elliptic flow ratios are robust against changes in dynamical description, supporting interpretations of data based on nuclear-geometry-driven effects. Triangular-flow ratios instead show substantially stronger sensitivity to nonequilibrium dynamics.

title: Pionization experiments in light nuclei
summary: The zero-energy antiproton absorption in light nuclei is considered. The ratios $R_{n/p}$ of antiproton-neutron versus antiproton-proton capture rates in the lightest nuclei $^2$H, $^3$He and $^4$He are analyzed, both from the experimental results and from some selected theoretical models. These models are used as key input in determining the level shifts and widths of the lowest states. We establish the capture orbit in $^3$He to be states of angular momentum $L=2$. Several N-N optical potentials are used to compute the $R_{n/p}$ values for several heavy nuclei and the results are found to be consistent with the data. However, the old chamber experiments studying pionization in Helium, are not consistent with models. Only the Paris potential is likely to succeed provided baryonia states predicted by this model are better understood.

title: Cumulative protons and pions at the intermediate energies in the FRAGM experiment

The parameterization of cumulative effect used in experiments investigating nucleus-nucleus interactions is discussed. It is shown, that the energy dependencies of these parameters are analogous to those observed in nucleon-nucleus interactions and indicate the presence of nuclear scaling behavior.

title: An improved statistical treatment for radioassay-based background projection incorporating part-to-part variation
summary: For low background experiments, prediction of the background from radioactivity in detector components is of critical importance. Radioassays are often conducted on small samples or individual parts, which may be subject to differences in production or handling resulting in a part-to-part variation. We propose a new method for the averaging of radioassays to incorporate this part-to-part variation into predictions of the total activity of parts. We also consider how to add component activities based on assays for component groups that are simulated as a single entity.

title: Probing nuclear deformation through global $Λ$ polarization in U$+$U collisions at HIAF
summary: We investigate the effects of nuclear deformation on global $Λ$ polarization in U+U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.85$~GeV using the JAM2 transport model, in view of future measurements at HIAF. These findings connect nuclear shape with hyperon spin, opening a new avenue for probing nuclear deformation through polarization measurements in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions.

title: Search for $\mathrm{GeV}$-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions

summary: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. title: Testing thermal equilibrium in heavy-ion collisions with electric-charge fluctuations
summary: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions exhibit several phenomena commonly associated with the formation of a thermalized quark--gluon plasma. title: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
summary: This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. title: Remembering Brown-Rho scaling
summary: The properties of hadrons in dense matter have been a core interest of mine since I entered graduate school at Stony Brook in 1984. This interest was shaped both by the strong research activity on the subject at Stony Brook at the time and by the influence of Mannque Rho, who was a frequent visitor there. In this memoir dedicated to Mannque, I describe a selection of his works that sparked my interest in the subject and present my current perspective on what Mannque, together with Gerry Brown, sought to emphasize in the often-misinterpreted Brown--Rho scaling. In light of recent developments, I also discuss refinements of Brown--Rho scaling for mesons and baryons, associated with spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking and $U_A(1)$-breaking effects.

title: M-SHIVA 1.0: A Relativistic Resistive MHD Code for Heavy-Ion Collisions, with Applications to Momentum Anisotropy and Joule Heating in QGP
summary: We present M-SHIVA 1.0 (Magneto-resistive Solver for Heavy Ions with finite-Volume Algorithms), a (2+1)-dimensional relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics code for heavy-ion collisions in Cartesian and boost-invariant Milne coordinates. The code reproduces standard shock-tube, cylindrical-blast-wave and relativistic-rotor benchmarks. We use the framework to investigate the momentum anisotropy and electromagnetic energy transfer in an expanding quark-gluon plasma (QGP). title: Triangular and fourth-order flow of D mesons in Pb-Pb collisions with event-by-event fluctuations
summary: Charm quarks are valuable probes of the transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), yet the role of event-by-event medium fluctuations in shaping their observables remains to be quantified. In contrast, the anisotropic flow coefficients $v_n$ are increasingly sensitive to fluctuations with rising harmonic order $n$. title: Density dependence of effective Lambda-nucleon interactions
summary: Orbital-dependent $Λ$ binding energies in hypernuclei such as $^{208}_Λ$Pb, $^{40}_Λ$K, and $^{48}_Λ$K are important objectives of planned experiments at J-PARC and JLab and provide information on the density-dependent features of effective $ΛN$ interactions. To investigate this relation we introduce the environmental density $\barρ_\text{env}$, defined as the overlap integral of the Λand nuclear core densities, as quantitative measure of the nuclear environment experienced by the $Λ$ in each orbital. We find an approximately linear relation between the orbital-dependent binding energies and $\barρ_\text{env}$, offering a quantitative means to test and refine effective $ΛN$ interactions using future orbital-dependent binding-energy data.

title: Nuclear medium and final state interaction effects in $η$ production induced by $ν_μ(\barν_μ)$ at SBN and DUNE energies
summary: We investigate nuclear-medium modification and final-state interaction in charged- and neutral-current $ν_μ(\barν_μ)$-induced $η$-meson production on $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$. title: Coherent control of quadrupolar order in solid spin-1 systems:\ majorization bounds, orientation-indexed adiabatic inversion, and order lifetime

title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
summary: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
summary: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.

title: Amplitudes separation and strong-electromagnetic phases determination in the $\boldsymbol{J/ψ}$ decays into baryon-antibaryon pairs
summary: We extract the relative phase between strong and electromagnetic amplitudes of the decays of a vector charmonium into spin-$1/2$ baryon-antibaryon pairs. Starting from a flavour-SU(3) effective Lagrangian with vector and tensor currents, we construct a parametrization in terms of partial waves coefficients. The electric and magnetic phases, the phase of the integrated complex overlap and the effective rate angle are derived from the same source amplitudes. We retain two possible solutions and both of them describe the scalar $Σ^+\barΣ^-$ scan phase within its uncertainty, while presenting tension with several electric-magnetic production phases.

title: From oxygen to lead: testing a common QGP description with high-$p_\perp$ probes
summary: The observation of suppression and finite high-$p_\perp$ elliptic anisotropy in O+O and Ne+Ne raises the question of whether a common quark--gluon plasma (QGP) description can simultaneously account for both observables across systems from oxygen to lead. The calculation reproduces the observed ordering of suppression and predicts elliptic anisotropies of comparable magnitude across the four systems in 10--20$\%$ collisions. We predict a modest centrality dependence of $v_2^{\mathrm{SP}}$ and a more pronounced decrease of $v_3^{\mathrm{SP}}$ toward peripheral light-ion collisions, in contrast to the corresponding trends in larger systems.
