title: Low-lying states of $^{115}$Cd modeled as a valence neutron coupled to $^{114}$Cd
summary: $^{114}$Cd has historically been regarded as an ideal quadrupole vibrator due to its near-canonical level spacings, though this interpretation is disputed due to electromagnetic transition data from the two- and three-phonon states. In this paper we investigate whether, with the extension of including the single-phonon octupole state, the model is still useful in describing the coupling of a neutron to a cadmium-114 core to model the lowest- energy cadmium-115 states, as the triplet states have small to no influence in the calculation. The results thus provide supporting evidence for the tentatively-assigned $J^π$ values of the lowest-energy $^{115}$Cd states. A more- rigorous derivation than often used for the vibrational B(Eλ) is used, in conjunction with the $^{115}$Cd structure calculation, to provide a theoretical prediction of the $^{114}$Cd octupole deformation.

title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
summary: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

title: A modern particle-in-cell code for beam-beam simulations of future colliders
summary: A key challenge in the design of next-generation colliders is predicting the effects of beam-beam interactions and using these predictions to optimize machine performance. Beam-beam interactions are characterized by strong focusing forces, radiative effects, and the generation of background particles. While analytical formulas provide insight into the dynamics of beam-beam interactions, these nonlinear, coupled effects are most accurately described with numerical methods. In this paper, we introduce the open-source particle-in-cell code WarpX as a modern tool for modeling the interaction point in future lepton colliders. WarpX provides high-performance execution on distributed GPU architectures within an open-source and actively maintained code base. title: HOM Mitigation
summary: Higher Order Modes (HOMs) in accelerating structures are resonant electromagnetic fields excited and left behind by charged particle bunches. They can severely degrade the beam quality in accelerators, such as the multi-bunch energy spread and transverse emittance, and therefore one must carefully study and mitigate them. In this lecture, various methods of HOM mitigation are reviewed. On one hand, one tries to avoid their existence, for example by careful design of the accelerating structures and damping systems. On the other hand, one can reduce the effect of the excited HOM fields, for example by means of fast feedbacks or beam alignment. Additionally, a few ways to make HOM signals useful are referred to, such as diagnostics of the beam or of accelerating structures.

title: Anomaly Detection in Bunch Oscillations for Early Warning of Sudden Beam Loss at SuperKEKB

title: Brilliance: toward autonomous computational research in particle accelerator physics
summary: Computational research requires repeated decisions about models, calculations and the interpretation of results. title: Physics of stabilization and dynamic control of CW magnetrons for superconducting accelerators
summary: Powerful CW magnetrons were suggested for feeding RF cavities of superconducting accelerators because they provide higher efficiency and lower RF power cost than the traditionally used klystrons, IOTs, or solid-state amplifiers. summary: A comprehensive (start-to-end) simulation was performed regarding the formation of a front-tilted laser pulse and the subsequent acceleration of non-relativistic electrons moving along a reflective grating structure. title: AloHEP Software: A luminosity optimizer for High Energy Physics colliders
summary: The luminosity quoted for proposed particle colliders is usually derived from the analytic geometric formula, which assumes head-on collisions of identical, rigid Gaussian bunches. We present \textbf{AloHEP} (A luminosity optimizer for High Energy Physics), an open-source, cross-platform Java application that simulates the interaction region of both symmetric and asymmetric colliders. title: Limits on energy recovery for positron acceleration in a warm plasma column
summary: Beam-driven plasma wakefield acceleration (PWFA) is a promising candidate for realizing a future linear collider, owing to the extremely high field gradients that are produced in plasmas. Despite recent success in high-gradient and high-efficiency electron PWFA, efficient positron PWFA remains a challenge. The warm plasma column regime offers stable, high-quality acceleration of positron beams in a plasma electron filament, albeit at low energy-transfer efficiencies. We explore the possibility of employing an electron energy recovery beam to extract residual energy from the plasma wakefield and increase the efficiency of this scheme. title: Reveal normal form structure for nonlinear map in accelerator beam physics with symplectic neural network
summary: Long-term multi-turn tracking is required to study nonlinear phenomena in circular accelerators, such as resonances, chaotic motion, and the dynamic aperture. General-purpose neural networks do not preserve the symplectic structure of Hamiltonian dynamics, so their errors can grow over many turns. Symplectic neural networks (SympNets) guarantee symplecticity through their architecture rather than through a loss penalty. In this work, we use a SympNet to learn the normal-form transformation of a nonlinear map from tracking data. In the learned coordinates, the dynamics become a rotation of each mode, whose amplitude-dependent phase advance is given by a second network. We demonstrate the method on a four-dimensional McMillan-type map. title: Design of the Electron-Beam Collimator for the Electron-Ion Collider
summary: The design and optimization of a beam collimator for the Electron Storage Ring (ESR) of the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) are presented. An integrated design approach combining beam-loss tracking, electromagnetic-shower simulations, thermomechanical analysis, and impedance calculations is developed and benchmarked against published simulations and beam-impact experiments. A comparison of candidate absorber materials identifies Al2219-T62 as providing a favorable balance of beam-impact robustness, thermal and electrical conductivity, mechanical strength, and ultra-high-vacuum compatibility. title: Quarter-wave shift for an extra pass in an energy recovery linac
summary: Energy Recovery Linacs (ERLs) are advanced particle accelerators that recover the kinetic energy of the beam after interaction, significantly improving efficiency. In this paper we discuss an alternative operation mode for multi-pass ERLs with an extra pass at top energy, allowing a doubled beam current at the expense of an increased energy spread. We explain the theoretical concept behind this approach, detailing how the phase shift enables an extra acceleration pass without requiring additional hardware. Preliminary simulations on a lattice similar to the PERLE one explore the feasibility of this method. The results are discussed in the context of ERL performance optimization, and potential applications for future accelerator designs are explored.

Key parameters, such as substrate thickness and undulator period, were meticulously refined to ensure uniform deformation while minimizing the impact of higher harmonics, which could degrade performance. title: The JO&Minna Framework: A Method to Interpret Depth Profiles of Activation
summary: A novel analytical framework, designated as the JO\&Minna method, is presented for interpreting the depth profiles of residual activation induced by heavy-ion beams in thick structural materials. By combining the limiting fragmentation and factorization principles, the JO-factor formalism rigorously links the spatial distribution of projectile-like fragments to the range derivatives and electronic stopping powers. title: High-Field Brightness Limits of Alkali-Antimonide Photocathodes
summary: Pushing the brightness limit of electron sources requires simultaneously minimizing the intrinsic emittance and maximizing the accelerating field. Alkali-antimonide photocathodes exhibit excellent properties at low fields, yet their high-field photoemission physics remains poorly understood owing to acute vacuum sensitivity. The measured field dependence of the intrinsic emittance provides direct insight into photoemission physics at high fields. title: Recent radiological studies at NSLS-II using the Monte Carlo code FLUKA
summary: This work details some of the recent radiological studies performed at National Synchrotron Light Source II (NSLS-II) using the Monte Carlo (MC) particle transport code FLUKA. In particular, it assesses the radiation protection challenges posed by the anticipated NSLS-II facility upgrade, taking into consideration various upgrade options. Also, it evaluates the impact related to the use of different shielding materials and the employment of ambient dose H* as the external radiation exposure estimator of effective dose. Lastly, a demonstration of synchrotron radiation transport is provided for an in-silico beamline, all the way from the radiation source to end-station, utilizing FLUKA's recent X-ray reflectivity capabilities.

title: Compact ultrafast intense LWFA-driven crystal-based source of $γ$-radiation, positrons and neutrons
summary: Compact sources of intense $γ$-rays, positrons and neutrons can bring radiation and particle-beam capabilities to small university-scale laboratories that would otherwise rely on large accelerator facilities. Here we propose and simulate a compact, laser-driven source that combines laser plasma wakefield acceleration (LWFA) with oriented crystalline targets to enhance the conversion of relativistic electron beams into high-energy photons and secondary particles. Electrons aligned with major crystallographic directions undergo coherent interactions, including channeling radiation and coherent bremsstrahlung, producing substantially enhanced photon emission compared with amorphous targets. Moreover, the strong angular-spectral correlation of the emitted radiation enables the generation of collimated $γ$-ray beams with reduced spectral bandwidth. title: Beam Tracking I & II
summary: Longitudinal beam dynamics simulations are an essential tool for the design and operation of circular and linear accelerators alike, fundamentally supporting everything from RF system design to the interpretation of beam-based measurements. This paper gives a practical, self-contained introduction to longitudinal beam tracking, aimed at newcomers to the field who wish to build, or better understand, their simulation tools. Starting from the analogy between beam tracking and particle-in-cell plasma simulations, the basic equations of motion, their discretisation, and the choice of phase-space coordinates are introduced, followed by the collective effects driven by the machine impedance. The modelling of the RF system and its associated control loops, and the generation and matching of realistic particle distributions are discussed thereafter. title: Emittance tuning of the FCC-ee high energy booster ring
summary: The Future Circular Collider (FCC), in its leptonic configuration has been chosen by CERN as main proposition for the next high-energy collider. This project aims to achieve luminosities one to two orders of magnitude higher than ever. Feasibility studies have led to the definition of tolerances on magnet imperfections and correction strategies. This is crucial for ensuring the performance of one of the main elements of the acceleration chain, the High Energy Booster (HEB) ring. The efficiency and overall performance of these strategies greatly influence new magnet specifications and tolerances, affecting main optic functions. Horizontal and vertical orbit corrections use horizontal and vertical kickers, respectively. Skew quadrupoles address vertical dispersion and transverse coupling. title: Liquid xenon positron target flow optimizations
summary: In a previous work, we explored liquid xenon (LXe)-based positron targets as an alternative to conventional high-Z metallic targets for high energy physics applications. In this paper, we apply computational fluid dynamics simulations to the LXe target and containment vessel, including entrance and exit windows. We design a flow geometry that is able to quickly move heated LXe from previous beam pulses out of the target volume without significant boil-off. While our simulations indicate that the temperature of the exit window can be kept stable, the peak energy deposition density exceeds the widely accepted damage threshold of 35 Jg$^{-1}$ for ILC-like conditions.

title: Laser-Polarization Dependence of Betatron X-Ray Production and Angular Collection in Laser-Wakefield Acceleration
summary: Laser polarization affects both the production of betatron x rays and their angular distribution, which together determine the photon yield collected within a fixed angular acceptance. We investigate these effects using particle-in-cell simulations of laser-wakefield acceleration with linearly polarized (LP) and circularly polarized (CP) pulses of equal energy in helium--nitrogen targets of two different lengths. In the longer target, CP produces more photons early in propagation, whereas LP produces more later. For 20--60-keV photons transmitted through 2 mm of aluminum, the LP/CP yield ratio before angular selection changes from 0.88 early on to 1.91 in a late stage. Late-emitting LP electrons develop pronounced transverse oscillations along the laser polarization direction, accompanied by angular broadening of the radiation. title: Input to the SCAC Facilities Subcommittee from the U.S. Muon Collider Collaboration
summary: This document presents input from the U.S. Muon Collider Collaboration to the SCAC Facilities Subcommittee. It outlines the scientific motivation for a future Muon Collider, the R&D and demonstration program needed to establish its feasibility, and its relevance to U.S. facilities planning for 2026-2036. It also discusses opportunities for leveraging existing U.S. capabilities, developing the accelerator workforce, and building synergies with other DOE programs and international efforts.

title: Electron Rephasing in a Truncated Tunable Plasma Channel
summary: We report the acceleration of stable electron beams with energies up to 1.5 GeV using a 50 TW laser pulse guided in a preformed plasma channel generated by an axiparabola-focused heater pulse. Varying the channel length changes the plasma density beyond the channel end and produces distinct electron spectra. A short channel causes a large decrease in bubble size after the truncated channel, leaving only part of the electron bunch in the accelerating phase and resulting in a quasi-monoenergetic peak. For a longer channel ending near the target density down-ramp, the smaller density increase rephases and further accelerates a larger fraction of the bunch, producing a continuous high-charge spectrum. title: Calculation of the temporal structure for a pulsed slow positron beam based on superconducting accelerator
summary: The development of superconducting accelerator (SCA) provides a novel approach to generating pulsed slow positron beams with high time resolution and high intensity. SCAs can produce electron beams with repetition frequencies on the order of MHz and pulse widths of less than 100 ps. A pulsed positron beam based on SCA can, to a certain extent, preserve the excellent temporal structure of the primary electron beam. However, thermalization, diffusion, and surface re-emission of positrons in the moderator will inevitably lead to time broadening of positron pulses. In this paper, a calculation model coupling Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations with positron diffusion theory is established to evaluate the effect of the positron moderation process on time broadening. title: Terahertz-driven electron acceleration from subrelativistic to fully relativistic energies in stepped dielectric-lined waveguides
summary: The short wavelength of terahertz (THz) waves makes the acceleration of electrons, from typical electron gun energies to fully relativistic energies, challenging due to the need to match the velocities over comparably long distances. However, the inherent laser synchronisation of a photogun to the THz drive laser offers significant advantage in applications where timing is critical. We present a novel design process for high-gradient THz-driven dielectric-lined waveguide injectors and demonstrate designs for rectangular and cylindrical geometries. These structures utilize novel tapering and stepping schemes to manipulate the phase velocity, controlling the position of the electron bunch relative to the phase of the accelerating field. title: Electrons with Anomalous Energy Generated in Vacuum Diodes with Different Pulse Duration
summary: This paper presents results from an experimental study in which anomalous energy electrons (AEE) appear in vacuum diodes under varying amplitude and pulse-duration conditions. AEE refer to high-energy discharge electrons with kinetic energy $T$ exceeding $eU$ values (where $e$ is the electron charge and $U$ is the amplitude gap voltage). Here, two experimental setups were used to generate electron beams with different pulse durations. The electron energy spectra were reconstructed from the beam attenuation curves using an AI-driven methodology for solving an ill-posed inverse problem for the Fredholm equation. This confirms that vacuum diodes generate electron beams with a significant AEE fraction (up to 25~\%) only when operating with nanosecond-long voltage pulses. title: Circular-Mode Optics for High-Intensity Beams and High-Luminosity Colliders
summary: We study circular-mode optics as a framework for transporting and accelerating intrinsically flat beams while maintaining a round transverse projection in physical space. Motivated by the strong degradation of flat beams under low-energy space-charge forces, we develop a coupled-optics description of circular modes, analyze their formation and preservation, and derive lattice design conditions for conserving canonical angular momentum and coupling phase. These conditions motivate rotationally invariant transport and ring cells based on solenoids, symmetric alternating-gradient structures, and indexed dipoles. We further derive space-charge tune-shift and tune-spread expressions for circular-mode beams in uncoupled and coupled lattices, showing that they preserve the leading-order space-charge behavior of round beams while retaining intrinsic eigenemittance flatness. title: Magnetizing nonlinear plasma wakefields for positron acceleration: mechanism and operating limits
summary: Positron acceleration is possible in linear plasma wakes, but the nonlinear electron-driven blowout regime confines simultaneous acceleration and focusing to narrow regions of returning plasma electrons. Here we investigate how an axial magnetic field reorganizes this nonlinear return to open an operating regime for sustained positron acceleration in a uniform plasma. Using quasi-3D and full-3D particle-in-cell simulations, we connect the formation of finite-radius electron columns, or gyro images, to witness transport and its operating limits. The image spacing is governed by the quasi-static invariant, while canonical angular momentum limits the return radius. Modified by the orbit-sampled wake potential, this mechanism yields a positioning law that accurately predicts the density peaks across a wide range of magnetic field strengths. title: Physics-based logarithmic description of electrostatic field enhancement in hemisphere-on-cylindrical-post structures for high-field applications
summary: Electrostatic (ES) field enhancement at sharp conducting structures plays a central role in lightning protection, corona discharge, electrical breakdown in vacuum (for example in particle accelerators), and more generally in technological applications of field electron emitters. A canonical geometry for studying this ES effect is the hemisphere-on-cylindrical-post (HCP) model, in the regime where the structure stands on a planar conductor of large lateral extent, and a large gap exists between the structure and the counter-electrode. title: Hydrogen mon amour
summary: The FCC's projected average electricity consumption is 1.3 TWh per year. If supplied entirely by nuclear power, this would represent about 10% of the annual output of a large third-generation nuclear reactor, together with a corresponding share of its radioactive waste. By 2050, however, renewable sources could provide up to 80% of this electricity on a substantially decarbonised European grid, supported by long-term power-purchase agreements and flexible operation. This could reduce the residual nuclear requirement, and its associated waste, by up to a factor of five. This essay asks whether hydrogen could help bridge the remaining periods of low wind and solar generation. title: Incorporating Heightened Scrutiny into a Large HEP Software Project
summary: In 2023, DUNE began re-evaluating the requirements of its data-processing framework, which led to commissioning a new design that would better fit neutrino physics than the existing reconstruction frameworks designed for collider physics. Due to the radical changes expected, significant multi-institutional effort has been directed toward the creation of the Phlex framework. In addition, the tight timelines in which to implement such a framework have invited scrutiny from various parties, including DUNE itself, the host laboratory Fermilab, and the US Department of Energy. After briefly discussing the unique needs of neutrino physics, we will recount how the Phlex development team has approached the design and development of a framework in the context of this heightened scrutiny. title: Generation of 10-TW Attosecond X-Ray Pulses in a Free Electron Laser
summary: Attosecond pulses provide direct access to electron dynamics in atoms, molecules, and solids on their natural timescales. While table-top sources have achieved attosecond pulse durations at moderate intensities, extending attosecond science to high peak powers in the x-ray regime requires free-electron lasers (FELs). Here we report the generation of soft-x-ray pulses with a duration of $\sim\!100$ as and peak power on the order of 10 TW at the European XFEL. The unprecedented combination of pulse duration and peak power is enabled by operation of a soft-x-ray undulator at high electron energy together with five-stage bunch compression, producing ultrahigh peak currents. These millijoule-level attosecond x-ray pulses establish a new regime for attosecond science.

title: Fabry-Pérot Resonance Shifts as a Novel Non-destructive In Situ Surface Damage Diagnostic
summary: Current surface damage evaluation for nanostructured electronic devices requires specialized equipment or conditions outside the designed operating environment and cannot be used for in situ evaluation of surface damage. In this work, we developed a non-destructive method to probe the surface sublimation of a semiconductor heterostructure which can be applied to other semiconductor damage mechanisms. This approach employs shifts in the resonances of an optical cavity comprising the surface and an integrated distributed Bragg reflector fabricated below the semiconductor heterostructure undergoing sublimation. We performed the demonstration of this technique under vacuum, but surface damage effects can be observed in any operational environment either in situ or ex situ.

title: From Routing Delay Shifts to Silent Data Corruption: Neutron-Induced SEU Effects in AXI-Based Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoCs
summary: SRAM-based FPGA system-on-chip devices are vulnerable to single-event upsets (SEUs) in configuration memory, which may perturb programmable routing resources and degrade communication fabrics. In modern Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoCs, such routing disturbances can introduce small propagation delay shifts that remain logically transparent yet compromise AXI-based data transfers and lead to silent data corruption. Although routing delay degradation and AXI interconnect failures have been studied independently, their experimental correlation under neutron irradiation has not been established. This work presents a cross-layer investigation on a ZCU104 platform integrating routing-dominated delay sensors with an AXI interconnect benchmark comprising replicated accelerators. title: Climate, Science, and the FCC: Think Clearly, Choose Wisely, Act Swiftly
summary: Could a collider become the symbol of everything that must be abandoned to save the climate? In the summer of 2026, this question ran through discussions within the Particles and Fields Division of the French Physical Society. An unacceptable carbon footprint, two EPR nuclear reactors, five hundred deaths, billions to be reallocated and, to top it all, unclear scientific objectives: the objections to CERN's Future Circular Collider (FCC) appeared to form an overwhelming indictment. This essay examines each charge in turn. Grounded in a clear and compelling scientific vision, it confronts emotionally charged imagery with orders of magnitude, distinguishes a project's footprint from its full balance sheet, considers the costs of postponing or abandoning it, and explores ways of reducing its impacts-including the still uncertain prospect of natural hydrogen. title: Production of a Titanium Ion Beam Using Fluorides and Fluorine-Forming Precursors in an ECR Ion Source
summary: The production of multiply charged titanium ions is of significant interest for accelerator-based experiments, surface modification technologies, and applications in nuclear physics. Due to the low saturated vapor pressure of titanium at temperatures below 1000 °C, the generation of titanium ion beams from an electron cyclotron resonance ion source (ECRIS) remains a challenging task. The choice of titanium vapor injection methods into the ECR plasma plays a key role in achieving high ionization efficiency, plasma stability, and reliable long-term source operation. In this work, alternative approaches for the injection of neutral titanium atoms into the ECR plasma are investigated, focusing on the use of fluorine-containing compounds. title: Imaging with GeV muons produced via laser-wakefield-accelerated electrons
summary: Artificially generated muon beams, with tunable parameters, are highly valuable in imaging objects that are opaque to any other scanning technique. Lower-energy muon beams are currently produced at accelerator facilities, while higher energies have only recently been observed as a result of the interaction of laser-wakefield-accelerated electrons and solid targets. This work focuses on using muography imaging detectors to measure the profile of a muon beam generated via the Bethe-Heitler process and to perform muon imaging in an experimental setup extending up to 42 meters from the muon source. By comparing the data with Monte Carlo simulations, we confirm that the measured beam profile and object imaging are consistent with artificially produced muons of energy of a few GeV. title: Development and Testing of Tools for ORM Measurements and Quadrupole Centering
summary: In preparation for the commissioning of Linac2 (formerly referred to as the {PIP-II} linac) at Fermilab, we are developing high-level applications that automate Orbit Response Matrix (ORM) measurement and beam-based localization of quadrupole magnetic centers. Both procedures are designed to run in a low-amplitude mode compatible with otherwise regular operation. The ORM is measured by exciting multiple dipole correctors simultaneously at low amplitude, each at a distinct frequency, and applying a Discrete Fourier Transform to the recorded BPM signals to extract per-element transfer function with quantified noise. title: Vector Potential-based Beam Current Sensors: Applications for Mu2e, and Picosecond Bunch Substructure
summary: We report on a new beam current monitor system based on work originally done to develop timing planes for future collider detectors. In contrast to sensors based on wall currents or toroid inductance, we make use of electric field induced by the electromagnetic vector potential of the beam current as it passes near or through a transmission line (TL), arranged with its dominant TEM or TE10 fields aligned with the current, thus directly coupling to TL modes. For resonantly extracted proton pulses currently being commissioned at the Fermilab Delivery Ring, we utilized a TEM parallel-plate TL geometry, since the requirements included measuring the structure of the bunch over $\sim{}200~\rm{ns}$ time scales. title: Integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge Access in the ELBE Accelerator Control System
summary: The efficient operation of accelerator facilities increas- ingly relies on rapid access to heterogeneous operational knowledge, including logbooks, interlock reports, machine parameters, and historical archive data. At ELBE, we pro- posed a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frame- work that integrates facility documentation and operational records into a unified AI-assisted support tool for operators. The system is expected to index electronic logbooks, ma- chine archive time-series data, and subsystem manuals using domain-adapted embeddings stored in a vector database. User queries will be expected to be processed through a large language model that retrieves the most relevant oper- ational context and generates structured, operator-oriented responses with traceable source references. title: Thermomechanical rf breakdown from magnetically focused field emission in high-gradient normal-conducting cavities
summary: Normal-conducting radiofrequency (rf) cavities for muon-collider ionization cooling must operate at high accelerating gradients in strong solenoidal magnetic fields, where rf breakdown can be enhanced by the magnetic focusing of field-emitted electrons. In this work, field-emitted electrons were tracked in the realistic field maps of rectilinear cooling-lattice cavities to test the validity of the previously developed localized-bombardment picture with simplified field maps. Under comparable reduced-field assumptions, the tracking results show good agreement with previous results. title: Stable 50 MeV Beams from a 100 Hz Laser-Wakefield Accelerator Driven by an OPCPA Laser
summary: We demonstrate a laser-wakefield accelerator driven by a high-repetition-rate optical parametric chirped-pulse amplification (OPCPA) laser, producing stable, quasi-monoenergetic electron beams at 100 Hz. Using 70 mJ, 8.1 fs laser pulses, we obtain 47 MeV electron beams with 15 pC charge and an intrinsic energy spread below 10%. Measurements over 10,000 consecutive shots show rms fluctuations of only 1.4% in peak energy and 12% in charge, together with low pointing jitter. Principal-component analysis reveals that the beam fluctuations are described by five physically interpretable modes, dominated by slow variations below 1 Hz. title: Spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration and muon mean lifetime
summary: In this paper, it is shown that in spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration, there is a reduction of the mean lifetime of the muon. We consider several candidates for the maximal proper acceleration. For all of them, the induced corrections are small, but for the case when the maximal proper acceleration is identified with the Schwinger's acceleration, the effect is detectable in future muon collider facilities.

title: Bayesian Optimization of The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider Luminosity via $s^*$ Control
summary: Maximizing luminosity at the interaction point (IP) requires the collision location $s_{IP}$ to coincide with the longitudinal position of the minimum beta function, $s^$. Accurate optics measurements and control of $s^$ are therefore essential for luminosity optimization. At the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC), average horizontal beta-beat measurements between operating IPs are approximately $20%$, with significant variation in measured $s^*$. Precise control of the beam waist position $s^$ is particularly challenging for modern high-energy colliders with short bunch lengths and large crossing angles. We present an online Bayesian optimization (BO) application using the GPTune framework to optimize sPHENIX luminosity through $s^$ control at RHIC. title: Design and Operation of a 3-Crystal Multi-Volume Reflection Array for Loss Reduction in CERN SPS Slow Extraction
summary: The flux of protons slow-extracted from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) to the North Area experiments is limited by the induced radioactivity of the beam lost on the electrostatic septum during third-integer resonant extraction. Crystal shadowing, in which a thin bent silicon crystal deflects the protons that would otherwise hit the septum wires, has been in operation at the SPS since 2021; a single crystal at a non-local position halved the extraction losses relative to the local crystal alone, short of the fourfold reduction that future high-intensity operation requires. title: Experimental Verification of Circumferential Bunch Length Variation and Head-Tail Exchange Affecting Microwave Instability in a Storage Ring
summary: Classical analyses of microwave instability are built upon the longitudinal adiabatic approximation, which assumes that the bunch length remains constant around the storage ring. However, in a storage ring with small global phase slippage, the bunch length can vary around the ring and some particles can experience head-tail exchange due to the partial phase slippage and transverse-longitudinal coupling. Our theoretical study reveals that these effects can be beneficial for suppressing microwave instability. A new microwave instability threshold evaluation method has been correspondingly proposed to account for these effects. title: Moderator Modeling for High Intensity Slow Positron Sources
summary: Slow positron beams enable diverse applications, from surface-sensitive materials studies to positronium physics, but progress is limited by source intensity and brightness. In linac-based sources, mono-energetic, slow positrons are produced by moderating the broad, divergent distribution of fast positrons produced by high-energy electrons incident on a high-Z target. This process is intrinsically inefficient. Conventional linac-based designs place the moderator close to the target. Tungsten moderators become less efficient when heated by high-power, fast positrons, leading to defect-related losses. Cryogenic moderators, like solid neon, melt when exposed to high-power, fast positrons. summary: A new semi-analytical model for electron scattering in foils is presented valid for thin foils and electron-beam kinetic energies up to roughly $100$ keV and from 20 keV at a dimensionless foil thickness of $20$, and higher energies for thinner foils. To perform calculations, an approximate solution is constructed by Hankel transforms of an adapted Bethe transport equation for electron scattering. title: A compact fibre-coupled active beamstop for fast time-resolved monitoring of synchrotron X-ray beams
summary: We have developed a compact fibre-coupled active beamstop for simultaneous interception and time-resolved monitoring of the direct X-ray beam in synchrotron diffraction experiments. The complete beamstop tip has a maximum transverse dimension of 1 mm and incorporates a 700 $μ$m-wide Ce:YAG scintillator. The scintillator converts the intercepted X-rays into visible light, which is transported through a multimode optical fibre to a silicon photodiode at the bottom of the blade that is connected to a dedicated fast amplifier electronics. Tests with a pulsed laser yielded a system decay time of 69.4 ns, consistent with reported luminescence decay times for Ce:YAG. title: Reconstruction of Beam Transverse Parameters in the Fermilab Side-Coupled Linac Using a Normalized Coordinate Framework
summary: Quadrupole scans are a commonly used tool for beam second moment reconstruction. Limitations in the strength of the magnets and layout of the beamline elements frequently preclude simple quadrupole-drift-detector scans from collecting sufficient data for reconstruction. Using a normalized coordinate framework, we characterize the prerequisites for a robust simple quadrupole scan and expand these prerequisites to reconstruction from more complex optics. The beam second moments are investigated at two locations in the Fermilab Side-Coupled Linac under simple and complex optics, using this framework to maximize information gained from wire scanner profile measurements.

title: Coherent collective amplification of terahertz microbunching seeded by laser frequency beating in relativistic electron beams
summary: High-power, continuously tunable terahertz sources based on free-electron lasers require precise control of electron-beam microstructures. To describe this coupled evolution, a nonlinear model is developed for microbunching seeded by a frequency-beating laser heater. title: Heavy ion driven plasma wakefield acceleration with drift-like phase-shift acceleration scheme
summary: Traditional plasma density modulation schemes can extend the dephasing length but suffer from wakefield degradation as plasma density increases. title: Ultralow Mean Transverse Energy and High Quantum Efficiency Cryogenic Bialkali Photocathode for MHz-Repetition-Rate Electron Sources
summary: Simultaneously achieving high quantum efficiency (QE), ultralow mean transverse energy (MTE), and robust long-term operation under conditions relevant to continuous-wave (CW) X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) remains a central challenge for semiconductor photocathodes. This challenge arises from the trade-off between QE and MTE, as well as the difficulty of maintaining stable operation in high-field CW electron guns. Here we demonstrate a cryogenic K2CsSb photocathode that simultaneously achieves high QE, ultralow MTE, and robust long-term operation in a CW gun under XFEL-relevant operating conditions. Under cryogenic operation, the photocathode achieves an MTE of 50 meV while sustaining a QE of 5.4%. title: First Cobotic-Assisted String Assembly of PIP-II SSR2 Cavities at Fermilab
summary: Achieving robotic-assisted string assembly has been a longstanding objective in superconducting cavity pro-duction to improve precision, repeatability, and through-put while reducing operator-dependent variability. At Fermilab, robotic systems have been successfully deployed for the installation of individual components on SSR2 cavities inside a cleanroom environment. The single-cavity installations validated the feasibility of robotic techniques and provided confidence to extend automation to the assembly of a full prototype cavity string. Leveraging lessons learned from earlier operations, the robotic system was adapted for the string assembly. title: PIP-II Project Progress and Challenges
summary: The Proton Improvement Plan-II (PIP-II) project is under construction to provide the Fermilab Accelerator Complex with a new H$^-$ superconducting radiofrequency (SRF) linac and beam transfer line delivering 800 MeV protons at Booster injection at double energy and double intensity (6.7x10$^{12}$ protons per 20 Hz pulse) in comparison with the present Linac. The design goals of PIP-II Linac will be described, including delivering 1.2 kW beam power on Long Baseline Neutrino Facility (LBNF) target, continuous wave (CW) operation compatibility and future upgrades. The progress of the Linac construction and the development of the Commissioning Plan will be presented. Test results for a single cell and the full 32 cell system will be presented.

title: Direct observation of electron shedding from a laser-plasma accelerator

title: Damping Ring Optimization in Natural Emittance and IBS Dominated Regimes

title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
summary: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The relative sensitivities achieved for various principal quantum numbers are presented. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.

title: Exceptional Points as Witnesses of Non-Gaussian Noise
summary: Efficient control of quantum devices requires the knowledge of their environmental noise, yet the commonly measured power spectrum does not fully characterize non-Gaussian fluctuations of realistic environments. Here we show that exceptional points (EPs) in the noise-averaged dephasing response can expose observable signatures of non-Gaussian statistics, distinguishing environments with identical lower-order statistics. We also introduce a theoretical model that describes dephasing environments in terms of identical independent noise sources while preserving the power spectrum. Given a calibrated single-source model, the largest EP order extracted from the measured dephasing response determines the number of sources and predicts the higher-order statistics of the combined noise. title: Ionization and Dissociation Energies of Molecular Hydrogen
summary: Molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) is the simplest neutral molecule and its ionization and dissociation energies are key benchmarks for testing first-principles calculations of nonadiabatic, relativistic, quantum-electrodynamic and finite-nuclear-size effects in molecules. To obtain improved H$_2$ ionization and dissociation energies, we performed precision measurements of 15 transition frequencies in para-H$_2$. They connect the X $^1Σ_g^+(v=0,N=0)$ ground state, the long-lived EF $^1Σ_g^+(v=0,N=0)$ excited state, and several high members of the $n$p and $n$d Rydberg series with principal quantum number $n$ in the range between 48 and 70. The new data by itself leads to a five times more accurate value of the ionization energy of the ground state of para-H$_2$, equivalent to a relative frequency accuracy of $5\times 10^{-11}$. title: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array
summary: Neutral atoms in optical tweezer arrays have emerged as a leading platform for quantum information processing. The fidelity of entangling gates mediated by Rydberg interactions has improved rapidly and is increasingly constrained by blackbody-radiation-induced transitions, which shorten Rydberg lifetimes and create contaminant states that can cause correlated errors. Cryogenic environments can suppress these transition rates by more than an order of magnitude. However, realizing a universal gate set in such an environment has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate a universal quantum gate set in a cryogenic $^{133}$Cs atom array, with a single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.970(2)% and a raw two-qubit entangling-gate fidelity of 99.76(8)%, within the range of leading room-temperature implementations. title: Resolving Photochemical Reaction Pathways Using Field-Induced Surface Hopping Simulation of fs-EUV-TRPES: The Case of Furan
summary: Recent advances in femtosecond extreme ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy have enabled insight into photochemistry in gases, condensed phases, and at interfaces. Assigning spectral features to reaction pathways requires theoretical predictions connecting nonadiabatic dynamics to measured observables. Here, we present a general approach for resolving photochemical reaction pathways by combining field-induced surface hopping with explicit pulse excitation, RMS-CASPT2, and simulations of time-resolved photoelectron spectra. The pump field prepares the excited-state ensemble under experimental conditions, while the multireference treatment describes excited states, conical intersections, and bond-breaking coordinates. title: Simultaneous SI-traceable measurement of the amplitude and the ellipticity of microwave fields with cold Rydberg atoms
summary: We present a method for the simultaneous measurement of the amplitude and the ellipticity of microwave fields using trap-loss spectroscopy based on Rydberg excitation of a cold ensemble of 87Rb atoms. The measurement consists of probing the energy spectrum of the $61S_{1/2}$ to $61P_{1/2}$ transition in the presence of microwave, which depends on the electric field amplitude $|E|$ and the third Stokes parameter $|S_3|$. We use a millimeter-size magneto-optical trap to perform strongly-localized measurements, which mitigates the effect of microwave field inhomogeneities. This allows us to work with large Rabi frequencies and thus resolve small deviations from linear or circular states of polarization. title: Optical clock network tracks tidal variations of the gravity potential
summary: Gravity affects the passage of time, as described by General Relativity. On Earth, the rate of a clock as seen by a fixed observer changes by about one part in $10^{16}$ per metre in height. Chronometric levelling exploits this effect to directly measure differences in gravity potential by comparing distant clocks. It has been proposed as a complementary approach to established geodetic techniques for linking height reference systems and monitoring the terrestrial gravity potential. Experimental demonstrations have to date focused primarily on static potential differences. Yet, the potentials of the Moon, the Sun and other celestial bodies as well as the Earth's response to their tidal forcing change clock rates by several $10^{-17}$, providing a predictable test signal to demonstrate optical clock networks resolving small variations in relativistic time dilation. title: Reverse Quantum Annealing for Ground-State Energy Calculation in Molecule
summary: We present the results of our reverse quantum annealing computations of the ground-state energies of alkaline-earth monofluoride molecules. By partitioning the Dirac--Coulomb electronic Hamiltonian into sub-QUBOs and refining forward-annealing solutions through optimized reverse-annealing schedules, residual configuration errors are systematically minimized. The electronic ground-state wave functions and energies are obtained using the Quantum Annealing Eigensolver algorithm. This work provides a pathway for achieving sub-milliHartree chemical accuracy and advancing molecular electronic structure calculations in the quantum annealing paradigm.

title: Theoretical Study of Classical Dynamics of Electron in Two-Frequency Paul Trap
summary: We present a theoretical study of trapping an electron in a two-frequency Paul trap, motivated by future hybrid architecture consisting of a doubly charged calcium ion (Ca$^{2+}$) and an electron. By isolating the electron from ionic-electron interactions, we formulate the equations of motion for the electron in the time-dependent trap potentials and cast them in the Hill form. Stability and dynamics are then analysed in terms of the dimensionless q-parameters, which encode the applied voltages, drive frequencies, trap geometry, and the particle's charge-to-mass ratio. Under the combined action of the two radio-frequency fields, the trapped electron's classical motion is shown to be approximated well by a slow secular oscillation modulated by two distinct motion sidebands originating from the low- and high-frequency RF drives. title: Gravitational Interactions in Nuclear Clocks
summary: Atomic clocks achieve extraordinary precision through quantum control over large ensembles of atoms, with precision increasing and atom number advancing steadily. Emerging nuclear clock technology encodes clock states in nuclear rather than electronic transitions, offering a new frontier for precision measurement. Here we study whether a large ensemble of such clock nuclei could be used to observe their mutual gravitational interaction. We investigate the gravitational redshift induced by neighboring atoms, including nuclear energy superpositions as sources of gravity, giving rise to a genuinely quantum gravitational interaction between pairs of nuclei. title: Light and charge yields from nuclear recoils in noble liquids: From sub-keV energies to 1 MeV
summary: We present a first-principles study of total quanta and charge recombination in noble liquids, based on a solution of Lindhard's integro-differential equation for atomic motion with electronic straggling and detailed modeling of inter-atomic potentials. We introduce the electronic scaling length $ξ_e$ as a fundamental parameter related to a physical observable of the system. We study the energy and electric-field dependence of the exciton-to-ion ratio for nuclear recoils based on the Bates-Griffing process and semiclassical atomic interactions. The resulting light and charge yields are expressed through the recombination probability in the Thomas-Imel box model using the calculated parameter $ξ_e$ and one fitted constant. title: Extending the limits of rotationally resolved mid-IR spectroscopy: an accurate model of trioxane derived from combining Fourier transform and sub-Doppler measurements
summary: 1,3,5-Trioxane, a polyoxymethylene (POM) molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry and astrophysics, exhibits a dense rovibrational spectrum that challenges high-resolution spectroscopic characterization. Here, we report an extensive study of its $ν$ 5 CO symmetric stretching mode (960-1000 cm -1 ) by combining broadband high-resolution FTIR spectroscopy (0.001 cm -1 resolution, >2000 transitions) with SI-traceable sub-Doppler saturated absorption measurements using frequency-stabilized CO 2 lasers and a frequency-comb-referenced quantum cascade laser. The latter achieve lineposition uncertainties as low as 40 kHz, revealing inaccuracies in the FTIR frequency scale. A frequency-scale correction is determined by maximizing the global consistency of the complete spectroscopic data set. title: $3\times10^{-16}$ Stable Laser Deployed on a 4.3 km Mountain
summary: We present a transportable stable laser system based on a 10 cm reference cavity and an all-fiber phase-stabilized distribution network for the $^{171}$Yb clock wavelength. We highlight an extended cuboid cavity geometry with 4 times smaller spacer volume than a traditional cubic cavity of the same length [30]. We demonstrate repeatable acceleration sensitivities below $2\times10^{-10}$ g$^{-1}$ in all axes and fractional frequency instability as low as $3 \times 10^{-16}$. We also demonstrate accurate distribution of the stable light over 10 m fibers below the $1\times10^{-18}$ level in an all-fiber optic system. We report the successful deployment of the laser system to the summit of Mount Blue Sky at 4300 m, and for the first time, we report 16-digit laser instability measured outside the lab.

title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
summary: Feynman once remarked that the double-slit experiment has in its heart the only mystery of quantum mechanics. Arguably, the scientific significance of double-slit experiments lies in motional decoherence and the mechanism behind it. Decoherence of motional states underpins our understanding of quantum-to-classical transition. It is also central to the operation of miniaturized quantum electron devices and poses a resolution limit for electron microscopes. In this work, we provide experimental evidence for the critical role of quantum Brownian motion in electron motional decoherence. We demonstrate, for the first time, clear signatures of electron-metal decoherence and its continuous tunability. title: Controlled Dark-State Energy Storage and Work Extraction in V-Type Quantum Batteries
summary: The performance of a quantum battery depends not only on its ability to retain stored energy against unwanted discharge but also on the amount of useful work that can be extracted from it. Here, we investigate these complementary aspects in an ensemble of V-type qutrits coupled to a lossy cavity. By applying a finite splitting pulse to the two excited states of each qutrit, cavity-bright excitations are converted into atomic dark states, whose populations remain protected upon restoring degeneracy, even while the light-matter coupling remains active. Simulations with finite-duration pulses reveal a capture window governed by the competition among energy transfer, bright-to-dark conversion, and photon leakage. title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
summary: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
summary: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. title: Nuclear recoil effects with a realistic nuclear charge form factor
summary: We introduce a novel two-parameter Gamma model of the nuclear charge distribution as an alternative to the widely used Fermi distribution. The model yields simple analytical formulas for all moments of the charge distribution and closed-form expressions for the electrostatic potential and momentum-space form factor, the latter satisfying the correct analyticity requirements for a physical charged particle. We apply the model to calculate the nuclear recoil correction to the Lamb shift in electronic and muonic atoms and analyze its nuclear-model dependence. We find that the nuclear-size recoil corrections to energy levels of heavy muonic atoms are strongly sensitive to higher moments of the nuclear charge distribution, highlighting the importance of realistic nuclear modeling. title: Derivation of OH sum rules without Rayleigh--Jeans approximation: a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants
summary: In this paper, we show that the optical depths of any OH $Λ$-doublet quartet obey one exact linear relation in every velocity channel. No approximation is needed. The only exception is the $^{2}Π_{1/2}$ $J{=}1/2$ level, which has three transitions only, because its $F{=}0{\leftrightarrow}0$ line is strictly forbidden. The relation is $τ_{S_1}(v)/μ_{S_1}^{2}+τ_{S_2}(v)/μ_{S_2}^{2}=τ_{M_1}(v)/(aμ_{M_1}^{2})+τ_{M_2}(v)/(bμ_{M_2}^{2})$, where $a=2J^{2}+J-1$, $b=2J^{2}+3J$, and the $μ_i^{2}$ are reduced transition dipole moments derived from the catalogued Einstein $A$ coefficients. It holds equally for gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), for non-LTE gas, for masers and for conjugate gas. We suggest that it is a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants.

title: A low-volume cold-atom microwave clock with an additively manufactured cavity
summary: We present the performance of a compact microwave interrogated atomic clock based on laser cooled $^{87}$$\rm{Rb}$ atoms. The clock utilizes a micro-fabricated grating magneto-optical trap (gMOT) to cool and trap atoms, and an additively manufactured microwave cavity for microwave interrogation. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $370$ at a 1 Hz bandwidth and mid-term instability of $6.7\times10^{-14}$ at an averaging time of $τ=3 \times 10^{4}$ s. In addition, a low cost mu-metal foil has been implemented on the vacuum chamber to reduce the quadratic Zeeman shift which was previously limiting stability beyond $τ= 10$ s.

title: Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed beyond electrically small antennas
summary: The reception of electromagnetic signals becomes increasingly challenging at longer wavelengths, as conventional antenna feeds must scale with the operating wavelength, making it difficult to reconcile compactness with high sensitivity. Rydberg atoms enable direct field-to-optical conversion within deeply subwavelength sensing volumes, yet an effective receiving feed that couples incident fields into the atomic interaction volume remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce a Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed (RAFEF) that integrates electromagnetic field capture and enhancement with Rydberg-atomic transduction. We establish a physical model to quantify its receiving capability, Phi, that jointly accounts for sensitivity enhancement, receiving bandwidth and normalized three-dimensional volume, and experimentally obtain Phi_dB = 70.81 dB. title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.08E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
summary: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18

title: Long-Baseline Phase-Coherent Microwave Reception Using Rydberg Atoms
summary: A long baseline phase-coherent microwave receiver is demonstrated using a remotely interrogated cesium Rydberg atom sensor over an 8 m free-space optical link. A 3.989 GHz local oscillator (LO) is intensity-modulated onto an 852 nm optical probe and recovered remotely for atomic superheterodyne detection. A 509 nm coupling laser establishes a Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) system addressing the 6S1/2 to 6P3/2 to 56D5/2 ladder, with microwave coupling to 57P3/2. A test signal offset by 5 kHz generates an optically detected intermediate-frequency (IF) response returned to the reference station for centralized coherent acquisition. This eliminates independent remote oscillators, electronic IF acquisition, and distributed clock synchronization. title: A new analytical finding for the Born-Infeld integral potential
summary: A new finding regarding the Born-Infeld potential for short range distances from the charge revealed that its integral form can be almost exact written as the difference between a Coulomb-type potential and a Yukawa-type potential. This allowed for an immediate physical interpretation in terms of classical vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Subsequently, a new U(r) is proposed to cover the entire space. This formulation is then applied to calculate, in a closed manner, the first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms; a comparison of these shifts with high-precision spectroscopic data provides a model-dependent lower bound for the maximum field intensity parameter b.

title: A classical trajectory method for diatom-atom-atom ternary association reactions
summary: We introduce a classical trajectory method for calculating direct diatom-atom-atom ternary association re- action rates that incorporates the rotational degrees of freedom of the diatomic reactant. By treating the diatomic molecule as a rigid rotor, we include the effects of the anisotropy of the molecule-atom interaction and the dynamical effects of the rotational motion. We apply this approach to a system of experimental interest, CD+ + He + He, along with the isotopic variant CH+ + He + He -> CHHe+ + He, and examine the role of the internal, rotational degrees of freedom of the diatomic molecule. In particular, we find that in the regime where the collision energy is much smaller than the rotational energy of the entrance channel, the rotational motion leads to deviation from the classical threshold law by violating the assumptions of long-range capture theory models.

title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
summary: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
summary: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. title: Zero photoemission from icosahedral superatoms
summary: Photoemission is expected to occur when the photon energy exceeds the binding energy of an electron, with the photoemission yield generally remaining non-zero above this threshold. Yet, it can be suppressed at specific photon energies, a phenomenon known as the Cooper minimum. Although complete suppression represents an extreme limit of this phenomenon, such zero photoemission has previously been reported only for atoms with an outermost s-type orbital and has never been observed in non-atomic systems. Here, we demonstrate the deliberate realization of zero photoemission from Ag12W-, an artificial icosahedral superatom, by observing a vanishing photoemission cross section 0.85 eV above the detachment threshold and reproducing this behavior in theoretical simulations. title: Thermal-noise-limited stabilization of a self-injection-locked diode laser using a miniature Fabry-Perot cavity
summary: We present an ultrastable laser system based on miniature core components: a self-injection-locked laser comprising a distributed-feedback laser diode and an integrated microring resonator, together with a 3-ml vacuum-gap Fabry-Perot cavity. By carefully addressing technical noise sources, in particular residual amplitude modulation, we demonstrate a thermal-noise-limited fractional frequency instability of $5\cdot10^{-15}$ for averaging times between 1 and 10 s, which is among the lowest reported for compact cavity-stabilized lasers. This performance is achieved with conventional multilayer mirrors and a moderate cavity finesse of $10^5$. Such stability of the output frequency, combined with the small size of the core components and a possibility to generate a Kerr frequency comb in the very same microring resonator, provides a path towards fully integrated photonic frequency references

title: Photoelectrons resolve the phase-dependent variance of bright squeezed vacuum
summary: The variance of bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) is not only strong but also phase dependent, yet recent strong-field experiments with BSV have recorded only its magnitude. A coherent field of the same color provides the phase reference that resolves this phase-dependent noise. Strong-field ionization of xenon by this light shows that the photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature along the coherent field, and that the nonlinearity of ionization amplifies the quadrature noise many times over in the electron yield. The noise is moreover distributed unevenly over the photoelectron momentum distribution, differing by an order of magnitude between ionization channels. Strong-field ionization thus offers a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector of quantum light, while the quadrature noise of quantum light offers a probe of the intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.

title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
summary: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.

title: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers
summary: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. title: Precise Determination of Electric Dipole Polarizabilities of Sr Clock States Using Linear-Response and Equation-of-Motion Relativistic Coupled-Cluster Methods
summary: We present accurate values of the electric dipole polarizabilities ($α$) of the ground and excited states of Sr using four-component relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) theory within the linear-response (LR) and equation-of-motion (EOM) frameworks. We first investigated accuracy of the ground-state polarizability using the LR-RCC method in both spherical and Cartesian coordinate representations. Upon obtaining consistent results for the ground state, we determine the polarizabilities of the excited states using the EOM-RCC method within the finite-field approach. The uncertainties in our results are assessed by examining the completeness of the basis set, higher-order relativistic corrections, and contributions from higher-level excitation configurations beyond the truncation in our RCC method. title: Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster study of systematic shifts and fine-structure constant sensitivity in {\rm Cf$^{17+}$}, {\rm Cm$^{15+}$} and {\rm Bk$^{16+}$} highly charged ions
summary: Highly charged ions (HCIs) are among the most promising candidates proposed for the development of next-generation optical clocks and the precision tests of fundamental physics. In this work, we investigate the clock-relevant properties of $\rm Cf^{17+}$, $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ HCIs using Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster (FSRCC) theory. The corrections from Breit interaction, QED effects and perturbative triples are incorporated to improve the accuracy of results further. We compute excitation energies, transition amplitudes, lifetimes, hyperfine structure constants, electric quadrupole moments, and electric dipole polarizabilities for low-lying states of these ions. These properties are further used to characterize important clock transitions and estimate key systematic frequency shifts. title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
summary: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) accelerates exact trajectory simulation by sampling noise before state evolution. This method requires the outcome probability of every stochastic event to be independent of the state, which excludes mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. We present a generalization of PTSBE to measurement and Kraus operators without approximation. title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
summary: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) make atomistic simulations possible at scales beyond the reach of density functional theory (DFT). Matlantis PFP is a uMLIP that treats a variety of domains, including crystals, molecules, and surfaces, with a single model. PFP v8 incorporated a training dataset computed with the r2SCAN functional, chosen for its good agreement with experiment, but the elements and domains covered by that dataset were limited. title: Real-space electrostatic sums through truncation error analysis
summary: Methods that treat electrostatics in real space, without explicit reciprocal-space evaluation, are appealing for large-scale atomistic simulations. They typically employ local charge-neutralization schemes, but their relationship to the underlying error contributions of the full Ewald sum has not been fully characterized. A principled basis for parameter selection is also lacking. In this work, we show that the correction terms of Wolf's and Pickard's real-space methods approximate the truncation error of real-space electrostatic sums. This perspective motivates simplified fixed-radii and force-shifted Pickard variants that preserve the truncation-error compensation behavior while enforcing continuity of pair energy and force at the cutoff. title: Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language
summary: Preparing, executing, and validating strongly coupled multi-physics simulations require expert time. Agentic workflows use large language models (LLMs) to coordinate them from natural-language descriptions, but reliability requires checks of physical consistency and fidelity to the problem description. Our agentic harness implements explicit task allocation: LLMs interpret user requests and simulator diagnostics, generate input components not covered by predefined construction rules, and propose repairs, while deterministic routines construct supported components and check inputs, edits, and results. We evaluate CO2-storage problems using the multi-physics simulator GEOS, from compositional flow to flow-poromechanics with frictional fault contact. title: OpenPINN/PINO: An Extensible Open-Source Framework for Agent-Assisted Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Neural Operators
summary: Substantial challenges in physics-informed learning have motivated many improvements, but fragmented implementations hinder systematic organization, integration, and comparison. We propose OpenPINN/PINO, an extensible open-source PyTorch framework for physics-informed neural networks and neural operators. Two shared specifications connect problem setup, local computation, and evaluation. Agents support problem formulation, solver planning, and diagnosis. ProblemSpec defines geometry, governing equations, constitutive relations, parameters, initial and boundary conditions, and optional data. MethodSpec configures the model, sampling, loss, optimization, and differentiation. title: Right shape, wrong time: phase errors of ODE solvers in the flame problem

title: Global sensitivity analysis of transient regimes in non-Newtonian dam-break flows applied in rheometry
summary: Non-Newtonian dam-break flows are a classical problem with numerous engineering applications. However, the lifting dynamics of the containing obstacle introduce inertial effects that can compromise the accurate estimation of these properties. These effects are influenced by the lifting velocity, the fluid's viscosity, and the initial geometry of the sample. This study aims to quantify the influence of lifting velocity and to provide physical insights into how inertial effects influence the flow. summary: Reactive phase change fluids have been shown to enhance thermodynamic performance by integrating chemical reactions with thermodynamic cycles. summary: The effect of aiding buoyancy on flow past a square cylinder has previously been shown to suppress vortex shedding above a critical Richardson number (Ri), transitioning from unsteady to steady flow. title: Will it bend? Modelling hydrogel box hinges with a gel Lattice Spring Method
summary: Hydrogels are biocompatible smart materials comprised of a hydrophilic polymer network which can absorb a large volume of water (swelling). title: The Akhmediev breather for the Dysthe equation and the unstable manifold of the Stokes wave
summary: In this article we define and compute the breather of the Dysthe equation for deep water waves, the analogue of the Akhmediev breather of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS). title: A Five-Dimensional Geometric Formulation of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics

title: Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
summary: We develop a data assimilation framework to address the ``ship-as-a-buoy'' problem, i.e., estimation of the wave field from time series of ship motion. title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
summary: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these particles in a laboratory wind-wave tank, then use this data to model how much sunlight the particles would be exposed to in an aquatic environment. In particular, we explore how their orientation affects their sunlight exposure in these conditions, since most studies to date do not account for orientation, turbulent shear flow, and wind-waves at the water surface. We find that in all cases, particles prefer certain orientations, and this causes the average sunlight exposure of the particles to be 5 to 40\% higher than would be expected if their orientations were random. summary: Controlling and reducing undesirable vortical structures in unsteady flows is a major issue in aerodynamics. This paper presents an active control methodology that combines topological data analysis (TDA) through persistence diagrams, a reduced-order model based on dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) and receding-horizon model predictive control (MPC). Vortices are detected and characterised by the persistence diagram of the absolute value of the vorticity, which makes it possible to define a target flow in which only the useful vortices are retained. This target flow is computed offline in the reduced space by gradient descent, the derivative of a persistence diagram being defined through a parametrisation of the space of diagrams. title: Interaction between fluids and Helfrich membranes
summary: We propose a finite-element method to determine the dynamics of a fluid interacting with a membrane---a fluid layer equipped with a Helfrich elastic free energy [W. Helfrich, Z. Naturforschung C, 28, 693, (1973)]. Our analysis is based on a partitioned approach, where the state of the fluid, of the membrane, and of the mesh, are solved for at staggered steps. We show the predicting capabilities of the method by considering a macroscopic example of an elastomer membrane, which bulges as it interacts with air injected through a channel. We demonstrate that our method allows for describing large membrane deformations which are not accessible by perturbative methods.
